etymology_story.zh: 该词在中古英语时期经法语及拉丁语传入，最终源于拉丁语 abiurare，由 ab-（离开）和 iurare（发誓）组成。原义强调通过誓言否认或放弃，后来也用于郑重弃绝某种信仰、立场或行为。
etymology_story.en: The word entered Middle English through French and Latin, ultimately from Latin abiurare, combining ab- ('away') with iurare ('to swear'). It originally emphasized renouncing or denying something under oath and later broadened to solemnly rejecting beliefs, positions, or practices.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可分析为 ab-（离开）＋黏着词根 jur（发誓）＋词尾 -e；-e 本身不承载独立词义。词族包括 abjures、abjured、abjuring、abjuration（郑重弃绝；宣誓放弃）、abjurer（宣誓放弃者）和较少见的 abjuratory（宣誓弃绝的）。
morphology_enriched.en: The structure is ab- ('away') + the bound root jur ('swear') + final -e, which has no separate meaning. The family includes abjures, abjured, abjuring, abjuration ('solemn renunciation'), abjurer ('someone who abjures'), and the less common adjective abjuratory ('involving renunciation under oath').

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: renounce（正式放弃）适用范围最广，不必涉及誓言；recant（公开撤回）强调收回先前表达的观点；forswear（发誓戒绝）与 abjure 最接近，常强调决心不再从事某种行为。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Renounce is the broadest term and need not involve an oath; recant emphasizes withdrawing a previously expressed belief or statement; forswear is closest to abjure and often stresses a determined promise to stop a practice.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: ab-＝离开，jur＝发誓：发誓与旧信念分开。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Ab- means 'away' and jur means 'swear': swear yourself away from an old belief.

etymology_story.zh: 该词源于希腊语 anthrōpikos（人的），其基础是 anthrōpos（人；人类），于19世纪进入英语。它保留了“与人类有关”的基本意义，后来在宇宙学术语 anthropic principle（人择原理）中获得专门用法。
etymology_story.en: The word derives from Greek anthrōpikos ('human'), based on anthrōpos ('human being'), and entered English in the nineteenth century. It retained the general meaning 'relating to humans' and later acquired a specialized use in the cosmological term anthropic principle.

morphology_enriched.zh: anthrop-（人；人类）＋-ic（与……有关的）构成形容词。直接派生形式有 anthropically（从人类存在或活动的角度）；共享 anthrop-／anthropo- 词根的相关词包括 anthropology（人类学）、anthropologist（人类学家）、anthropological（人类学的）、anthropocentric（以人类为中心的）、anthropocentrism（人类中心主义）、anthropogenic（人类活动造成的）、anthropomorphic（拟人的）和 anthropomorphism（拟人化；拟人观）。这些相关词并非都由 anthropic 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Anthrop- ('human') + -ic ('relating to') forms the adjective. A direct derivative is anthropically ('with reference to human existence or activity'); related formations sharing anthrop- or anthropo- include anthropology ('the study of humans'), anthropologist ('a researcher in anthropology'), anthropological ('relating to anthropology'), anthropocentric ('human-centered'), anthropocentrism ('a human-centered outlook'), anthropogenic ('caused by human activity'), anthropomorphic ('attributing human characteristics'), and anthropomorphism ('the attribution of human characteristics'). These related words are not all direct derivatives of anthropic.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: human（人类的）最普通、适用范围最广；anthropogenic（人为造成的）明确强调人类活动是成因；anthropocentric（以人类为中心的）强调观点或价值取向，而 anthropic 本身不必包含因果或价值判断。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Human is the ordinary, broad equivalent; anthropogenic specifically identifies human activity as the cause; anthropocentric describes a human-centered viewpoint or value system, while anthropic does not by itself imply either causation or a value judgment.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: anthrop-＝人类：anthropic 就是把问题与人的存在联系起来。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anthrop- means 'human': anthropic connects a subject with human beings or their existence.

etymology_story.zh: 该词在近代早期英语中由 brow（眉额；神情）和 beat（打击；压倒）组合而成。它描绘用凶狠的神情和气势压倒他人，逐渐固定为“以威吓迫使别人服从”的意思。
etymology_story.en: The word arose in early modern English as a compound of brow ('forehead or expression') and beat ('strike or overpower'). It evokes overpowering someone with a threatening expression and manner, developing the established meaning of intimidating someone into compliance.

morphology_enriched.zh: brow（眉额；神情）＋beat（打击；压倒）构成复合动词。屈折变化为 browbeats、browbeat（过去式）、browbeaten（过去分词）、browbeating（现在分词）；browbeating 也可作名词，表示“威吓行为”，browbeaten 也可作形容词，表示“受威吓而畏缩的”。
morphology_enriched.en: Brow ('forehead or expression') + beat ('strike or overpower') forms a compound verb. Its inflections are browbeats, browbeat (past tense), browbeaten (past participle), and browbeating (present participle); browbeating also functions as a noun meaning 'intimidating behavior,' and browbeaten as an adjective meaning 'cowed by intimidation.'

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: bully（欺凌；强逼）范围更广，可能涉及反复欺压或身体暴力；intimidate（恐吓）强调使人害怕的效果；hector（盛气凌人地训斥）强调咄咄逼人的说教，而 browbeat 强调以这种气势压服对方。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Bully is broader and may involve repeated abuse or physical force; intimidate emphasizes making someone afraid; hector stresses aggressive, domineering speech, while browbeat emphasizes using such pressure to overpower someone's resistance.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: brow＋beat：皱眉怒视，用气势把对方压下去。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Brow + beat: a threatening brow helps beat down someone's resistance.

etymology_story.zh: 该词直接源自拉丁语 cerebellum，是 cerebrum（脑）的指小形式，字面意思是“小脑”。这一名称反映其外形和相对大小，后来成为这一脑部结构的标准解剖学名称。
etymology_story.en: The word comes directly from Latin cerebellum, a diminutive of cerebrum ('brain'), literally meaning 'little brain.' The name reflects its appearance and relative size and became the standard anatomical term for this brain structure.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常将 cerebellum 作为完整的借入名词学习；医学构词使用 cerebell-／cerebello-（小脑）。复数为 cerebella 或 cerebellums；相关形式包括 cerebellar（小脑的，cerebell-＋-ar）、cerebellitis（小脑炎）、spinocerebellar（脊髓小脑的）和 cerebellopontine（小脑脑桥的）。cerebrum（大脑）和 cerebral（大脑的）在词源上相关，但不是 cerebellum 的现代派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English generally treats cerebellum as a complete borrowed noun; medical formations use cerebell- or cerebello- ('cerebellum'). Its plurals are cerebella and cerebellums; related forms include cerebellar ('relating to the cerebellum,' cerebell- + -ar), cerebellitis ('inflammation of the cerebellum'), spinocerebellar ('relating to the spinal cord and cerebellum'), and cerebellopontine ('relating to the cerebellum and pons'). Cerebrum and cerebral are historically related but are not modern derivatives of cerebellum.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: little brain（小脑）是解释词源的通俗别称；hindbrain（后脑）范围更大，包括小脑及其他结构；cerebrum（大脑）指另一脑部结构。后两者是辨析用的相关词，并非 cerebellum 的同义词；该词没有常用的精确单词同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Little brain is an informal nickname reflecting the word's origin; hindbrain is broader and includes the cerebellum and other structures; cerebrum names a different brain structure. The latter two are related terms for comparison, not synonyms, and cerebellum has no common exact single-word synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 字面是“小脑”：想象脑后的小教练，帮助动作协调、身体站稳。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Literally 'little brain': picture a small coach at the back of the brain helping movements stay coordinated and the body stay balanced.

etymology_story.zh: 经法语 commodieux 和中世纪拉丁语 commodiosus 传入英语，最终与拉丁语 commodus“合适的、便利的”有关。早期的“方便、合用”之义后来主要发展为描述空间“宽敞舒适”。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English through French commodieux and Medieval Latin commodiosus, ultimately related to Latin commodus, meaning suitable or convenient. Its earlier meaning of convenient or serviceable developed into the usual modern meaning of spacious and comfortable.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中以 commodious 为完整形容词词干，不拆成 commode + 后缀。词族：commodiously（宽敞舒适地）、commodiousness（宽敞舒适）；加否定前缀 in- 得到较少见的 incommodious（狭窄不便的），以及 incommodiously（狭窄不便地）、incommodiousness（狭窄不便）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, commodious is best treated as a complete adjective stem, not as commode plus a suffix. Its family includes commodiously and commodiousness; the negative prefix in- produces the less common incommodious, with incommodiously and incommodiousness.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: spacious（宽敞的）客观强调空间大；roomy（空间充足的）较口语化，常用于车辆、衣物或房间；commodious 较正式，兼有宽敞与使用舒适之意。

senses.meaning_zh: 一致；协调；相符
senses.meaning_en: agreement or compatibility

senses.meaning_zh: 协和；协和音程或和声的性质
senses.meaning_en: the stable or harmonious quality of musical sounds heard together
senses.english_definition: In music, consonance is the quality of notes that sound stable or harmonious when they are played together.
senses.collocation_en: consonance and dissonance; harmonic consonance
senses.collocation_zh: 协和与不协和；和声的协和性
senses.sentence_en: The final chord creates a sense of consonance after the tension of the previous passage.
senses.sentence_zh: 前一乐段营造出紧张感，最后的和弦则带来了协和感。

senses.meaning_zh: 辅音重复；辅音谐音
senses.meaning_en: the repetition of consonant sounds in nearby words
senses.english_definition: In poetry and other writing, consonance is the repetition of the same consonant sound in words close to each other.
senses.collocation_en: the use of consonance; consonance in poetry
senses.collocation_zh: 辅音重复手法的运用；诗歌中的辅音重复

senses.sentence_zh: blank 和 think 中重复出现的词尾辅音构成了辅音谐音。

etymology_story.zh: 经法语 consonance 源自拉丁语 consonantia，相关动词 consonare 由 con-“一起”和 sonare“发声”组成。“一起发声、声音和谐”的概念后来扩展到意见、行为或事物之间的一致。
etymology_story.en: Through French consonance, the word comes from Latin consonantia, related to consonare, formed from con-, together, and sonare, to sound. The idea of sounding harmoniously together extended to agreement between ideas, actions, or things.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代词族关系可记为 consonant（协调一致的；协和的）→ consonance（协调；协和），体现 -ant 与 -ance 的对应，而非 consonant + -ance 的直接拼接。词族还包括 consonantly（协调地）；consonant 作名词表示“辅音”，由此派生 consonantal（辅音的）、consonantally（以辅音方式）。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern family shows the pattern consonant → consonance, with corresponding -ant and -ance endings rather than simple addition of -ance to consonant. Related forms include consonantly; the noun consonant, meaning a consonant speech sound, also gives consonantal and consonantally.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: agreement（一致）最通用，侧重意见或事实相符；harmony（和谐）侧重各部分相处融洽或声音悦耳；accord（一致、协调）较正式。consonance 常突出相互契合，在音乐和修辞中另有专门含义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Agreement is the broadest term for matching views or facts; harmony emphasizes a pleasing relationship or combination of sounds; accord is a formal term for agreement. Consonance often emphasizes compatibility and also has specific musical and literary meanings.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: con-＝一起，son-＝声音：声音合拍是“协和”，意见合拍是“一致”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Con- means together and son- relates to sound: sounds fitting together suggest musical harmony, and ideas fitting together suggest agreement.

meaning: 禁忌证；不宜采用某治疗的医学理由

morphology.text: contra-（相反、反对）+ indication（指征）→ contraindication（不宜采用某治疗的指征）。

etymology.text: 近代医学英语用拉丁语来源的 contra-“反对”与 indication“指示、指征”构成；就像身体亮起一盏不宜使用某治疗的警示灯。

usage_note: 医学用语；常见 a contraindication to 某治疗。它是“不宜使用的理由”，不是使用之后才出现的不良反应。

senses.meaning_zh: 禁忌证；提示某治疗或操作不宜采用的医学情况或理由
senses.meaning_en: a medical condition or factor that makes a treatment or procedure inadvisable
senses.english_definition: A contraindication is a medical condition or other factor that makes a particular treatment or procedure unsuitable because it could cause harm.
senses.collocation_en: an absolute contraindication; a relative contraindication
senses.collocation_zh: 绝对禁忌证；相对禁忌证
senses.sentence_en: The doctor checked for contraindications before prescribing the medicine.
senses.sentence_zh: 医生在开这种药之前检查了是否存在禁忌证。

etymology_story.zh: 该词属于拉丁语来源的医学词汇，由 contra-“反对、相反”与 indication“指示、指征”组合而成。它表达的是“提示不宜治疗的因素”，与提示某治疗适用的 indication 形成对应。
etymology_story.en: The word belongs to medical vocabulary built from Latin elements, combining contra-, against, with indication. It expresses a factor pointing against a treatment, corresponding to an indication that points toward its use.

morphology_enriched.zh: contra-（反对）+ indication（指征）→ contraindication（禁忌证）；也可联系 contraindicate（表明……不宜采用）的名词形式理解。词族：contraindicate、contraindicates（第三人称单数）、contraindicated（过去式、过去分词；作形容词表示“属禁忌的”）、contraindicating（现在分词）、contraindications（复数）。
morphology_enriched.en: Contra- meaning against + indication gives contraindication; it can also be understood as the noun corresponding to contraindicate. The family includes contraindicate, contraindicates, contraindicated, contraindicating, and the plural contraindications; contraindicated also functions adjectivally.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: reason against treatment（不宜治疗的理由）是通俗近义表达；bar to treatment（治疗的阻碍因素）通常暗示更强的排除作用；precaution（慎用事项）只是需要谨慎或采取防护措施，并不必然构成禁忌证。contraindication 是较精确的医学术语，绝对禁忌证与相对禁忌证的限制程度不同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Reason against treatment is a plain-language equivalent; bar to treatment usually suggests a stronger obstacle. Precaution means that care or protective measures are needed and is not necessarily a contraindication. Contraindication is the precise medical term, with absolute and relative forms expressing different degrees of restriction.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: indication 指向“适用”，contra- 把方向反过来：contraindication＝提示“不宜用”的因素。
mnemonic_anchor.en: An indication points toward using a treatment; contra- reverses the direction, pointing against its use.

pronunciation.note: 主重音在 ˈ 后的音节；按词内音节连贯朗读。

forms: 通常不可数
family: denitrify 使脱氮；denitrifying 进行反硝化作用的

morphology.text: de-（去除、逆转）+ nitrification（硝化作用）→ denitrification（反硝化作用）。

etymology.text: 19世纪英语科学术语，由 de-“去除、逆转”与 nitrification“硝化作用”构成；用“把硝酸盐中的氮带走”帮助记忆。

usage_note: 环境科学用语；生物反硝化常指微生物把硝酸盐等转为气态氮的过程。不要与生成硝酸盐的 nitrification 混淆。

senses.meaning_zh: 反硝化作用；将硝酸盐或亚硝酸盐还原为气态氮产物的过程
senses.meaning_en: the reduction of nitrate or nitrite to gaseous nitrogen compounds or nitrogen gas
senses.english_definition: Denitrification is a process in which nitrate or nitrite is converted into gaseous forms of nitrogen, often by bacteria.
senses.collocation_en: biological denitrification; the denitrification rate
senses.collocation_zh: 生物反硝化；反硝化速率
senses.sentence_en: Denitrification helps remove nitrogen from wastewater by converting nitrate into nitrogen gas.
senses.sentence_zh: 反硝化作用通过将硝酸盐转化为氮气，帮助去除废水中的氮。

etymology_story.zh: 这是19世纪形成的科学术语，由表示“去除、逆转”的 de- 与 nitrification“硝化作用”构成。在氮循环研究中，它用来描述硝酸盐中的氮转变为气态产物的过程，但并非硝化反应的简单倒放。
etymology_story.en: This nineteenth-century scientific term was formed from de-, expressing removal or reversal, and nitrification. In studies of the nitrogen cycle, it came to describe the conversion of nitrate nitrogen into gaseous products, although the process is not simply nitrification running backward.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可按 de-（去除、逆转）+ nitrification（硝化作用）分析，并与动词 denitrify（使反硝化；脱氮）对应，体现 -ify → -ification 的名词化变化。词族：denitrify、denitrifies（第三人称单数）、denitrified（过去式及过去分词）、denitrifying（现在分词；反硝化的）、denitrifier（反硝化微生物）、denitrification（反硝化作用）；相关词有 nitrify（使硝化）、nitrification（硝化作用）、nitrate（硝酸盐）和 nitrite（亚硝酸盐）。
morphology_enriched.en: The word can be analyzed as de-, removal or reversal, + nitrification, and corresponds to denitrify through the noun-forming change -ify → -ification. Its family includes denitrify, denitrifies, denitrified, denitrifying, denitrifier, and denitrification; related words include nitrify, nitrification, nitrate, and nitrite.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 该词没有完全等义的常用替代词：nitrogen removal（脱氮）范围更广，还包括其他除氮过程；nitrate reduction（硝酸盐还原）也更广，因为其产物不一定是气态氮。denitrification 特指生成气态氮产物的这一过程。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact everyday synonym: nitrogen removal is broader and includes other processes, while nitrate reduction is also broader because its products need not be gaseous. Denitrification specifically involves the formation of gaseous nitrogen products.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: de- 提示“去除”：硝酸盐中的氮变成气体离开，记住“反硝化、脱氮”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Let de- suggest removal: nitrogen in nitrate becomes gas and leaves, anchoring the idea of denitrification.

senses.meaning_zh: 笨学生；学习迟钝的人；笨人，含贬义
senses.meaning_en: a person considered stupid or slow at learning
senses.english_definition: If someone calls a person a dunce, they mean that the person is stupid or finds it difficult to learn things.
senses.collocation_en: a dunce at mathematics; a dunce's cap
senses.collocation_zh: 数学不开窍的人；旧时惩罚笨学生戴的尖帽
senses.sentence_en: I felt like a dunce when I could not answer such a simple question.
senses.sentence_zh: 连这么简单的问题都答不上来，我觉得自己像个笨蛋。

etymology_story.zh: 源自中世纪学者 John Duns Scotus 名字中的 Duns，最初与其学说的追随者有关。16世纪，其追随者被论敌讥讽为顽固守旧、缺乏学识，名称便逐渐演变为“笨人、笨学生”的贬称。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Duns in the name of the medieval scholar John Duns Scotus and was originally associated with his followers. In the sixteenth century, opponents mocked those followers as stubbornly old-fashioned and unlearned, and the name developed into an insult for a stupid person or slow learner.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 dunce 是不可再作实用拆分的独立词干；复数 dunces（笨人们）。较少见的派生词包括 duncish（愚笨的，dunce 去掉末尾 -e 再加 -ish）、duncishly（愚笨地）、duncishness（愚笨）和 duncery（愚笨行为）；复合表达 dunce's cap 指“惩罚笨学生戴的尖帽”。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, dunce is an independent stem without a useful smaller morphological breakdown; its plural is dunces. Less common derivatives include duncish, formed by dropping the final -e before -ish, duncishly, duncishness, and duncery; the compound expression dunce's cap names the pointed cap formerly used to punish pupils.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: fool（傻瓜）常指判断失当或行为愚蠢的人；idiot（白痴、笨蛋）通常是更直接、更强烈的侮辱；dimwit（笨蛋）较口语化，强调脑子不灵。dunce 尤其容易让人联想到学习迟钝或功课差。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Fool often describes someone who shows poor judgment; idiot is usually a more direct and stronger insult; dimwit is informal and emphasizes limited intelligence. Dunce particularly suggests difficulty learning or doing schoolwork.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住“学者之名变成课堂骂名”：Duns → dunce，联想戴尖帽的笨学生。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A scholar's name became a classroom insult: Duns → dunce. Picture the slow pupil wearing a pointed cap.

pronunciation.note: 主重音在 ˈ 后的音节；按词内音节连贯朗读。

etymology_story.zh: 源自中古英语 filchen，意为“偷窃”，更早的来源尚不确定。现代用法尤其突出偷偷顺走小东西，语气有时带有轻微的幽默或责备。
etymology_story.en: Filch comes from Middle English filchen, meaning 'to steal'; its earlier origin is uncertain. Modern usage particularly suggests secretly taking small things, sometimes with a mildly humorous or disapproving tone.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：filch 是不可再作常规拆分的词根。屈折形式：filches、filched、filching；派生词：filch + -er → filcher（小偷；偷偷拿东西的人），复数 filchers。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: filch is a simple lexical base without a regular internal breakdown. Inflected forms are filches, filched, and filching; filch + -er produces filcher, meaning someone who steals, with the plural filchers.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: steal（偷窃）是最中性的总称；pilfer（小偷小摸）常指反复偷取少量财物，尤其是工作场所的东西；swipe（顺走）较口语化。filch 尤其强调悄悄拿走小物品。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Steal is the neutral general term; pilfer often suggests repeatedly stealing small amounts, especially from a workplace; swipe is informal. Filch particularly emphasizes secretly taking a small item.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 画面锚点：手指悄悄一夹，小东西就被顺走——filch。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a hand quietly pinching a small object and slipping it away: filch.

etymology_story.zh: 借自法语 glycogène，该名称由生理学家克洛德·贝尔纳创用，结合了表示“甜；糖”的希腊语成分和表示“产生”的成分。字面意思是“产生糖的物质”，反映了糖原能够分解生成葡萄糖的性质。
etymology_story.en: Glycogen was borrowed from French glycogène, a name introduced by the physiologist Claude Bernard using Greek elements meaning 'sweet or sugar' and 'producing.' Its literal sense, 'sugar-producing substance,' reflects its ability to yield glucose when broken down.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：glyco-（糖）+ -gen（产生某物的物质）→ glycogen。主要词族及相关构词：glycogenic（与糖原有关的；生成糖原的）、glycogenesis（糖原合成）、glycogenolysis（糖原分解）、glycogenolytic（糖原分解的）、glycogenosis（糖原贮积病；复数 glycogenoses）；常见复合词 glycogen synthase（糖原合酶）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: glyco- ('sugar') + -gen ('a substance that produces something') → glycogen. Principal family members and related formations include glycogenic ('relating to or producing glycogen'), glycogenesis ('glycogen formation'), glycogenolysis ('glycogen breakdown'), glycogenolytic ('relating to glycogen breakdown'), and glycogenosis ('a glycogen storage disorder'; plural glycogenoses); a common compound is glycogen synthase.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: animal starch（动物淀粉）是糖原的历史性别称。starch（淀粉）和 glucose（葡萄糖）是相关对比词：淀粉是植物主要的葡萄糖储存物质，葡萄糖则是构成糖原的单糖，二者均不能直接替代 glycogen。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Animal starch is a historical alternative name for glycogen. Starch and glucose are related comparison terms: starch is the principal glucose-storage substance in plants, while glucose is the simple sugar from which glycogen is built; neither is interchangeable with glycogen.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: glyco-＝糖，-gen＝产生：需要能量时，糖原仓库释放葡萄糖。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Glyco- means sugar and -gen suggests producing: glycogen is a stored reserve that yields glucose.

etymology_story.zh: 由 herring（鲱鱼）和 bone（骨头）组成，以鲱鱼脊骨两侧斜列细骨的形状命名。这个名称用于针法及织物等纹样，后来也扩展到铺装图案和留下类似足迹的滑雪登坡动作。
etymology_story.en: Herringbone combines herring and bone, referring to the slanting bones on either side of a herring's backbone. The name was applied to stitches and textile patterns and later extended to paving arrangements and a skiing movement that leaves similarly shaped tracks.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：herring（鲱鱼）+ bone（骨头）→ herringbone，属于复合词；可用作名词、形容词和动词。词形包括 herringbones（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、herringboned（过去式、过去分词，也可表示“制成人字纹的”）、herringboning（现在分词或表示该动作的名词）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: herring + bone → herringbone, a compound used as a noun, adjective, and verb. Forms include herringbones (plural noun or third-person singular verb), herringboned (past tense, past participle, and sometimes an adjective meaning 'made in a herringbone pattern'), and herringboning (present participle or an action noun).

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: chevron（V形纹）突出连续或单独的V形；zigzag（之字形）泛指来回折转的线条；fishbone（鱼骨形）强调与鱼骨的外观相似。herringbone 更具体地指短线或长方形单元交替斜排的结构，铺装中的 chevron 与 herringbone 还可指不同的拼接方式。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Chevron emphasizes individual or repeated V shapes; zigzag broadly describes a line that repeatedly changes direction; fishbone emphasizes resemblance to a fish skeleton. Herringbone more specifically describes alternating diagonal strokes or rectangular units, and in flooring, chevron and herringbone can denote different joint arrangements.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a herring's backbone with slanting bones on each side: the same shape links fabric, flooring, and uphill skiing.

etymology_story.zh: 源自新拉丁语 japonica，即 japonicus（日本的）的阴性形式，常出现在植物学名称中。英语从这类学名中借出它作为山茶、木瓜属观赏灌木等植物的俗名，并在稻作分类中用于指粳稻类群。
etymology_story.en: Japonica comes from New Latin japonica, the feminine form of japonicus, meaning 'Japanese,' widely used in botanical names. English adopted it from such names for plants including camellias and flowering quinces, and it also identifies the japonica group of cultivated rice.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中作为完整借词使用；历史结构为 Japon-（日本）+ -ic-（形容词成分）+ -a（拉丁语阴性词尾）。指单株观赏植物时可数，复数 japonicas；指稻米或稻作类群时通常不可数。相关地名词族有 Japan（日本）、Japanese（日本的；日本人；日语）；japonicus、japonica、japonicum 是新拉丁语形容词的不同性别形式。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, japonica functions as a whole borrowed word; its historical structure is Japon- ('Japan') + -ic- (an adjectival element) + -a (a Latin feminine ending). For individual ornamental plants it is countable, with the plural japonicas; for rice or the rice group it is generally uncountable. Related geographical vocabulary includes Japan and Japanese; japonicus, japonica, and japonicum are gender forms of the New Latin adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: flowering quince（木瓜属观赏灌木；贴梗海棠等）对应其常见英式植物义；Japanese camellia（日本山茶）对应山茶义；japonica rice（粳稻；粳米）明确限定稻作义。这三个名称分别对应不同所指，不能跨义项互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Flowering quince corresponds to the common British garden-plant sense; Japanese camellia corresponds to the camellia sense; japonica rice explicitly identifies the rice sense. These names refer to different things and are interchangeable with japonica only within the relevant sense.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: japon- 联想 Japan：原意“日本的”，具体是哪种花或哪类稻，要看植物语境。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect japon- with Japan: the original idea is 'Japanese,' while the botanical context identifies the plant or rice group.

senses.pos: n. 名词（不可数，正式用语）

etymology_story.zh: 经中古法语 obeissance（服从）进入英语，最终源于拉丁语 oboedire（听从；服从），其构词与“听”有关。英语中的含义从服从、恭顺延伸到以鞠躬或屈身表达这种态度的具体动作。
etymology_story.en: Obeisance entered English through Middle French obeissance, meaning 'obedience,' ultimately from Latin oboedire, 'to listen to or obey.' In English, the meaning extended from obedience and submission to the bodily gestures, such as bowing, that express them.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：整体借词，可结合词族 obeisant（恭顺的）和名词后缀 -ance 理解其结构；obeisance 与 obeisant 对应时，词尾表现为 -ance／-ant 的替换。直接词族有 obeisant、obeisantly（恭顺地）以及复数 obeisances；历史相关词族有 obey（服从）、obedience（服从）、obedient（顺从的）、obediently（顺从地）、disobey（违抗）、disobedience（不服从）和 disobedient（不顺从的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: a borrowed word whose form can be understood alongside obeisant ('submissively respectful') and the noun suffix -ance; the corresponding endings are -ance in obeisance and -ant in obeisant. Its direct family includes obeisant, obeisantly, and the plural obeisances; historically related words include obey, obedience, obedient, obediently, disobey, disobedience, and disobedient.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: bow（鞠躬）主要描述身体动作；homage（崇敬；致敬）强调对卓越、地位或成就的敬意；deference（尊重；顺从）强调尊重他人的判断或权威。obeisance 可兼指行礼动作与恭顺态度，涉及权势时有时暗含过度屈从。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Bow primarily names a physical movement; homage emphasizes admiration or respect for distinction, status, or achievement; deference emphasizes respect for another person's judgment or authority. Obeisance can name both a gesture and an attitude of submission, sometimes suggesting excessive submission to power.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“听从”到“低头”：先服从权威，再用鞠躬把恭顺表现出来。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Move from 'listening and obeying' to 'bowing': submission becomes a visible gesture.

etymology_story.zh: 英语通过法语 polychrome 借入此词，最终源于希腊语 polykhrōmos，意为“多色的”，由表示“多”的 poly- 和表示“颜色”的 khrōma 构成。英语随后也用它指多色艺术品，以及给物体施以多色彩绘的行为。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed the word through French polychrome, ultimately from Greek polykhrōmos, meaning “many-colored,” formed from poly- meaning “many” and khrōma meaning “color.” English also developed noun and verb uses for a multicolored artwork and the act of decorating something in several colors.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：poly-（多）+ -chrome（颜色）；这里的 -chrome 是构词成分，不是指铬或镀铬的日常名词 chrome。词族包括 polychromes（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、polychromed（过去式、过去分词）、polychroming（现在分词）、polychromy（多色装饰或彩绘艺术）、polychromic／polychromatic（多色的）和 polychromatically（以多色方式）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: poly- (“many”) + -chrome (“color”); -chrome here is a word-forming element, rather than the everyday noun chrome referring to chromium or chromium plating. The family includes polychromes, polychromed, polychroming, polychromy (“multicolored decoration or its practice”), polychromic and polychromatic (“many-colored”), and polychromatically (“in a many-colored manner”).

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: multicolored（多色的）最通用；polychromatic（多色的）也用于光学等技术语境；variegated（杂色的、斑驳的）强调颜色呈条纹、斑块等变化。polychrome 尤常用于艺术、建筑和彩绘装饰。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Multicolored is the broad everyday term; polychromatic also appears in technical contexts such as optics; variegated emphasizes variation in patches, streaks, or other patterns. Polychrome is especially associated with art, architecture, and painted decoration.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: poly- 是“多”，-chrome 是“颜色”：给一尊雕像涂上多种颜色。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Poly- means “many” and -chrome means “color”: picture a statue painted in several colors.

senses.meaning_zh: 残留物；处理后剩余的物质，尤用于科技语境
senses.meaning_en: material remaining after a process, especially in scientific or technical contexts
senses.english_definition: A residuum is the material that remains after the rest has been removed or changed by a process.
senses.collocation_en: oily residuum; distillation residuum
senses.collocation_zh: 油性残留物；蒸馏残余物

senses.meaning_zh: 剩余部分；残存因素，属正式用语
senses.meaning_en: a remaining portion or surviving element, in formal usage
senses.english_definition: A residuum of something is the small part of it that remains after most of it has disappeared or been dealt with.

etymology_story.zh: 英语在17世纪借入拉丁语 residuum，原意为“剩下的东西”，是 residuus（剩余的）的中性形式。它最终源于 residēre（留下、停留），由 re-（往回、留在后面）和 sedēre（坐）构成，核心意象是“其余都走了，它还留着”。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed Latin residuum in the seventeenth century, meaning “what is left,” the neuter form of residuus (“remaining”). It ultimately comes from residēre (“remain or stay behind”), formed from re- (“back”) and sedēre (“sit”), suggesting something that stays after the rest has gone.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中宜将 residuum 作为完整的借入词识记；residu- + -um 可说明其拉丁语词干与词尾，但不是能自由套用的英语构词公式。复数为 residua，也可用 residuums；同源词族包括 residue（残留物）、residual（残余的；残余量）、residually（残余地）、residuary（剩余财产的）和 residuals（残余量；某些合同中的后续使用报酬）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, residuum is best treated as a complete borrowed word; residu- + -um identifies its Latin stem and ending, rather than a productive English formation. Its plurals are residua and residuums; related words include residue, residual (“remaining,” or a remaining quantity), residually, residuary (“relating to a remaining estate”), and residuals (“remaining quantities,” or certain payments for subsequent use).

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: residue（残留物）适用最广，尤其指处理后留下的物质；remainder（剩余部分）可指数量、物品或抽象内容；remnant（残余、遗存）强调原来整体中幸存的一小部分。residuum 比这些词更正式，也更有科技或学术色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Residue is the broadest choice for material left after a process; remainder can refer to quantities, objects, or abstract content; remnant emphasizes a small surviving part of a former whole. Residuum is more formal and often more technical or scholarly.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“留下来”的核心：处理结束，容器底部还剩着的就是 residuum。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor it to “staying behind”: after processing ends, the material still in the container is the residuum.

etymology_story.zh: accursed 来自中古英语 acursen（诅咒）的过去分词形式，其中 a- 是旧时的加强前缀，词干与 curse（诅咒）相同。它最初表示“受到诅咒的”，后来也用于表达说话者的强烈厌恶或恼怒。
etymology_story.en: Accursed developed from the past participle of Middle English acursen (“to curse”), containing an old intensive prefix a- and the same stem as curse. Its literal meaning “under a curse” later extended to things that provoke strong hatred or irritation.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词关系为 accurse（诅咒，现已罕用）+ -ed → accursed（形容词）；现代英语通常将 accursed 作为固定形容词学习。直接派生词有 accursedly（可恶地；受诅咒般地）和 accursedness（受诅咒的状态；可恶）；相关词族有 curse（诅咒）、cursed（被诅咒的；可恶的）、cursing（咒骂）和 curselike（像诅咒一样的）。
morphology_enriched.en: The formation is accurse (“to curse,” now rare) + -ed → accursed; modern learners usually encounter accursed as an established adjective. Direct derivatives include accursedly and accursedness; the related family includes curse, cursed, cursing, and curselike.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cursed（被诅咒的；可恶的）与其最接近，使用范围更广；damned（该死的；受永罚的）常作强烈的愤怒表达，也有宗教含义；execrable（极其恶劣的）强调质量或行为令人厌恶。accursed 常带文学、宗教或戏剧化语气。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cursed is the closest equivalent and has wider use; damned often expresses strong anger and can also refer to religious condemnation; execrable emphasizes extremely bad quality or hateful behavior. Accursed often sounds literary, religious, or dramatic.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 看到 curse 就想到“诅咒”：既可真的“受诅咒”，也可气得骂一句“该死的”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Spot curse: something may literally be under a curse, or annoy you enough to call it “accursed.”

etymology_story.zh: caisson 借自法语，原指“大箱子”，通常追溯至意大利语 cassone，即 cassa（箱子）的指大形式，最终与拉丁语 capsa（箱子）有关。箱形容器这一基本意象发展出了弹药箱、弹药车、水下施工沉箱和浮箱闸门等含义。
etymology_story.en: Caisson was borrowed from French, where it meant a large box, generally traced through Italian cassone, an augmentative of cassa (“box”), ultimately related to Latin capsa (“box”). This boxlike-container image developed into senses involving ammunition chests and wagons, underwater construction chambers, and floating dock gates.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 caisson 是完整借入的单纯词，不宜拆成英语词根与后缀；复数为 caissons。它没有常用的丰富派生词族；罕见的 caissoned 表示“装有沉箱或由沉箱支承的”，常见复合术语有 caisson foundation（沉箱基础）、caisson disease（沉箱病，即减压病）和 caisson gate（浮箱闸门）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, caisson is an unanalyzed loanword, rather than an English root-plus-suffix formation; its plural is caissons. It has no extensive everyday derivative family; the rare adjective caissoned means “provided with or supported by caissons,” while established compounds include caisson foundation, caisson disease (“decompression sickness”), and caisson gate.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cofferdam（围堰）通常围起并抽干一片施工区域；caisson（沉箱）本身是放入或下沉到施工位置的箱形结构，两者不能简单互换。ammunition wagon（弹药车）和 funeral carriage（灵柩车）分别对应其军事运输和葬仪含义，不能替代工程义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A cofferdam generally encloses an area that is drained for construction, whereas a caisson is itself a boxlike structure placed or sunk at the work site, so the terms are not interchangeable. Ammunition wagon and funeral carriage correspond to its military transport and funeral senses, rather than its engineering sense.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“大箱子”：沉到水下是沉箱，装炮弹是弹药车，封住船坞是浮箱闸门。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a large box: sink it for construction, load it with ammunition, or float it into a dock entrance.

etymology_story.zh: gastroenteritis 是19世纪形成的医学术语，使用希腊语来源的 gastr-（胃）、enter-（肠）和表示炎症的 -itis 构成。这个名称按受累器官及病变性质命名，并不限定为某一种病原体引起的疾病。
etymology_story.en: Gastroenteritis is a nineteenth-century medical formation using Greek-derived gastr- (“stomach”), enter- (“intestine”), and -itis (“inflammation”). The name identifies the affected organs and the inflammatory condition, rather than specifying a particular infectious cause.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：gastr/o（胃，o 为连接元音）+ enter（肠）+ -itis（炎症）→ gastroenteritis。相关医学词族包括 gastroenteritic（胃肠炎的）、gastritis（胃炎）、enteritis（肠炎）、gastric（胃的）、enteric（肠的）、gastroenterology（胃肠病学）、gastroenterologist（胃肠科医生）和 gastroenterological（胃肠病学的）；这些词共享构词成分，并非全由 gastroenteritis 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: gastr/o (“stomach,” with linking vowel o) + enter (“intestine”) + -itis (“inflammation”) → gastroenteritis. The related medical family includes gastroenteritic, gastritis, enteritis, gastric, enteric, gastroenterology, gastroenterologist, and gastroenterological; these share combining elements rather than all deriving directly from gastroenteritis.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: stomach bug（肠胃感染）是较宽泛的非正式说法；stomach flu（肠胃型流感）是俗称，但通常并非流感病毒所致；enteritis（肠炎）只指肠道炎症。gastroenteritis 是明确包含胃和肠道的医学名称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Stomach bug is a broader informal expression for a gastrointestinal infection; stomach flu is a colloquial label, although the illness is usually unrelated to influenza; enteritis refers specifically to intestinal inflammation. Gastroenteritis is the medical term involving both the stomach and intestines.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: gastro＝胃，enter＝肠，itis＝炎：按顺序读就是“胃—肠—炎”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Gastro = stomach, enter = intestine, itis = inflammation: read the word as “stomach–intestine–inflammation.”

etymology_story.en: Longshore developed as a shortened form of alongshore, meaning 'along the shore.' It retained the idea of extending or moving along a coastline and became established in coastal geography and waterfront work.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可将 longshore 作为整体词干识记；历史形成方式为 alongshore → longshore，不能按 long“长的”＋ shore“海岸”解释其来源。相关形式：alongshore（沿岸）；longshoreman（码头装卸工），复数 longshoremen；longshorewoman（女性码头装卸工），复数 longshorewomen；longshore worker（码头装卸工）。
morphology_enriched.en: Treat longshore as a whole stem in modern English; historically, alongshore became longshore through loss of the initial a-, rather than through a combination of long and shore. Related forms include alongshore, longshoreman (plural longshoremen), longshorewoman (plural longshorewomen), and the compound longshore worker.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: alongshore 同样表示“沿岸”，方向含义最接近；coastal 表示“海岸的”，强调位置或关联，不一定表示平行于海岸的运动；shore-parallel 明确表示“与岸线平行的”，常见于技术描述。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Alongshore is the closest equivalent and shares the directional meaning; coastal describes a location or connection with the coast without necessarily implying movement along it; shore-parallel explicitly describes an orientation parallel to the shoreline, especially in technical writing.

senses.sentence_zh: 这块猪肉用大蒜和酸橙汁调成的莫霍酱腌制过。

etymology_story.zh: 表示魔力的 mojo 于20世纪初见于非裔美国英语，其更早来源不确定，通常被认为与非洲语言有关，后来引申为个人魅力、自信和良好状态。表示调味酱的 mojo 则是另一个来源不同的同形词，借自西班牙语 mojo。
etymology_story.en: The magical sense of mojo appeared in African American English in the early twentieth century; its earlier origin is uncertain but is generally associated with African languages, and it later developed meanings involving charm, confidence, and effectiveness. The sauce sense is a separate word borrowed from Spanish mojo.

morphology_enriched.zh: 两种来源的 mojo 在现代英语中都作为完整词干使用，没有可分析的英语词根和词缀。表示魅力或魔力时通常不可数；指具体护符或不同种类的酱时可数，复数为 mojos；mojo bag、mojo hand、mojo sauce 是复合表达；mojoless 是偶见的非正式派生词，不能视为常用核心词族成员。
morphology_enriched.en: Both historically distinct words are whole stems in modern English, without an internal English root-and-affix breakdown. Mojo is usually uncountable when referring to charm or magical power; individual charms or varieties of sauce can take the plural mojos. Mojo bag, mojo hand, and mojo sauce are compound expressions; mojoless is an occasional informal derivative rather than an established core family member.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: charisma 强调吸引并影响他人的魅力；confidence 强调对自己能力的信心；magic 强调神奇力量或令人惊叹的效果。mojo 在非正式表达中可同时包含魅力、自信和表现出色的状态；这些近义词不适用于调味酱义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Charisma emphasizes the ability to attract and influence others; confidence emphasizes belief in your own ability; magic emphasizes supernatural power or a remarkable effect. Informal mojo can combine charm, confidence, and effective performance; these equivalents do not apply to the sauce sense.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“护符的魔力”联想到“人的魅力”：找回 mojo，就是找回那股劲。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Move from a charm's magical power to a person's personal power: getting your mojo back means recovering your spark.

etymology_story.zh: nosh 借自意第绪语 nashn，意为“吃零食、吃一点”，与德语 naschen“吃零嘴”同源。它在英语中成为非正式动词，也用作表示食物或便餐的名词。
etymology_story.en: Nosh was borrowed from Yiddish nashn, meaning 'to snack or nibble,' a word related to German naschen. In English it became an informal verb and also a noun referring to food or a casual meal.

morphology_enriched.zh: nosh 是完整词干；名词和动词形式相同，可视为零派生关系。动词变化为 noshes、noshed、noshing；nosh ＋ -er → nosher（爱吃零食的人）；名词表示一次便餐时可用复数 noshes，泛指食物时通常不可数。
morphology_enriched.en: Nosh is a whole stem, and its identical noun and verb forms illustrate conversion without an added suffix. Verb forms are noshes, noshed, and noshing; nosh + -er forms nosher, someone who snacks. The noun can have the plural noshes when referring to individual meals, but is usually uncountable when it means food generally.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: snack 强调在正餐之外吃少量食物；nibble 强调一小口一小口地吃；munch 强调咀嚼，常带有吃得津津有味的意味。nosh 语气更口语化，侧重轻松随意地吃点东西。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Snack emphasizes eating a small amount between meals; nibble emphasizes taking small bites; munch emphasizes chewing, often with an impression of enjoyment. Nosh is particularly informal and suggests casual eating.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 正餐还没到，先随手吃几口：nosh。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Dinner can wait; have a few casual bites: nosh.

senses.english_definition: A palmtop computer is small enough to be held in the palm of your hand.
senses.collocation_en: a palmtop computer; a palmtop PC

etymology_story.zh: palmtop 于20世纪80年代作为电脑名称出现，由 palm“手掌”和 top 组合而成，命名方式仿照 desktop、laptop 等词。它以设备能放在手掌上的特点命名，尤其用于智能手机普及前的一类小型电脑。
etymology_story.en: Palmtop emerged as a computer term in the 1980s, combining palm with top on the model of desktop and laptop. It names the device by its ability to fit in the hand and is especially associated with small computers used before smartphones became widespread.

morphology_enriched.zh: palm（手掌）＋ top（仿 desktop、laptop 中的命名成分）→ palmtop，是复合词；名词复数为 palmtops，也可作形容词置于 computer 等名词前。无常用的进一步派生词；desktop、laptop 是构词模式相近的词，不是 palmtop 的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Palm + top, with top following the naming pattern of desktop and laptop, forms the compound palmtop. Its noun plural is palmtops, and it also functions adjectivally before nouns such as computer. There are no common further derivatives; desktop and laptop share its naming pattern but are not derived from palmtop.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: handheld computer 范围更广，泛指能手持使用的电脑；PDA 强调日程、联系人等个人信息管理功能，与部分早期掌上电脑重合；pocket computer 强调体积小到可以放进口袋。palmtop 直接突出能托在掌心的尺寸。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Handheld computer is a broader term for a computer operated in the hand; PDA emphasizes personal information functions such as calendars and contacts and overlaps with some early palmtops; pocket computer emphasizes fitting into a pocket. Palmtop directly highlights palm-sized dimensions.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: desktop 放桌上，laptop 放腿上，palmtop 托掌上。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A desktop sits on a desk, a laptop on your lap, and a palmtop in your palm.

etymology.text: 经中古英语 pultes 和中世纪拉丁语，最终来自拉丁语 puls“稠粥”；因为外敷物呈软糊状，可以用“像粥一样的药糊”记忆。

usage_note: 指敷在身体表面的软糊状材料，不是口服药。多见于历史、文学或传统护理描述。

senses.meaning_zh: 糊状外敷剂；敷贴药糊

etymology_story.zh: 该词经中古英语及法语形式传入，最终源自拉丁语 puls（属格 pultis），意为“稠粥”。名称从食物般的软糊状物发展为敷在身体上的药糊，随后又用作表示“敷药糊”的动词。
etymology_story.en: The word came through Middle English and French forms ultimately from Latin puls, genitive pultis, meaning thick porridge. Its meaning developed from a soft, porridge-like preparation to a medicinal dressing, and the noun later became a verb meaning to apply such a dressing.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中以 poultice 为不可再作常用词缀分析的词基；名词直接转为动词，无须添加词缀。常用词形：poultices（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、poulticed（过去式及过去分词）、poulticing（现在分词或动名词，去掉末尾 -e 再加 -ing）；没有常用的进一步派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, poultice is a base with no productive internal affix division; the noun becomes a verb by conversion. Regular forms are poultices, poulticed, and poulticing, with final -e dropped before -ing; there are no widely used further derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: compress（敷布）侧重湿润的布垫，本身不一定含药糊；plaster（药膏贴）通常指涂有药物的贴敷材料；cataplasm（泥罨剂、糊状外敷剂）与 poultice 意义接近，但更偏专业或旧式用语。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A compress is a moist cloth or pad and need not contain a paste; a plaster is usually a dressing carrying a medicinal substance; cataplasm is a close synonym of poultice but is more technical or old-fashioned.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 词源核心是“稠粥”：像粥一样的药糊，敷在身体上。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture the original thick porridge becoming a medicinal paste spread on the body.

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆；sangria + -style → sangria-style（桑格利亚风味的）。

etymology.text: 从西班牙语 sangría 借入英语，词形与 sangre“血”有关，名称来自传统红葡萄酒饮料的红色。

senses.meaning_zh: 桑格利亚酒；通常用葡萄酒、水果和其他饮料调制的酒饮
senses.meaning_en: A drink made with wine, fruit, and other ingredients.
senses.english_definition: Sangria is an alcoholic drink made by mixing wine, usually red wine, with pieces of fruit and other drinks.
senses.collocation_en: a pitcher of sangria; red wine sangria
senses.collocation_zh: 一壶桑格利亚酒；红葡萄酒桑格利亚

etymology_story.zh: 该词借自西班牙语 sangría，与 sangre“血”同源，名称呼应传统红葡萄酒调饮的血红色。英语保留了它作为这种水果葡萄酒饮料名称的用法。
etymology_story.en: The word was borrowed from Spanish sangría, related to sangre, meaning blood, in reference to the blood-red colour of the traditional red-wine drink. English retained it as the name of this fruit-and-wine mixture.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 sangria 是整体借入的单一词基，不能分析为常用英语词根与后缀。通常作不可数名词；指多份或多种桑格利亚酒时可用 sangrias；sangria-style（桑格利亚风格的）是临时构成的复合表达，不是独立的常用派生词，sangria 作名词前置修饰语时也不因此成为独立形容词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, sangria is a single borrowed base rather than an English root-plus-suffix formation. It is usually uncountable, but sangrias can refer to servings or varieties; sangria-style is a freely formed compound expression, not an established derivative, and attributive use of sangria does not establish a separate adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: punch（潘趣酒、混合饮料）是更宽泛的类别，可含酒也可不含酒；wine cup（水果葡萄酒调饮）是较旧式的近似说法；mulled wine（香料热葡萄酒）通常加香料并加热，不能与一般的 sangria 互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Punch is a broader category of mixed drinks and may be alcoholic or non-alcoholic; wine cup is a somewhat old-fashioned term for a similar wine-based mixture; mulled wine is normally spiced and heated, so it is not interchangeable with sangria.

senses.meaning_en: Quiet, inactive, and sleepy in atmosphere.
senses.english_definition: A somnolent place or atmosphere is so quiet and inactive that it seems almost asleep.

etymology_story.zh: 该词来自法语 somnolent 或其拉丁语来源 somnolentus“困倦的”，最终以 somnus“睡眠”为基础。英语保留了表示困倦的本义，并将其引申用于仿佛沉睡、缺乏活动的地方或氛围。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from French somnolent or its Latin source somnolentus, meaning sleepy, ultimately based on somnus, sleep. English retained the literal meaning and extended it to places or atmospheres that seem asleep or inactive.

morphology_enriched.zh: 这是整体借入的学术词；可用 somn-（睡眠）识别词根，但不宜把 -olent 当作现代英语中可自由使用的后缀。核心词族：somnolence（困倦、嗜睡）、somnolency（较少见的同义名词）、somnolently（困倦地）；同根相关词有 somnambulism（梦游）和 insomnia（失眠），它们并非由 somnolent 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: This is a learned borrowing: somn- identifies the sleep root, but -olent should not be treated as a freely productive modern English suffix. Its core family includes somnolence, the less common noun somnolency, and somnolently; somnambulism and insomnia share the sleep root but are not direct derivatives of somnolent.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sleepy（困的）最日常，可表示想睡或需要睡；drowsy（昏昏欲睡的）强调清醒程度下降；lethargic（无精打采的）强调精力不足，不一定有睡意。somnolent 较正式，常见于文学或医学语境。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sleepy is the everyday word for wanting or needing sleep; drowsy emphasizes reduced alertness; lethargic emphasizes lack of energy without necessarily implying sleepiness. Somnolent is more formal and often appears in literary or medical contexts.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: somn-＝睡眠：人带着睡意，地方像在沉睡。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Somn- means sleep: a person feels asleep, and a place seems asleep.

senses.pos: v. 不及物动词（植物学或较少见用法）
senses.meaning_zh: 生长；进行植物性生长
senses.meaning_en: To grow or develop as a plant.
senses.english_definition: When a plant vegetates, it grows and carries on its basic life processes.

etymology_story.zh: 该词来自拉丁语 vegetare“使有活力、使生长”，与 vegetus“有生气的”有关。英语早期用它表示植物般地生长，后来引申为只维持基本生活、缺乏思想或活动，形成今天常见的贬义。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin vegetare, meaning to enliven or cause to grow, related to vegetus, lively. Early English used it for plant-like growth; it later acquired the common disapproving sense of merely existing without much thought or activity.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可分析为 veget-（与植物生长、生命力有关的词干）＋-ate（动词词尾），但它本身是拉丁语来源的借词。屈折形式：vegetates、vegetated、vegetating；核心相关词族：vegetation（植被；植物生长）、vegetative（植物生长的；营养生长的）、vegetatively（以营养生长方式）、vegetational（植被的）、vegetatively derived 的常用表达 vegetative propagation（营养繁殖）。vegetable（蔬菜）和 vegetarian（素食者；素食的）属于相关词族，并非简单由现代动词 vegetate 逐一派生。
morphology_enriched.en: It can be analysed as veget-, a stem associated with plant growth and vitality, plus the verb ending -ate, although the word itself is a Latin-based borrowing. Inflected forms are vegetates, vegetated, and vegetating; the core related family includes vegetation, vegetative, vegetatively, and vegetational, with vegetative propagation as an established expression. Vegetable and vegetarian belong to the related family rather than being straightforward successive derivatives of the modern verb vegetate.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: idle（闲着、混日子）强调不工作或不做有用的事；laze（懒散度日）通常带有享受放松的意味；stagnate（停滞不前）强调长期没有进步。vegetate 尤其突出思想和活动都很少的被动状态。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Idle emphasizes doing no work or nothing useful; laze often suggests enjoying relaxed inactivity; stagnate emphasizes a prolonged lack of progress. Vegetate particularly suggests passive existence with little mental or physical activity.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“像植物一样生长”联想到“像盆栽一样待着”：活着，却很少行动或动脑。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Move from growing like a plant to sitting like a houseplant: alive, but doing and thinking very little.

etymology_story.en: The word entered English through Anglo-French and is connected with verge, a ceremonial staff, ultimately from Latin virga, a rod or staff. It originally emphasized the staff-bearing ceremonial role and later also described an official assisting with services and practical church duties.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可用 verge（仪式用杖）＋-er（从事某项职责的人）理解其构词关系；从现代拼写看，去掉 verge 末尾的 -e，再加 -er。词形及派生：vergers（复数）、vergership（司事职务或任期）；verge 的“边缘”义不能直接解释 verger 的现代意义。
morphology_enriched.en: The formation can be understood through verge, a ceremonial staff, plus the person suffix -er; in modern spelling terms, drop the final -e of verge before adding -er. Forms and derivatives include vergers and vergership, the office or tenure of a verger; the edge sense of verge does not directly explain the modern meaning of verger.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sexton（教堂管理员）通常侧重建筑、场地及墓地等事务；sacristan（圣器室管理员）主要负责圣器、祭服及礼拜用品；usher（引座员）侧重迎接和安排座位。verger 通常兼有礼拜组织、仪式引导及实际事务职责，具体分工因教堂而异。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A sexton usually focuses on church property, grounds, and sometimes burial duties; a sacristan looks after sacred vessels, vestments, and worship supplies; an usher welcomes people and helps seat them. A verger typically combines service organization, ceremonial guidance, and practical duties, with responsibilities varying between churches.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect verge, the ceremonial staff, with the church official who carries it and guides the service.

usage_note: 可用于组织缺氧或环境缺氧；anoxic 通常比 hypoxic 更强调没有氧或氧极其不足。

etymology_story.zh: anoxic 是近现代科学英语中与 anoxia“组织无氧、缺氧”对应的形容词，包含希腊语来源的 an-“无”、oxygen“氧”的词干成分及形容词后缀 -ic。它既用于描述组织的氧气供应缺失，也用于描述水体、沉积物等环境中的无氧状态。
etymology_story.en: Anoxic developed in modern scientific English as the adjective corresponding to anoxia, combining Greek-derived an- “without,” a stem element from oxygen, and the adjective suffix -ic. Its uses cover both oxygen deprivation in tissues and oxygen-free conditions in environments such as water and sediments.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词：an-（无）+ ox-（来自 oxygen，氧）+ -ic（形容词后缀）；也可通过 anoxia → anoxic 的名形对应记忆。词族：anoxia（名词，无氧或组织缺氧）、anoxic（形容词）；anoxically（副词，在无氧条件下，少见）。相关对照词：hypoxia（低氧）、hypoxic（低氧的），并非 anoxic 的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: an- “without” + ox- from oxygen + adjectival -ic; the noun–adjective pairing anoxia → anoxic is also useful. Family: anoxia, anoxic, and the uncommon adverb anoxically. Related contrast terms hypoxia and hypoxic indicate reduced oxygen and are not direct derivatives of anoxic.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: oxygen-free（无氧的）直接说明没有氧气；anaerobic（厌氧的、无氧条件下的）常描述不需要氧气的生物或过程；hypoxic（低氧的）指氧气不足，而 anoxic 严格说指氧气缺失，医学语境中也可指极重度缺氧。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Oxygen-free directly states that oxygen is absent; anaerobic often describes organisms or processes that do not require oxygen; hypoxic means oxygen is insufficient, whereas anoxic strictly indicates its absence, with some medical use extending to extreme deprivation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: an-＝无，ox-＝氧：氧气供应归零，就是 anoxic。
mnemonic_anchor.en: An- means “without,” and ox- points to oxygen: oxygen supply at zero means anoxic.

pronunciation.note: 主重音在 ˈ 后的音节；按词内音节连贯朗读。

forms: 本义固定用 bitters；不把 bitter 当作这种调酒料的单数

usage_note: 常用 a dash of bitters 或 a few drops of bitters；表示少量苦味调酒料，不能理解成啤酒 bitter 的普通复数。

etymology_story.zh: bitters 在18世纪由 bitter“苦的”发展为苦味药剂及酒剂的名称，后来尤其用于指调酒苦精。bitter 可追溯至古英语 biter，与 bite“咬”同源，反映了苦味带来的尖锐刺激感。
etymology_story.en: Bitters developed in the eighteenth century from bitter as a name for bitter medicinal and alcoholic preparations, later becoming especially associated with cocktail flavorings. Bitter goes back to Old English biter and is related to bite, suggesting a sharp, biting taste.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词：bitter（苦的）+ -s → bitters，属于已经词汇化的复数形式名称；指苦精时通常保留 -s，不能机械地改成单数 bitter。基础词族：bitter（形容词，也可作名词及较少见的动词）、bitterly（副词）、bitterness（名词）、bitters（名词）；相关复合词 bittersweet（苦甜交织的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: bitter + -s → bitters, a lexicalized plural-form name; the preparation normally retains its final -s rather than taking an ordinary singular bitter. The base family includes bitter as an adjective, noun, and less common verb, plus bitterly, bitterness, and bitters; bittersweet is a related compound.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cocktail bitters（调酒苦精）明确强调调酒用途；aromatic bitters（芳香苦精）是以香料和草本香气为特色的一类苦精；bitter liqueur（苦味利口酒）通常可直接饮用，不能与少量添加的浓缩调酒苦精完全互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cocktail bitters explicitly identifies the mixing ingredient; aromatic bitters names a subtype characterized by spice and herbal aromas; a bitter liqueur is generally suitable for drinking as a beverage and is not fully interchangeable with concentrated cocktail bitters.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: bitter 是“苦”，bitters 是给酒添苦香的“小几滴”；记住名称末尾的 -s。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Bitter names the taste; bitters adds that taste a few drops at a time. Keep the final -s.

etymology_story.zh: corticosteroid 是20世纪科学英语中由 cortico-“皮质”与 steroid“类固醇”组合而成的名称，其中 cortico- 最终源于拉丁语 cortex“树皮、外层”。该名称最初对应肾上腺皮质产生的激素，也用于具有类似作用的药物。
etymology_story.en: Corticosteroid was formed in twentieth-century scientific English from cortico- “cortex” and steroid; cortico- ultimately comes from Latin cortex, meaning “bark” or “outer layer.” The name identifies hormones produced by the adrenal cortex and also medicines with similar effects.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词：cortico-（皮质，此处指肾上腺皮质）+ steroid（类固醇）。词族：corticosteroid（名词）、corticosteroids（复数）、corticosteroidal（形容词，皮质类固醇的）；相关词包括 cortex（皮质）、cortical（皮质的）、steroid（类固醇）、steroidal（类固醇的）。glucocorticoid（糖皮质激素）和 mineralocorticoid（盐皮质激素）是相关类别名称。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: cortico- “cortex,” here the adrenal cortex, + steroid. Family: corticosteroid, plural corticosteroids, and adjectival corticosteroidal. Related words include cortex, cortical, steroid, and steroidal; glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid name related hormone classes.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: corticoid（皮质激素）与 corticosteroid 意义接近；glucocorticoid（糖皮质激素）是其中主要涉及代谢调节和抗炎作用的一类；steroid（类固醇）范围更广，日常医疗表达中有时简称皮质类固醇药物，但也可指其他甾体物质。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Corticoid is a close equivalent; glucocorticoid names a subgroup especially associated with metabolic regulation and anti-inflammatory effects; steroid is broader, although medical conversation sometimes uses it as shorthand for a corticosteroid medicine.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: cortico-＝外层皮质，steroid＝类固醇：从肾上腺“外层”得名的激素及其类似药物。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Cortico- points to the outer cortex; steroid names the chemical class: hormones from the adrenal outer layer and medicines that mimic them.

etymology_story.zh: cyclotron 是20世纪30年代出现的装置名称，由希腊语来源的 cyclo-“圆、回旋”与从 electron 等词中发展出的装置词尾 -tron 组合而成。名称突出了带电粒子在磁场中不断回旋、同时被加速的运动方式。
etymology_story.en: Cyclotron appeared in the 1930s, combining Greek-derived cyclo- “circle” with the device-forming ending -tron, developed from words such as electron. The name highlights the circulating motion of charged particles as they are accelerated in a magnetic field.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词：cyclo-（圆、回旋）+ -tron（装置名称词尾）。词族及相关扩展：cyclotron（名词）、cyclotrons（复数）、cyclotronic（形容词，回旋加速器的或回旋运动的）；synchrocyclotron（同步回旋加速器）是相关复合词；cyclotron resonance（回旋共振）是常见专业术语。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: cyclo- “circle, circular motion” + device-forming -tron. Family and related extensions: cyclotron, plural cyclotrons, and adjectival cyclotronic; synchrocyclotron is a related compound, and cyclotron resonance is an established technical expression.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: particle accelerator（粒子加速器）是上位词；synchrotron（同步加速器）通常使粒子沿固定环形轨道运行，并同步调节相关场；linear accelerator（直线加速器）沿直线路径加速粒子，而 cyclotron 使用向外扩展的回旋路径。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Particle accelerator is the broader category; a synchrotron generally keeps particles on a fixed circular orbit while adjusting the relevant fields; a linear accelerator speeds particles along a straight path, whereas a cyclotron uses an outward-spiraling path.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: cyclo- 联想 cycle“循环”：粒子一圈圈转，速度一次次增。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect cyclo- with cycle: particles go around repeatedly and gain speed on successive passes.

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 expiare，意为“赎罪、洁净”，由表示充分完成的 ex- 和意为“以宗教仪式平息、赎罪”的 piare 构成；piare 与 pius“虔诚的”同源。英语保留了宗教上的赎罪义，也将其用于弥补一般的道德过错。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin expiare, meaning 'to atone for or purify,' combining an intensive ex- with piare, 'to appease through religious observance,' related to pius, 'devout.' English retained the religious meaning and extended it to making amends for moral wrongdoing more generally.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中宜将 expiate 作为借入的动词词基整体识记，不把 pi- 当作可自由构词的英语词根。主要词族：expiation（赎罪、补偿）、expiatory（赎罪的）、expiable（可赎清的）、inexpiable（不可赎清的）；常用屈折形式为 expiates、expiated、expiating。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, treat expiate as a borrowed verb base rather than treating pi- as a productive English root. Principal family members are expiation, expiatory, expiable, and inexpiable; inflected forms are expiates, expiated, and expiating.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: atone 通常与 for 连用，强调为过错赎罪；redeem 强调挽回名誉、价值或道德地位；make amends 是更日常的表达，强调采取行动补偿。expiate 较正式，直接以罪过或罪责作宾语，常带有受罚或牺牲的意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Atone usually takes for and emphasizes making up for wrongdoing; redeem emphasizes restoring worth, reputation, or moral standing; make amends is more everyday and focuses on compensatory action. Expiate is formal, takes the wrongdoing or guilt directly as its object, and often suggests punishment or sacrifice.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把罪责“清偿掉”：通过补偿或承担代价，使过错得到弥补。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think 'clear the moral debt': make amends by offering compensation or bearing a cost.

meaning: 衣着邋遢守旧的人（常贬指女性）
aliases: 衣着邋遢守旧的人（常贬指女性）

forms: 复数 frumps
family: frumpy 衣着土气的；frumpish 邋遢守旧的

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆；frump + -y → frumpy（衣着土气的）。

etymology.text: 19世纪英语开始用 frump 贬指衣着守旧、样子邋遢的人；此前英语里相关形式曾表示嘲弄或坏脾气，更早来源不明。用老气又不整洁的穿着画面记忆即可。

usage_note: 带侮辱和性别偏见色彩，多用于理解引语或人物自嘲，避免用它评价他人外貌。

senses.meaning_zh: 衣着老气、不讲究外表的人，通常贬指女性
senses.meaning_en: an unfashionably dressed or dowdy person, usually a woman
senses.english_definition: If someone calls a woman a frump, they mean that her clothes and appearance are unattractive and old-fashioned.
senses.collocation_en: look like a frump; feel like a frump
senses.collocation_zh: 看起来像个衣着老气的人；觉得自己穿得土里土气
senses.sentence_en: She said the shapeless coat made her look like a frump.
senses.sentence_zh: 她说那件毫无版型的大衣让她看起来土里土气。

etymology_story.zh: frump 的更早来源不确定；英语中的早期用法涉及嘲弄或性情乖戾的人。后来它发展出“衣着老气、不注重外表的人”这一含义，并常被贬义地用于女性。
etymology_story.en: The earlier origin of frump is uncertain; early English uses involved mockery or an ill-tempered person. It later developed the meaning of a dowdy or unfashionably dressed person, especially as a disparaging description of a woman.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 frump 是不可再作可靠拆分的简单词。主要词族：frump + -y → frumpy（衣着老气的），frumpy + -ly → frumpily（土气地），frumpy + -ness → frumpiness（土气、不修饰）；另有 frumpish（老气的）。屈折形式包括 frumps、frumpier、frumpiest。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, frump is a simple base with no reliable smaller morphological division. Its principal family includes frumpy (frump + -y), frumpily (frumpy + -ly), frumpiness (frumpy + -ness), and frumpish; inflected forms include frumps, frumpier, and frumpiest.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: dowdy person 最接近，强调衣着老气、缺乏吸引力；slob 强调邋遢、不整洁，未必穿着过时；plain dresser 仅指穿着朴素，语气通常较中性。frump 带有明显的外貌评价和贬义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Dowdy person is closest and emphasizes an old-fashioned, unattractive appearance; slob emphasizes untidiness or poor cleanliness rather than outdated fashion; plain dresser describes simple clothing and is usually more neutral. Frump carries a distinctly disparaging judgment about appearance.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 核心画面是“穿得老气又没精神”；关键在土气，不一定是脏。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture someone looking dowdy in dated clothes: the central idea is an unfashionable appearance.

pronunciation.note: 主重音在 ˈ 后的音节；按词内音节连贯朗读。

forms: 复数 interstices
family: interstitial 间隙中的

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆；同族词 interstiti-（间隙词干）+ -al → interstitial（间隙中的）。

etymology.text: 经古法语及拉丁语 interstitium 进入英语，拉丁语由 inter“之间”和 stare“站立”的词干构成；想象两块石头之间留下的一线空隙。

usage_note: 常用复数 interstices；本课用单数呈现词形，通常指物体之间的小空隙，也可比喻时间间隙。

senses.meaning_zh: 物体之间的细小空隙；缝隙
senses.meaning_en: a small space between objects or parts
senses.english_definition: An interstice is a small space between things or between parts of something.
senses.collocation_en: interstices between grains; fill the interstices
senses.collocation_zh: 颗粒之间的空隙；填满缝隙
senses.sentence_en: Water seeped into the interstices between the stones.
senses.sentence_zh: 水渗入了石块之间的缝隙。

senses.meaning_zh: 活动之间的短暂空当；事物之间的空隙或薄弱环节
senses.meaning_en: a small interval or opening between activities or within a larger system
senses.english_definition: The interstices of an activity or system are the small intervals or openings that exist between its main parts.
senses.collocation_en: the interstices of daily life; the interstices of the law
senses.collocation_zh: 日常生活中的零碎空当；法律的空隙地带
senses.sentence_en: She wrote poetry in the interstices of a busy working life.
senses.sentence_zh: 她利用繁忙工作生活中的零碎空当写诗。

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 interstitium“间隔、空隙”，与 intersistere“站在其间”有关，其中 inter- 表示“在……之间”，后半部分与“站立”有关。实际物体之间的空隙，后来也成为时间空当和制度缝隙的比喻。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin interstitium, 'an interval or gap,' related to intersistere, 'to stand between,' with inter- meaning 'between' and a second element associated with standing. Physical gaps later supplied a metaphor for intervals in time and openings within systems.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 interstice 通常作为完整的借入名词识记；历史上的 inter- 可辨认，但 -stice 不是自由使用的英语词。复数为 interstices；派生时使用 interstiti- 词干：interstitial（间隙的、间质的）、interstitially（在间隙中地、以间质方式）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, interstice is normally learned as a complete borrowed noun; historical inter- is recognizable, but -stice is not an independent English word. The plural is interstices, and the related stem interstiti- appears in interstitial and interstitially.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: gap 是最通用的“空隙”，不限大小；crevice 强调岩石、墙面等处狭窄而较深的裂缝；interval 强调时间或距离上的间隔。interstice 较正式，常指相邻部分之间细小的空隙，并常用复数。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Gap is the broadest term and does not specify size; crevice suggests a narrow, often deep opening in rock or another surface; interval emphasizes separation in time or distance. Interstice is more formal, often denotes a small space between adjacent parts, and frequently occurs in the plural.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: inter- 表示“之间”：把注意力放在两部分之间留下的那一点空隙。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Inter- means 'between': focus on the little space left between two parts.

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆；kaolin + -ite（矿物名称后缀）→ kaolinite（高岭石）。

etymology.text: 经法语 kaolin 来自中国江西地名“高岭”的旧式转写；当地的瓷土使这个名称进入欧洲语言，记住“高岭的瓷土”。

usage_note: 一种常呈白色的细黏土，用于陶瓷、纸张填料等；不要把它理解成金属薄片。

senses.meaning_zh: 高岭土；主要由高岭石组成、用于制瓷等的黏土
senses.meaning_en: a clay consisting mainly of kaolinite, used especially in making porcelain
senses.english_definition: Kaolin is a fine clay, usually white, that is used to make porcelain and in products such as paper and paint.
senses.collocation_en: kaolin deposits; calcined kaolin
senses.collocation_zh: 高岭土矿床；煅烧高岭土
senses.sentence_en: The factory uses kaolin to make fine porcelain.
senses.sentence_zh: 这家工厂用高岭土制作精细瓷器。

etymology_story.zh: 英语 kaolin 经法语借入，最终来自中国江西景德镇附近地名“高岭”的旧式转写。当地出产的制瓷黏土使这个地名成为国际通用的材料名称。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed kaolin through French, ultimately from an older transcription of Gaoling, a place near Jingdezhen in Jiangxi, China. Clay obtained there for porcelain manufacture turned the place name into an international name for the material.

morphology_enriched.zh: kaolin 是由地名形成的借词，在现代英语中不拆分为 kao- 和 -lin。主要词族：kaolin + -ite → kaolinite（高岭石），kaolinic（高岭土的），kaolinitic（含高岭石的、高岭石的），kaolinize／kaolinise（使高岭土化），kaolinization／kaolinisation（高岭土化作用）。
morphology_enriched.en: Kaolin is a place-name borrowing and is not divided into kao- and -lin in modern English. Principal family members include kaolinite (kaolin + the mineral suffix -ite), kaolinic, kaolinitic, kaolinize/kaolinise, and kaolinization/kaolinisation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: china clay 通常是 kaolin 的同义名称；clay 是范围更广的“黏土”；kaolinite 是高岭土的主要矿物“高岭石”，并不等同于整种黏土材料。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: China clay is normally a synonym for kaolin; clay is the broader material category; kaolinite is the principal mineral in kaolin, rather than an interchangeable name for the whole clay material.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: kaolin 就是“高岭”的国际化名字：高岭的土，制瓷的料。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Kaolin carries the name Gaoling: remember the place through its porcelain-making clay.

morphology.text: lass-（疲倦）+ -itude（状态）→ lassitude（倦怠、乏力）；这是拉丁语来源的词干结构。

etymology.text: 15世纪英语从拉丁语 lassitudo 借入，其基础 lassus 意为疲倦；可联想到身体和精神都提不起劲的状态。

usage_note: 较正式或文学用语，既可指身体疲倦，也可指缺乏精神和动力；不是懒惰的道德评价。

senses.meaning_zh: 身心倦怠；乏力；提不起劲
senses.meaning_en: physical or mental weariness accompanied by a lack of energy
senses.english_definition: Lassitude is a feeling of tiredness that leaves you with little energy or desire to do anything.
senses.collocation_en: a feeling of lassitude; a sense of lassitude
senses.collocation_zh: 一种倦怠感；一种乏力、提不起劲的感觉
senses.sentence_en: The afternoon heat filled her with lassitude.
senses.sentence_zh: 午后的炎热使她浑身倦怠，提不起精神。

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 lassitudo“疲倦”，其基础是 lassus“疲倦的”。英语保留了身心疲乏的核心含义，也常用它描写炎热、疾病或精神消沉带来的无精打采。
etymology_story.en: The word derives from Latin lassitudo, 'weariness,' based on lassus, 'tired.' English preserved the core meaning of physical or mental fatigue and also uses it for the listlessness associated with heat, illness, or low spirits.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 lassitude 主要作为完整借词使用；历史上可理解为 lass-（疲倦）加表示状态的 -itude，但 lass- 在英语中不是能自由构词的词根。该词没有常用的现代派生词族；表达形容词意义时通常使用 tired、weary 或 listless，而不是另造同根词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English mainly treats lassitude as a complete borrowed noun; historically, it contains lass-, 'tired,' and the state-forming ending -itude, but lass- is not a productive English root. There is no commonly used modern derivative family; adjectives such as tired, weary, or listless normally express the related quality.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: fatigue 强调疲劳，可由用力、压力或疾病引起；lethargy 强调迟钝、缺乏活力，有时带嗜睡意味；listlessness 强调没有精神或兴趣。lassitude 较正式或文学化，突出疲乏与不想活动相结合的状态。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Fatigue emphasizes tiredness from exertion, stress, or illness; lethargy emphasizes sluggishness and sometimes drowsiness; listlessness emphasizes a lack of energy or interest. Lassitude is formal or literary and combines weariness with a disinclination to act.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: lass- 的历史含义是“疲倦”：身体没劲，精神也懒得动。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Historical lass- means 'tired': the body lacks energy, and the mind lacks the urge to act.

senses.meaning_zh: 放荡的；纵欲的
senses.meaning_en: sexually unrestrained and indifferent to conventional morality
senses.english_definition: Libertine behavior or attitudes show little respect for accepted moral rules, especially rules about sexual relationships.
senses.chinese_definition: libertine 形容行为或态度不太顾及公认的道德规范，尤其是不顾有关性关系的规范。

etymology_story.zh: 该词经法语 libertin 传入英语，源自拉丁语 libertinus，原指获释的奴隶或与获释者身份有关的人。英语早期也用它指不受宗教观念约束的自由思想者，后来主要指摆脱道德约束、尤其在性方面放纵的人。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English through French libertin, from Latin libertinus, which referred to a freed slave or someone associated with freed status. Early English also used it for a religious freethinker; its dominant later meaning became someone free from moral restraints, especially sexual ones.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中宜把 libertine 作为整体词基，不机械拆成 liberty 加后缀。主要派生词：libertine 去词尾 e 加 -ism → libertinism（放荡主义；纵欲生活）；libertinage（放荡行为）是相关的法语借词；libertines 是名词复数。liberty（自由）、liberate（解放）、liberation（解放）属于历史同源词群，并非由 libertine 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, treat libertine as a whole base rather than mechanically analyzing it as liberty plus a suffix. Its main derivative is libertinism, formed by dropping final e and adding -ism; libertinage is a related French borrowing, and libertines is the noun plural. Liberty, liberate, and liberation belong to the historical root family but are not direct derivatives of libertine.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: rake（浪荡子）常带旧时代上流社会男性的色彩；debauchee（纵欲者）更强调沉溺酒色等感官享乐；hedonist（享乐主义者）强调追求快乐，本身不必含有道德败坏或性放纵的意思。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Rake often suggests a fashionable, sexually dissolute man in a historical setting; debauchee emphasizes excessive indulgence in sensual pleasures; hedonist describes someone who prioritizes pleasure without necessarily implying sexual misconduct or moral corruption.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 共同的“自由”词源线索：自由越过道德约束，就成了放纵；这是助记概括。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use the shared idea of freedom as a memory hook: freedom carried beyond moral restraints becomes license.

senses.meaning_zh: 没药；某些没药属植物产生的芳香树脂
senses.meaning_en: an aromatic resin obtained from certain Commiphora trees
senses.english_definition: Myrrh is a fragrant resin from certain trees that is used in incense, perfumes, and some traditional medicines.
senses.chinese_definition: myrrh 是从某些树木中取得的芳香树脂，用于熏香、香水以及一些传统药物。
senses.collocation_en: frankincense and myrrh; myrrh resin
senses.collocation_zh: 乳香与没药；没药树脂
senses.sentence_en: The incense contained a mixture of frankincense and myrrh.
senses.sentence_zh: 这种熏香含有乳香和没药的混合物。

etymology_story.zh: 该词可追溯至古英语 myrre，经拉丁语 myrrha 或 murra，来自希腊语 myrrha。更早的来源属于闪米特语言，与表示“苦”的词根有关，呼应这种树脂的苦味。
etymology_story.en: The word goes back to Old English myrre, through Latin myrrha or murra, from Greek myrrha. Its earlier source is Semitic and is connected with a root meaning 'bitter,' reflecting the resin's taste.

morphology_enriched.zh: myrrh 在现代英语中是不可再作常规拆分的简单词，通常作不可数名词。罕见派生词 myrrhy＝myrrh＋-y，意为“含没药的；有没药气味的”；myrrh oil（没药油）、myrrh resin（没药树脂）和 myrrh-bearing（产没药的；携带没药的）属于复合表达，并非独立后缀派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Myrrh is a simple word with no productive internal breakdown in modern English and is normally uncountable. The rare derivative myrrhy consists of myrrh plus -y and means containing or smelling of myrrh; myrrh oil, myrrh resin, and myrrh-bearing are compound expressions rather than separate suffixal derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: gum resin（胶树脂）是没药所属的材料类别，并非专指没药；incense（熏香）指为产生香气而燃烧的材料，可能含没药；frankincense（乳香）是常与没药并提的另一种树脂，不能与没药互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Gum resin names the broader material category rather than myrrh specifically; incense is material burned for its fragrance and may contain myrrh; frankincense is a different aromatic resin often mentioned alongside myrrh, not an interchangeable synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 词源抓住“苦”，实物抓住“香”：苦味的芳香树脂，就是没药。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link its bitter-name origin with its fragrant use: a bitter aromatic resin is myrrh.

meaning: 固定音型（反复出现的乐句）

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆；ostinato + -like → ostinato-like（像固定音型一样反复的），-like 表示“像……的”。

etymology.text: 借自意大利语 ostinato，原意是“固执的”，上溯拉丁语 obstinatus。把同一乐句“固执地一再出现”作为助记。

usage_note: 音乐术语，强调一个音型反复出现；不等于整首曲子重放。

senses.meaning_zh: 固定音型；持续反复的节奏或旋律型
senses.meaning_en: a musical pattern repeated persistently through a passage
senses.english_definition: An ostinato is a short pattern of notes or beats that is repeated many times while other parts of the music continue or change.
senses.chinese_definition: ostinato 是一组短小的音符或节奏，在音乐的其他声部继续进行或发生变化时多次反复出现。
senses.collocation_en: a rhythmic ostinato; a bass ostinato
senses.collocation_zh: 节奏固定音型；低音固定音型
senses.sentence_en: The cellos repeat a bass ostinato beneath the changing melody.
senses.sentence_zh: 大提琴在不断变化的旋律下方反复演奏一个低音固定音型。

etymology_story.zh: ostinato 借自意大利语，原义为“固执的；执拗的”，源于拉丁语 obstinatus。音乐术语借用这种“坚持不变”的含义，指持续反复出现的音型。
etymology_story.en: Ostinato was borrowed from Italian, where it means 'obstinate' or 'stubborn,' ultimately from Latin obstinatus. Its musical meaning applies that idea of persistence to a pattern that keeps returning.

morphology_enriched.zh: ostinato 是整体借入的音乐名词，现代英语中不宜拆成英语词根和后缀；复数为 ostinatos 或保留意大利语形式的 ostinati。没有常用的英语后缀派生词；ostinato pattern（固定音型模式）、ostinato accompaniment（固定音型伴奏）中的 ostinato 是名词作定语，ostinato-like（像固定音型的）是临时复合形式。obstinate（固执的）是历史同源词，并非其英语派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Ostinato is a borrowed musical noun and should not be divided into English roots and suffixes; its plurals are ostinatos and the Italian form ostinati. It has no common English suffixal derivatives: in ostinato pattern and ostinato accompaniment it is an attributive noun, while ostinato-like is a freely formed compound. Obstinate is historically related, not an English derivative of ostinato.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: riff（反复乐句）多见于爵士、摇滚等音乐，常有鲜明的旋律或节奏特征；repeated motif（反复动机）范围更宽，动机可以间隔出现；ground bass（固定低音）专指低音声部反复的模式，而 ostinato 可以出现在不同声部。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Riff is common in jazz and rock and often has a distinctive melodic or rhythmic character; repeated motif is broader and may recur at intervals; ground bass specifically repeats in the bass, whereas an ostinato can occur in different musical parts.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “固执”的音乐：同一个音型坚持一遍又一遍。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A stubborn musical pattern insists on repeating itself.

pronunciation.note: 重音符号 ˈ 标示主重音；采用宽式音标。

forms: 食物义通常不可数；词典也收录复数 poi、pois，用于种类等语境。

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆；poi + -based → poi-based（以芋泥为原料的），如 poi-based bread。

etymology.text: 英语从夏威夷语等波利尼西亚语言借入 poi，保留当地食物名称。记住把煮熟的芋头捣成泥的画面。

usage_note: 本课只学食物义：熟芋头加水捣成糊状，并非一种饼。

senses.meaning_en: a ball on a cord used in Māori performance, or the performance using such balls
senses.english_definition: Poi are balls attached to cords that performers swing in patterns, and poi also names the Māori performance tradition and related modern spinning activities.
senses.chinese_definition: poi 可以指表演者按一定轨迹挥舞的带绳球，也可以指毛利人的这种表演传统及相关的现代绳球旋转活动。

senses.collocation_zh: 绳球旋转表演；一场球舞表演

etymology_story.zh: 食物义直接借自夏威夷语 poi，保留了当地传统食物的名称。绳球及表演义则借自毛利语 poi，原指球；英语中的这两组用法来自不同的直接借词来源。
etymology_story.en: The food sense was borrowed directly from Hawaiian poi, retaining the name of the traditional food. The ball and performance senses were borrowed from Māori poi, meaning a ball; the two groups therefore have different immediate borrowing sources in English.

morphology_enriched.zh: poi 是简单借词，没有可用英语词根和后缀分析的内部结构，也没有常用后缀派生词。食物义通常不可数；表演用具义常用不变复数 poi；poi-based（以芋泥为基础的）、poi spinner（绳球表演者）、poi spinning（绳球旋转活动）和 fire poi（火绳球）属于复合表达。
morphology_enriched.en: Poi is a simple borrowing with no internal English root-and-affix structure and no common suffixal derivatives. The food sense is normally uncountable; the performance implement commonly has the unchanged plural poi. Poi-based, poi spinner, poi spinning, and fire poi are compound expressions.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 食物义可用 taro paste（芋头糊）或 pounded taro（捣制芋头）描述，但这些说法未必指夏威夷传统制法；表演义可用 tethered balls（带绳球）描述器具，不能涵盖 poi 的文化及表演含义。这些是近义描述，没有跨两种词义通用的准确同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the food, taro paste and pounded taro are descriptive near-equivalents but do not necessarily imply traditional Hawaiian preparation. For the performance sense, tethered balls describes the equipment but omits its cultural and performance meanings. There is no exact synonym covering both senses.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 用两个场景分别记：夏威夷碗里的芋泥；毛利舞者手中的绳球。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Keep two separate pictures: taro paste in a Hawaiian bowl, and corded balls in a Māori performer's hands.

etymology_story.zh: pommel 来自中古英语 pomel，经盎格鲁法语或古法语传入，其词源是拉丁语 pomum（果实）的指小形式，体现圆头像小果实的形状。该词用于柄首、鞍前桥等凸起部件，动词后来表示反复击打，现代更常写作 pummel。
etymology_story.en: Pommel comes from Middle English pomel, borrowed through Anglo-French or Old French from a diminutive of Latin pomum, meaning fruit, with reference to a small fruit-shaped knob. It names projecting fittings such as hilt ends and saddle fronts; the later verb means to strike repeatedly and is now more commonly spelled pummel.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 pommel 是整体词基；名词复数及动词第三人称单数均为 pommels。动词过去式和过去分词：英式通常 pommelled，美式通常 pommeled；现在分词：英式通常 pommelling，美式通常 pommeling；形容词 pommelled 或 pommeled 可表示“有圆头或鞍前桥的”。pommel horse（鞍马）是复合名词；pummel 是相关的动词变体，并非添加后缀形成的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Pommel functions as a whole base in modern English; pommels is both the noun plural and the third-person singular verb. The past tense and participle are usually pommelled in British English and pommeled in American English; the corresponding present participles are pommelling and pommeling. The adjective pommelled or pommeled can mean fitted with a pommel. Pommel horse is a compound noun, while pummel is a related verb variant rather than a suffixal derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: knob（圆形凸起）是较宽泛的形状词，不能准确指明马鞍或剑柄上的部位；pummel（连续猛击）是动词义更常见的拼法；batter（接连猛击）更突出猛烈冲击及可能造成的损伤。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Knob is a broader shape word and does not identify a specific saddle or hilt fitting; pummel is the more usual spelling of the striking verb; batter emphasizes heavy repeated blows and often their damaging effects.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“小果实”记住圆形凸头：剑柄末端、马鞍前部；动词另联想 pummel＝连续捶打。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a little fruit-shaped knob on a sword hilt or saddle; link the verb with the more familiar pummel, repeated blows.

usage_note: 医学名词，指形成炎性细胞结节的疾病；不要与 sarcoma“肉瘤”混淆。

etymology_story.zh: 该病名由 sarcoid 和表示病理状态的 -osis 构成；sarcoid 中的希腊语源成分分别表示“肉”和“像……的”。名称保留了早期对病变外观的描述，后来成为这一疾病的专名。[词源来源：韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/sarcoidosis)
etymology_story.en: The name combines sarcoid with -osis, a suffix denoting a pathological condition; the Greek elements underlying sarcoid mean 'flesh' and 'resembling.' An early description of the lesions thus became the name of the disease. [Etymology source: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/sarcoidosis)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代专业构词：sarcoid（肉样的；结节病的）+ -osis（病理状态）→ sarcoidosis。词族及相关形式：sarcoidoses（疾病名称的复数形式）、sarcoid（形容词，也可作结节病的名词简称）、sarcoidal、sarcoidotic（形容词，结节病的）、neurosarcoidosis（神经系统结节病）。本词没有常用动词或副词形式。CEFR-C2 为教学难度估计，并非经核实的官方单词分级；考试词表归属未核实。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern technical formation: sarcoid + -osis 'pathological condition' → sarcoidosis. Family and related forms: sarcoidoses, the plural; sarcoid, an adjective and a shortened disease name; sarcoidal and sarcoidotic, adjectives; and neurosarcoidosis, involving the nervous system. There is no common verb or adverb form. CEFR-C2 is an estimated learning level, not a verified official word-level classification; examination-list membership is unverified.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sarcoid（结节病）是临床语境中的简称；Boeck's disease（伯克病）是历史性别名。granulomatous disease（肉芽肿性疾病）是范围更广的类别，不能直接替换；sarcoma（肉瘤）是另一种疾病，不是近义词。[医学释义来源：美国国家癌症研究所](https://www.cancer.gov/publications/dictionaries/cancer-terms/def/sarcoidosis)
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sarcoid is a clinical short form; Boeck's disease is a historical alternative name. Granulomatous disease names a broader category and is not interchangeable with sarcoidosis; sarcoma is a different disease, not a synonym. [Medical definition source: National Cancer Institute](https://www.cancer.gov/publications/dictionaries/cancer-terms/def/sarcoidosis)

mnemonic_anchor.zh: sarc- 肉 + -oid 像 + -osis 病态：从“肉样病变”的旧称，记住“形成肉芽肿的结节病”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Flesh + resembling + disease: an old appearance-based name anchors the modern disease involving granulomas.
