etymology_story.en: Formed from slip and shod, slipshod originally described someone wearing loose shoes or slippers in the late sixteenth century, and later suggested shabby footwear or appearance. That association developed into the modern sense of careless, poorly executed work. [Source: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/slipshod)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可识别结构：slip + shod → 复合形容词 slipshod；shod 是 shoe 作动词时的不规则过去式和过去分词，表示“穿上鞋的”。词族：slipshoddiness / slipshodness（马虎、草率，名词）、slipshodly / slipshoddily（马虎地，较少见的副词形式）。本词在现代常用语中作形容词。CEFR-C2 为教学难度估计，并非经核实的官方单词分级；考试词表归属未核实。
morphology_enriched.en: Recognizable modern structure: slip + shod → the compound adjective slipshod; shod is the irregular past tense and past participle of the verb shoe, meaning 'provided with shoes.' Family: slipshoddiness / slipshodness, nouns, and slipshodly / slipshoddily, less common adverbs. The headword itself is an adjective in ordinary modern usage. CEFR-C2 is an estimated learning level, not a verified official word-level classification; examination-list membership is unverified.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: careless（粗心的）泛指不够留心；sloppy（马虎的、凌乱的）更口语化，也可形容外观；perfunctory（敷衍的）强调只做表面功夫。slipshod 尤其批评工作方法或成果因不认真而质量低劣。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Careless broadly describes insufficient attention; sloppy is more informal and can also describe untidy appearance; perfunctory emphasizes doing only the minimum required. Slipshod particularly criticizes methods or results whose quality suffers from carelessness.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 鞋子松垮，做事也松垮：从穿鞋不利索，联想到工作不细致。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Loose shoes, loose standards: picture someone shuffling in slippers and doing careless work.

meaning: 孤立子（一种能保持形态传播的孤立波）

pronunciation.note: 重音符号 ˈ 标示主重音；采用宽式音标。

forms: 可数名词；复数 solitons。
family: solitary 孤立的；soliton-like 类孤立子的。

morphology.text: solit-（取自 solitary“孤立的”）+ -on（粒子类名称词尾）→ soliton（孤立子）。

etymology.text: 20世纪英语科学造词，由 solitary 的截短部分和 -on 组成，1965年已有记录。想象一个保持形状向前移动的独立波包。

usage_note: 物理学术语，常见于非线性波和光学；不是任意一个波峰都叫 soliton。

senses.meaning_zh: 孤立子；传播时保持形态，并在与同类波相互作用后恢复其特征的局域非线性波
senses.meaning_en: A localized nonlinear wave that maintains its form and retains its characteristic properties after interacting with similar waves.
senses.english_definition: A soliton is a localized wave that travels without spreading out and, in the classical sense, emerges from a collision with another such wave with its shape and speed unchanged.
senses.collocation_en: optical soliton; soliton propagation
senses.collocation_zh: 光孤立子；孤立子传播
senses.sentence_en: The researchers generated an optical soliton that maintained its shape as it travelled through the fibre.
senses.sentence_zh: 研究人员产生了一个光孤立子，它在光纤中传播时保持了自身形态。

etymology_story.zh: soliton 是20世纪的科学造词，由 solitary“孤立的”的截短部分与粒子名称中常见的词尾 -on 组成，1965年已有用例。这个名称体现了某些孤立波在传播和碰撞中表现出的粒子般稳定性。[来源：韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/soliton)
etymology_story.en: Soliton is a twentieth-century scientific coinage combining a shortened form of solitary with -on, a particle-name ending, and is attested from 1965. The name reflects the particle-like stability of certain solitary waves during propagation and collisions. [Source: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/soliton)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代造词分析：solit-（截取自 solitary“孤立的”，并非独立英语单词）+ -on（粒子类名称词尾）→ soliton。词族：solitons（复数）、solitonic（孤立子的）、soliton-like（类似孤立子的）。solitary（孤独的、单独的）和 solitude（独处）提供词源上的记忆联系，并非由 soliton 派生。本词没有常用动词或副词形式。所列音标为美式。CEFR-C2 为教学难度估计，并非经核实的官方单词分级；考试词表归属未核实。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern coinage: solit-, clipped from solitary and not an independent English word, + -on, a particle-name ending, → soliton. Family: solitons, solitonic, and soliton-like. Solitary and solitude provide etymological memory connections but are not derivatives of soliton. There is no common verb or adverb form. The IPA given is American. CEFR-C2 is an estimated learning level, not a verified official word-level classification; examination-list membership is unverified.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: solitary wave（孤立波）是最接近的术语，但严格意义上并非所有孤立波都具有孤立子的碰撞保持性；wave packet（波包）泛指局域化的波群，可能随传播而展宽；pulse（脉冲）强调短时扰动，不保证稳定传播。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Solitary wave is the closest term, but strictly not every solitary wave has a soliton's collision-preserving properties; wave packet broadly denotes a localized group of waves that may spread; pulse emphasizes a brief disturbance without implying stable propagation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: solitary 的“独行”加 -on 的“粒子感”：像粒子一样保持形态前进的波。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Solitary supplies 'travelling alone'; -on suggests a particle: remember a wave that travels with particle-like stability.

meaning: 圣痕（类似耶稣受难伤口的身体痕迹）

pronunciation.note: 重音符号 ˈ 标示主重音；采用宽式音标。

forms: 本词本身是复数；语法上用复数谓语，如 the stigmata are visible。单数形式为 stigma。
family: stigma 印记；污名；stigmatic 有圣痕的。

morphology.text: stigmat-（印记词干）+ -a（希腊语式中性复数词尾）→ stigmata（多处印记）；这里保留借入的复数形式。

etymology.text: 来自拉丁语 stigma，源于希腊语表示“刺出的印记、烙印”的 stigma；stigmata 保留其复数形式。宗教用法把这些印记与受难伤痕相联系。

usage_note: 本课限定宗教义；描述信仰或艺术形象时使用，不把其形成原因作为词义的一部分。

senses.meaning_zh: （正式或文学用语）某种经历或状况留下的明显印记，常带负面意味
senses.meaning_en: Distinctive, often negative marks left by a condition or experience, in formal or literary usage.

etymology_story.zh: stigmata 是 stigma 保留的古典复数形式，经拉丁语追溯到希腊语 stigma“刺出的印记、烙印”，与表示“刺印、文身”的动词有关。具体的身体印记后来发展出宗教上的“圣痕”、医学上的特征性体征及比喻性的烙印等含义。[来源：韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/stigmata)
etymology_story.en: Stigmata preserves the classical plural of stigma, borrowed through Latin from Greek stigma 'punctured mark, brand,' related to a verb meaning 'to tattoo.' Physical marks developed into religious wounds, diagnostic signs, and figurative marks of an experience or condition. [Source: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/stigmata)

morphology_enriched.zh: 屈折分析：stigmat-（stigma 的古典词干）+ -a（古典中性复数词尾）→ stigmata；这是复数变化，不是新词派生。stigma 的复数还有 stigmas，社会污名义和植物柱头义通常用 stigmas；圣痕义固定使用复数 stigmata，并接复数谓语。词族：stigmatic、stigmatize / stigmatise（使蒙受污名）、stigmatized / stigmatised、stigmatizing / stigmatising、stigmatization / stigmatisation、stigmatizingly / stigmatisingly。两种所列读音存在交叉使用，并非严格按义项区分。[读音来源：剑桥词典](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/pronunciation/english/stigmata) CEFR-C2 为教学难度估计，并非经核实的官方单词分级；考试词表归属未核实。
morphology_enriched.en: Inflectional analysis: stigmat-, the classical stem of stigma, + -a, a classical neuter plural ending, → stigmata; this is plural formation, not derivation. Stigmas is another plural, usual for social stigmas and botanical stigmas; the religious sense uses plural stigmata with plural agreement. Family: stigmatic; stigmatize / stigmatise; stigmatized / stigmatised; stigmatizing / stigmatising; stigmatization / stigmatisation; and stigmatizingly / stigmatisingly. The two listed pronunciations overlap in use and are not strictly separated by meaning. [Pronunciation source: Cambridge Dictionary](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/pronunciation/english/stigmata) CEFR-C2 is an estimated learning level, not a verified official word-level classification; examination-list membership is unverified.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: marks（痕迹）最宽泛，不自带宗教或诊断含义；signs（体征、征象）在医学中指可观察到的疾病表现，范围更广；scars（瘢痕、伤疤）指损伤愈合后留下的痕迹。stigmata 强调具有识别意义的印记，宗教语境中特指与受难伤口相似的圣痕。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Marks is general and carries no necessary religious or diagnostic meaning; signs is broader in medicine and denotes observable indications of disease; scars are traces left after injuries heal. Stigmata emphasizes identifying marks and, in religious contexts, specifically marks resembling the wounds of the Crucifixion.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: stigma 是一个印记，stigmata 是多个印记：身体上的圣痕、疾病的体征、经历留下的烙印。
mnemonic_anchor.en: One stigma, several stigmata: connect bodily marks with sacred wounds, diagnostic signs, and the marks of experience.

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆；trompe + -like → trompe-like（像水风筒的），-like 表示“像……的”。

etymology.text: 借自法语 trompe，原义是“号角”，上溯古法语。装置把空气导向炉内，可用“向炉子送气的大号角”作形象助记。

usage_note: 历史冶金和水力工程术语，利用下落水流携带空气供气；不是手动风箱。

etymology_story.zh: 借自法语 trompe，意为“号角、喇叭形管”，可追溯至古法语。这个名称后来用于借助下落水流向熔炉等设备供应压缩空气的装置。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from French trompe, meaning a horn or trumpet-shaped tube, and goes back to Old French. The name came to designate an apparatus that uses falling water to supply compressed air to furnaces and other equipment.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中为不可再作常用词缀分析的借词：trompe；复数为 trompes。没有常用的直接派生词；hydraulic trompe（水力压气装置）和 trompe system（水风筒系统）是技术搭配，trompe-like（像水风筒的）只是可临时构成的形容词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, trompe is a borrowed base without a productive internal affix structure; its plural is trompes. It has no common direct derivatives. Hydraulic trompe and trompe system are technical combinations, while trompe-like is a possible occasional formation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hydraulic air compressor（水力空气压缩机）是最接近的功能性名称；air compressor（空气压缩机）范围更广；bellows（风箱）也可向炉内送风，但依靠可伸缩气室工作，结构和原理不同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hydraulic air compressor is the closest functional equivalent; air compressor is a broader category. Bellows can also supply air to a furnace, but work through an expanding and contracting chamber and are mechanically different.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把法语“号角”联想成向炉内送气的管子：水往下落，空气被带下去并压缩。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture the French “horn” as an air-supply pipe: falling water carries air downward and compresses it.

senses.meaning_zh: 促使行动；驱使；激发
senses.meaning_en: to motivate someone to act
senses.english_definition: If a feeling or purpose actuates someone, it makes them act in a particular way.
senses.collocation_en: be actuated by ambition; be actuated by a sense of duty
senses.collocation_zh: 受雄心驱使；出于责任感而行动
senses.sentence_en: She was actuated by a sense of duty rather than a desire for recognition.
senses.sentence_zh: 促使她行动的是责任感，而不是获得认可的愿望。

etymology_story.zh: 源自中世纪拉丁语 actuare（使付诸行动、使成为现实）的过去分词 actuatus，进一步关联拉丁语 actus（行动）。英语中的核心意义是“使行动起来”，既可指启动机械，也可正式地表示动机驱使人行动。
etymology_story.en: Actuate comes from Medieval Latin actuatus, the past participle of actuare, meaning to put into action or make actual, ultimately related to Latin actus, “action.” Its central idea of causing action applies both to operating machinery and, in formal usage, motivating people.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可按 actu-（与行动、实现有关的拉丁语词干）+ -ate（动词形式）理解，但 actu- 不是现代英语中可自由使用的独立词。常用词族包括 actuates、actuated、actuating，以及 actuation（驱动；启动）和 actuator（执行器；致动器）；act、action、active、actual 属于更广的同源词群，并非都由 actuate 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: The word can be understood as actu-, a Latin-derived stem associated with action or realization, plus the verb ending -ate; actu- is not a free-standing modern English word. Its usual family includes actuates, actuated, actuating, actuation, and actuator. Act, action, active, and actual belong to the wider related family rather than all being derivatives of actuate.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: activate（激活）强调使某物进入工作状态；operate（操作；使运转）可强调持续控制设备；motivate（激励；促使）对应人的动机义，而 actuate 用于此义时更正式，常见于被动结构。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Activate emphasizes bringing something into an active state; operate can emphasize controlling equipment over time. Motivate corresponds to the human-motivation sense, for which actuate is more formal and often passive.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住 act“行动”：让机器动起来，也让人因某种动机行动起来。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor it to act: cause a mechanism to move or a person to take action.

senses.meaning_zh: 疆南星属植物；广义也指某些天南星科植物
senses.meaning_en: a plant of the genus Arum, or a related plant of the arum family

etymology_story.zh: 来自拉丁语 arum，源自古希腊语 aron，是古代对这类植物的称呼。Arum 后来成为植物属名，英语小写 arum 则可指该属植物，也见于某些相关植物的俗名。
etymology_story.en: Arum comes from Latin arum, from ancient Greek aron, an old name for this kind of plant. Arum later became a botanical genus name, while lowercase arum is used for its plants and in some common names for related plants.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是不可作常用词根词缀拆分的借词：arum；复数为 arums。常见组合有 arum family（天南星科）和 arum lily（通常指马蹄莲）；aroid（天南星科植物；天南星科的）是相关植物学词，不能机械分析成 arum 加普通英语后缀。
morphology_enriched.en: Arum is a borrowed base without a productive modern English root-and-affix breakdown; its plural is arums. Common combinations include arum family and arum lily, the latter usually referring to a Zantedeschia. Aroid is a related botanical term, not a simple formation made by adding an ordinary English suffix to arum.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: aroid（天南星科植物）范围更广，涵盖整个天南星科；cuckoopint（斑叶疆南星）特指 Arum maculatum；calla lily（马蹄莲）通常指马蹄莲属植物，与疆南星属同科但不同属，不能严格互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Aroid is broader and can refer to any member of the family Araceae. Cuckoopint specifically names Arum maculatum. Calla lily usually refers to a Zantedeschia, which belongs to the same family but a different genus and is not an exact synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the characteristic shape: a central flower spike wrapped by a spathe.

senses.meaning_en: the monetary unit of Thailand

etymology_story.zh: 借自泰语 baht，原来也是贵金属的重量单位。由于货币价值曾与金属重量相联系，这个名称也用于货币，后来成为泰国货币单位的英语名称。
etymology_story.en: Baht was borrowed from Thai, where the word also named a unit of weight for precious metals. Because monetary value was historically linked to metal weight, the name was also used for money and became the English name of Thailand’s currency unit.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是不可再分的借词：baht；表示金额时复数通常仍为 baht。没有常用的直接派生词；baht-denominated（以泰铢计价的）是复合形容词，其中 denominated 来自 denominate，并非 baht 的后缀。
morphology_enriched.en: Baht is an unanalyzable borrowed base in modern English; its plural in monetary amounts is normally baht. It has no common direct derivatives. Baht-denominated is a compound adjective: denominated comes from denominate and is not a suffix attached to baht.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Thai baht（泰铢）是明确国家归属的完整说法；THB 是货币代码，并非普通近义词；satang（萨当）是其辅币单位，100 萨当等于1泰铢，不能与 baht 互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Thai baht is the fuller name identifying the country. THB is the currency code rather than an ordinary synonym. Satang names a subdivision worth one hundredth of a baht and is not interchangeable with baht.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“称金银的重量”联想到“按金属重量计值的钱”：泰国价格牌上的 baht 就是泰铢。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect precious-metal weight with money valued by that weight: baht is the unit on a Thai price tag.

etymology_story.zh: 借自德语 Choral，是 Choralgesang（合唱圣歌）的缩略形式，其词源与中世纪拉丁语 choralis（合唱的）及 chorus（合唱队）有关。英语中先用于赞美诗及其曲调，后来也用于和声编曲，并在美国英语中指合唱团。
etymology_story.en: Chorale comes from German Choral, shortened from Choralgesang, “choral song,” and is related to Medieval Latin choralis and chorus. English uses the word for a hymn or its tune, for a harmonized setting, and, especially in American English, for a choir.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中把 chorale 作为完整借词处理，不宜分析为英语 choral 加后缀 -e；复数为 chorales。常见组合有 chorale tune（众赞歌曲调）、chorale harmonization（众赞歌和声编配）和 chorale prelude（众赞歌前奏曲）；choral（合唱的）、chorally（以合唱方式）和 chorus（合唱队；合唱）是相关词，并非都由 chorale 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, chorale is a complete borrowed base, not English choral plus a suffix -e; its plural is chorales. Common combinations include chorale tune, chorale harmonization, and chorale prelude. Choral, chorally, and chorus are related words rather than all being direct derivatives of chorale.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hymn（赞美诗）泛指宗教赞歌，范围更广；hymn tune（赞美诗曲调）明确只指旋律；choir（合唱团）对应 chorale 的团体义，而 chorale 常用于正式团名，并带有特定的音乐传统色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hymn is the broader term for a religious song; hymn tune refers specifically to its melody. Choir matches the ensemble sense of chorale, which often appears in formal group names and carries particular musical associations.

etymology_story.zh: 该词由 crank“曲柄”和 shaft“轴”复合而成，直接按机械结构命名。两个组成词都有古英语渊源，复合词后来成为发动机等机械中曲轴的标准名称。
etymology_story.en: The word combines crank and shaft, naming the component directly from its mechanical structure. Both elements have Old English ancestry, and the compound became the standard name for this component in engines and other machinery.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：crank“曲柄”＋shaft“轴”→crankshaft“曲轴”，属于名词复合词，没有常用的独立动词或形容词用法。复数：crankshafts；相关构词：crankpin“曲柄销”、crankcase“曲轴箱”、crankshaft bearing“曲轴轴承”。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: crank + shaft → crankshaft, a compound noun with no common independent verb or adjective use. Plural: crankshafts. Related formations include crankpin, crankcase, and crankshaft bearing.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: shaft“轴”是上位词，不一定带曲柄；crank axle“曲柄轴”是结构相近的术语，常见于机车语境。camshaft“凸轮轴”是相关而非同义的部件，主要利用凸轮控制气门等机构。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Shaft is the broader term and does not necessarily imply cranks; crank axle is a closely related structural term, especially in locomotive contexts. Camshaft names a related component rather than a synonym: it uses cams to operate mechanisms such as engine valves.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: crank 曲柄＋shaft 轴：轴上带曲柄，把活塞的直来直去变成旋转。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Crank + shaft: cranks on a shaft turn the pistons' back-and-forth movement into rotation.

meaning: 裙撑；使裙子蓬起的裙衬

pronunciation.note: 重音符号 ˈ 标示主重音；采用宽式音标。

forms: 此义可数；复数 crinolines；也可不可数地指硬衬布。
family: crinolined 穿着裙撑的；带裙撑的。

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆；crinoline + -ed → crinolined（穿着裙撑的），词尾 e 与后缀衔接。

etymology.text: 英语借自法语 crinoline，名称结合了拉丁语 crinis“毛发”和 linum“亚麻线”。早期材料含马毛与织线，后来名称转用于把裙子撑开的内衬和框架。

usage_note: 多见于19世纪服装史、戏服和礼服；不是外层裙子本身。

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自法语 crinoline，该法语词由 crin“马毛”和 lin“亚麻”组合而成，两者分别源自拉丁语 crinis“毛发”和 linum“亚麻”。它最初指含马毛的硬挺织物，后来转指用来撑起裙子的衬裙、框架及相应裙装。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed French crinoline, formed from crin 'horsehair' and lin 'flax,' ultimately from Latin crinis 'hair' and linum 'flax.' The name first referred to a stiff horsehair fabric and later extended to supporting petticoats, frameworks, and the skirts associated with them.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常把 crinoline 作为完整借词处理，不宜硬拆成常用英语词根和后缀；历史上的 crin＋lin 属于法语构词。相关形式：crinolines“多个裙撑或此类裙装”；crinolined“穿着或配有裙撑的”，为较少见的形容词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, crinoline is normally treated as a whole borrowed base rather than divided into productive English roots and suffixes; the historical crin + lin formation belongs to French. Related forms are the plural crinolines and the uncommon adjective crinolined, meaning wearing or fitted with a crinoline.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: petticoat“衬裙”强调穿在裙内的衣物，不一定硬挺；hoop skirt“圈撑裙／裙撑”强调环形支架，与框架式 crinoline 最接近；farthingale“鲸骨裙撑”指较早历史时期的裙撑，时代和轮廓不同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Petticoat emphasizes an underskirt and need not imply stiffness; hoop skirt emphasizes supporting hoops and is closest to a framework crinoline. Farthingale refers to an earlier historical skirt support with a different period and silhouette.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“马毛硬布”想到“撑开的裙摆”：材料名变成裙撑名。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture stiff horsehair cloth holding a skirt out: the material's name became the support's name.

meaning: 使非物质化；从有形状态消失

pronunciation.note: 重音符号 ˈ 标示主重音；采用宽式音标。

morphology.text: de-（去除、逆转）+ material（物质的）+ -ize（使成为）→ dematerialize（使非物质化）。

etymology.text: 英语在 materialize“使具体化、显现”前加 de- 形成反向意义；material 经法语和拉丁语 materialis 传来，与 materia“物质”有关。用“从有形变无形”记住方向。

usage_note: 可及物也可不及物；常见于科幻，金融中也可指取消纸质凭证而电子登记。

senses.meaning_zh: 使失去物质形态；从有形状态消失，常用于科幻语境

senses.pos: v. 动词（及物／不及物，专业用语）
senses.meaning_zh: 使生产或经济活动减少物质资源消耗；实现物质投入减量化
senses.meaning_en: To reduce the physical materials needed for production or economic activity.
senses.english_definition: If a business or economy dematerializes, it uses fewer physical materials to provide goods or services.
senses.collocation_en: dematerialize the economy; dematerialize production

senses.sentence_en: The strategy aims to dematerialize production by using less raw material per unit of output.
senses.sentence_zh: 该战略旨在降低单位产出的原材料用量，从而减少生产中的物质投入。

etymology_story.zh: 该词在 materialize“使具体化；显现”前加表示逆转或去除的 de- 构成；material 的词源可追溯到拉丁语 materia“材料；物质”。“失去物质形态”的意义后来扩展到以电子记录取代实体凭证，以及减少经济活动中的物质投入。
etymology_story.en: The word was formed by adding reversative or privative de- to materialize; material ultimately derives from Latin materia 'material; matter.' Its meaning of losing physical form later extended to replacing physical certificates with electronic records and reducing material inputs in economic activity.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：de-＋materialize；materialize 又可分为 material“物质的”＋-ize“使成为”。核心词族：dematerializes、dematerialized、dematerializing、dematerialization“非物质化；无纸化；物质投入减量化”；英式变体为 dematerialise、dematerialisation 及相应屈折形式。相关词族：material、materially、materiality、materialize、materialization、immaterial、immateriality、rematerialize、rematerialization。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: de- + materialize; materialize itself consists of material + -ize. The core family includes dematerializes, dematerialized, dematerializing, and dematerialization. British variants include dematerialise, dematerialisation, and their corresponding inflections. Related family members include material, materially, materiality, materialize, materialization, immaterial, immateriality, rematerialize, and rematerialization.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: disappear“消失”只说明不再可见，不强调物质形态的改变；digitize“数字化”强调转换为数字信息，不一定取消原有实体；dematerialize 则突出实体形式被消除、替代，或物质投入被减少。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Disappear means to become no longer visible without necessarily changing physical form; digitize emphasizes conversion into digital information and does not necessarily remove the original object. Dematerialize emphasizes eliminating or replacing physical form, or reducing material inputs.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: de- 去掉＋material 物质＋-ize 使成为：让“有形”退场。
mnemonic_anchor.en: De- reverses materialize: take away the material form.

pronunciation.note: 重音符号 ˈ 标示主重音；采用宽式音标。

morphology.text: frank（历史上有优良之意）+ incense（香）→ frankincense（乳香）；这是保留在整词中的历史组合。

etymology.text: 中古英语 fraunk encense 来自英法语 franc encens，由 franc 和 encens“香”组合，前者在这里通常解释为品质优良。记住它曾是珍贵的香树脂。

usage_note: 与宗教焚香、古代贸易及香水有关；不是英语 frank“坦率的”加上普通含义就能随意替换的短语。

etymology_story.zh: 中古英语通过古法语或盎格鲁法语借入 franc encens，其中 encens 意为“熏香”，franc 在这个组合中通常解释为“优质的；纯正的”。它原本相当于“上等熏香”，后来固定指乳香树脂。
etymology_story.en: Middle English borrowed Old French or Anglo-French franc encens, combining encens 'incense' with franc, usually interpreted here as 'high-quality' or 'pure.' The expression meant roughly 'fine incense' and became the established name for this particular aromatic resin.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常将 frankincense 作为固定整体词使用；历史构词可表示为 frank“优质的，历史义”＋incense“熏香”，其中 frank 不是现代常见的“坦率的”。该词通常不可数，无常用派生词；相关组合有 frankincense resin“乳香树脂”、frankincense oil“乳香精油”、frankincense tree“乳香树”。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English generally treats frankincense as a fixed lexical whole. Its historical structure is frank 'fine or high-quality' + incense; frank does not carry its usual modern meaning 'candid' here. The noun is normally uncountable and has no common derivatives; related combinations include frankincense resin, frankincense oil, and frankincense tree.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: olibanum“乳香”是同一树脂的另一名称，常见于技术或贸易语境；incense“熏香”是上位词，可指多种焚烧后散发香气的物质；myrrh“没药”是另一种芳香树脂，常与乳香并提，但不是同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Olibanum is another name for the same resin, especially in technical or commercial contexts; incense is the broader category of substances burned for their fragrance. Myrrh is a different aromatic resin often mentioned alongside frankincense, rather than a synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 历史上的 frank＝优质：frankincense 就是“上等的香”，即乳香。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Read historical frank as 'fine': frankincense is 'fine incense,' the fragrant resin.

usage_note: 常用 fraternize with somebody；经常出现于本不该过于亲近的群体之间，未必总带贬义。

senses.sentence_en: The visiting musicians fraternized with local performers after the concert.
senses.sentence_zh: 音乐会结束后，来访的音乐家与当地表演者进行了友好交流。

senses.meaning_zh: 与不应亲近的人交好；违规或不合身份地亲密交往
senses.meaning_en: To become friendly with people whom rules or social expectations discourage you from associating with.
senses.english_definition: If someone fraternizes with a particular group, they become friendly with its members even though this is considered improper or is forbidden.
senses.collocation_en: fraternize with the enemy; fraternize with subordinates
senses.collocation_zh: 与敌方人员亲善往来；与下属过从甚密
senses.sentence_en: The soldiers were ordered not to fraternize with the enemy.
senses.sentence_zh: 士兵们奉命不得与敌方人员亲善往来。

etymology_story.zh: 该词与法语 fraterniser 的形成有关，最终来自拉丁语 fraternus“兄弟般的”，其基础词是 frater“兄弟”。“像兄弟一样相处”的意义后来也用于描述跨越敌我、军阶或职业界限的交往，因此常带有“不合规定地亲近”的意味。
etymology_story.en: The word developed in connection with French fraterniser and ultimately derives from Latin fraternus 'brotherly,' based on frater 'brother.' The idea of behaving like brothers extended to friendships across enemy lines, ranks, or professional boundaries, giving the word its frequent implication of improper familiarity.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：fratern-，表示“兄弟”的黏着词根，＋-ize，动词后缀，→fraternize。核心词族：fraternizes、fraternized、fraternizing、fraternization“亲善往来；不当交往”、fraternizer“与人亲善交往者，较少见”；英式变体为 fraternise、fraternisation、fraterniser 及相应屈折形式。同根词：fraternal“兄弟般的”、fraternally“兄弟般地”、fraternity“兄弟情谊；同业团体；大学兄弟会”。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: fratern-, a bound root meaning 'brother,' + the verb-forming suffix -ize → fraternize. The core family includes fraternizes, fraternized, fraternizing, fraternization, and the less common agent noun fraternizer. British variants include fraternise, fraternisation, fraterniser, and their corresponding inflections. Related words are fraternal, fraternally, and fraternity.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: socialize“社交”最中性，强调与人相处；mingle“交际；混在一起”强调在人群中走动并与不同的人交流；consort with“与……交往”常带贬义或怀疑。fraternize 强调友好亲近，并常暗示跨越了某种不应跨越的界限。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Socialize is the most neutral term for spending time with others; mingle emphasizes moving among people and talking to different individuals; consort with often suggests disapproval or suspicion. Fraternize stresses friendly familiarity and frequently implies crossing an expected boundary.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: fratern-＝兄弟：处得像兄弟；若对象是敌人或受规则限制的人，就成了“不当亲近”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Fratern- means 'brother': treat someone like a brother; across a forbidden boundary, that becomes improper familiarity.

morphology.text: long（完整写出的）+ hand（书写）→ longhand（普通手写体），与 shorthand 对照记忆。

etymology.text: 英语由 long 和表示笔迹、书写的 hand 复合而成，两部分都来自古英语。名称强调把字母完整写出，与缩略的速记相对。

usage_note: 通常说 write in longhand；不指字体尺寸大，也不限于连笔书写。

etymology_story.zh: longhand 由 long 和表示“笔迹、书写方式”的 hand 复合而成，这两个词都源自古英语。它与 shorthand“速记”形成对照，强调把文字完整写出。
etymology_story.en: Longhand combines long with hand in its sense of handwriting or a style of writing; both elements descend from Old English. It developed in contrast with shorthand, emphasizing words written out in full.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：long（完整展开的）+ hand（书写）→ longhand。名词通常不可数，形容词和副词形式相同；没有常用的直接派生词。相关复合词有 shorthand（速记）、handwriting（手写；笔迹）和 handwritten（手写的），但它们不是由 longhand 派生的。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: long, suggesting full written forms, + hand, meaning writing, → longhand. The noun is normally uncountable, and the adjective and adverb have the same form; there are no common direct derivatives. Related compounds include shorthand, handwriting, and handwritten, but these are not derivatives of longhand.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: handwriting（手写；笔迹）范围更广，也可指个人字迹；ordinary script（普通书写体）强调常规字形；manuscript（手稿）指文稿本身，现代也可以是打印稿。longhand 特别强调完整书写，与速记相对。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Handwriting is broader and can refer to someone's individual writing style; ordinary script emphasizes conventional letter forms; manuscript names a document and can now include a typed text. Longhand specifically emphasizes full written forms in contrast with shorthand.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: long 是“完整展开”，hand 是“书写”：字母一个不少地写出来，就是 longhand。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of long as fully extended and hand as writing: write every letter out, and you have longhand.

meaning: 多中心的（涉及多个研究或医疗中心的）

pronunciation.note: 重音符号 ˈ 标示主重音；采用宽式音标。

forms: 形容词无复数；美式拼写 multicenter。
family: multicenter 美式拼写；multicentric 多中心的。

morphology.text: multi-（多个）+ centre（中心）→ multicentre（多中心的）。

etymology.text: 现代英语把拉丁语来源的 multi-“多”与 centre 组合；centre 经法语传入，上溯希腊语 kentron。记成“多个中心一起做”。

usage_note: 常放在 study、trial 等名词前，表示在多个机构开展；不等于一间医院有多个科室。

senses.meaning_zh: 多中心的；由多个研究或医疗中心共同开展的
senses.meaning_en: Involving several centres, especially research or medical centres.
senses.english_definition: A multicentre study or trial is carried out at several different research or medical centres.

senses.collocation_zh: 多中心研究；多中心临床试验

senses.sentence_zh: 这项治疗在一项涉及十二家医院的多中心试验中接受了评估。

etymology_story.zh: multicentre 是现代科学用语，由源自拉丁语 multus“多”的 multi- 与 centre“中心”组合而成。centre 经法语和拉丁语上溯至希腊语 kentron，原指“尖点”，后来也指圆规定位的中心点。
etymology_story.en: Multicentre is a modern scientific formation combining multi-, from Latin multus meaning many, with centre. Centre ultimately comes through French and Latin from Greek kentron, meaning a sharp point and, by extension, the central point marked by a compass.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：multi-（多）+ centre（中心）→ multicentre（多中心的）。美式拼写为 multicenter，也见带连字符的 multi-centre；相关形式有 multicentred／multicentered（具有多个中心的）、multicentric（多中心的）和 multicentricity（多中心性，专业用语）。这些形式意义相近，但在具体学科中未必能自由替换。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: multi- meaning many + centre → multicentre. The American spelling is multicenter, and the hyphenated form multi-centre also occurs. Related formations include multicentred or multicentered, multicentric, and the technical noun multicentricity; their meanings overlap, but they are not freely interchangeable in every discipline.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: multisite（多地点的）强调多个实施地点，不一定是独立机构；multi-institutional（多机构的）强调多个机构参与；collaborative（合作开展的）强调协作，本身不保证涉及多个中心。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Multisite emphasizes several locations, which need not be separate institutions; multi-institutional emphasizes participation by several institutions; collaborative emphasizes cooperation without necessarily implying several centres.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: multi-＝多个，centre＝中心：多个中心共同开展，就是 multicentre。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Multi- means many and centre means a centre: several centres working on one study make it multicentre.

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆；nautilus + -like → nautilus-like（像鹦鹉螺的），-like 表示相似。

etymology.text: 经新拉丁语和拉丁语传入，源于希腊语 nautilos，字面意思是“水手”，与 naus“船”有关。把它记成海中带壳的“小水手”。

usage_note: 本课只学海洋动物，首字母小写；作为船名或专名时的 Nautilus 不是本课义项。

etymology_story.zh: nautilus 经拉丁语传入英语，源于希腊语 nautilos，意为“水手”，与 naus“船”有关。古人曾用这个名称称呼被认为能借壳航行的海洋动物，后来它成为鹦鹉螺的名称。
etymology_story.en: Nautilus entered English through Latin from Greek nautilos, meaning sailor and related to naus, meaning ship. Ancient writers used the name for sea creatures believed to sail with their shells, and it later became the name for the chambered nautilus.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常把 nautilus 作为完整词干记忆，不拆成能自由组合的英语词素；复数为 nautiluses 或 nautili。相关构词有 nautiloid（鹦鹉螺类动物；鹦鹉螺类的），其中 -oid 表示“形似的、相关类型的”；nautilus-like（像鹦鹉螺的）是可按需构成的复合形容词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, nautilus is normally treated as a whole stem rather than divided into productive English morphemes; its plurals are nautiluses and nautili. A related formation is nautiloid, a noun or adjective referring to the broader nautiloid group, with -oid expressing resemblance or type. Nautilus-like is a freely formed compound adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: chambered nautilus（有分室外壳的鹦鹉螺）是常用的说明性名称；pearly nautilus（珍珠鹦鹉螺）突出壳内的珠母光泽，通常指现生鹦鹉螺。cephalopod（头足类动物）是上位词，还包括章鱼和鱿鱼，并非严格近义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Chambered nautilus is a common descriptive name; pearly nautilus highlights the shell's mother-of-pearl lining and generally refers to living nautiluses. Cephalopod is a broader category that also includes octopuses and squid, so it is not an exact synonym.

etymology_story.zh: organelle 形成于19世纪的生物学术语体系，以 organ“器官”配合指小词尾 -elle，表达“小器官”的意思。organ 最终源自希腊语 organon“工具、器具”，这一名称把细胞内的专门结构比作身体中分工明确的器官。
etymology_story.en: Organelle arose in nineteenth-century biological terminology as a diminutive formation based on organ, conveying the idea of a little organ. Organ ultimately comes from Greek organon, meaning tool or instrument, and the term compares specialized cell structures to organs with distinct jobs.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：organ（器官）+ -elle（指小词尾）→ organelle（细胞器）；复数为 organelles。直接相关形式有 organellar（细胞器的）、interorganelle（细胞器之间的）和 intraorganelle（细胞器内部的）；organ、organic、organism 属于较广的相关词族，不能视为由 organelle 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: organ + the diminutive suffix -elle → organelle; the plural is organelles. Directly related formations include organellar, interorganelle, and intraorganelle. Organ, organic, and organism belong to the broader related word family but are not derivatives of organelle.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cell organelle（细胞器）与 organelle 基本同义；subcellular structure（亚细胞结构）范围更广，还可包括不被归为细胞器的结构；cellular compartment（细胞区室）强调细胞内的分隔空间，不与所有类型的细胞器完全对应。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cell organelle is essentially synonymous with organelle; subcellular structure is broader and includes structures that may not be classified as organelles; cellular compartment emphasizes a distinct space within a cell and does not correspond exactly to every type of organelle.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: organ 是器官，-elle 表示“小”：细胞里的“小器官”就是 organelle。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Organ means organ and -elle makes it little: an organelle is a cell's little organ.

usage_note: 偏正式或历史叙述，通常指敌对或有争议的双方会谈；常见 hold a parley。

etymology_story.zh: parley 来自法语一类表示“谈话、商谈”的词形，与 parler“说话”有关；parler 上溯至通俗拉丁语 parabolare“交谈”，更早与表示“比喻、寓言”的 parabola 有关。英语中它逐渐特别用于敌对双方为商议条件而进行的会谈，动词则由名词转化而来。
etymology_story.en: Parley comes from French forms referring to speech or discussion and is related to parler, meaning to speak, ultimately from Vulgar Latin parabolare and Latin parabola, meaning comparison or parable. In English it became especially associated with discussions between opposing sides, and the verb developed from the noun.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语把 parley 作为完整词干；par- 和 -ley 在这里不是可拆解的现代词素。名词与动词通过零派生共用词形；名词复数及动词第三人称单数为 parleys，过去式和过去分词为 parleyed，现在分词为 parleying；parleyer（谈判者）是少见派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats parley as a whole stem; par- and -ley are not separate productive morphemes here. The noun and verb share their form through conversion. Parleys is the plural noun or third-person singular verb, parleyed is the past tense and past participle, and parleying is the present participle; parleyer is an uncommon derivative meaning a participant in a parley.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 作名词时，talks（会谈）最中性，negotiations（谈判）强调就具体条件争取协议，conference（会议）范围更广；相应动词为 talk、negotiate 和 confer。parley 尤其突出敌对双方之间的交涉，现代常带历史或文学色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: As nouns, talks is the most neutral, negotiations emphasizes bargaining over terms, and conference has a broader range; the corresponding verbs are talk, negotiate, and confer. Parley particularly suggests discussions between adversaries and often has a historical or literary tone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住词源中的“说话”：敌对双方暂时停手，开始谈条件，就是 parley。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor it to its historical meaning of speaking: opponents pause the fighting and talk terms—that is a parley.

etymology_story.en: Piton was borrowed from French, where it denotes a spike or pointed metal fitting. In English it became a climbing term for a spike driven into rock, and the noun also developed a technical verb use.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，piton 是不可再作有效拆分的借词，不宜拆成 pit + -on。词族与词形包括 pitons（复数或动词第三人称单数）、pitoned（过去式和过去分词）、pitoning（现在分词或动名词）及 pitonless（piton + -less，不使用岩钉的）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, piton is an unanalyzed loanword, not pit + -on. Its family and inflected forms include pitons, pitoned, pitoning, and pitonless (piton + -less, meaning without the use of pitons).

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: spike（尖钉）泛指尖头钉状物；peg（钉、桩）强调插入或打入后用于固定的物件；anchor（锚点、固定装置）强调固定功能。piton 专指打入岩缝的攀岩金属钉，可构成固定系统的一部分。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Spike is a general word for a pointed object; peg emphasizes an object inserted or driven in to secure something; anchor emphasizes a securing function. A piton is specifically a metal climbing spike driven into a rock crack and may form part of an anchoring system.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a metal spike in a rock crack: a piton is the spike, and to piton is to place or use it.

etymology_story.zh: 这是由 poly-“多”与 chlorinate“使氯化”组成的现代化学词。poly- 源于希腊语 polys“多”，chlorine“氯”的名称则源于希腊语 chlōros“黄绿色”，指氯气的颜色。
etymology_story.en: This modern chemical term combines poly-, meaning many, with chlorinate. Poly- comes from Greek polys, meaning many, while chlorine was named from Greek chlōros, meaning yellowish-green, in reference to the gas's color.

morphology_enriched.zh: poly-（多）+ chlorinate（使氯化）→ polychlorinate；chlorinate 又可分析为 chlorin(e)（氯，去掉词尾 e）+ -ate（构成动词）。直接词族包括 polychlorinates、polychlorinated、polychlorinating 和 polychlorination（多氯化）；相关基础词有 chlorine、chlorinate、chlorination 和 chlorinated。
morphology_enriched.en: Poly- (many) + chlorinate gives polychlorinate; chlorinate can itself be analyzed as chlorin(e), with the final e removed, + the verb-forming suffix -ate. The direct family includes polychlorinates, polychlorinated, polychlorinating, and polychlorination; related base words include chlorine, chlorinate, chlorination, and chlorinated.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: chlorinate（使氯化）不限定引入的氯原子数量；halogenate（使卤化）涵盖氯及其他卤素；perchlorinate（使完全氯化）强调达到完全氯化的程度。polychlorinate 强调引入多个氯原子，但不必达到完全氯化。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Chlorinate does not specify how many chlorine atoms are introduced; halogenate covers chlorine and other halogens; perchlorinate emphasizes exhaustive chlorination. Polychlorinate specifies the introduction of multiple chlorine atoms without necessarily implying complete chlorination.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: poly-＝多个，chlorinate＝引入氯：合起来就是“引入多个氯”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Poly- means many, and chlorinate means introduce chlorine: together, introduce multiple chlorine atoms.

etymology.text: 来自法语 rentier，关联 rente“收益、年金”，可上溯古法语。把它记成主要靠财产持续带来的收入生活的人。

etymology_story.zh: 借自法语 rentier，指领取 rente“定期收益、年金”的人，rente 最终与拉丁语 reddere“交还、支付”有关。英语保留了依靠财产收益生活的含义，并将其扩展用于描述具有类似收入结构的阶层、经济和国家。
etymology_story.en: Rentier was borrowed from French, where it denotes someone receiving a rente, or regular income or annuity; rente ultimately relates to Latin reddere, meaning to give back or pay. English retained the sense of living on property income and extended the term to classes, economies, and states with comparable income structures.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常把 rentier 作为完整借词处理；法语内部的构成为 rente（定期收益）+ -ier（表示相关的人），不宜把 -ier 当作可自由套用的英语后缀。主要词族包括 rentiers（复数）和 rentierism（rentier + -ism，食利主义或以食利收入为基础的经济制度）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English normally treats rentier as a complete loanword; its French structure is rente (regular income) + -ier (a person associated with it), rather than a freely productive English suffixation pattern. The main family includes rentiers and rentierism (rentier + -ism, an ideology or economic arrangement based on rentier income).

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: investor（投资者）强调投入资本的行为，不一定靠收益生活；landlord（房东、业主）强调出租房地产的身份；rent-seeker（寻租者）强调通过控制资源、特权或制度安排获取经济租金。rentier 强调收入和生活来源，不能与寻租者直接画等号。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Investor emphasizes committing capital and does not imply living on the returns; landlord identifies someone who rents out property; rent-seeker emphasizes obtaining economic rents through control of resources, privileges, or institutional arrangements. Rentier describes a source of income or livelihood and is not interchangeable with rent-seeker.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 由 rent“租金”联想到“让资产持续供养自己的人”，再扩展到食利型经济。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use rent as a cue: picture someone supported by recurring asset income, then extend that picture to an economy.

etymology_story.en: Rheumatology combines rheumat-, referring to rheumatic disease, with -logy, meaning a field of study. Rheumat- ultimately comes from Greek rheuma, meaning a flow or discharge, reflecting ancient explanations of certain painful conditions in terms of flowing bodily fluids before becoming part of a modern specialty name.

morphology_enriched.zh: rheumat-（风湿病）+ -o-（连接元音）+ -logy（学科）→ rheumatology。主要派生词包括 rheumatologist（风湿科医生）、rheumatological／rheumatologic（风湿病学的）和 rheumatologically（从风湿病学角度）；同词根相关词包括 rheumatic（风湿性的）、rheumatism（风湿病的传统统称）及 rheumatoid（类风湿的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Rheumat- (rheumatic disease) + linking -o- + -logy (a field of study) gives rheumatology. Principal derivatives include rheumatologist, rheumatological or rheumatologic, and rheumatologically; related words sharing the stem include rheumatic, rheumatism, and rheumatoid.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: rheumatic disease medicine（风湿性疾病诊疗）是解释性近义表达；clinical immunology（临床免疫学）研究更广泛的免疫系统疾病；orthopedics（骨科）侧重肌肉骨骼系统的结构问题及其治疗。后两者与风湿病学有交集，但不是同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Rheumatic disease medicine is a descriptive near-equivalent; clinical immunology covers a broader range of immune-system disorders; orthopedics focuses on structural conditions of the musculoskeletal system and their treatment. The latter two overlap with rheumatology but are not synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect rheumat- with rheumatic disease and -logy with a field of study: the specialty that studies and treats rheumatic conditions.

etymology_story.en: Sociocultural is a modern English formation combining socio-, meaning social, with cultural. Socio- ultimately relates to Latin socius, meaning companion, while cultural derives through culture from Latin cultura, meaning cultivation; the compound brings social relationships and cultural life into a shared perspective.

morphology_enriched.zh: socio-（社会）+ cultural（文化的）→ sociocultural；cultural = culture（文化，去掉词尾 e）+ -al（形容词后缀）。主要派生词包括 socioculturally（从社会文化角度）和 socioculturalism（社会文化主义，专业用语）；相关基础词包括 society、social、socially、culture 和 culturally。
morphology_enriched.en: Socio- (social) + cultural gives sociocultural; cultural is culture, with its final e removed, + the adjective suffix -al. Principal derivatives include socioculturally and the specialized term socioculturalism; related base-family words include society, social, socially, culture, and culturally.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: social（社会的）侧重社会关系、群体和制度；cultural（文化的）侧重共享的价值观、习俗和表达方式；societal（全社会的）侧重社会整体及其结构。sociocultural 明确同时涉及社会与文化，常强调两者相互影响。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Social emphasizes relationships, groups, and institutions; cultural emphasizes shared values, customs, and forms of expression; societal emphasizes society as a whole and its structures. Sociocultural explicitly combines social and cultural dimensions, often highlighting their interaction.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: socio- 看“人与人怎样组织”，cultural 看“大家怎样生活与思考”：合起来看社会文化。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Socio- asks how people organize themselves; cultural asks how they live and think: combine both perspectives.

etymology_story.zh: 借自新拉丁语 stalagmites，源头是希腊语 stalagma（水滴）或 stalagmos（滴落），均与“滴水”的动词有关。名称把形成过程中的“滴水”转用于指洞底逐渐积起的矿物柱。[《美国传统词典》词源](https://www.ahdictionary.com/word/search.html?q=stalagmite)
etymology_story.en: Borrowed from New Latin stalagmites, ultimately from Greek stalagma, meaning a drop, or stalagmos, meaning dripping, both related to a verb meaning to drip. The name connects dripping water with the mineral column that gradually accumulates on a cave floor. [American Heritage etymology](https://www.ahdictionary.com/word/search.html?q=stalagmite)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中以 stalagmite 为完整词基，不宜强拆为仍能自由组合的英语词素。屈折形式：stalagmites（石笋，复数）；直接派生：stalagmite 去末尾 e + -ic → stalagmitic（石笋的；石笋状的）。相关词 stalactite（钟乳石）有共同的滴水词源，但不是 stalagmite 的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, stalagmite functions as a complete base rather than a freely productive combination of English morphemes. Inflection: stalagmites, the plural; direct derivative: stalagmite minus final e + -ic → stalagmitic, meaning relating to or resembling stalagmites. Stalactite shares the historical dripping connection but is not derived from stalagmite.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有同样常用的严格同义词：speleothem（洞穴次生矿物沉积体）是上位词；dripstone（滴水石）泛指滴水沉积形成的石质结构；stalactite（钟乳石）是对照词，悬于洞顶，而 stalagmite 从洞底向上生长。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no equally common exact synonym: speleothem is the broader category of secondary cave mineral deposits; dripstone covers formations produced by dripping water; stalactite is a contrasting term for a formation hanging from the ceiling, whereas a stalagmite grows upward from the floor.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 滴水落地，积石向上；stalagmite 中的 g 联想 ground（地面）。这是拼写助记，并非词源拆解。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Drops reach the ground and build upward: connect the g in stalagmite with ground. This is a spelling mnemonic, not an etymological breakdown.

Modern usage chiefly concerns the Turkic language family and associated peoples, generally covering a wider scope than Turkish. morphology_enriched.zh: Turk（族名词基）+ -ic（与……有关的）→ Turkic；名词用法指整个语族，通常不加复数词尾。核心相关词族：Turk（土耳其人；依语境也可指突厥人）、Turks（复数）、Turkish（土耳其的；土耳其语）、Turkic-speaking（讲突厥语族语言的）；专业相关词：Turkology（突厥学）、Turkologist（突厥学者）、Turkological（突厥学的）。这些是相关词族成员，并非全由 Turkic 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Turk, the ethnic-name base, + -ic, meaning relating to, → Turkic; the noun names the language family and normally has no plural ending. The core related family includes Turk, Turks, Turkish, and Turkic-speaking; specialist relatives include Turkology, the study of Turkic languages and cultures, Turkologist, a scholar in that field, and Turkological, relating to that study. These are related family members rather than all being direct derivatives of Turkic.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有通用的严格同义词：Turkic-speaking（讲突厥语族语言的）明确强调语言使用；Turkish（土耳其的；土耳其语的）范围较窄；Pan-Turkic（泛突厥的）强调跨突厥语民族的联系、联合或共同认同，不能一般性替换 Turkic。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no general exact synonym: Turkic-speaking explicitly emphasizes language use; Turkish usually has the narrower reference to Turkey, its people, or its language; Pan-Turkic emphasizes connections, unity, or shared identity across Turkic peoples and is not a general substitute.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Turk + -ic：从一个族名扩展到整个语言家族；Turkish 是其中较具体的一支。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Turk + -ic: think of the wider language family, with Turkish as one specific member.

meaning: 傲慢的；自以为高人一等的

pronunciation.note: 重音符号 ˈ 标示主重音；采用宽式音标。

forms: 形容词；比较程度可用 more / most uppity。
family: uppitiness 傲慢；较少见拼写 uppityness。

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆；uppity + -ness → uppitiness（傲慢），y 变 i 后加后缀。

etymology.text: 19世纪美国英语口语中已有这个词，通常认为与 up 和带表现力的词尾 -ity 有关。可用“把自己摆在别人上面”帮助记住傲慢的语气。

usage_note: 非正式、略显旧式，带贬义；用于少数族裔尤其黑人时有强烈种族歧视历史，宜理解其语气，避免用来称呼他人。

senses.meaning_zh: 傲慢的；自命不凡的；摆架子的（非正式，贬义）
senses.meaning_en: Arrogant or self-important in a way the speaker dislikes; informal and disapproving.
senses.english_definition: If you describe someone as uppity, you mean that they act as though they are more important than you think they are.
senses.collocation_en: get uppity; an uppity attitude
senses.collocation_zh: 变得傲慢起来；傲慢的态度
senses.sentence_en: He called the restaurant uppity because the staff looked down on casually dressed customers.
senses.sentence_zh: 他称这家餐厅摆架子，因为店员看不起穿着休闲的顾客。

senses.meaning_zh: 被认为不知本分、不肯顺从的；敢于挑战权威的（非正式，常带贬意，有时用于反讽或自我认同）
senses.meaning_en: Considered insufficiently deferential or too assertive for one's supposed position; sometimes used ironically or approvingly.
senses.english_definition: Someone may be called uppity when they refuse to behave as submissively as other people expect them to.
senses.collocation_en: an uppity woman; get a little uppity
senses.collocation_zh: 被指不肯顺从的女人；表现得强硬一点、不再一味顺从
senses.sentence_en: She was dismissed as uppity simply for questioning the rules.
senses.sentence_zh: 她仅仅因为质疑那些规定，就被贬斥为不知本分。

etymology_story.zh: 出现于19世纪后期的美国英语，是由 up 发展出的表现性构词，用“往上摆”的意象表达自视过高或不肯屈从。它后来尤其与美国种族主义语境中对“不肯安守低位”的黑人的贬称相联系，这一历史仍影响其语气。[牛津词源说明](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/us/definition/english/uppity)；[用法背景](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/uppity)
etymology_story.en: The word emerged in late nineteenth-century American English as an expressive formation from up, suggesting elevated self-importance or a refusal to submit. It became particularly associated with racist descriptions of Black people deemed unwilling to accept an inferior position, a history that still affects its tone. [Oxford word origin](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/us/definition/english/uppity); [usage background](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/uppity)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代以 uppity 为完整形容词词基；历史上与 up 有关，不能把末尾机械地当作普通名词后缀 -ity。主要名词派生：uppity 的 y 变 i + -ness → uppitiness（傲慢；不肯顺从），亦作 uppityness；比较级、最高级通常用 more uppity、most uppity，也有 uppitier、uppitiest。相关词 uppish（傲慢的）是平行构词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats uppity as a complete adjective base; historically it is connected with up, but its ending should not be mechanically identified with the ordinary noun-forming suffix -ity. The main noun derivative is uppitiness, formed by changing y to i before -ness, also spelled uppityness; comparison usually uses more uppity and most uppity, with uppitier and uppitiest also occurring. Uppish, meaning arrogant, is a related parallel formation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: arrogant（傲慢的）泛指自视过高；haughty（高傲冷慢的）强调居高临下的姿态；presumptuous（冒昧放肆的）强调越过他人认定的权限或礼数。uppity 常额外暗示说话者认为对方没有资格如此自信或不服从。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Arrogant broadly describes an inflated sense of importance; haughty emphasizes a visibly superior, disdainful manner; presumptuous emphasizes overstepping assumed limits or conventions. Uppity often additionally suggests that the speaker thinks the person has no right to be so confident or assertive.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: up：把自己摆得高，或不肯被压低；两种语境共用一个“向上”的意象。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Up: placing yourself high, or refusing to be kept low—the same upward image connects both uses.

forms: 本词是复数，常用 the cognoscenti；单数 cognoscente。
family: cognoscente 行家；鉴赏家（单数）。

morphology.text: cognoscent-（知晓者的词干）+ -i（意大利语阳性复数词尾）→ cognoscenti（行家们）。

etymology.text: 借自意大利语 cognoscente 的复数，意为“懂行的人”，动词 cognoscere“知道”上溯拉丁语 cognoscere。记住他们是某个领域里真正“知其门道”的人。

usage_note: 偏正式，常用于艺术、音乐、美食等领域，通常带定冠词 the，谓语用复数。

senses.meaning_zh: 行家们；内行人士；鉴赏家群体（正式用语，尤用于艺术领域）
senses.meaning_en: People with expert knowledge or informed appreciation of a subject, especially an art; formal.
senses.english_definition: The cognoscenti are people who understand a particular subject very well and can appreciate qualities that others may miss.
senses.collocation_en: the literary cognoscenti; among the cognoscenti
senses.collocation_zh: 文学界的行家们；在内行人士中
senses.sentence_en: The painter was admired by the cognoscenti long before her work became widely known.
senses.sentence_zh: 这位画家的作品还远未广为人知时，就已受到行家们的推崇。

etymology_story.zh: 借自意大利语 cognoscente 的复数形式，意为“知情者、懂行者”；这个较古老的形式对应现代意大利语 conoscente，并上溯拉丁语 cognoscere（认识、了解）。英语将其用于某领域知识精深的群体，尤其是艺术鉴赏圈。[柯林斯词源与释义](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/us/dictionary/english/cognoscenti)
etymology_story.en: Borrowed as the plural of Italian cognoscente, meaning a knowledgeable person, an older form corresponding to modern Italian conoscente and ultimately derived from Latin cognoscere, to know or learn. English uses it for an informed circle of specialists, particularly in artistic appreciation. [Collins etymology and definition](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/us/dictionary/english/cognoscenti)

morphology_enriched.zh: 这是带意大利语复数形式的借词：cognoscente（单个行家）→ cognoscenti（行家们），词尾 -e 换为 -i；也可用 cognoscent- + -i 作历史形态分析。通常搭配复数谓语，如 the cognoscenti are；不要再加 -s。常见英语词源亲属包括 cognition（认知）、cognitive（认知的）、cognizant／cognisant（知晓的）、cognizance／cognisance（知晓；察觉），它们并非 cognoscenti 的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: This borrowing retains an Italian plural: cognoscente, one knowledgeable person, → cognoscenti, knowledgeable people, with final -e replaced by -i; historically it can also be analyzed as cognoscent- + -i. It normally takes a plural verb, as in the cognoscenti are, and does not take an additional -s. Common English etymological relatives include cognition, cognitive, cognizant or cognisant, and cognizance or cognisance; these are not direct derivatives of cognoscenti.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: connoisseurs（鉴赏家们）强调凭经验判断品质，尤用于艺术、饮食等；experts（专家们）强调专门知识或技能，适用范围最广；aficionados（爱好者们）强调热爱和投入，未必具有同等专业判断力。cognoscenti 常带“少数真正懂行者”的圈内意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Connoisseurs emphasize experienced judgment of quality, especially in art, food, or drink; experts emphasize specialized knowledge or skill across a broad range of fields; aficionados emphasize enthusiasm and devotion without necessarily implying equal expertise. Cognoscenti often suggests a select circle of people who truly know the field.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 连接 cognition（认知）：他们不仅喜欢，而且懂门道；词尾 -i 提醒你是一群人。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect it with cognition: these people do more than enjoy the subject—they understand it; final -i signals the group.

meaning: 喷出物（火山或撞击抛出的物质）

pronunciation.note: 重音符号 ˈ 标示主重音；采用宽式音标。

forms: 地质学中作复数名词，常接复数谓语；可用 a piece of ejecta 指一块喷出物。
family: eject 喷出；ejection 喷出过程。

morphology.text: e-（向外）+ ject-（投掷）+ -a（拉丁语中性复数词尾）→ ejecta（被抛出的东西）；这是历史词形线索。

etymology.text: 来自新拉丁语，承接拉丁语 ejectus“被抛出的”的中性复数形式，关联 ejicere“向外抛”。想象火山或撞击把物质抛向四周的画面。

usage_note: 常用于火山学和行星地质学；不限定为熔岩，也可包括碎岩、火山灰等物质。

senses.pos: n. 名词（复数形式，常作物质总称）
senses.meaning_zh: 喷出物；抛出物，尤指火山喷发或天体撞击抛出的物质
senses.meaning_en: Material thrown out, especially by a volcanic eruption or an impact.
senses.english_definition: Ejecta are materials thrown out of a volcano or away from the site where an object strikes a surface.
senses.collocation_en: volcanic ejecta; an ejecta blanket
senses.collocation_zh: 火山喷出物；抛射物覆盖层
senses.sentence_en: A blanket of ejecta surrounded the impact crater.
senses.sentence_zh: 撞击坑周围覆盖着一层抛射物。

etymology_story.zh: 借自新拉丁语 ejecta，承接拉丁语 ejectus（被抛出的）的中性复数形式；ejectus 是意为“向外抛”的动词 eicere 的过去分词。这个字面上的“被抛出的东西”成为科学语境中喷出或抛出物质的总称。[《美国传统词典》词源](https://www.ahdictionary.com/word/search.html?q=ejecta)
etymology_story.en: Borrowed from New Latin ejecta, continuing the neuter plural of Latin ejectus, the past participle of eicere, meaning to throw out. Literally denoting things thrown out, it became a scientific term for expelled material. [American Heritage etymology](https://www.ahdictionary.com/word/search.html?q=ejecta)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 ejecta 是完整的科学借词；历史结构可理解为 e-（向外）+ ject-（投掷）+ -a（拉丁语中性复数词尾），并非现代英语中可任意套用的复数规则。它通常作为喷出物总称使用，不说 an ejecta，单个碎块用 a piece of ejecta。核心相关词族：eject（喷出；弹出）、ejects／ejected／ejecting（动词变化）、ejection（喷出；弹出）、ejector（喷射器；弹出装置）、ejective（喷音；喷音的，语音学术语）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, ejecta is a complete scientific borrowing; its historical structure can be understood as e-, out, + ject-, throw, + -a, the Latin neuter plural ending, rather than a productive English plural pattern. It commonly names expelled material collectively: use a piece of ejecta, not an ejecta, for one fragment. The core related family includes eject; its inflections ejects, ejected, and ejecting; ejection, the act of expelling; ejector, an expelling device; and ejective, a phonetic term used as a noun and adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: ejected material（抛出物质）是范围最接近的中性释义；tephra（火山碎屑物）专指火山喷出的碎屑，不包括撞击抛出物；debris（碎屑；残骸）强调破碎后的物质，不要求经过喷射或抛射。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Ejected material is the closest neutral paraphrase; tephra specifically means fragmental material expelled by a volcano and excludes impact ejecta; debris emphasizes broken remains without requiring that they were expelled or thrown outward.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: eject 是“向外抛”，ejecta 就是“抛出去的那些东西”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Eject means throw out; ejecta are the things thrown out.

etymology.text: 借自法语 exactitude，由 exact 和表示状态的词尾构成；exact 最终来自拉丁语 exactus，含经过严格要求、完成的意思。可用“一点也不差”来记其严谨意味。

usage_note: 正式用语，常用 with exactitude；比普通的 accuracy 更有书面色彩。

senses.english_definition: Exactitude is the quality of being completely accurate or taking great care to get every detail right.
senses.collocation_en: with great exactitude; mathematical exactitude
senses.collocation_zh: 极其精确地；数学般的精确
senses.sentence_en: She reproduced the pattern with remarkable exactitude.
senses.sentence_zh: 她极其精确地复现了这个图案。

etymology_story.zh: 英语 exactitude 借自法语 exactitude，其基础 exact 最终来自拉丁语 exactus，包含完成、经过严格要求的意思。英语沿用了其精确、严谨的含义。[词源参考](https://www.etymonline.com/word/exactitude)
etymology_story.en: English borrowed exactitude from French exactitude, based on exact and ultimately Latin exactus, associated with completion and strict requirements. It retained the meaning of accuracy and meticulous care. [Etymology reference](https://www.etymonline.com/word/exactitude)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代词族分析：exact（精确的）+ -itude（性质、状态）→ exactitude（精确）；这是对借入词的结构分析，并非该词最初在英语中的独立造词过程。核心词族：exact（形容词：精确的；动词：索取、强求）、exactly（精确地；正是）、exactness（精确性）、inexact（不精确的）、inexactly（不精确地）、inexactness（不精确性）；动词分支有 exacted（索取了）、exacting（要求严格的）、exactingly（苛求地）、exactingness（苛刻）、exaction（强行索取；苛征）、exactor（强行索取者）。exactitude 通常为不可数名词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern family analysis: exact + -itude, a suffix expressing a quality or state, → exactitude; this analyzes an established borrowing rather than its original formation within English. The core family includes exact (adjective: precise; verb: demand or obtain), exactly, exactness, inexact, inexactly, and inexactness. The verb branch includes exacted, exacting, exactingly, exactingness, exaction, and exactor. Exactitude is normally uncountable.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: accuracy（准确性）强调符合事实或正确结果；precision（精密性、精确性）强调细节或测量的精细程度；exactness（精确性）与 exactitude 最接近，但更中性，exactitude 更正式，也常突出一丝不苟的态度。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Accuracy emphasizes agreement with facts or a correct result; precision emphasizes fine detail or measurement; exactness is the closest neutral equivalent, while exactitude is more formal and often suggests meticulous care.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: exact 是“一点不差”，exactitude 就是“做到一点不差的严谨”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Exact means nothing is off; exactitude is the care and accuracy that keep every detail exact.

etymology_story.zh: homeboy 由 home 和 boy 复合而成；现代“同乡”义见于二十世纪的非裔美国人英语，后来扩展为亲近伙伴。更早虽有同形用法，但其含义不同，不能直接等同于今天的俚语义。[词源参考](https://www.etymonline.com/word/homeboy)
etymology_story.en: Homeboy combines home and boy; its modern hometown sense is recorded in twentieth-century African American English and later broadened to a close companion. Earlier uses of the same form had different meanings and should not be equated with the current slang senses. [Etymology reference](https://www.etymonline.com/word/homeboy)

morphology_enriched.zh: home（家乡、社区）+ boy（男孩、男子）→ homeboy；复数 homeboys。相关词有缩略形式 homie、homey（哥们儿；此处为名词），以及平行复合词 homegirl（同乡女性；女伙伴）；没有常用的派生动词或副词。homeboy 在称呼语中使用时仍是名词。
morphology_enriched.en: Home + boy → homeboy; plural homeboys. Related forms include the shortened nouns homie and homey, plus the parallel compound homegirl for a female from the same community or a close female friend. There are no common derived verbs or adverbs. Direct address with homeboy remains a noun use.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: homie（哥们儿）是更简短、同样带俚语色彩的近义词；buddy（朋友、伙计）更通用，不要求共同地域背景；hometown friend（家乡的朋友）明确强调同乡关系，但不带 homeboy 的群体认同色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Homie is a shorter slang equivalent; buddy is more general and does not imply a shared community; hometown friend explicitly identifies a shared place of origin without the same in-group flavor.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 同一个 home 的 boy → 同乡伙伴 → 亲近的哥们儿。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A boy from your home community becomes a familiar companion: shared home → close friend.

meaning: 破除传统观念；挑战公认信条

pronunciation.note: 重音符号 ˈ 标示主重音；采用宽式音标。

morphology.text: icono-（形象、偶像）+ -clasm（打破）→ iconoclasm；从打破偶像引申为挑战传统。

etymology.text: 借自新拉丁语 iconoclasmus，关联希腊语中的“毁像者”和表示行为的词尾。原来指破坏宗教图像，后来引申为打破人们奉为权威的观念。

usage_note: 常用于文化、艺术及思想评论；本课是引申义，未必涉及实际破坏物品。

etymology_story.zh: iconoclasm 的词源可追溯至希腊语 eikōn（图像）和表示打破的词干 klas-，其原始意象是毁坏宗教圣像。英语先使用其毁像义，十九世纪又发展出攻击受尊崇观念和制度的比喻义。[词源参考](https://www.etymonline.com/word/iconoclasm)
etymology_story.en: Iconoclasm ultimately draws on Greek eikōn, meaning image, and the breaking stem klas-, originally evoking the destruction of religious images. English first used the literal sense and developed the figurative sense of attacking cherished beliefs and institutions in the nineteenth century. [Etymology reference](https://www.etymonline.com/word/iconoclasm)

morphology_enriched.zh: icono-（图像、偶像）+ -clasm（打破、破坏）→ iconoclasm。核心词族：iconoclast（圣像破坏者；挑战传统者）、iconoclastic（破坏圣像的；反传统的）、iconoclastically（以挑战传统的方式）；iconoclast 的复数为 iconoclasts。iconoclasm 通常为不可数名词，没有常用的对应动词。
morphology_enriched.en: Icono- (image or idol) + -clasm (breaking or destruction) → iconoclasm. The core family includes iconoclast, a destroyer of religious images or challenger of convention; iconoclastic, the adjective; and iconoclastically, the adverb. The plural of iconoclast is iconoclasts. Iconoclasm is normally uncountable and has no common corresponding verb.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: nonconformity（不墨守成规）侧重不遵循常规，未必主动攻击传统；irreverence（不敬、对权威缺少敬畏）侧重态度；radicalism（激进主义）主张根本改变，而 iconoclasm 特别强调打破被奉为权威的观念。三者主要对应其比喻义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Nonconformity means departing from convention without necessarily attacking it; irreverence describes a lack of customary respect; radicalism advocates fundamental change, whereas iconoclasm specifically attacks revered beliefs or authorities. These are near-synonyms chiefly for the figurative sense.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 打碎有形的偶像，也打破思想中的偶像。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Break a physical idol; then picture breaking an unquestioned intellectual idol.

etymology_story.en: Koala comes from a Dharug animal name recorded as gula and related forms, with early English spellings including coola and koolah. The modern spelling may have arisen through a misreading of those earlier forms. [Etymology reference](https://ahdictionary.com/word/search.html?q=koala)

morphology_enriched.zh: koala 是整体借入的单一词素，现代英语中不能可靠地拆成有意义的词根和词缀。复数为 koalas；koala + -like → koala-like（像考拉的）。相关复合表达有 koala bear（考拉的俗称）和 koala habitat（考拉栖息地）；koala 作名词定语不构成独立形容词词性。
morphology_enriched.en: Koala is a monomorphemic borrowing with no reliable division into meaningful English roots and affixes. Its plural is koalas; koala + -like produces koala-like. Related compounds include koala bear and koala habitat. Attributive noun use does not establish a separate adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: koala bear（考拉、树袋熊）是常见俗称，但考拉并非熊；native bear（澳大利亚本土熊）是较旧的俗称，也容易造成分类误解；marsupial（有袋动物）是上位词，不能作为精确同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Koala bear is a common informal alternative, although a koala is not a bear; native bear is an older informal name with the same misleading implication. Marsupial is a broader category, not an exact synonym.

etymology_story.zh: lobelia 借自新拉丁语属名 Lobelia，该名称纪念佛兰德植物学家 Matthias de Lobel。英语随后用这一属名指称属内植物，包括园艺栽培的观赏种类。[词源与释义参考](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/lobelia)
etymology_story.en: Lobelia was borrowed from the New Latin genus name Lobelia, honoring the Flemish botanist Matthias de Lobel. English adopted the name for plants in the genus, including species cultivated as ornamentals. [Etymology and definition reference](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/lobelia)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代普通英语中，lobelia 通常作为整体植物名称处理；历史命名结构为 Lobel（人名）+ -ia（植物属名常见词尾）。复数为 lobelias；相关专业词有 lobeliaceous（半边莲类的；传统分类中半边莲科的），可分析为 lobeli(a) + -aceous，以及 lobeline（洛贝林；山梗菜碱）。这些专业词不代表 lobelia 另有常用动词或形容词词性。
morphology_enriched.en: In ordinary modern English, lobelia is treated as a whole plant name; its historical naming structure is Lobel, a personal name, + -ia, a common ending in botanical genus names. The plural is lobelias. Specialist relatives include lobeliaceous, analyzable as lobeli(a) + -aceous and referring to lobelias or their traditional family, and lobeline, an alkaloid name. These relatives do not establish common verb or adjective uses of lobelia itself.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: lobelia 没有覆盖整个属的常用精确同义词：edging lobelia（翠蝶花）通常指 Lobelia erinus；cardinal flower（鲜红半边莲）通常指 Lobelia cardinalis；Indian tobacco（祛痰半边莲）指 Lobelia inflata。这些是特定种的俗名，不能在所有语境中替换 lobelia。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Lobelia has no common exact synonym covering the entire genus: edging lobelia usually means Lobelia erinus; cardinal flower usually means Lobelia cardinalis; Indian tobacco means Lobelia inflata. These are common names for particular species and are not universally interchangeable with lobelia.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Lobel 的名字变成 Lobelia：用植物学家的名字记住一属花。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Lobel → Lobelia: remember a genus of flowers through the botanist it honors.

etymology_story.zh: 该词最终源于拉丁语 omnivorus，意为“什么都吃的”，由 omnis（所有的）和 vorare（吞食）组成。在英语中，它成为表示兼食植物和动物的生物的名词。
etymology_story.en: The word ultimately comes from Latin omnivorus, meaning 'all-eating', from omnis, 'all', and vorare, 'to devour'. In English, it became a noun for a creature that eats both plants and animals.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：omni-（全部）+ -vore（以某类食物为食的动物或人）。常用词族：omnivores（复数）、omnivorous（杂食的）、omnivorously（以杂食方式）、omnivorousness（杂食性）、omnivory（杂食现象或习性）；后两种名词中，omnivory 更常用于生态学。相关构词：herbivore（植食动物）、carnivore（肉食动物）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: omni- ('all') + -vore ('an animal or person eating a particular kind of food'). The word family includes omnivores, omnivorous, omnivorously, omnivorousness, and omnivory; omnivory is especially useful in ecology. Related formations include herbivore and carnivore.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: omnivorous animal（杂食动物）是直接释义；generalist feeder（广食性取食者）强调食物来源广，但不一定兼食植物和动物；非正式表达 all-round eater（什么都吃的人）主要描述人的饮食习惯。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Omnivorous animal is a direct equivalent. Generalist feeder emphasizes a broad diet without necessarily implying both plant and animal foods. The informal expression all-round eater mainly describes a person's eating habits.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: omni-＝全，-vore＝吃者：植物和动物都吃，就是杂食者。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Omni- means 'all' and -vore means 'eater': eating both plants and animals makes an omnivore.

etymology_story.en: The word comes from French ovoïde, formed from Latin ovum, 'egg', and the Greek-derived shape element -oid. English uses it both to describe an egg-like shape and to name an object with that shape.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词分析：ov-（蛋；与 ovum 同源）+ -oid（形似……的）；词干也见于组合形式 ovo-。词族：ovoids（名词复数）、ovoidal（卵形的）、ovoidally（呈卵形地，少用）。相关而非直接派生的词有 ovum（卵；复数 ova）、ovate（卵形的，常用于叶片）和 oviform（蛋形的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern analysis: ov- ('egg', related to ovum) + -oid ('resembling'); the stem also appears as the combining form ovo-. The family includes ovoids, ovoidal, and the uncommon adverb ovoidally. Related rather than directly derived words include ovum, plural ova, ovate, and oviform.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：pectoral → pec，属于截短构词，不能再把 pec 拆成现代英语词根和词缀。常用形式与组合：pecs（复数）、pec deck（夹胸训练器）、pec tear（胸肌撕裂）；原词家族包括 pectoral（胸部的；胸肌）和 pectorals（胸肌）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: pectoral → pec by clipping; pec has no further productive root-and-affix breakdown in modern English. Common forms and combinations include pecs, pec deck, and pec tear. The source-word family includes pectoral and pectorals.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pectoral（胸肌）是较完整、较中性的说法；chest muscle（胸部肌肉）是范围更宽的通俗表达；pectoralis major（胸大肌）是精确的解剖学名称，指健身语境中 pec 通常所指的大块胸肌。

etymology_story.zh: 该词经新拉丁语进入英语，由表示“近”的 peri- 和希腊语 hēlios（太阳）构成。它作为天文学术语，专指绕日轨道上最接近太阳的位置。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English through New Latin, combining peri-, meaning 'near', with Greek hēlios, 'Sun'. As an astronomical term, it names the position in a solar orbit nearest to the Sun.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代学术构词可分析为 peri-（近）+ helion（与太阳有关的术语成分，源于 hēlios）；peri- 在这里不能解释为“周围”。词族：perihelia（传统复数）、perihelions（规则复数）、perihelic 和 perihelial（近日点的，均为专业用语）。对应的反义术语为 aphelion（远日点）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern scientific vocabulary, the word can be analyzed as peri- ('near') + helion (a Sun-related technical element from hēlios); peri- does not mean 'around' here. The family includes the plurals perihelia and perihelions and the technical adjectives perihelic and perihelial. Its opposite is aphelion.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: closest approach to the Sun（最接近太阳的位置或过程）是通俗释义；periapsis（近拱点）适用于绕任何中心天体的轨道；periastron（近星点）用于绕恒星的轨道。后两者适用范围更广，不能在所有语境中与 perihelion 自由替换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Closest approach to the Sun is a plain-language paraphrase. Periapsis applies to an orbit around any central body, while periastron applies to an orbit around a star. The latter two have broader applications and are not freely interchangeable with perihelion in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: peri-＝近，heli-＝太阳：轨道上最近太阳的一点。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Peri- means 'near' and heli- points to the Sun: the nearest point to the Sun.

etymology_story.zh: 该词最终来自拉丁语 praecessio（先行），与 praecedere（走在前面）有关，由 prae-（在前）和 cedere（行进）组成。天文学中的名称与分点相对于恒星逐渐向西移动有关，后来也用于旋转轴和轨道方向的进动。
etymology_story.en: The word ultimately comes from Latin praecessio, 'a going before', related to praecedere, from prae-, 'before', and cedere, 'to go'. Its astronomical use refers to the equinoxes gradually shifting westward relative to the stars, and the term also came to describe changes in the direction of rotating axes and orbits.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代词族关系：precess（发生进动）+ -ion（过程或现象）→ precession；历史词素可分析为 pre-（在前）+ cess-（行进）+ -ion。词族：precesses、precessed、precessing（动词形式）、precessional（进动的；岁差的）、precessionally（以进动方式，少用）。precede（先于）与它同源，但不是由 precession 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern word-family relation: precess ('undergo precession') + -ion ('process or phenomenon') → precession; historically, the elements are pre- ('before') + cess- ('go') + -ion. The family includes precesses, precessed, precessing, precessional, and the uncommon adverb precessionally. Precede is historically related but is not a direct derivative of precession.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: axis drift（轴向漂移）是较宽泛的描述，不限定具体运动机制；wobble（摇摆）是通俗近似说法，物理含义不够精确；nutation（章动）指叠加在进动上的周期性小幅摆动，是相关现象而非严格近义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Axis drift is a broader description that does not specify the mechanism. Wobble is an accessible but physically imprecise approximation. Nutation means a smaller periodic oscillation superimposed on precession, so it is a related phenomenon rather than an exact synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 想象陀螺仍在自转，而轴尖缓慢画圈：轴的方向也在“行进”，就是进动。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a spinning top whose axis slowly circles: the object spins while its axis also moves.

etymology_story.zh: 英语经印地语和乌尔都语借入此词，最终源自阿拉伯语 ṣāḥib，意为“同伴、拥有者或主人”。它在南亚发展为尊称，并在殖民时期的英语中尤其与对欧洲男子的称呼联系起来。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed the word through Hindi and Urdu from Arabic ṣāḥib, meaning 'companion, possessor, or master.' It developed into a respectful title in South Asia and became especially associated in colonial English with European men.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中视为不可再作常规拆分的借词：sahib；复数为 sahibs。相关借词 memsahib（旧时对欧洲女性的敬称）的前半部分 mem 来自英语 ma'am；其复数为 memsahibs。没有常用的英语派生动词或形容词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, sahib is an unanalyzed loanword; its plural is sahibs. The related loanword memsahib, historically a respectful title for a European woman, contains mem, derived from English ma'am; its plural is memsahibs. There are no common derived English verbs or adjectives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sir（先生）是更普遍的礼貌称呼；master（主人、老爷）突出主仆关系；sahib 带有特定的南亚文化背景，在英语中常具有殖民时期色彩，三者不能在所有场景下互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sir is a more general polite form of address; master emphasizes authority over servants; sahib carries a specifically South Asian background and often a colonial association in English, so these terms are not interchangeable in every context.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是不可常规拆分的借词：schnapps；末尾的 -s 不是英语复数词尾。常作不可数名词，也可用 a schnapps 表示一份酒；schnaps 是另一种拼写。常见组合有 peach schnapps（桃味甜酒）和 peppermint schnapps（薄荷味甜酒），没有常用的派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, schnapps is an unanalyzed loanword; its final -s is not an English plural ending. It is usually uncountable, although a schnapps can mean one serving; schnaps is an alternative spelling. Common combinations include peach schnapps and peppermint schnapps, and there is no established family of common derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Spirits is the broad category of distilled alcoholic drinks; brandy is distilled from wine or fermented fruit juice and can overlap with traditional fruit schnapps; liqueur emphasizes added sweetness and flavoring and is closer to sweet American schnapps.

etymology_story.zh: 由英语 slip 和 stream 合成，早期用于航空语境，指螺旋桨产生的气流，后来也指运动物体后方的尾流。利用尾流省力的现象进一步产生了“借势”的比喻用法，以及软件更新整合的技术用法。
etymology_story.en: Formed from English slip and stream, the word was used in early aviation for the airflow produced by a propeller and later for airflow behind moving objects. Taking advantage of this airflow also inspired figurative uses about benefiting from another's progress and a technical use for integrating software updates.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代复合词：slip（滑行）＋ stream（流）→ slipstream；名词可直接转作动词，不另加词缀。常见形式为 slipstreams（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、slipstreamed（过去式及过去分词）和 slipstreaming（现在分词，也可作动名词表示跟随尾流或整合更新这一活动）。
morphology_enriched.en: A modern compound: slip ('move smoothly') + stream ('a flow') → slipstream. The noun also functions as a verb through conversion without an added affix. Common forms are slipstreams, the noun plural or third-person singular verb; slipstreamed, the past tense and past participle; and slipstreaming, the present participle or an activity noun.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: wake（尾流）可用于空气或水等介质，范围更广；drafting（跟随尾流行进）常见于美式赛车和自行车语境，强调利用前方选手降低风阻；integrate（整合）对应软件义，但本身不限定整合进安装文件。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Wake is broader and can describe disturbed air or water behind a moving object; drafting, especially in American racing and cycling usage, emphasizes following a competitor to reduce drag; integrate matches the software sense but does not specifically imply incorporation into installation files.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 顺着前方留下的“流”滑行：实义是跟随尾流，比喻义是借势，软件义是把更新并入安装流程。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Slip along in the stream left ahead of you: follow airflow, benefit from existing momentum, or fold updates into an installation.

etymology_story.zh: 英语经西班牙语 alpaca 借入，通常追溯到安第斯地区的艾马拉语 allpaqa。这个动物名称后来也用于指它的毛纤维，以及用这种纤维制成的织物。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed alpaca from Spanish, which is generally traced to Aymara allpaqa in the Andes. The animal's name was extended to its fiber and to fabric made from that fiber.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中视为不可常规拆分的借词：alpaca；指动物时为可数名词，复数 alpacas，指纤维或织物时通常不可数。常见名词组合包括 alpaca wool（羊驼毛）、alpaca yarn（羊驼毛纱线）和 alpaca farming（羊驼养殖）；这些组合中的 alpaca 是名词作定语，无须另立常用形容词词性。没有常用的派生动词或副词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, alpaca is an unanalyzed loanword. It is countable for the animal, with plural alpacas, and usually uncountable for the fiber or fabric. Common noun combinations include alpaca wool, alpaca yarn, and alpaca farming; alpaca functions as a noun modifier in these expressions rather than requiring a separate common adjective entry. There are no common derived verbs or adverbs.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 动物义没有常用的完全同义词：llama（美洲驼）是另一种体型通常更大的近缘动物；纤维义中的 fleece（动物剪下的毛、毛被）范围更广；wool（羊毛；毛纤维）通常指绵羊毛，但也可泛指某些其他动物的毛纤维。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no common exact synonym for the animal: a llama is a different, usually larger relative. For the fiber sense, fleece is broader and refers to an animal's coat or the fiber shorn from it; wool usually means sheep's fiber but can also refer more broadly to fiber from certain other animals.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture an Andean alpaca with a soft fleece: animal → fiber → fabric.

etymology_story.zh: 这是现代科学英语中由 amino-（氨基）与 glycoside（糖苷）组成的名称，反映了这类抗生素的化学结构。glycoside 中的糖相关词根最终源于希腊语 glykys，意为“甜”。

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：amino-（氨基）+ glycoside（糖苷）→ aminoglycoside；复数为 aminoglycosides。相关词族包括 amino（氨基的）、glycoside（糖苷）和 glycosidic（糖苷的）；这些是构词成分的相关词，并非都直接由 aminoglycoside 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: amino- + glycoside → aminoglycoside; the plural is aminoglycosides. Related vocabulary includes amino, glycoside, and glycosidic; these belong to the families of its components rather than all being direct derivatives of aminoglycoside.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no common exact synonym. Antibiotic is a broader category; antibacterial, used as a noun, has a wider scope; gentamicin names one member of the class rather than the class itself.

etymology_story.zh: 美国专栏作家 Herb Caen 于1958年创造了 beatnik，将 Beat Generation 中的 Beat 与受 Sputnik 一词启发的 -nik 结合。这个带有戏谑意味的标签后来常指垮掉派文化的追随者或其刻板形象，不完全等同于该文学运动的核心作家。
etymology_story.en: American columnist Herb Caen coined beatnik in 1958 by combining Beat, from Beat Generation, with -nik, inspired by Sputnik. The initially mocking label came to describe followers or stereotypes of Beat culture, rather than precisely identifying the movement’s central writers.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：Beat（垮掉派）+ -nik（与某种活动、身份或思想相关的人）→ beatnik；复数为 beatniks。Beat、Beat Generation 和 beatnik 是相关表达，但 beatnik 并不是动词 beat 的屈折变化；作前置修饰语时通常仍可分析为名词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: Beat + -nik, a suffix identifying a person associated with an activity, identity, or outlook, → beatnik; the plural is beatniks. Beat, Beat Generation, and beatnik are related expressions, but beatnik is not an inflected form of the verb beat; its attributive uses can normally be analyzed as noun modification.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：book（书）+ worm（虫）→ bookworm，是名词复合词；复数为 bookworms。派生形容词 bookwormish 表示“书虫般的、爱埋头读书的”，但不常见；相关的 bookish（爱读书的；书卷气的）由 book + -ish 构成，并非直接由 bookworm 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: book + worm → bookworm, a compound noun; the plural is bookworms. The derivative adjective bookwormish means book-loving or absorbed in books but is uncommon; the related adjective bookish comes from book + -ish rather than directly from bookworm.

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自法语 camisole，其词源最终可追溯到晚期拉丁语 camisia，意为“衬衣”。这个词早先用于一些短上衣或贴身上衣，现代英语中的常用义逐渐集中为女式轻薄无袖背心。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed camisole from French; the word ultimately traces back to Late Latin camisia, meaning “shirt.” Earlier uses covered various short or close-fitting upper-body garments, while the usual modern English meaning narrowed to a light sleeveless women’s top.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中以 camisole 为完整借词词干，不宜拆成 cami + sole；复数为 camisoles。cami 是常见的非正式截短形式，复数为 camis；camisole top 是名词组合，本词没有常用的后缀派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, camisole is a complete borrowed base and should not be analyzed as cami + sole; its plural is camisoles. Cami is a common informal clipping, with the plural camis; camisole top is a noun combination, and there is no common family of suffix-derived forms.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cami 是 camisole 的非正式简称，意义基本相同；tank top（背心）通常肩带更宽，风格也更偏休闲；slip（衬裙）一般向下延伸，通常比 camisole 长。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cami is an informal shortened form with essentially the same meaning; tank top usually suggests broader shoulder straps and a more casual style; slip generally extends farther down the body and is usually longer than a camisole.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“衬衣”缩到轻薄上身衣物：两根肩带，一件 camisole。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Follow the old “shirt” idea to a light upper-body garment: two straps and a camisole.
