etymology_story.zh: 英语在19世纪中叶借入法语 canard，原义为“鸭子”；“谣言”义与法语旧习语 vendre des canards à moitié（字面为“半卖鸭子”，意为欺骗）有关，但该习语背后的故事已经失传。航空义另由早期这类飞机像鸭子的外形发展而来。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed French canard, meaning “duck,” in the mid-nineteenth century; its false-report sense developed from an older French expression about half-selling ducks, meaning to deceive, whose underlying story is unknown. The aviation sense arose separately from the ducklike appearance of early aircraft of this design. [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/canard)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语将 canard 视为不可再分析的借词词基，不宜拆成 can + -ard。屈折形式：canards（复数）；常见复合表达：canard wing（鸭翼）、canard aircraft（鸭式飞机）、canard configuration（鸭式布局）；没有常用的直接派生动词、形容词或副词，canard-like 只是可临时组成的“类似谣传的／类似鸭翼的”。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, canard is an unanalyzed borrowed base, not can + -ard. Its plural is canards; established combinations include canard wing, canard aircraft, and canard configuration. It has no common directly derived verb, adjective, or adverb; canard-like is a possible descriptive formation rather than a core family member.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 传闻义：rumor（传闻）未必虚假；fabrication（捏造）强调人为编造；hoax（骗局、恶作剧）强调有意使人上当的行为或安排。Canard 通常指流传的虚假说法，常带有陈旧、反复传播或损害名誉的意味。航空义中，foreplane（前翼）指前置翼面，不一定指整架鸭式飞机。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the report sense, rumor need not be false, fabrication emphasizes invention, and hoax emphasizes a deliberate deception or deceptive event. Canard typically denotes a circulating false claim, often an old or damaging one. In aviation, foreplane names the forward wing surface rather than necessarily the complete aircraft.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 一只“鸭子”连两义：旧法语骗术带出“假消息”，鸭形飞机带出“前置鸭翼”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: One duck, two branches: an old deception expression leads to false news; a ducklike aircraft leads to the forward wing.

etymology_story.zh: 这是现代医学中由 cardio-（心脏）与 pulmonary（肺的）组合而成的术语；前者源自希腊语 kardia（心脏），后者来自拉丁语 pulmo、词干 pulmon-（肺）。两个器官名称结合，表示心脏与肺共同涉及的结构、功能或医疗过程。

[Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/cardiopulmonary), [NCI](https://www.cancer.gov/publications/dictionaries/cancer-terms/def/cardiopulmonary)

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：cardi/o-（心脏结合形式，o 为连接元音）+ pulmon-（肺）+ -ary（……的）→ cardiopulmonary。全词没有常用的直接派生名词或动词；共享词根的主要词族包括 cardiac（心脏的）、cardiology（心脏病学）、cardiologist（心脏科医生）、cardiological（心脏病学的）、cardiovascular（心血管的）、pulmonary（肺的）、pulmonology（肺病学）、pulmonologist（肺科医生）、pulmonological（肺病学的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: cardi/o- (heart combining form, with linking vowel o) + pulmon- (lung) + -ary (relating to) → cardiopulmonary. The whole adjective has no common directly derived noun or verb. Major related root-family members include cardiac, cardiology, cardiologist, cardiological, cardiovascular, pulmonary, pulmonology, pulmonologist, and pulmonological.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cardiorespiratory（心脏与呼吸系统的）在功能描述中常与 cardiopulmonary 接近，但范围可涵盖整个呼吸系统；cardiac（心脏的）只指心脏；pulmonary（肺的）只指肺。后二者单独使用都不能表达“心肺两者”。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cardiorespiratory is often close in functional contexts but can encompass the respiratory system more broadly. Cardiac concerns the heart alone, while pulmonary concerns the lungs alone; neither independently expresses involvement of both organs.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: cardio- 心脏 + pulmon- 肺：两个器官一起工作，就是“心肺的”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Cardio- gives the heart; pulmon- gives the lungs: put them together for “heart-and-lung.”

etymology_story.zh: Coon 在18世纪的美国英语中由 raccoon 截去开头部分形成；raccoon 本身来自北美阿尔冈昆语族的波瓦坦语动物名称。后来 coon 被用于贬损黑人，并在澳大利亚用于贬损原住民，这些种族辱骂义必须与动物简称义区别标注。
etymology_story.en: Coon arose in eighteenth-century American English by shortening raccoon, itself borrowed from a Powhatan animal name within the Algonquian language family. It later acquired racist uses targeting Black people and, in Australia, Aboriginal people, which require explicit separation from the animal sense. [Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/coon), [Merriam-Webster: raccoon](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/raccoon)

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词方式：raccoon → coon，属于词首截短，不是前缀派生；复数为 coons。动物义相关构词包括 coon + hound → coonhound（猎浣熊犬）、coon dog（猎浣熊犬）、coon hunting（猎浣熊）；coonskin（浣熊皮）、coonskin cap（浣熊皮帽）。这些是动物义的复合词，不应自动套用种族辱骂义；现代中性表述动物时通常优先用 raccoon。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: raccoon → coon through initial clipping, not prefixation; the plural is coons. Animal-related formations include coonhound and coon dog (dogs used to hunt raccoons), coon hunting, coonskin (raccoon fur or hide), and coonskin cap. These animal compounds do not automatically carry the racial meaning; raccoon is generally preferable for neutral modern reference to the animal.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 动物义：raccoon（浣熊）是标准中性名称；racoon 是较少见的拼写变体，并非另一种动物。涉及人时，没有可作为中性近义词替换的对应关系：Black person（黑人）和 Aboriginal Australian（澳大利亚原住民）是相应的中性称谓，coon 则表达种族侮辱。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the animal, raccoon is the standard neutral term, while racoon is a less common spelling variant rather than a different animal. For people, Black person and Aboriginal Australian are neutral descriptions of the respective referents; coon adds racist abuse and is not interchangeable with them in tone or social meaning.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: raccoon 去掉开头就是 coon：说动物是简称，说人则是严重种族辱骂。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Clip the beginning of raccoon to get coon: an animal shortening, but a severe racial insult when applied to people.

etymology_story.zh: Copter 是20世纪中叶由 helicopter 截短而成的非正式名称。Helicopter 经法语 hélicoptère 形成，历史构词成分是希腊语 heliko-（螺旋）与 pteron（翅膀）；现代英语后来将 -copter 重新分析为表示旋翼飞行器的构词成分。
etymology_story.en: Copter developed in the mid-twentieth century as an informal shortening of helicopter. Helicopter came through French hélicoptère from Greek elements meaning “spiral” and “wing”; English subsequently reanalyzed -copter as an element for naming rotor-driven aircraft. [Collins: copter](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/copter), [Merriam-Webster: helicopter](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/helicopter)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：helicopter → copter（截短）；复数为 copters，也可写作 'copter。重新分析后的 -copter 可与数量成分组合：tri- + copter → tricopter（三旋翼飞行器）、quad- + copter → quadcopter（四旋翼飞行器）、hexa- + copter → hexacopter（六旋翼飞行器）、octo- + copter → octocopter（八旋翼飞行器）、multi- + copter → multicopter（多旋翼飞行器）；这些是相关构词，不意味着历史上的 helicopter 原本由 heli- + copter 构成。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: helicopter → copter by clipping; the plural is copters, and the spelling 'copter also occurs. Reanalyzed -copter combines with number elements in tricopter (three rotors), quadcopter (four), hexacopter (six), octocopter (eight), and multicopter (multiple rotors). These related formations do not imply that helicopter was historically formed from heli- + copter.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: helicopter（直升机）是标准、中性的完整名称；chopper（直升机）更口语化，也有其他含义；rotorcraft（旋翼航空器）是范围更广的技术上位词，包括直升机等类型。Copter 是简短的非正式名称，常见于新闻报道与口语。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Helicopter is the standard neutral full term; chopper is more colloquial and has additional meanings. Rotorcraft is a broader technical category that includes helicopters and other aircraft using rotating wings. Copter is a short informal name common in reporting and conversation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: helicopter 留下尾部 copter；再在前面加“四、六、多”，就得到各种旋翼飞行器名称。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Keep the end of helicopter to get copter; add four, six, or multi in front to name related rotorcraft.

etymology_story.zh: 英语在17世纪经法语 espalier 借入此词；法语词源自意大利语 spalliera，原指靠背或肩背所倚靠的支撑物，又来自 spalla（肩），最终追溯至晚期拉丁语 spatula（肩胛）。支撑身体的概念转用于支撑植物的棚架，继而指经此法整形的植物及整形过程。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed espalier through French in the seventeenth century; the French word came from Italian spalliera, a backrest or shoulder support, from spalla meaning “shoulder,” ultimately from Late Latin spatula meaning “shoulder blade.” The supporting structure gave its name to the trained plant and the training method. [Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/espalier)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语将 espalier 作为完整借词词基，不把 es- 或 -ier 当作此词中可自由分析的英语词缀；名词通过零派生兼作动词。屈折词族：espaliers（名词复数／动词第三人称单数）、espaliered（过去式／过去分词，也可作分词形容词“经棚架整形的”）、espaliering（现在分词／动名词“进行棚架整形”）；常见表达有 espalier-trained（经棚架整形培育的）、espalier training（棚架整形培育），没有常用的直接派生副词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats espalier as a complete borrowed base, without freely analyzing es- or -ier as English affixes in this word; the noun also functions as a verb through conversion. Its inflectional family is espaliers (plural noun or third-person singular verb), espaliered (past tense, past participle, and participial adjective), and espaliering (present participle or gerund). Related expressions include espalier-trained and espalier training; there is no common directly derived adverb.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 支架义：trellis（格架）通常指格状植物支架，用途比 espalier 更广。植物义：wall-trained tree（沿墙整形树）是解释性近义表达，强调沿墙培育。动词义：train（引导整形）可用于多种植物形态，espalier 则具体要求枝条形成平面布局。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the support, trellis usually denotes a lattice framework and has broader uses than espalier. For the plant, wall-trained tree is a descriptive near-equivalent emphasizing growth against a wall. As a verb, train covers many ways of directing plant growth, whereas espalier specifically involves a flat arrangement.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把棚架想成树的“靠背”：枝条靠着支撑展平，便串起支架、整形树、整形法和整形动作。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a backrest for a tree: its branches spread flat against support, linking the frame, the trained plant, the method, and the action.

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 invehi，意为“冲向、攻击”，也可指言语上的攻击；其对应主动形式 invehere 由 in-（向内、朝向）和 vehere（运载）组成。“冲向某人”的动作意象发展为猛烈的言语抨击。
etymology_story.en: It comes from Latin invehi, meaning to rush against or attack, including verbally; the corresponding active form invehere combines in-, meaning into or toward, with vehere, meaning to carry. The image of charging against someone developed into forceful verbal criticism.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中把 inveigh 作为完整动词词干学习，不宜机械拆成仍有独立意义的英语词素。屈折形式：inveighs、inveighed、inveighing；派生词：inveigher（抨击者）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, inveigh is best learned as a whole verb stem rather than divided into independently meaningful English morphemes. Inflected forms: inveighs, inveighed, inveighing; derivative: inveigher, a person who inveighs.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: rail 指愤怒地大声抱怨或斥责；denounce 指公开谴责，强调认定对象有错；fulminate 指激烈而愤怒地抨击。inveigh 较正式，强调以言语或文字猛烈攻击，通常接 against。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Rail suggests angry, often loud complaint; denounce emphasizes public condemnation of wrongdoing; fulminate suggests vehement, angry denunciation. Inveigh is formal and emphasizes forceful spoken or written criticism, usually followed by against.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 词源画面：朝对方冲过去 → 用言辞猛烈攻击；记住 inveigh against。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture charging toward an opponent, then doing it with words: inveigh against.

senses.meaning_zh: 文人；文学界人士；有文学修养的知识分子群体
senses.meaning_en: Educated people who write about or take a serious interest in literature.
senses.english_definition: The literati are people who are knowledgeable about literature, especially writers and literary critics.
senses.collocation_en: the literary tastes of the literati; the city's literati
senses.collocation_zh: 文人群体的文学趣味；这座城市的文学界人士
senses.sentence_en: The café became a popular meeting place for the city's literati.
senses.sentence_zh: 这家咖啡馆成了城中文人喜爱的聚会场所。

etymology_story.zh: 源头是拉丁语 litteratus（有学问的、通晓文字的），其复数为 litterati，与意大利语 literati 相联系；更深层的词根是 littera（字母）。含义从“有文字学问的人”逐渐集中到文人和文学知识界。
etymology_story.en: Its source is Latin litteratus, meaning learned or acquainted with letters, with the plural litterati, also reflected in Italian literati; the underlying word is littera, meaning a letter. The meaning narrowed from learned people generally to literary and intellectual circles.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 literati 是整体借入的复数名词，词尾 -i 保留了来源语言的复数标记；通常说 the literati，指一个群体，谓语用复数。历史相关词族包括 literate（有读写能力的）、illiterate（不识字的）、literacy（读写能力）、illiteracy（文盲状态）、literary（文学的）和 literature（文学）；这些词并非由 literati 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, literati is a borrowed plural noun whose final -i preserves a source-language plural ending; the literati normally denotes a group and takes plural agreement. Historically related words include literate, illiterate, literacy, illiteracy, literary, and literature; these are not direct derivatives of literati.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: intellectuals 泛指从事思想或学术活动的知识分子；intelligentsia 指作为社会阶层的知识界；men and women of letters 明确指文学作者或学者。literati 特别突出文学修养及文学圈身份，有时略带调侃意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Intellectuals broadly concerns people engaged in serious thought or scholarship; intelligentsia presents educated intellectuals as a social group; men and women of letters specifically denotes literary writers or scholars. Literati emphasizes literary culture and membership of literary circles, sometimes with a mildly mocking tone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 字母 → 通晓文字 → 文人群体；末尾 -i 提醒这是复数。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Letters lead to learning, then to literary people; the final -i reminds you that the word is plural.

meaning: 典范；最集中体现某种特质的事物

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；重音以 ˈ 标出。

forms: 此义常用单数，通常为 the quintessence of。
family: quintessential 典型的；quintessentially 典型地

morphology.text: quint-（第五） + essence（本质） → quintessence；从第五元素引申为精髓与典范。

etymology.text: 中古英语经中古法语 quinte essence 借自中世纪拉丁语 quinta essentia，原为第五种精质；古人把天体的精质视作高于四种地上元素。

usage_note: 常用 the quintessence of；表示一种特质的极致体现，不只是随意举例。

senses.meaning_zh: 典范；某种特质最纯粹、最集中的体现
senses.meaning_en: The most perfect or characteristic example of a quality or type.
senses.english_definition: If someone or something is the quintessence of a particular quality, they represent that quality in its purest or most typical form.
senses.collocation_en: the quintessence of elegance; the quintessence of luxury
senses.collocation_zh: 优雅的典范；奢华的极致体现
senses.sentence_en: With its clean lines and fine materials, the chair is the quintessence of elegance.
senses.sentence_zh: 这把椅子线条简洁、用料考究，堪称优雅的典范。

senses.meaning_zh: 精髓；本质中最集中、最核心的部分
senses.meaning_en: The purest and most concentrated essence of something.
senses.english_definition: The quintessence of something is its most essential nature, expressed in a pure or concentrated form.
senses.collocation_en: capture the quintessence of something; distill the quintessence of something
senses.collocation_zh: 捕捉某事物的精髓；提炼某事物的精髓
senses.sentence_en: The final paragraph captures the quintessence of her argument.
senses.sentence_zh: 最后一段抓住了她论证的精髓。

etymology_story.zh: 经法语进入英语，源自中世纪拉丁语 quinta essentia，字面意为“第五种本质”。它原指区别于土、水、气、火四种元素的天体精质，后来引申为事物最纯粹的精髓或最典型的体现。
etymology_story.en: It entered English through French from medieval Latin quinta essentia, literally the fifth essence. Originally the celestial substance distinguished from earth, water, air, and fire, it later came to mean the purest essence or most characteristic embodiment of something.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词可联系 quint-（第五）与 essence（本质），但全词属于已经固定的借词。词族：quintessence（精髓、典范）、quintessential（最典型的、精髓性的）、quintessentially（典型地、本质上）；名词复数为 quintessences，实际较少使用。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern word can be understood through quint-, meaning fifth, and essence, although it is an established borrowing. Its word family includes quintessence, quintessential, meaning most characteristic or essential, and quintessentially, meaning in a highly characteristic way; the noun plural quintessences is uncommon.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: essence 强调决定事物性质的核心本质；epitome 强调某种类型或特征的典型实例；embodiment 强调抽象性质在具体人或物中的体现。quintessence 兼有“最纯粹的精髓”和“最集中的典型体现”两层意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Essence emphasizes the defining inner nature of something; epitome emphasizes a representative example; embodiment emphasizes an abstract quality expressed in a concrete person or thing. Quintessence combines the ideas of utmost purity and concentrated representation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 四元素之外的“第五精质” → 提纯到极致的精髓 → 最典型的体现。
mnemonic_anchor.en: The fifth essence beyond the four elements becomes the purest essence, then the ultimate example.

meaning: 甜腻做作的（情感或表达）

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；重音以 ˈ 标出。

forms: 形容词无复数或时态变化。
family: saccharinity 甜腻；saccharin 糖精

morphology.text: sacchar-（糖） + -ine（具有某种性质的） → saccharine（糖似的），引申为表达甜腻做作。

etymology.text: 英语基于拉丁语 saccharum（糖）形成；像糖放得过多一样，后来用来形容过分甜蜜而显得做作的表达。

usage_note: 常带贬义；本课讲评论语，不是名词 saccharin（糖精）。

senses.meaning_zh: （贬义）甜腻做作的；过分煽情的
senses.meaning_en: Excessively sweet, sentimental, or emotionally artificial.
senses.english_definition: If you describe something as saccharine, you mean that it expresses sweetness or emotion in an excessive and artificial way.
senses.collocation_en: a saccharine smile; saccharine sentimentality
senses.collocation_zh: 甜得做作的微笑；甜腻的感伤情调
senses.sentence_en: The film's saccharine ending felt completely unearned.
senses.sentence_zh: 这部电影甜腻煽情的结局毫无铺垫，显得十分生硬。

senses.meaning_zh: （较正式或技术用语）糖的；含糖的；有甜味的
senses.meaning_en: Relating to sugar, containing sugar, or having a sweet taste.
senses.english_definition: A saccharine substance contains sugar or tastes sweet.
senses.collocation_en: saccharine matter; a saccharine taste
senses.collocation_zh: 糖类物质；甜味
senses.sentence_en: The extract has a distinctly saccharine taste.
senses.sentence_zh: 这种提取物有明显的甜味。

etymology_story.zh: 由表示糖的词干形成，历史上可追溯到拉丁语 saccharum、希腊语 sakkharon，最终关联梵语 śarkarā（碎石、砂糖）。“像糖一样甜”的字面意义后来发展出“情感或表达甜得过头”的贬义。
etymology_story.en: The word was formed from a stem meaning sugar, traceable through Latin saccharum and Greek sakkharon ultimately to Sanskrit śarkarā, meaning gravel or granulated sugar. Its literal association with sweetness developed into a disapproving description of excessively sweet emotion or expression.

morphology_enriched.zh: sacchar-（糖）＋ -ine（表示性质或关联的形容词后缀）→ saccharine。直接派生词包括 saccharinely（甜腻地、做作地）和 saccharinity（甜味、甜腻做作）；同根词包括 saccharide（糖类）和 saccharin（糖精，通常不带末尾 e），后者是特定甜味剂的名称。
morphology_enriched.en: Sacchar- means sugar, and -ine is an adjective suffix indicating a quality or relationship. Direct derivatives include saccharinely and saccharinity; related formations include saccharide, a sugar compound, and saccharin, normally spelled without a final e, the name of a particular sweetener.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cloying 强调甜味或情感过量而令人厌腻；mawkish 强调伤感得不自然或令人不适；sentimental 指感情丰富或偏重感伤，未必含贬义。saccharine 通常同时暗示甜腻过度和不真诚。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cloying emphasizes sweetness or emotion that becomes unpleasant through excess; mawkish emphasizes embarrassing or disagreeable sentimentality; sentimental can describe strong emotion without necessarily being critical. Saccharine usually suggests both excessive sweetness and artificiality.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: sacchar- 是糖：糖放太多会腻，感情表达太甜也会显得做作。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Sacchar- means sugar: too much sugar cloys, and too much emotional sweetness feels artificial.

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；重音以 ˈ 标出。

forms: 可数；复数 simpletons。
family: simple 简单的；simple-minded 头脑简单的

morphology.text: simple（头脑简单的） + -ton（仿人名的词尾） → simpleton（傻瓜）。

etymology.text: 十七世纪英语由 simple 加上人名式词尾 -ton 形成；像给头脑简单的人起了一个绰号。

usage_note: 贬义且冒犯，不宜随意用来称呼别人；simple 表示简单时不必有贬义。

senses.meaning_zh: （贬义，略显老派）傻瓜；头脑简单、缺乏判断力的人
senses.meaning_en: A foolish or excessively naive person who lacks good judgment.
senses.english_definition: If you call someone a simpleton, you mean that they are foolish and easily deceived.
senses.collocation_en: a complete simpleton; a gullible simpleton
senses.collocation_zh: 十足的傻瓜；容易受骗的傻瓜
senses.sentence_en: They treated him as a simpleton because he trusted everyone he met.
senses.sentence_zh: 他见谁都相信，因此他们把他当作傻瓜。

etymology_story.zh: 十七世纪英语中出现，由 simple 当时“头脑简单、愚钝”的意义加上 -ton 构成。这个词尾可能仿照英语姓氏的形式，使全词像是给愚笨的人起的绰号。
etymology_story.en: The word appeared in seventeenth-century English, combining simple in its sense of foolish or mentally unsophisticated with -ton. The ending may imitate English surnames, making the word resemble a nickname for a foolish person.

morphology_enriched.zh: simple（头脑简单的）＋ -ton（此词中的人物称呼词尾，来源并不完全确定）→ simpleton；复数为 simpletons。相关词族包括 simple（简单的、单纯的）、simply（简单地、仅仅）、simplicity（简单、质朴）、simplify（简化）、simplification（简化）、simplistic（过分简单化的）和 simplistically（过分简单化地）；这些相关词并不都含“愚笨”之意。
morphology_enriched.en: Simple, in the sense of foolish or naive, combines with -ton, a person-denoting ending here whose origin is not completely certain, to form simpleton; the plural is simpletons. Related words include simple, simply, simplicity, simplify, simplification, simplistic, and simplistically; these relatives do not all imply foolishness.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: fool 泛指行为或判断愚蠢的人；dupe 强调被别人欺骗或利用的人；innocent 强调不谙世故，往往较温和。simpleton 带轻蔑意味，突出头脑简单、容易轻信。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Fool broadly describes someone who acts or judges unwisely; dupe emphasizes someone deceived or manipulated; innocent emphasizes lack of worldly experience and is often gentler. Simpleton is contemptuous and particularly suggests limited judgment and easy trust.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 simple 想成“头脑过于简单”，再给这个人贴上 simpleton 的绰号。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of someone whose thinking is too simple, then imagine Simpleton as their unflattering nickname.

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；重音以 ˈ 标出。

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆；upbraid + -er → upbraider（严厉责备者），不要按现代 braid（编辫子）硬拆。

senses.meaning_zh: 严厉责备；斥责
senses.meaning_en: to criticize or scold someone severely
senses.english_definition: If you upbraid someone, you tell them strongly that they have done something wrong.
senses.collocation_en: upbraid someone for negligence; upbraid someone for being late
senses.collocation_zh: 因某人疏忽而严厉责备；因某人迟到而斥责
senses.sentence_en: The director upbraided the team for ignoring repeated warnings.
senses.sentence_zh: 主管严厉责备团队无视一再发出的警告。

etymology_story.zh: 源自古英语 ūpbregdan，经中古英语 upbreiden 演变而来；古英语词义包括向上提起、提出某事和责备。其语义联系可以理解为把某人的过错提出来，当面加以指责。
etymology_story.en: It comes from Old English ūpbregdan through Middle English upbreiden; the Old English verb included senses of lifting up, bringing something forward, and reproaching. The semantic connection is that someone's faults are brought up against them.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中宜把 upbraid 作为完整动词词干记忆，不拆成 up + braid（编辫子）。屈折形式：upbraids、upbraided、upbraiding；派生词：upbraider（责骂者，少见），upbraiding（责骂，也可作名词或形容词）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, treat upbraid as a whole verb stem, rather than as up + braid in the hair-weaving sense. Inflected forms: upbraids, upbraided, upbraiding; derivatives: upbraider, an uncommon noun for someone who scolds, and upbraiding, also used as a noun or adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: scold（责骂）常用于日常训斥；rebuke（斥责）强调明确而严肃地表达不满；reproach（责备）常带失望或受伤的情绪。upbraid 较正式或带文学色彩，强调直接而严厉地数落过错。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Scold commonly describes everyday reprimanding; rebuke emphasizes a clear, serious expression of disapproval; reproach often conveys disappointment or hurt. Upbraid is formal or literary and emphasizes directly and severely criticizing someone's faults.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把过错“提出来”痛批：upbraid＝严厉责备；与编辫子无关。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Bring someone's faults up against them: upbraid means to scold severely; it has no connection with braiding hair.

etymology_story.en: Whoopee developed as an exclamation based on whoop, a shout of excitement, and is recorded from the nineteenth century. It later acquired a noun use for revelry, while make whoopee also became a humorous expression for having sex.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中把 whoopee 作为完整的感叹词或名词记忆，词尾 -ee 不是这里可自由套用的派生后缀。相关词有 whoop（欢呼；欢呼声）、whooping（欢呼的；欢呼）；复合词 whoopee cushion 指坐下时发出类似放屁声音的恶作剧坐垫。

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hooray commonly expresses celebration or approval; yippee sounds particularly excited or childlike; woo-hoo is an informal, exuberant cheer. Whoopee likewise expresses delight, but can also sarcastically suggest that something is unimpressive.

etymology_story.zh: 这是现代科技英语由 bio-（生命、生物）与 remediation（修复、补救）组合而成的术语。bio- 源于希腊语 bios（生命），remediation 所属词族最终可追溯到拉丁语 remedium（补救办法、药物），合起来表示借助生物治理污染。
etymology_story.en: This modern scientific term combines bio-, meaning life or living organisms, with remediation, meaning corrective treatment. Bio- comes from Greek bios, 'life', while the remediation family ultimately traces to Latin remedium, 'a remedy or cure', giving the idea of treating pollution through biological activity.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：bio-（生物）+ remediation（修复）→ bioremediation（生物修复）；remediation 与 remediate（修复、治理）及名词后缀 -ion 对应。词族包括 bioremediate（进行生物修复）、bioremediates、bioremediated、bioremediating；基础相关词包括 remedy（补救办法；补救）、remedial（补救的）、remediation（修复治理）。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: bio- 'biological' + remediation 'corrective treatment' → bioremediation; remediation corresponds to remediate plus the noun-forming suffix -ion. The family includes bioremediate, bioremediates, bioremediated, and bioremediating; related base-family words include remedy, remedial, and remediation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: biological treatment（生物处理）范围更广，也包括常规污水处理；biodegradation（生物降解）强调生物分解物质的过程，本身不一定是人为治理措施；phytoremediation（植物修复）专指利用植物修复污染，是生物修复的一类。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Biological treatment is broader and includes routine wastewater processing; biodegradation describes biological breakdown itself and need not involve a deliberate cleanup project; phytoremediation specifically uses plants and is a type of bioremediation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: bio＝生物，remediation＝修复：让生物来清理污染。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Bio means living organisms; remediation means corrective treatment: let living things help clean up pollution.

etymology_story.zh: 英语 boreal 借自晚期拉丁语 borealis（北方的），其基础是拉丁语 Boreas，源头为希腊语 Boreas，即北风及北风神之名。原来的“北方”含义后来在生态学中专门用于北方寒冷的森林地带。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed boreal from Late Latin borealis, 'northern', based on Latin Boreas and ultimately Greek Boreas, the north wind and its personification. The general meaning 'northern' later developed a specialized ecological application to the cold northern forest belt.

morphology_enriched.zh: 这是整体借入的形容词，历史结构为 bore-（北方、北风）+ -al（……的）；bore- 在现代普通英语中不是独立使用的词根，勿与 bore（使厌烦；钻孔）混同。相关构词包括 subboreal（亚北方的；亚寒温带的）和 circumboreal（环北方分布的）；borealis 保留在 aurora borealis（北极光）等拉丁语名称中。
morphology_enriched.en: This is a borrowed adjective with the historical structure bore- 'north or north wind' + -al 'relating to'; bore- is not an independent everyday English base and is unrelated to bore meaning 'make holes' or 'make someone bored'. synonyms_and_nuances.zh: northern（北方的）最通用，只表示方位或地域；subarctic（亚北极的）强调邻近北极的气候与地理带；taiga（泰加林、北方针叶林）是名词，指与 boreal forest 大体对应的森林类型。boreal 尤其常用于北方森林与生态学描述。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Northern is the general geographical adjective; subarctic emphasizes the climatic or geographical zone near the Arctic; taiga is a noun naming the forest biome broadly corresponding to boreal forest. Boreal is particularly common in descriptions of northern forests and ecology.

senses.sentence_zh: 她把后移到最后制胜的那一格，说：“将死！”

etymology_story.zh: 中古英语经盎格鲁法语借入这一棋语，更早的传播经过阿拉伯语，并可追溯到波斯语 shāh māt，通常理解为“王已被困住或击败”。其核心不是把王实际吃掉，而是王已无法摆脱攻击；后来引申为彻底挫败对手。
etymology_story.en: Middle English acquired the chess term through Anglo-French, with earlier transmission through Arabic from Persian shāh māt, conventionally understood as 'the king is helpless or defeated'. Its central idea is a king that cannot escape attack, and it later developed the figurative meaning of decisively defeating an opponent.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语可分析为 check（将军）+ mate（将死），但整个词有借入历史；此处 mate 是棋语，与“朋友、配偶”的 mate 词源不同。名词与动词同形；屈折形式有 checkmates（复数名词或第三人称单数动词）、checkmated（过去式、过去分词）、checkmating（现在分词）；相关棋语包括 check（将军）和 stalemate（逼和）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English permits the analysis check 'an attack on the king' + mate 'checkmate', although the whole expression has a borrowing history; this chess sense of mate is etymologically distinct from mate meaning 'friend or partner'. The noun and verb share a form; inflections are checkmates, checkmated, and checkmating. Related chess vocabulary includes check and stalemate.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: mate 是 checkmate 在棋语中的简略同义词；defeat（击败）含义更广，不一定使对手毫无应对之策；outmaneuver（以策略胜过）强调通过更高明的行动取得优势，未必已经彻底获胜。stalemate（逼和）并非近义词：被逼和的一方无合法着法，但王没有被将军。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Mate is a shorter chess synonym for checkmate; defeat is broader and does not necessarily imply that every response has been eliminated; outmaneuver emphasizes gaining an advantage through superior strategy without necessarily securing final victory. Stalemate is not a synonym: the player has no legal move, but the king is not in check.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: check＝王正被攻击，mate＝无合法解围办法：将军加无路可解，就是将死。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Check means the king is attacked; mate means there is no legal way out: attack plus no escape equals checkmate.

etymology_story.zh: cyan 最终源自希腊语 kyanos，指深蓝色物质或深蓝色，具体所指材料并不完全确定。现代英语用它表示蓝绿色，这一意义在彩色印刷和色彩技术中得到固定。
etymology_story.en: Cyan ultimately comes from Greek kyanos, referring to a dark-blue substance or colour, although the precise material is uncertain. In modern English, it denotes a greenish blue, a meaning established in colour printing and colour technology.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代颜色词 cyan 是单纯词，不宜继续拆分。相关构词成分 cyan-／cyano- 表示“蓝色”或特定化学联系，见 cyanotype（蓝晒图像）、cyanosis（发绀）、cyanotic（发绀的）、cyanobacterium／cyanobacteria（蓝细菌，单数／复数）、cyanogen（氰）、cyanide（氰化物）、cyanine（菁染料）；这些属于相关的科学词族，并非都由现代颜色词直接派生。常见复合形式有 cyan-coloured（青色的）。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern colour word cyan is a simple word without a useful smaller morphological division. The related combining forms cyan- and cyano- indicate blue or particular chemical relationships in cyanotype, cyanosis, cyanotic, cyanobacterium/cyanobacteria, cyanogen, cyanide, and cyanine; these belong to related scientific vocabulary rather than all being direct derivatives of the modern colour word. A common compound is cyan-coloured.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: blue-green（蓝绿色）是较宽泛的描述；turquoise（绿松石色）通常指明亮、近似绿松石的蓝绿色；teal（深蓝绿色）通常更深、更暗。cyan 在印刷和数字色彩中具有更明确的技术含义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Blue-green is a broad descriptive term; turquoise usually suggests a bright blue-green resembling the gemstone; teal is generally darker and more subdued. Cyan has a more specific technical meaning in printing and digital colour.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住 cyan- 的“蓝”色线索：现代 cyan 是打印机里的蓝绿色。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect cyan- with blue: modern cyan is the greenish blue in a printer.

morphology_enriched.zh: 从历史构词看，可分析为 cygn-（天鹅）＋小称词尾 -et；现代英语通常把 cygnet 作为完整名词使用。常用形式为 cygnet／cygnets（单数／复数）；相关的罕见形容词 cygnine 意为“天鹅的、似天鹅的”。swan（天鹅）、cob（雄天鹅）和 pen（雌天鹅）属于相关词汇，并非其派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Historically, the word can be analysed as cygn- meaning swan plus the diminutive suffix -et; modern English normally treats cygnet as a whole noun. Its usual forms are cygnet and cygnets; the rare related adjective cygnine means relating to or resembling swans. Swan, cob, and pen are associated vocabulary, not derivatives.

morphology_enriched.zh: deca-（十）＋-athlon（多项目竞技比赛）→ decathlon；复数为 decathlons。主要词族成员有 decathlete（十项全能运动员）和较少见的 decathletic（十项全能运动的）；pentathlon（五项全能）、heptathlon（七项全能）和 triathlon（铁人三项）是共享构词成分的相关词，不是 decathlon 的派生词。

Principal family members include decathlete and the less common adjective decathletic. Pentathlon, heptathlon, and triathlon share related combining elements but are not derivatives of decathlon.

etymology_story.zh: expository 属于拉丁语 exponere 的词族；exponere 由表示“向外”的 ex- 和表示“放置”的 ponere 构成，原意为“摆出来”。“把内容摆在面前”的意象发展为“陈述、解释”，形成了今天的“说明性的”之义。
etymology_story.en: Expository belongs to the family of Latin exponere, formed from ex- meaning out and ponere meaning put or place. The image of setting something out developed into presenting or explaining it, producing the modern explanatory meaning.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代学术构词可分析为 exposit-（陈述、解释的词干）＋-ory（表示性质或作用的形容词后缀）。主要词族包括 exposition（阐述；说明）、expositor（阐释者）、expositive（解释性的）和 expositional（阐述的）；expound（详述、阐明）是同源的相关动词，并不是直接去掉 -ory 得到的形式。
morphology_enriched.en: In learned word formation, expository can be analysed as exposit-, a stem associated with presenting or explaining, plus the adjective-forming suffix -ory. Principal family members include exposition, expositor, expositive, and expositional. Expound is a related verb from the same historical family, not a form obtained simply by removing -ory.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: explanatory（解释性的）最通用，强调帮助理解；informative（提供信息的）强调增加知识，未必展开解释；explicative（阐释性的）较正式，常强调对意义或细节的解说。expository 尤其常用于说明文体或系统阐述。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Explanatory is the broadest term for helping someone understand; informative stresses providing knowledge without necessarily explaining it; explicative is more formal and often concerns interpreting meanings or details. Expository is especially associated with explanatory prose and systematic presentation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把知识“摆出来”，按条理讲清楚，就是 expository。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Set the information out clearly: expository writing explains it in an organised way.

senses.meaning_zh: 活动挡片；翻板；尤指抽水马桶水箱中的拍盖式排水阀
senses.meaning_en: a movable flap that opens or closes a passage, especially the outlet of a toilet tank

etymology_story.zh: flapper 由 flap 加 -er 构成，早期可指拍动的东西或幼鸟，后来也用于年轻女孩；人物义的具体发展路径并不完全确定。到了二十世纪二十年代，它尤其指以服饰和行为挑战传统的年轻女性，而机械义保留了“活动片拍动、开合”的形象。
etymology_story.en: Flapper was formed from flap plus -er and had early uses for things that flap and for young birds, later also being applied to young girls; the precise development of the human sense is uncertain. By the 1920s, it particularly denoted young women who challenged convention through dress and behaviour, while the mechanical sense retained the image of a moving flap.

morphology_enriched.zh: flap（拍动；活动片）＋-er（表示执行动作的人或物）→ flapper；词尾 p 按构词拼写规则双写。常用相关形式有 flap、flaps、flapped、flapping、flapper、flappers，以及非正式形容词 flappy（松软拍动的）；flapper dress（摩登女郎式连衣裙）和 flapper valve（拍盖阀、翻板阀）是常见复合表达。
morphology_enriched.en: Flap, meaning to move loosely or a movable piece, + -er, indicating a person or thing associated with an action, forms flapper; the final p is doubled in the spelling. Common related forms include flap, flaps, flapped, flapping, flapper, flappers, and the informal adjective flappy. Flapper dress and flapper valve are common compound expressions.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 人物义：modern girl（摩登少女）是较宽泛的时代性称呼，不能完全替代 flapper；对年轻女性使用的近义词并不必然包含其二十年代文化特征。机械义：flap（活动片）强调部件形状和运动方式；valve（阀）强调控制流体的功能，范围更广。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the historical sense, modern girl is a broader period expression and does not fully reproduce the 1920s cultural associations of flapper; there is no exact general synonym. For the mechanical sense, flap stresses the moving piece, while valve stresses the function of controlling fluid and covers a wider range of mechanisms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 机械义抓住 flap 的“拍动、开合”；人物义用爵士时代的短发和流苏舞裙定位，不把联想当作确证词源。
mnemonic_anchor.en: For the mechanical sense, picture a flap opening and closing; for the historical sense, picture a Jazz Age bob and fringed dress, using the image as a memory aid rather than a proven origin.

senses.meaning_zh: 通过持续否认或歪曲事实，操控某人，使其怀疑自己的记忆、判断或现实感
senses.meaning_en: to manipulate someone into doubting their own memory, judgment, or perception of reality
senses.english_definition: If someone gaslights you, they repeatedly deny or distort what has happened so that you begin to doubt your own memory or judgment.
senses.collocation_en: gaslight a partner; be gaslit into doubting yourself
senses.collocation_zh: 对伴侣实施心理操控；受心理操控而开始怀疑自己
senses.sentence_en: He tried to gaslight her by insisting that conversations she clearly remembered had never happened.
senses.sentence_zh: 他坚称她明明记得的那些谈话从未发生过，企图以此操控她，让她怀疑自己的记忆。

etymology_story.zh: 名词由 gas（煤气）和 light（光）合成，原指煤气燃烧产生的照明。心理操控的动词义源于1938年的戏剧《Gas Light》及其电影改编：故事中的丈夫操纵煤气灯等环境线索，并否认变化，使妻子怀疑自己的感知。
etymology_story.en: The noun combines gas and light and originally refers to illumination produced by burning gas. The psychological verb comes from the 1938 play Gas Light and its film adaptations, in which a husband manipulates environmental clues, including the gas lighting, and denies the changes to make his wife doubt her perceptions.

morphology_enriched.zh: gas（煤气）+ light（光）→ gaslight；名词直接转用为动词。主要词族和词形：gaslights（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、gaslighted／gaslit（过去式及过去分词）、gaslighting（现在分词，也作名词，指这种心理操控）、gaslighter（实施这种操控的人）。
morphology_enriched.en: gas + light → gaslight; the noun also becomes a verb through conversion. Principal family members and inflections are gaslights, gaslighted/gaslit, gaslighting, and gaslighter; gaslighting also functions as a noun naming the manipulation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 心理操控义：manipulate（操纵）范围更广；deceive（欺骗）强调使人相信假话；undermine（逐渐削弱）强调损害信心或权威。gaslight 特指使受害者怀疑自己的记忆、判断或现实感。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the psychological sense, manipulate is broader, deceive emphasizes causing false beliefs, and undermine emphasizes gradually weakening confidence or authority. Gaslight specifically involves making someone distrust their own memory, judgment, or sense of reality.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 灯光明明变了，对方却说“是你记错了”：从煤气灯联想到让人怀疑自己的心理操控。
mnemonic_anchor.en: The gaslight changes, but someone insists you imagined it: connect the lamp with manipulation that makes you doubt yourself.

etymology_story.zh: 英语经西班牙语 guano 借入此词，源头是克丘亚语 wanu，意为粪肥或肥料。英语中主要用它指海鸟或蝙蝠聚居处积累的粪便，尤其强调其肥料用途。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed guano through Spanish from Quechua wanu, meaning dung or fertilizer. In English it chiefly denotes accumulated seabird or bat droppings, particularly as a source of fertilizer.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 guano 是整体借词，不宜拆成英语词根与词缀，通常作不可数名词。相关罕见技术词包括 guanoize（施鸟粪肥）及 guanoization（施鸟粪肥这一过程）；这些派生词不意味着 guano 本身具有常用动词词性。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, guano is an unanalyzed loanword rather than a combination of English roots and affixes, and it is normally uncountable. Rare technical relatives include guanoize, meaning to fertilize with guano, and guanoization, the process of doing so; these derivatives do not establish a common verb use of guano itself.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: droppings（动物粪便）强调动物排出的粪粒；manure（粪肥）通常指用作肥料的牲畜粪便；fertilizer（肥料）还包括矿物或合成肥料。guano 更具体，指海鸟或蝙蝠的粪便及其堆积物。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Droppings refers to animal feces, often as individual pellets; manure usually means livestock dung used as fertilizer; fertilizer also includes mineral and synthetic products. Guano specifically identifies seabird or bat droppings and their deposits.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 鸟群或蝙蝠群聚居，粪便积成肥料：把 guano 整体记成“群居动物留下的天然粪肥”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a seabird colony or bat roost building up a natural fertilizer deposit: remember guano as one whole borrowed word.

etymology_story.zh: 此词来自新拉丁语解剖学名称，由希腊语来源的 hypo-（在下方）和 thalamus（丘脑）构成，名称直接说明其相对位置。thalamus 最终源于希腊语中表示“内室”的词，后来成为脑部结构的名称。

morphology_enriched.zh: hypo-（在下方）+ thalamus（丘脑）→ hypothalamus（下丘脑）。主要词族和词形：hypothalami（复数）、hypothalamic（下丘脑的）；thalamus 和 thalamic（丘脑的）是相关基础词，而非由 hypothalamus 派生的词。
morphology_enriched.en: hypo- (below) + thalamus → hypothalamus. Principal family forms are hypothalami, the plural, and hypothalamic, the adjective; thalamus and thalamic are related base forms rather than derivatives of hypothalamus.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有常用的单词近义词。hypothalamic region（下丘脑区）和 hypothalamic area（下丘脑区域）可作描述性近义表达，但可能泛指该区域；thalamus（丘脑）和 pituitary gland（垂体）是相关但不同的结构，不能互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no common single-word synonym. Hypothalamic region and hypothalamic area are descriptive near-equivalents, although they may refer more broadly to the region; thalamus and pituitary gland name related but distinct structures and are not interchangeable.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: hypo- 表示“在下方”：丘脑下方，就是下丘脑；再联想它帮助调节体温、饥渴和激素。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hypo- means below: below the thalamus sits the hypothalamus, helping regulate temperature, hunger, thirst, and hormones.

morphology_enriched.zh: lark（云雀）+ spur（距）→ larkspur，是名词加名词构成的合成词。复数为 larkspurs；没有常用的派生动词或形容词，larkspur seeds 中的 larkspur 是名词作定语。
morphology_enriched.en: lark + spur → larkspur, a noun–noun compound. The plural is larkspurs; there are no common derived verbs or adjectives, and larkspur in larkspur seeds is a noun used attributively.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: delphinium（翠雀类植物）与 larkspur 的指称重叠，但园艺中 delphinium 常让人想到多年生的高大翠雀；annual larkspur（一年生飞燕草）是范围更窄的名称。不同地区的普通植物名用法可能不同，不能始终视为严格同义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Delphinium overlaps with larkspur, but in gardening it often suggests tall perennial plants; annual larkspur is a narrower name for annual forms. Common plant names vary regionally, so these expressions are not always exact synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 看花背后的小尖距：lark（云雀）+ spur（距），像云雀伸出的爪。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Look at the pointed spur behind the flower: lark + spur evokes a lark's projecting claw.

pronunciation.note: 重音按音标中的 ˈ 标记朗读；本卡采用英语词典中的读法。

forms: 可数或不可数名词；可数时复数 libations。
family: libationary 奠酒仪式的

morphology.text: libate（奠酒）+ -ion（动作名词后缀）→ libation（奠酒）；接后缀时去掉 libate 末尾的 e。

etymology.text: 中古英语从拉丁语 libatio 借入，来自 libare（把酒倾倒出来作祭献）。记住把少量酒洒在地上祭献的画面。

usage_note: 本课学宗教仪式中的祭酒或奠酒；现代也有人幽默地用它指一杯酒，语气不同。

senses.meaning_zh: 奠酒；倾洒酒或其他液体以敬神、祭亡者的仪式，亦指所献液体
senses.meaning_en: the ritual pouring of a liquid as an offering, or the liquid offered
senses.english_definition: A libation is an act of pouring wine or another liquid as an offering to a god or a dead person, or the liquid poured in this way.
senses.collocation_en: pour a libation; offer a libation
senses.collocation_zh: 倾酒祭献；献上奠酒
senses.sentence_en: They poured a libation of wine in honor of their ancestors.
senses.sentence_zh: 他们洒酒祭奠祖先。

senses.meaning_zh: 酒；一杯酒精饮品，常为幽默或故作文雅的说法
senses.meaning_en: an alcoholic drink, especially in humorous or deliberately elegant usage
senses.english_definition: People sometimes call an alcoholic drink a libation when they want to sound humorous or unusually elegant.
senses.collocation_en: evening libations; enjoy a libation
senses.collocation_zh: 晚间小酌的酒饮；喝上一杯酒
senses.sentence_en: After the concert, we stopped at a bar for a celebratory libation.
senses.sentence_zh: 音乐会结束后，我们到一家酒吧喝了一杯庆祝酒。

etymology_story.zh: 英语 libation 可追溯至拉丁语 libatio（倾酒祭献），来自 libare（倾出少量液体作祭献）。它原指宗教仪式中的液体供献，后来也被幽默地用来指普通酒饮。
etymology_story.en: English libation traces back to Latin libatio, a pouring out as an offering, from libare, to pour a small amount as a sacrifice. The ritual meaning later broadened into a humorous term for an ordinary alcoholic drink.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可按拉丁来源词干 libat-（倾液祭献）+ 名词后缀 -ion 分析；现代英语还有罕见动词 libate（倾液祭献），与 libation 构成词族，但不宜把英语历史说成先有 libate、再派生 libation。主要相关形式：libations（复数）、libate、libated、libating，以及较少见的形容词 libational／libatory（奠酒的、祭献液体的）。
morphology_enriched.en: The learned structure is Latin-derived libat- (pour as an offering) + the noun suffix -ion. The rare English verb libate belongs to the same family, but libation should not be presented historically as an English derivative formed from an earlier libate. Principal related forms include libations, libate, libated, libating, and the uncommon adjectives libational and libatory.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: offering（祭品、供献）范围更广，不限液体；drink（饮品）是中性普通词，也可指非酒精饮料；tipple（酒、常喝的酒）带非正式或诙谐色彩。libation 在仪式语境中强调倾液祭献，在社交语境中则带故作文雅或幽默的语气。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Offering is broader and need not involve liquid; drink is neutral and may be nonalcoholic; tipple is informal or playful and can mean someone's usual alcoholic drink. Libation emphasizes a poured offering in ritual contexts and sounds deliberately elegant or humorous in social contexts.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“倾出少量酒液”：献给神灵是奠酒，留给自己喝则可幽默地称为一杯 libation。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor the word in pouring a little wine: offered ceremonially, it is a libation; enjoyed socially, it can humorously be called one too.

pronunciation.note: 重音按音标中的 ˈ 标记朗读；本卡采用英语词典中的读法。

forms: 形容词；比较程度用 more / most loquacious。
family: loquaciously 健谈地；loquaciousness 多话；健谈

morphology.text: loquacious + -ly → loquaciously（健谈地）。loquacious 在使用时整体记忆，词根 loqu- 与“说话”有关，不按字母硬拆。

etymology.text: 来自拉丁语 loquax（多话的），词根来自 loqui（说话），17世纪进入英语。把它与一个能一直聊下去的人联系起来。

usage_note: 较正式，指一个人话很多；视语境可带欣赏或轻微嫌烦的语气。

senses.meaning_zh: 话多的；健谈的；喋喋不休的
senses.meaning_en: very talkative, sometimes excessively so
senses.english_definition: Someone who is loquacious talks a lot, sometimes more than other people want them to.
senses.collocation_en: a loquacious host; a loquacious mood
senses.collocation_zh: 健谈的主人；想滔滔不绝说话的心情
senses.sentence_en: Our loquacious host entertained us with stories throughout dinner.
senses.sentence_zh: 晚餐期间，健谈的主人一直给我们讲故事，逗我们开心。

etymology_story.zh: loquacious 于17世纪进入英语，源自拉丁语 loquax，其词干 loquac- 表示“多话的”，与 loqui“说话”有关。英语保留了“话很多”的核心意思，既可形容健谈，也可暗示话多得令人厌烦。
etymology_story.en: Loquacious entered English in the seventeenth century from Latin loquax, with the stem loquac-, meaning “talkative” and related to loqui, “to speak.” It retained the idea of abundant speech and can suggest either engaging conversation or an irritating excess of talk.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中宜把 loquacious 视为整体借入的形容词；loqu- 是表示“说话”的拉丁语词根线索，不能据此把全词当作自由组合的现代英语词。常用词族：loquacious + -ly → loquaciously（健谈地；话多地）；loquacious + -ness → loquaciousness（健谈；多话）；另有同源名词 loquacity（健谈；多话）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, loquacious is best treated as a borrowed adjective; loqu- provides a Latin root connection meaning “speak,” rather than a freely productive English formation. Its established family includes loquacious + -ly → loquaciously, loquacious + -ness → loquaciousness, and the related noun loquacity, meaning talkativeness.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: talkative（爱说话的）最常见、最中性；garrulous（絮叨的）通常强调冗长琐碎、令人厌烦；voluble（口若悬河的）强调说得流利而连续。loquacious 较正式，核心是话多，褒贬取决于语境。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Talkative is the most ordinary and neutral choice; garrulous usually suggests tedious talk about minor matters; voluble emphasizes fluent, continuous speech. Loquacious is more formal and focuses on the amount of speech, with approval or criticism supplied by context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住 loqu- 的“说话”线索：说个不停的人，就是 loquacious。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect loqu- with “speak”: someone whose speech keeps flowing is loquacious.

pronunciation.note: 重音按音标中的 ˈ 标记朗读；本卡采用英语词典中的读法。

morphology.text: mis-（厌恶，此处是希腊语来源的成分）+ anthrop-（人）→ misanthrope（厌恶人类的人）；不要套用“错误”的 mis-。

etymology.text: 来自希腊语 misanthropos（厌恶人类的），由“厌恶”与“人”两个成分组成，16世纪进入英语。

usage_note: 形容对人类整体抱有反感的人，语气较强；一个人喜欢独处，并不足以称他为 misanthrope。

senses.meaning_zh: 厌恶人类的人；不信任或鄙视世人的人
senses.meaning_en: a person who dislikes or distrusts humankind
senses.english_definition: A misanthrope is someone who dislikes people in general and often avoids their company.

etymology_story.zh: misanthrope 于16世纪经法语进入英语，最终源自希腊语 misanthrōpos，由表示“憎恨”的 misein 和表示“人”的 anthrōpos 构成。它指厌恶人类或世人的人，不能简单等同于悲观的人或喜欢独处的人。
etymology_story.en: Misanthrope entered English in the sixteenth century through French, ultimately from Greek misanthrōpos, combining misein, “to hate,” with anthrōpos, “human being.” It denotes dislike of humankind, rather than merely pessimism or a preference for solitude.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可按古典构词成分理解为 mis-（憎恨）+ anthrop-（人）+ 词尾 -e；这里的 mis- 与 misunderstand 中表示“错误”的日耳曼语前缀不同。主要词族：misanthrope（厌人者）、misanthropy（厌恶人类的态度）、misanthropic（厌恶人类的）、misanthropically（以厌人的态度）；misanthropist 是 misanthrope 的较少用变体，misanthropical 是 misanthropic 的较少用变体。
morphology_enriched.en: The classical components are mis- “hate” + anthrop- “human” + the final -e; this mis- is distinct from the Germanic prefix meaning “wrongly” in misunderstand. The main family comprises misanthrope, misanthropy, misanthropic, and misanthropically; misanthropist is a less common alternative to misanthrope, and misanthropical is a less common alternative to misanthropic.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: misanthropist（厌人者）基本同义，但较少用；cynic（愤世嫉俗者）主要怀疑人的动机，未必厌恶所有人；recluse（隐居者）强调远离社交，其原因未必是厌恶人类。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Misanthropist is a less common near-exact equivalent; a cynic primarily doubts people's motives and need not dislike everyone; a recluse lives apart from others, possibly for reasons unrelated to hatred of humankind.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: mis- 在这里是“憎恨”，anthrop- 是“人”：把厌恶指向整个人类的人。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Here mis- means “hate” and anthrop- means “human”: a misanthrope directs that dislike toward humankind.

morphology.text: paella 作为独立词素记忆，不硬拆；可看西班牙语派生：paella + -era → paellera（做这种饭的平底锅），接词尾时省去末尾 a。

etymology.text: 英语从加泰罗尼亚语 paella 借入，原指烹调用的锅；更早经古法语 paelle，追溯到拉丁语 patella（小平锅）。菜名沿用了锅名。

usage_note: 指西班牙风味的米饭菜肴，配料可有海鲜、肉或蔬菜；不要求每一份都同时含鸡肉和海鲜。

etymology_story.zh: paella 的名称来自瓦伦西亚语（加泰罗尼亚语的一种）中表示“平锅”的 paella，这个词最终可追溯到拉丁语 patella“小浅盘；小平锅”。锅名后来转指锅中烹制的米饭菜肴，菜名随之传播到英语。
etymology_story.en: The name paella comes from the Valencian variety of Catalan, where paella means “pan,” ultimately tracing back to Latin patella, “small shallow dish or pan.” The name of the cooking vessel came to designate the rice dish prepared in it and subsequently entered English.

morphology_enriched.zh: paella 是整体借入英语的名词，在现代英语中不作有意义的内部拆分；复数为 paellas，可指多份、多锅或不同种类的这种饭。英语没有常用的直接派生词；相关借词 paellera 指专用浅平锅，属于西班牙语词族，不是英语中临时添加后缀形成的词。
morphology_enriched.en: Paella is a borrowed noun with no useful internal morphological division in modern English; its plural is paellas, referring to multiple dishes, pans, or varieties. It has no common direct English derivatives; the related borrowing paellera names the specialized shallow pan and belongs to the Spanish word family rather than a productive English suffix formation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有严格同义词。rice dish（米饭菜肴）是上位概念；risotto（意大利烩饭）通常边加汤边搅拌，质地较绵滑；pilaf（抓饭；焖饭）通常强调米粒分明，配料和做法与 paella 不同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact synonym. Rice dish is a broader category; risotto is typically stirred while stock is added, producing a creamy texture; pilaf generally emphasizes separate grains and differs from paella in its ingredients and preparation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“锅”记到“饭”：宽浅平锅里的西班牙米饭，就是 paella。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the vessel-to-dish connection: the Spanish rice cooked in the wide, shallow pan is paella.

etymology_story.zh: roadie 是20世纪形成的非正式称呼，由 road 加人物称呼后缀 -ie 构成；巡演工作人员这一意义与 on the road“在外巡演”有关。在骑行语境中，同样的词形也用于称呼主要在公路上骑车的人。
etymology_story.en: Roadie developed in twentieth-century informal English from road plus the familiar person-forming suffix -ie; its touring-crew meaning connects with on the road, meaning away on tour. In cycling, the same formation also labels someone who mainly rides on roads.

morphology_enriched.zh: road（公路；在巡演义中联系 on the road）+ -ie（非正式人物称呼后缀）→ roadie；复数为 roadies。没有常用的直接派生形容词或副词；road crew（巡演工作人员团队）、road manager（巡演经理）和 road cycling（公路自行车运动）是相关表达，不是 roadie 的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Road, connected with on the road in the touring sense, + the informal person-forming suffix -ie → roadie; the plural is roadies. There are no common directly derived adjectives or adverbs; road crew, road manager, and road cycling are related expressions rather than derivatives of roadie.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 巡演义：touring technician（巡演技术员）强调技术职责；stagehand（舞台工作人员）侧重舞台上的体力或技术工作，不一定随团巡演；crew member（工作人员）范围更广。骑行义中，road cyclist（公路骑行者）是更中性的对应表达。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the touring sense, touring technician emphasizes technical duties; stagehand focuses on practical stage work and need not involve touring; crew member is broader. In the cycling sense, road cyclist is the more neutral equivalent.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: road + 人物后缀 -ie：跟着巡演“上路”的工作人员，也可是在公路上骑车的人。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Road + the person suffix -ie: someone on the road with a touring act, or someone riding a road bike.

etymology_story.zh: scarab 经法语源自拉丁语 scarabaeus“甲虫”。由于古埃及人把圣甲虫与太阳运行及再生联系起来，这个名称也用于圣甲虫形的护符、饰物和印章。
etymology_story.en: Scarab came through French from Latin scarabaeus, meaning “beetle.” Because ancient Egyptians associated the sacred beetle with the sun's movement and renewal, the name also came to denote beetle-shaped amulets, ornaments, and seals.

morphology_enriched.zh: scarab 在现代英语中作为整体词干使用，复数为 scarabs；scarab + -oid（形似……的）→ scaraboid（圣甲虫形的；圣甲虫形物件）。相关的专业词 scarabaeid（金龟子科甲虫；金龟子科的）和 scarabaeoid（金龟子总科的）共享拉丁语词干 scarabae-，不宜机械分析为在英语 scarab 后直接添加完整词尾。
morphology_enriched.en: Scarab functions as a whole stem in modern English, with the plural scarabs; scarab + -oid, meaning “resembling,” → scaraboid, an adjective or noun for a scarab-like form. The related technical terms scarabaeid, referring to the scarab family, and scarabaeoid, referring to the scarab superfamily, share the Latin stem scarabae- rather than being straightforward additions to the English word scarab.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 甲虫义：scarabaeid（金龟子科甲虫）是专业对应词；dung beetle（蜣螂；粪金龟）按食性和行为命名，与 scarab 的范围部分重叠；beetle（甲虫）范围更广。器物义中的 amulet（护符）只说明用途，并不限定圣甲虫形状。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the insect, scarabaeid is the technical family-level equivalent; dung beetle identifies insects by their feeding habits and behavior and overlaps only partly with scarab; beetle is broader. For the artifact, amulet describes its protective function without specifying a beetle shape.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 先记“滚粪球的圣甲虫”，再记“仿照它做成的护符”：一个形象连接昆虫和器物两义。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture the sacred dung beetle, then a charm carved in its shape: one image connects the insect and the artifact.

etymology_story.en: Seamy was formed from seam and -y and originally described something having or showing seams. The seam-showing underside of clothing later supplied a metaphor for the unpleasant aspects of life that are normally hidden.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：seam（接缝）+ -y（具有……的）→ seamy。比较级 seamier，最高级 seamiest；派生词 seaminess（丑恶；肮脏）、seamily（丑恶地，少用）。相关词族包括 seam（接缝；缝合）、seamed（有接缝的）和 seamless（无接缝的；流畅无间的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: seam + -y ('having or characterized by') → seamy. Comparative: seamier; superlative: seamiest. Derivatives include seaminess and the uncommon adverb seamily. Related family members include seam as a noun and verb, seamed, and seamless.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sordid（肮脏卑劣的）强调令人厌恶的道德败坏；sleazy（低俗不正派的）常涉及色情、欺诈或廉价感；disreputable（声名不佳的）侧重社会评价。seamy 尤其强调体面表象背后被隐藏的丑恶。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sordid emphasizes disgusting moral degradation; sleazy often suggests sexual impropriety, dishonesty, or cheapness; disreputable focuses on a bad reputation. Seamy particularly suggests ugliness concealed beneath a respectable surface.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 翻到衣服露接缝的反面，就看见生活不体面的“另一面”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Turn clothing over to expose its seams: seamy reveals life's unattractive underside.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：sooth（真相，古语）+ say（说）+ -er（做某事的人）→ soothsayer。复数为 soothsayers；主要相关形式有 soothsaying（占卜；预言，也可作形容词表示预言的）和 soothsay（预言，罕用动词）。sooth 本身现主要见于古雅表达。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: sooth ('truth,' archaic) + say + -er ('a person who does something') → soothsayer. The plural is soothsayers. Principal related forms are soothsaying, a noun and adjective, and the rare verb soothsay. Sooth itself now occurs chiefly in archaic expressions.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: A fortune-teller commonly predicts an individual's future; a diviner seeks hidden knowledge through signs or divination; a prophet often speaks with religious or solemn authority. Soothsayer has a distinctly historical or literary flavor.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Sooth means 'truth': a soothsayer claims to tell the truth about the future.

senses.english_definition: If someone calls a man a tomcat, they mean that he frequently seeks sexual relationships with different people.
senses.collocation_en: an old tomcat; a notorious tomcat
senses.collocation_zh: 老色鬼；臭名昭著的好色之徒
senses.sentence_en: He had a reputation as a tomcat who was always chasing women.
senses.sentence_zh: 他是个出了名的好色之徒，总是追逐女人。

senses.meaning_zh: 到处寻欢；滥交（非正式，贬义，通常指男人）
senses.meaning_en: To seek frequent casual sexual relationships, usually said of a man.
senses.english_definition: If a man tomcats around, he spends time seeking casual sexual relationships with different people.
senses.collocation_en: tomcat around; go tomcatting
senses.collocation_zh: 四处寻欢；出去寻花问柳
senses.sentence_en: He spent his weekends tomcatting around town.
senses.sentence_zh: 他每逢周末就在城里四处寻欢。

etymology_story.zh: tomcat 由男性名字 Tom 与 cat 合成；Tom 后来也用于称呼某些雄性动物。公猫四处寻找配偶的行为又促成了“好色男人”的比喻义，以及表示四处寻欢的动词用法。
etymology_story.en: Tomcat combines the male name Tom with cat; Tom also came to serve as a name for males of certain animal species. The roaming mating behavior associated with male cats motivated the figurative noun for a promiscuous man and the corresponding verb.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：tom（雄性动物的称呼）+ cat（猫）→ tomcat；名词可零派生为动词。复数及动词第三人称单数为 tomcats；过去式和过去分词为 tomcatted，现在分词为 tomcatting，词尾 t 双写。tomcatting 也可作名词，表示四处寻欢的行为。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: tom ('a male animal') + cat → tomcat; the noun also becomes a verb by conversion. The plural and third-person singular are tomcats. The past tense and past participle are tomcatted, and the present participle is tomcatting, with final t doubled. Tomcatting can also name the behavior.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: male cat（公猫）是中性、明确的动物称谓；womanizer（玩弄女性的男人）对应人的比喻义，强调反复追逐女性；philander（拈花惹草）对应动词义，强调随意或不忠的情爱关系。tomcat 用于人时更口语化，也更具动物比喻色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Male cat is the neutral, explicit animal term; womanizer matches the figurative noun and emphasizes repeated pursuit of women; philander matches the verb and suggests casual or unfaithful romantic involvement. Applied to people, tomcat is more colloquial and vividly animal-based.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Tom 是公猫；想到公猫四处找伴侣，就能联想到“到处寻欢”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture Tom the male cat roaming for mates: the same image explains the figurative noun and verb.

forms: 可数名词；复数 toupees；也常写作 toupée。
family: toupeed 戴局部假发的

morphology.text: toupee 作为独立词素记忆；toupee + -ed → toupeed（戴假发的），这里 -ed 构成描述外观的形容词。

etymology.text: 18世纪英语从法语 toupet 借入，原指一小簇毛发；法语中表示“小”的词尾让人想到补在头顶的一小片头发。

usage_note: 通常指覆盖男性局部秃顶的假发片，比覆盖整个头部的 wig 更具体。

senses.meaning_zh: 男用局部假发；遮盖秃顶部位的假发片
senses.meaning_en: A small hairpiece worn to cover a bald area, usually by a man.
senses.english_definition: A toupee is a small piece of artificial or natural hair that a person, usually a man, wears to cover a bald part of the head.
senses.collocation_en: wear a toupee; a badly fitting toupee
senses.collocation_zh: 戴局部假发；不合头型的局部假发
senses.sentence_en: He wore a toupee to cover the bald patch on top of his head.
senses.sentence_zh: 他戴了一块局部假发，遮住头顶的秃发处。

etymology_story.zh: toupee 借自法语 toupet，原指一小簇头发；toupet 是表示一簇毛发的词的指小形式。英语中的词义逐渐专指用于遮盖秃发部位的小块假发。
etymology_story.en: Toupee was borrowed from French toupet, meaning a small tuft of hair and formed as a diminutive of a word for a tuft. In English, its meaning developed into a small hairpiece used to cover baldness.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 toupee 是不可再作常用英语词根、词缀拆分的借词，也写作 toupée。复数为 toupees；派生形容词 toupeed（亦作 toupéed）表示戴局部假发的，但不常见。toupee-wearing（戴局部假发的）是透明的复合修饰语；本词没有庞大的常用派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, toupee is a borrowed base without a useful breakdown into productive English roots and affixes; toupée is a spelling variant. The plural is toupees. The uncommon adjective toupeed, also toupéed, means wearing a toupee. Toupee-wearing is a transparent compound modifier; there is no extensive common derivative family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hairpiece（假发片）是更宽泛的称呼，可用于遮秃或增加发量；wig（假发）通常覆盖整个头部；rug（假发）是戏谑俚语。toupee 特指通常由男性佩戴、遮盖局部秃发的小块假发。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hairpiece is broader and can cover baldness or add volume; a wig usually covers the whole head; rug is a humorous slang term for a wig or toupee. Toupee specifically denotes a small piece covering a bald area, usually worn by a man.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“一小簇头发”想到“补在秃顶上的一小片头发”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think 'a little tuft of hair' becoming a little patch that covers a bald spot.

morphology.text: yeti 作为独立词素记忆；yeti + -like → yeti-like（像雪人的）。不要把它拆成英语 yet 和 i。

etymology.text: 20世纪英语从喜马拉雅地区夏尔巴人使用的藏语中借入 yeti，用来称呼当地传说中的神秘生物。

usage_note: 指传说中的喜马拉雅类人怪物，不是用雪堆成的 snowman；也可见首字母大写的 Yeti。

senses.meaning_zh: 雪人；传说中生活在喜马拉雅山区的大型类人生物
senses.meaning_en: A large, hairy, humanlike creature said to inhabit the Himalayas.
senses.english_definition: A yeti is a large, hairy creature resembling a human that some people believe lives in the Himalayan mountains.
senses.collocation_en: a yeti sighting; yeti footprints
senses.collocation_zh: 雪人目击事件；据称是雪人留下的脚印
senses.sentence_en: The climbers reported seeing footprints that they believed belonged to a yeti.
senses.sentence_zh: 登山者报告说，他们看到了自己认为是雪人留下的脚印。

etymology_story.zh: yeti 于20世纪从喜马拉雅地区的夏尔巴语借入英语，其来源与藏语有关。它原是当地传说中一种生物的名称，后来成为英语中称呼喜马拉雅雪人的常用词。
etymology_story.en: Yeti entered English in the twentieth century from Sherpa, a Himalayan language, with an origin connected to Tibetan. A local name for a legendary creature became the usual English term for the Himalayan yeti.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 yeti 是整体借入的单纯词，不能拆成 yet + i。复数通常为 yetis，也可见不变形式 yeti；yeti-like（像雪人的）由 yeti + -like 构成。本词没有常用的独立动词、形容词或副词派生形式；yeti 在 yeti sightings 等组合中是名词作定语。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, yeti is a borrowed simple base, not yet + i. The usual plural is yetis, although unchanged yeti also occurs. Yeti-like combines yeti with -like. There are no established common verb, adjective, or adverb derivatives; yeti functions as a noun modifier in combinations such as yeti sightings.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Abominable Snowman（喜马拉雅雪人）是 yeti 的传统英语别称；Bigfoot（大脚怪）和 Sasquatch（萨斯夸奇）通常指北美传说中的类似生物，二者彼此近义，但并非 yeti 的严格同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Abominable Snowman is a traditional English alternative name for the yeti. Bigfoot and Sasquatch usually name a similar legendary North American creature; they are close synonyms of each other, but not exact synonyms of yeti.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 yeti 整体对应到“喜马拉雅山中的毛茸茸雪人”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor yeti to one image: a shaggy, humanlike creature in the snowy Himalayas.

etymology.text: 19世纪英语用拉丁语来源的 bi-（二）与 annual（每年的）组合出 biannual。记成一年内安排两回。

usage_note: 本课采用“一年两次”的常见义。实际安排宜写明月份，以免与 biennial（两年一次）混淆。

senses.meaning_zh: 一年两次的；每半年一次的
senses.meaning_en: happening twice a year
senses.english_definition: A biannual event happens twice each year.
senses.collocation_en: a biannual conference; a biannual review
senses.collocation_zh: 一年举行两次的会议；每半年一次的审查
senses.sentence_en: The committee holds biannual meetings in April and October.
senses.sentence_zh: 委员会每年在四月和十月各举行一次会议。

etymology_story.zh: biannual 在19世纪由表示“两次”的前缀 bi- 与 annual（每年的）组合而成，两部分都具有拉丁语来源。它的标准含义是“一年两次”，但实际使用中有时会与表示“每两年一次”的 biennial 混淆。
etymology_story.en: Biannual was formed in the nineteenth century from bi-, meaning 'twice,' and annual, meaning 'yearly'; both elements have Latin origins. Its standard meaning is 'twice a year,' although it is sometimes confused with biennial, meaning 'every two years.'

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：bi-（两次）+ annual（每年的）→ biannual（一年两次的）；biannual + -ly → biannually（一年两次地）。基础词族包括 annual（每年的；年刊）和 annually（每年）；biennial（每两年一次的）是相关词，不是 biannual 的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: bi- ('twice') + annual ('yearly') → biannual; biannual + -ly → biannually ('twice a year'). The base family includes annual ('yearly; a yearly publication') and annually ('every year'); biennial ('every two years') is related but is not derived from biannual.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: semiannual（每半年一次的）与 biannual 通常同义，常用于财务或行政语境；twice-yearly（一年两次的）最直白，尤其适合需要避免歧义的表达。注意 biennial 表示“每两年一次”，不是同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Semiannual normally means the same as biannual and is common in financial or administrative contexts; twice-yearly is especially explicit and useful when ambiguity matters. Biennial means 'every two years' and is not a synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: bi- 表示“两次”，annual 表示“每年”：一年日历上打两个点。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Bi- means 'twice' and annual means 'yearly': put two dots on one year's calendar.

pronunciation.note: 重音按音标中的 ˈ 标记朗读；本卡采用英语词典中的读法。

morphology.text: bijou 作为独立词素记忆；法语派生 bijou + -terie → bijouterie（珠宝饰品），后者也借入了英语。

etymology.text: 经法语 bijou（珠宝）借入英语；更早来自布列塔尼语 bizou（戒指），与 biz（手指）有关。从小首饰联想到小巧精致。

usage_note: 常放在住宅、房间等名词前，表示小而精致；房产广告中有时带委婉或幽默语气。

senses.meaning_zh: 小巧精致的；小而雅致的，尤用于房屋或场所
senses.meaning_en: small, attractive, and elegantly arranged, especially of a home or venue
senses.english_definition: A bijou house or other place is small but attractive and elegant.
senses.collocation_en: a bijou apartment; a bijou residence
senses.collocation_zh: 小巧精致的公寓；小而雅致的住宅
senses.sentence_en: They rented a bijou apartment overlooking the harbour.
senses.sentence_zh: 他们租了一套小巧精致、可以俯瞰港口的公寓。

senses.meaning_zh: 小件珠宝；精巧的装饰品，属较少见用法
senses.meaning_en: a small jewel or finely made ornament; an uncommon use
senses.english_definition: A bijou is a small piece of jewellery or another delicate ornamental object.
senses.collocation_en: an antique bijou; a collection of bijoux
senses.collocation_zh: 一件古董珠宝饰品；一批小件珠宝或精巧饰品
senses.sentence_en: The catalogue described the tiny enamel pendant as a bijou.
senses.sentence_zh: 目录将那枚小巧的珐琅吊坠称为一件精巧珠宝。

etymology_story.zh: bijou 于17世纪从法语借入英语，原指珠宝或精巧饰品；其更早来源通常追溯到布列塔尼语 bizou（戒指），与 biz（手指）有关。英语后来把“小件珠宝”的精致感引申到小而雅致的住宅和其他场所。
etymology_story.en: Bijou entered English from French in the seventeenth century, originally meaning a jewel or delicate ornament; its earlier source is generally traced to Breton bizou ('ring'), related to biz ('finger'). English later extended the elegance of a small jewel to small, attractive homes and other places.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 bijou 是整体借词，不宜拆成英语词根和词缀；名词复数为 bijoux，也可用 bijous。相关借词 bijouterie 表示“小件珠宝；饰品”，在法语中由 bijou 所属词干加 -erie 构成，并非英语中常用的自由派生形式；bijou 本身没有常用的英语派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, bijou is a whole-word borrowing rather than an English root-and-affix formation; its noun plurals are bijoux and bijous. The related borrowing bijouterie means 'small jewellery or ornaments' and was formed in French with -erie; it is not a freely productive English derivative. Bijou has no common English derivational family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: dainty（小巧秀美的）强调精细、轻巧的外观；compact（紧凑的）强调体积小和空间利用，不一定雅致；jewel（珠宝；珍品）可对应名词义，而 bijou 更突出小巧、精致的饰物。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Dainty emphasizes delicate, attractive appearance; compact emphasizes small size and efficient use of space without necessarily implying elegance. Jewel overlaps with the noun sense, while bijou particularly suggests a small, finely made ornament.

etymology_story.zh: blitzkrieg 于20世纪30年代从德语 Blitzkrieg 借入英语，由 Blitz（闪电）与 Krieg（战争）组成，字面意思是“闪电般的战争”。它因第二次世界大战初期德国的快速攻势而广为人知，后来也用于比喻迅猛、集中的宣传或其他攻势。
etymology_story.en: Blitzkrieg entered English in the 1930s from German Blitzkrieg, combining Blitz ('lightning') and Krieg ('war'). It became widely known through Germany's rapid offensives early in the Second World War and later acquired figurative uses for sudden, concentrated publicity or other campaigns.

morphology_enriched.zh: 来源语言构词：德语 Blitz（闪电）+ Krieg（战争）→ Blitzkrieg；英语将整个复合词借入，再通过零派生用于动词。英语屈折形式包括 blitzkriegs、blitzkrieged、blitzkrieging；相关缩略词 blitz（猛烈袭击；集中行动）又有 blitzes、blitzed、blitzing 等形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Source-language formation: German Blitz ('lightning') + Krieg ('war') → Blitzkrieg; English borrowed the compound and also converted it into a verb without an added suffix. English inflected forms include blitzkriegs, blitzkrieged, and blitzkrieging. The related shortening blitz ('an intense attack or concentrated campaign') has the forms blitzes, blitzed, and blitzing.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: lightning offensive（闪电攻势）最接近其军事本义，强调速度与突然性；onslaught（猛攻）强调攻击的强度，不一定迅速结束；blitz（猛烈袭击；集中行动）更简短，且更常用于宣传、工作等非军事语境。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Lightning offensive is closest to the military meaning and emphasizes speed and surprise; onslaught emphasizes the intensity of an attack without necessarily implying a quick conclusion. Blitz is shorter and more readily used for publicity, work, and other non-military campaigns.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Blitz 是“闪电”，Krieg 是“战争”：像闪电一样迅速压倒对手。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Blitz is 'lightning' and Krieg is 'war': overwhelm the opponent at lightning speed.

etymology_story.zh: catcall 出现于17世纪，由 cat（猫）与 call（叫声）组成，早期指模仿猫叫的尖锐哨声或发出这种声音的哨子，常用于在剧场表达不满。它后来泛指嘲弄的叫喊或口哨声，并发展出如今常见的公共场所性骚扰用法。
etymology_story.en: Catcall arose in the seventeenth century from cat and call, initially referring to a shrill, catlike whistle or an instrument producing it, often used to express disapproval in theatres. It later broadened to mocking shouts and whistles and developed the now-common sense of unwanted sexual remarks or whistles in public.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：cat（猫）+ call（叫声）→ catcall，为复合词；名词与动词之间无需添加词缀即可转换。词族及屈折形式：catcalls（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、catcalled（过去式及过去分词）、catcalling（现在分词；起哄或街头言语性骚扰）、catcaller（起哄者；发出骚扰性叫喊或口哨声的人）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: cat + call → catcall, a compound with noun and verb uses linked by conversion without an added suffix. Its family and inflected forms include catcalls (plural noun or third-person singular verb), catcalled (past tense and past participle), catcalling (present participle; mocking or sexual street harassment), and catcaller (a person who makes such calls).

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: jeer（嘲弄的叫喊；嘲笑）强调轻蔑或讥讽，不必含性意味；boo（嘘声；喝倒彩）特指用“嘘”一类声音表示不满；wolf-whistle（挑逗性的口哨声；吹挑逗口哨）仅指口哨，而性骚扰义的 catcall 也可包含言语叫喊。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Jeer emphasizes contempt or mockery and need not be sexual; boo specifically means a vocal sound of disapproval. Wolf-whistle refers specifically to a sexually suggestive whistle, whereas a sexual catcall can also consist of shouted words.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“刺耳的猫叫”记住“冲人发出的刺耳叫喊”：可表示嘲弄，也可构成骚扰。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with a harsh catlike call, then picture a harsh call directed at a person: it may mock or sexually harass.

morphology.text: 法语 coul-（来自 couler，流动）+ -oir（地点或器具后缀）→ couloir（通道）；英语整体借入后用于狭窄山沟。

etymology.text: 19世纪英语从法语 couloir 借入；法语中这个词可指通道，英语登山用语把山间长而窄的陡沟比作通道。

usage_note: 登山与滑雪语境常见，通常指山侧陡峭而狭窄的沟槽，不是一般宽阔山谷。

etymology_story.zh: couloir 于19世纪从法语借入英语；法语中该词表示通道或走廊，与 couler（流动）有关，更早可追溯到拉丁语 colare（过滤）。英语登山用语沿用了“通道”的形象，用它指山体上狭长、陡峭的沟槽。
etymology_story.en: Couloir entered English from French in the nineteenth century; in French it means a passage or corridor and is related to couler ('to flow'), ultimately from Latin colare ('to strain or filter'). English mountaineering usage applies the image of a passage to a steep, narrow mountain gully.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 couloir 是整体借词，没有常用的英语前后缀拆分；复数为 couloirs。历史上的法语构词可分析为 coul-（与 couler“流动”有关）+ -oir（构成地点或器具名词的后缀）；英语中没有常用的直接派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, couloir is a whole-word borrowing with no usual English prefix-and-suffix breakdown; its plural is couloirs. Its historical French formation can be analysed as coul- (related to couler, 'to flow') + -oir (a suffix forming names of places or instruments). It has no common direct English derivational family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: gully（沟壑）含义较广，不一定位于高山或十分陡峭；chute（陡槽；滑道）在滑雪语境中可指类似地形，强调陡降通道；ravine（深而狭窄的峡谷）通常规模更大，也不一定适合作为登山或滑雪路线。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Gully is broader and need not describe high or especially steep terrain; chute can describe similar skiing terrain and emphasizes a steep descending channel. Ravine usually denotes a larger, deep, narrow valley and does not necessarily suggest a climbing or skiing route.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 couloir 想成山上的“天然走廊”：两侧是岩壁，中间是狭长陡沟。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a natural mountain corridor: rock walls on either side and a steep, narrow channel between them.

etymology.text: 这是拉丁语词素组成的科学名称，falc- 表示镰刀；名称与这种疟原虫镰刀状的配子体有关，随后进入英语医学用语。

usage_note: 医学与寄生虫学用词，常见完整名称 Plasmodium falciparum；不是泛指所有疟原虫。

etymology_story.zh: Falciparum 是新拉丁语科学命名用词，历史成分包括源于 falx（镰刀）的 falci- 和与 parere（产生、孕育）有关的 -parum。名称意为“产生镰刀状结构的”，指这种疟原虫特有的镰刀状配子体，后来随学名进入英语医学用语。
etymology_story.en: Falciparum is a scientific New Latin formation combining falci-, from falx meaning 'sickle,' with -parum, related to parere meaning 'to produce or bring forth.' The name refers to the parasite's sickle-shaped gametocytes and entered medical English through its scientific name.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语将 falciparum 作为完整的科学名称成分使用，没有常用的英语派生词，也通常不加复数词尾。历史构词为 falci-（镰刀）+ -parum（产生、孕育）；falciform（镰刀状的）是共享镰刀词根的相关词，并非由 falciparum 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats falciparum as a complete scientific-name element, with no common English derivatives or regular plural ending. Its historical structure is falci- ('sickle') + -parum ('producing or bearing'); falciform ('sickle-shaped') shares the sickle root but is not derived from falciparum.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Plasmodium falciparum（恶性疟原虫）是完整学名，P. falciparum 是属名缩写后的同义形式；malaria parasite（疟原虫）范围更广，可指其他引起疟疾的物种，不能作为精确替换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Plasmodium falciparum is the full scientific name, while P. falciparum is its abbreviated equivalent. Malaria parasite is broader and can refer to other malaria-causing species, so it is not an exact substitute.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 镰刀形配子体 → falci- 的“镰刀” → 恶性疟原虫。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Sickle-shaped gametocytes → the 'sickle' in falci- → the falciparum parasite.

morphology.text: Garden（人名）+ -ia（植物名称常见词尾）→ gardenia（栀子）；不要拆成 garden + ia 并理解成“小花园”。

etymology.text: 18世纪的新拉丁语植物名 Gardenia 纪念博物学家 Alexander Garden，英语随后采用 gardenia 作为植物与花朵的名称。

usage_note: 可指栀子植株或栀子花；普通花名小写，科学属名 Gardenia 首字母大写。

senses.meaning_zh: 栀子属植物，尤指栀子；栀子花
senses.meaning_en: A gardenia shrub, especially one grown for its fragrant white flowers, or one of its flowers
senses.english_definition: A gardenia is a shrub grown for its sweet-smelling, usually white flowers, and a flower from this shrub is also called a gardenia.
senses.collocation_en: gardenia flowers; a gardenia bush
senses.collocation_zh: 栀子花；一丛栀子
senses.sentence_en: She placed a white gardenia in a small vase.
senses.sentence_zh: 她把一朵白色栀子花插进了一个小花瓶。

etymology_story.zh: 18世纪，博物学家 John Ellis 将这一植物属命名为 Gardenia，以纪念医生兼博物学家 Alexander Garden。英语随后采用 gardenia，既指植物，也指它的花朵。
etymology_story.en: In the eighteenth century, the naturalist John Ellis named the genus Gardenia in honour of the physician and naturalist Alexander Garden. English subsequently adopted gardenia for both the plant and its flowers.

morphology_enriched.zh: 命名结构为 Garden（人名）+ -ia（用于属名等名称的词尾）；现代英语将 gardenia 作为完整名词使用。常规复数为 gardenias（栀子植株或花朵），没有常用的进一步派生词；Gardenia jasminoides 是常见栀子的学名。
morphology_enriched.en: The naming structure is Garden (a person's surname) + -ia (a name-forming ending used in genus names). Modern English treats gardenia as a complete noun; its regular plural is gardenias, and it has no common further derivatives. Gardenia jasminoides is the scientific name of the familiar cultivated gardenia.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Cape jasmine 和 cape jessamine 都是 Gardenia jasminoides 的俗名，通常均译作“栀子”；gardenia 的范围更广，还可指栀子属其他植物及其花朵。这些俗名中的 jasmine 不表示栀子属于真正的茉莉属。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cape jasmine and cape jessamine are alternative common names for Gardenia jasminoides. Gardenia is broader, covering other members of the genus and their flowers; the word jasmine in those common names does not make gardenias members of the true jasmine genus.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Garden 是被纪念的人名：Garden + -ia → 以人名命名的栀子。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the person Garden: Garden + -ia → the gardenia named in his honour.

pronunciation.note: 重音按音标中的 ˈ 标记朗读；本卡采用英语词典中的读法。

forms: 不可数名词；不把词尾 s 当作英语复数。
family: gravity 严肃；重力（同源词）

morphology.text: 拉丁语 grav-（重）+ -itas（性质）→ gravitas（分量；庄重）；英语整体借入，现代使用时作为独立词素记忆。

etymology.text: 英语直接借自拉丁语 gravitas（分量、严肃），与 gravis（重的）有关。把一个人讲话“有分量”的感觉与庄重气度联系起来。

usage_note: 较正式，常评价人的气度、发言或表现有分量；不是物理学的重力术语。

senses.meaning_zh: 庄重；使人信服并产生敬意的严肃气度或威严
senses.meaning_en: Seriousness and dignity that make someone seem worthy of respect and trust
senses.english_definition: If someone has gravitas, their serious and dignified manner makes other people respect them and take them seriously.
senses.collocation_en: have gravitas; lend gravitas to something
senses.collocation_zh: 具有庄重威严的气度；为某事增添庄重感或分量
senses.sentence_en: Her calm delivery lent gravitas to the speech.
senses.sentence_zh: 她沉稳的表达让这篇演讲更显庄重，更有分量。

etymology_story.zh: 英语直接借用了拉丁语 gravitas，原义包括“重量、分量”和“严肃、庄重”，其基础词 gravis 意为“重的”。从实际重量到人格与言行的“分量”，形成了现代英语中令人敬重的庄重气度之义。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed Latin gravitas, which meant both 'weight' and 'seriousness or dignity,' from gravis meaning 'heavy.' The movement from physical weight to the figurative weight of someone's character or conduct explains its modern meaning.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 gravitas 是整体借入的不可数名词，通常没有复数，也没有常用的直接派生词。历史结构为 grav-（重）+ 拉丁语抽象名词后缀 -itas（性质、状态）；相关词包括 grave（严肃的）、gravity（重力；严肃）、gravitate（受吸引而趋向）和 gravitation（引力作用），它们是同源相关词，并非都由英语 gravitas 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, gravitas is a borrowed uncountable noun, normally without a plural or common direct derivatives. Its historical structure is grav- ('heavy') + the Latin abstract-noun suffix -itas ('quality or state'); related words include grave, gravity, gravitate, and gravitation, which belong to the same historical family rather than all deriving from English gravitas.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: dignity（尊严、庄重）强调值得尊重的举止或身份；solemnity（肃穆、庄严）强调严肃的情绪或场合；authority（权威）强调使人信服或服从的力量。gravitas 特别强调一个人因沉稳庄重而显得有分量。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Dignity emphasizes respectable bearing or status; solemnity emphasizes a serious mood or occasion; authority emphasizes the power to command belief or obedience. Gravitas particularly suggests the personal weight created by a serious, composed manner.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 思想和言行“有重量” → 为人有分量 → gravitas。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Weight in someone's words and manner → personal weight → gravitas.

pronunciation.note: 重音按音标中的 ˈ 标记朗读；本卡采用英语词典中的读法。

morphology.text: 日语 hai-（取自 haikai，俳谐）+ ku（句）→ haiku（俳句）；英语把这个诗体名称整体借入。

etymology.text: 19世纪末英语从日语 haiku 借入；名称取自 haikai 的 hai 与表示诗句的 ku。记住短小而凝练的日式诗歌。

usage_note: 一种日本短诗体。英文俳句常写成三行；日语传统的音数不能简单等同于所有英文作品的音节规则。

senses.pos: n. 名词（诗作可数；诗体可作不可数用法）
senses.meaning_zh: 俳句；传统上采用五、七、五音拍结构的日本短诗及其诗体
senses.meaning_en: A Japanese short poetic form, or a poem in that form, traditionally using a 5–7–5 pattern of Japanese sound units
senses.english_definition: A haiku is a very short poem in a Japanese tradition, often capturing a moment in nature; traditional Japanese haiku use a pattern of five, seven, and five sound units.
senses.collocation_en: write a haiku; a collection of haiku
senses.collocation_zh: 写一首俳句；一本俳句集
senses.sentence_en: She wrote a haiku about rain falling on an empty street.
senses.sentence_zh: 她写了一首俳句，描绘雨落在空荡街道上的情景。

etymology_story.zh: 英语 haiku 借自日语“俳句”，其名称结合了 haikai（俳谐）的 hai 与 ku（句）。这一现代名称由19世纪末的正冈子规推广，用于从较早的发句传统中发展出来的独立短诗。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed haiku from Japanese, where the name combines hai from haikai with ku meaning 'verse.' Masaoka Shiki popularized the modern term in the late nineteenth century for independent short poems developed from the earlier hokku tradition.

morphology_enriched.zh: 日语来源结构为 hai（取自 haikai，俳谐）+ ku（句）；现代英语整体借入，不把这两个成分当作能产的英语词缀。复数可用 haiku 或 haikus；haiku poet（俳句诗人）和 haiku poetry（俳句诗歌）是常见组合，没有常用的英语直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: The Japanese source structure is hai (from haikai) + ku ('verse'); English borrows the whole word rather than using these components as productive English affixes. Both haiku and haikus occur as plurals; haiku poet and haiku poetry are common combinations, and there are no common direct English derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: haiku poem（俳句诗）是含义相同的展开表达。相关术语 hokku（发句）原指连歌的起首诗节，是俳句的重要历史来源；senryu（川柳）是相近的短诗形式，通常更侧重人情世态，不能与 haiku 完全互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Haiku poem is an equivalent expanded expression. The related term hokku originally names the opening verse of linked poetry and is a historical predecessor of haiku; senryu is a related short form usually focused more on human behaviour, so neither term is fully interchangeable with haiku.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: hai（俳谐）+ ku（句）→ 用极短的诗捕捉一个瞬间；日语传统节奏为五、七、五音拍。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hai from haikai + ku meaning 'verse' → a tiny poem capturing a moment, traditionally in a Japanese 5–7–5 sound-unit pattern.

pronunciation.note: 重音按音标中的 ˈ 标记朗读；本卡采用英语词典中的读法。

morphology.text: honey（蜂蜜）+ dew（露）→ honeydew；本课的蜜瓜义可联想它甜而多汁的果肉。

etymology.text: honeydew 是英语 honey 与 dew 的复合词，早期用于甜的露状物；后来也用作一种甜瓜的名称。

usage_note: 本课学蜜瓜义，常说 honeydew melon；在昆虫和植物语境中 honeydew 还可指蜜露，须看语境。
