etymology_story.zh: Honeydew 由 honey（蜂蜜）和 dew（露水）组成，早期指植物表面像露珠一样的甜液，后来也用于特定的甜瓜名称。昆虫蜜露义保留了“甜露”的直观意象，甜瓜义则让人联想到果肉的甜味与汁水。
etymology_story.en: Honeydew combines honey and dew and originally referred to sweet, dew-like liquid found on plants; it was later also used as the name of a type of melon. The insect secretion retains the image of 'sweet dew,' while the melon sense evokes sweetness and juiciness.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词为 honey（蜂蜜；甜味）+ dew（露水）→ honeydew，是名词与名词组成的复合词。指整只甜瓜时复数为 honeydews；指果肉或昆虫蜜露时通常不可数；honeydew melon（蜜露甜瓜）是常见扩展名称，没有常用的进一步派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern structure is honey + dew → honeydew, a noun–noun compound. Honeydews is the plural for whole melons, while the flesh and insect secretion are normally uncountable; honeydew melon is a common expanded name, and there are no common further derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: honeydew melon（蜜露甜瓜）与水果义的 honeydew 同义；melon（甜瓜）是范围更广的上位词；cantaloupe（另一类甜瓜，通常为橙色果肉）是相关水果，不能精确替换。昆虫分泌物义没有同样常用的单词同义词，nectar（花蜜）来源不同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Honeydew melon is an exact equivalent for the fruit sense; melon is a broader category; cantaloupe is a related melon, usually with orange flesh, rather than an exact synonym. The insect secretion has no equally common single-word synonym, and nectar comes from a different source.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 像 honey 一样甜、像 dew 一样成滴 → 叶上的蜜露；再联想到甜而多汁的蜜露甜瓜。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Sweet as honey, droplet-like as dew → honeydew on leaves; extend the image to a sweet, juicy honeydew melon.

meaning: 好打官司的；动辄诉讼的

pronunciation.note: 重音按音标中的 ˈ 标记朗读；本卡采用英语词典中的读法。

forms: 形容词；比较程度用 more / most litigious。

morphology.text: litigious + -ness → litigiousness（好诉讼的倾向）；litigious 整体记忆，litig- 与争讼有关。

usage_note: 通常带批评意味，强调过于容易起诉；不只是“懂法律”。本课不学“与诉讼有关的”另一义。

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 litigiosus，意为“好争讼的”，与 litigium（争执、诉讼）及 litigare（争讼）同源。英语保留了争讼这一核心意义，现代尤其强调频繁诉诸法院的倾向。
etymology_story.en: The word derives from Latin litigiosus, meaning disposed to disputes or lawsuits, and is related to litigium, a dispute, and litigare, to litigate. English retained this connection with disputes, especially a tendency to take them to court.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可分析为 litig-（与诉讼有关的词干）+ -ious（形容词后缀）；不是由现代动词 litigate 直接规则派生。直接派生词：litigiously（好诉讼地）、litigiousness（好诉讼的倾向）；同源词族：litigate（进行诉讼）、litigation（诉讼）、litigant（诉讼当事人）、litigator（诉讼律师）。
morphology_enriched.en: A useful modern analysis is litig- (a stem associated with legal disputes) + -ious (an adjective-forming suffix); it is not a regular direct formation from the modern verb litigate. Direct derivatives are litigiously and litigiousness; related family members include litigate, litigation, litigant, and litigator.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: lawsuit-prone 指容易或经常提起诉讼，最接近核心义；contentious 强调容易引起争议或喜欢争辩；quarrelsome 强调爱与人争吵，通常不涉及法律。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Lawsuit-prone is closest to the central meaning of frequently bringing lawsuits; contentious emphasizes controversy or argument; quarrelsome describes a tendency to argue with people, usually without a legal implication.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 litig- 连到 litigation（诉讼）：遇到争执就想到打官司。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link litig- to litigation: a dispute immediately becomes a lawsuit.

pronunciation.note: 重音按音标中的 ˈ 标记朗读；本卡采用英语词典中的读法。

usage_note: 生物学与皮肤相关语境常见；不要与拼写相近的 melatonin（褪黑素）混淆。

senses.meaning_zh: 黑色素；一类影响皮肤、毛发和眼睛颜色的天然色素
senses.meaning_en: A group of natural pigments that contribute to the color of skin, hair, and eyes.
senses.english_definition: Melanin is a natural pigment that helps give your skin, hair, and eyes their color and helps protect your skin from ultraviolet radiation.
senses.collocation_en: melanin production; melanin levels
senses.collocation_zh: 黑色素的生成；黑色素含量
senses.sentence_en: Exposure to sunlight can increase melanin production in the skin.

etymology_story.zh: 这是19世纪形成的科学术语，由源自希腊语 melas（黑色的）的 melan- 与物质名词后缀 -in 构成。名称最初突出色素的深色特征，现代则涵盖包括棕黑色和黄红色色素在内的黑色素类别。
etymology_story.en: This nineteenth-century scientific term combines melan-, from Greek melas, meaning black, with the substance-forming suffix -in. Its name highlights dark coloration, although the modern category includes both brown-black and yellow-red pigments.

morphology_enriched.zh: melan-（黑、深色）+ -in（物质名词后缀）→ melanin。相关词族：melanic（黑色素的；深色的）、melanism（黑化现象）、melanistic（黑化的）、melanize/melanise（使黑化）、melanization/melanisation（黑化；黑色素沉积）；同词根术语有 melanocyte（黑色素细胞）、melanogenesis（黑色素生成）、eumelanin（真黑色素）、pheomelanin（褐黑色素）、neuromelanin（神经黑色素）。
morphology_enriched.en: melan- (black or dark) + -in (a substance-forming suffix) → melanin. Related family members include melanic, melanism, melanistic, melanize/melanise, and melanization/melanisation; terms sharing the combining form include melanocyte, melanogenesis, eumelanin, pheomelanin, and neuromelanin.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有严格的日常同义词：pigment（色素）是上位词；eumelanin（真黑色素）指棕黑色的一类黑色素；pheomelanin（褐黑色素）指黄红色的一类黑色素，后两者都不能替代整个类别。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact everyday synonym: pigment is a broader category; eumelanin is the brown-black type of melanin; pheomelanin is the yellow-red type. Neither subtype name replaces the name of the whole group.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: melan- 表示“黑”，-in 表示“物质”：与深色有关的天然色素。
mnemonic_anchor.en: melan- means black and -in names a substance: think of the natural pigment behind darker coloring.

etymology_story.zh: 英语在19世纪由 periscopic 逆构出 periscope，相关构词成分来自希腊语 peri（周围）和 skopein（观察）。这个名称最初体现向周围观察的概念，后来尤其与潜艇越过水面观察的装置联系起来。
etymology_story.en: English formed periscope in the nineteenth century by back-formation from periscopic, using elements from Greek peri, meaning around, and skopein, meaning to look. The name expressed the idea of looking around and became especially associated with instruments used to observe the surface from submarines.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可分析为 peri-（周围）+ -scope（观察仪器）→ periscope。词族：periscopic（潜望镜的；借助潜望镜的）、periscopically（以潜望镜方式）；periscopes 是名词复数。现代构词分析与历史上的逆构方向应分别理解。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern structure is peri- (around) + -scope (a viewing instrument) → periscope. Family members include periscopic and periscopically; periscopes is the noun's plural. This structural analysis should be distinguished from the historical direction of back-formation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有完全对应的常用同义词：indirect-viewing instrument（间接观察仪器）强调绕过直视限制的功能；viewing tube（观察管）强调管状结构，范围更宽，不能准确指明潜望镜。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact common synonym: indirect-viewing instrument describes the function of seeing without a direct line of sight; viewing tube describes a broader structural category and does not specifically identify a periscope.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: peri-（周围）+ scope（看）：视线绕过遮挡，人藏着也能看。
mnemonic_anchor.en: peri- means around and -scope means viewing: your line of sight goes around an obstacle.

etymology_story.zh: 这是英语 sea（海）与 worthy（适合的、足以胜任的）组成的复合词，用来描述船只是否能胜任海上航行。这里 worthy 的意义从“值得的”延伸为“适合某种用途的”。
etymology_story.en: This English compound joins sea with worthy in the sense of fit or suitable, describing a vessel's fitness for travel at sea. Here worthy extends beyond deserving something to being suitable for a particular use.

morphology_enriched.zh: sea（海）+ worthy（适合的）→ seaworthy；seaworthy 去掉词尾 y 并加 -iness → seaworthiness（适航性）。词族还包括 unseaworthy（不适航的）和 unseaworthiness（不适航性）。
morphology_enriched.en: sea + worthy (fit or suitable) → seaworthy; replacing the final y with -iness gives seaworthiness. The family also includes unseaworthy and unseaworthiness.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: fit to sail 指状况适合航行，最接近核心义；sea-ready 强调已经做好出海准备；ocean-going 强调适于或用于远洋航行，并不单独保证船只当前适航。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Fit to sail closely matches the core meaning of being in suitable condition; sea-ready emphasizes readiness to depart; ocean-going describes suitability or intended use for ocean voyages without by itself guaranteeing a vessel's present condition.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: sea + worthy：船能胜任大海，才算适航。
mnemonic_anchor.en: sea + worthy: a boat must be fit for the sea.

senses.meaning_zh: 形成新物种；发生物种分化

senses.english_definition: When a population speciates, it evolves into one or more species that are distinct from the original species.

senses.meaning_zh: 对……进行化学形态分析；鉴定或测定其中的化学物种

etymology_story.zh: 英语在20世纪从 speciation（物种形成）逆构出动词 speciate；其基础 species 来自拉丁语 species，原意包括“外观、形态、种类”。化学也用 species 表示特定化学物种，因此 speciate 还用于分析物质以哪些化学形态存在。
etymology_story.en: English formed speciate in the twentieth century by back-formation from speciation; the underlying word species comes from Latin species, meaning appearance, form, or kind. Chemistry also uses species for a particular chemical entity, supporting the analytical sense of identifying a substance's chemical forms.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可分析为 speci-（与 species“物种、种类”有关的词干）+ -ate（动词后缀）→ speciate；历史上则是由 speciation 逆构而来。词族：species（物种；化学物种）、speciation（物种形成；化学形态分布或形态分析）；动词变化为 speciates、speciated、speciating。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern structure can be analyzed as speci- (a stem associated with species or kinds) + -ate (a verb-forming suffix), although historically the verb was back-formed from speciation. The family includes species and speciation, which has both biological and chemical uses; verb forms are speciates, speciated, and speciating.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 生物学中，evolve（进化）范围更广，不一定产生新物种；diversify（发生多样化）强调差异增加，也不一定跨越物种界限。化学中，determine chemical forms（测定化学形态）是对应的解释性近义表达。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: In biology, evolve is broader and does not necessarily involve new species; diversify emphasizes increasing variety and may occur without crossing species boundaries. In chemistry, determine chemical forms is an explanatory equivalent.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住 species 的“种类”：生物分出新物种，化学分清不同形态。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor it to species as kinds: biology produces new species; chemistry distinguishes chemical forms.

pronunciation.note: 重音按音标中的 ˈ 标记朗读；本卡采用英语词典中的读法。

forms: 名词复数 toadies；同形动词有 toadies、toadied、toadying。
family: toadyism 谄媚；toadyish 谄媚的

morphology.text: toady + -ism → toadyism（谄媚行为）；toady 作为独立词素记忆，不把它理解为“小蟾蜍”。

etymology.text: 英语 toady 由较早的 toadeater 缩短而来，原先用于江湖卖药人的跟班，后来转指为了好处而讨好人的人。

usage_note: 贬义，强调为了个人利益而卑躬屈膝地讨好有权势者。

senses.meaning_zh: 谄媚者；为谋取好处而讨好权势者的人
senses.meaning_en: A person who flatters someone powerful to gain an advantage.
senses.english_definition: If you call someone a toady, you disapprove of them because they flatter and obey someone powerful to gain an advantage.
senses.collocation_en: a servile toady; a political toady
senses.collocation_zh: 卑躬屈膝的谄媚者；政治上的马屁精
senses.sentence_en: He surrounded himself with toadies who agreed with everything he said.
senses.sentence_zh: 他身边围着一群马屁精，无论他说什么都表示赞同。

senses.meaning_zh: 谄媚；巴结；奉承权势者以谋利
senses.meaning_en: To flatter or behave submissively toward someone powerful to gain an advantage.
senses.english_definition: If someone toadies to a powerful person, they flatter that person and try excessively to please them.
senses.collocation_en: toady to the boss; toady to those in power
senses.collocation_zh: 巴结老板；谄媚当权者
senses.sentence_en: She refused to toady to the boss just to get promoted.
senses.sentence_zh: 她不愿仅仅为了升职就去巴结老板。

etymology_story.zh: toady 是 toadeater 的缩略形式；后者原指江湖卖药人的助手，据说他们吞下被认为有毒的蟾蜍，以配合展示所谓解毒药的功效。这个称呼后来转指卑躬屈膝的帮闲，再发展为“谄媚者”，并用作动词。
etymology_story.en: Toady is a shortened form of toadeater, originally a quack doctor's assistant who supposedly swallowed toads, believed to be poisonous, to help demonstrate an alleged antidote. The name came to mean a servile dependent and then a flatterer, and it also became a verb.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 toady 视为完整词基，不拆成 toad（蟾蜍）+ -y 来解释现义；名词与动词形式相同。复数及动词第三人称单数：toadies；过去式和过去分词：toadied；现在分词及行为名词：toadying（谄媚；巴结行为）；较少见的派生词：toadyism（谄媚作风）、toadyish（谄媚的）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, treat toady as a whole base rather than interpreting its current meaning as toad + -y; the noun and verb have the same form. Inflections are toadies, toadied, and toadying; toadying also names the behavior. Less common derivatives include toadyism, meaning servile flattery, and toadyish, meaning sycophantic.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sycophant（谄媚者）较正式，突出为私利奉承权势者；flatterer（奉承者）侧重说好听的话，不一定涉及权势关系；yes-man（应声虫）突出一味附和上级。toady 同时强调讨好和卑躬屈膝，贬义明显。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sycophant is relatively formal and emphasizes flattering influential people for personal gain; flatterer focuses on excessive praise without necessarily implying a power relationship; yes-man emphasizes unquestioning agreement with a superior. Toady combines ingratiating behavior with servility and is strongly disapproving.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“卖药人的跟班”记到“权势者的跟班”：人是马屁精，行为是拍马屁。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture the quack's assistant becoming a powerful person's obedient follower: the person is a toady, and the behavior is to toady.

pronunciation.note: 重音按音标中的 ˈ 标记朗读；本卡采用英语词典中的读法。

forms: 此义为不可数名词；常用 take umbrage at。
family: umbrageous 易生气的；多荫的

morphology.text: umbrage 作为独立词素记忆；umbrage + -ous → umbrageous（易生气的；多荫的），接后缀时保留末尾 e。

etymology.text: 中古英语从古法语借入，源头与拉丁语 umbra（阴影）有关；从心里蒙上阴影联想到受冒犯后的不快。

usage_note: 较正式，常说 take umbrage at a remark，表示觉得一句话冒犯了自己。

hint: Focus on feeling offended by a remark or action.

teaching.sentence: The reviewer took umbrage when the editor questioned his honesty.
teaching.translation: 编辑质疑评论者是否诚实，评论者因此感到受了冒犯。

senses.meaning_zh: 因认为受到冒犯或轻视而产生的不快；愤懑
senses.meaning_en: Offense or resentment caused by a perceived insult or slight.
senses.english_definition: If you take umbrage at something, you feel offended because you think it insults you or treats you without enough respect.
senses.collocation_en: take umbrage at a remark; take umbrage at being ignored
senses.collocation_zh: 因一句话而感到受冒犯；因受到冷落而心生不快
senses.sentence_en: She took umbrage at his suggestion that she needed help.
senses.sentence_zh: 他提出她需要帮助，这让她觉得受到了冒犯。

etymology_story.zh: umbrage 经法语进入英语，最终源自拉丁语 umbra（阴影），早期具有树荫、阴影等含义。它后来发展出疑虑、不满和受冒犯之感等抽象含义，现代主要保留在 take umbrage 这一搭配中。
etymology_story.en: Umbrage entered English through French and ultimately derives from Latin umbra, meaning shade or shadow; its early meanings included shade cast by trees. It later developed abstract senses involving suspicion, displeasure, and offense, and now occurs chiefly in the expression take umbrage.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 umbrage 作为完整词基，不按普通英语后缀 -age 拆解。umbrage + -ous → umbrageous（多荫的；易感到受冒犯的，罕用），保留词尾 e；进一步派生 umbrageously（以多荫或易愠怒的方式，罕用）、umbrageousness（多荫；易愠怒，罕用）。umbra（本影；阴影）是同源词，并非由 umbrage 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Treat umbrage as a whole base in modern English rather than analyzing its ending as the ordinary English suffix -age. Umbrage + -ous forms the rare adjective umbrageous, meaning shady or easily offended, with the final e retained; further rare derivatives are umbrageously and umbrageousness. Umbra, meaning a shadow or the darkest part of a shadow, is related historically rather than derived from umbrage.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: offense（受冒犯之感）最通用；resentment（怨愤）通常更持久，常源于不公待遇；indignation（愤慨）突出认为某事不公或不当。umbrage 较正式，尤其强调把某事视为对自己的轻慢。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Offense is the broadest term for feeling insulted; resentment usually lasts longer and often arises from unfair treatment; indignation emphasizes anger at something considered unjust or improper. Umbrage is relatively formal and particularly suggests interpreting something as a personal slight.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 umbra 的“阴影”当作记忆画面：觉得被轻慢，心头蒙上一层阴影。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use umbra, meaning shadow, as a memory image: a perceived slight casts a shadow over your mood.

pronunciation.note: 重音按音标中的 ˈ 标记朗读；本卡采用英语词典中的读法。

forms: 通常作不可数名词；另有拼写 velours。

morphology.text: velour 在英语中作为独立词素记忆；velour + -like → velour-like（像丝绒状织物的），用 -like 描述质感。

etymology.text: 英语从法语 velours（天鹅绒）借入，较早形式与拉丁语 villosus（多毛的）有关；词名让人想到表面细密的绒毛。

usage_note: 指表面有绒毛、类似天鹅绒的面料，常用于服装和家具；不必然说明纤维是丝。

senses.meaning_zh: 丝绒状织物；具有柔软绒面的织物
senses.meaning_en: A fabric with a soft, thick pile resembling velvet.
senses.english_definition: Velour is a fabric with a soft, thick surface like velvet, used for clothing and furnishings.
senses.collocation_en: a velour tracksuit; velour upholstery
senses.collocation_zh: 丝绒运动套装；绒面家具包覆织物
senses.sentence_en: She wore a blue velour tracksuit on the flight.
senses.sentence_zh: 她乘飞机时穿了一套蓝色丝绒运动服。

etymology_story.zh: velour 借自法语 velours（天鹅绒），经古法语形式追溯到拉丁语 villosus（多毛的），与 villus（毛、绒毛）有关。英语用它指表面具有柔软绒毛、质感类似天鹅绒的织物。
etymology_story.en: Velour was borrowed from French velours, meaning velvet, and traces through Old French forms to Latin villosus, meaning hairy, related to villus, meaning hair or a tuft. In English it names fabrics whose soft pile resembles velvet.

morphology_enriched.zh: velour 是整体借入的词，现代英语中没有可直接拆分的常用词根与词缀，通常作不可数名词；velours 是另一种拼写，不应一概理解为英语复数。velour-like（像丝绒状织物的）是可自由构成的描述形式；velour tracksuit 中的 velour 是名词作前置修饰语，无须另立常用形容词词性。
morphology_enriched.en: Velour is a whole-word borrowing with no ordinary modern English root-and-affix breakdown and is usually uncountable. Velours is an alternative spelling, not necessarily an English plural. Velour-like is a freely formed descriptive compound; in velour tracksuit, velour is a noun used attributively rather than a separate common adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: velvet（天鹅绒）通常指具有短而密绒面的织物；plush（长毛绒）通常绒毛更长、更蓬松；velveteen（平绒）通常是棉制的仿天鹅绒织物。velour 强调柔软的丝绒状表面，常见于针织服装和家具面料。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Velvet generally has a short, dense pile; plush usually has a longer, fluffier pile; velveteen is typically a cotton fabric made to resemble velvet. Velour emphasizes a soft, velvet-like surface and is common in knitted clothing and upholstery.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从词源中的“绒毛”想到手感：表面一层软绒，就是 velour 的核心。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect the historical idea of hair or tufts with the feel of the fabric: velour has a soft, furry surface.

pronunciation.note: 重音按音标中的 ˈ 标记朗读；本卡采用英语词典中的读法。

forms: 不可数名词；不加复数 -s。
family: verbose 冗长啰嗦的；verbosity 冗长啰嗦

morphology.text: 法语 verbi-（来自 verbier，絮叨）+ -age（名词后缀）→ verbiage（冗词）；英语整体借入，不把 verb 简单译成“动词”来拼义。

etymology.text: 18世纪英语借自法语 verbiage，相关动词 verbier 表示絮叨。记住话很多、信息却被淹没的感觉。

usage_note: 本课采用贬义“冗词、啰嗦的话”；美式语境中也可能中性地指措辞，须看上下文。

senses.meaning_zh: 冗词赘语；啰嗦而缺乏实质内容的表达
senses.meaning_en: Excessive wording that conveys little useful information.
senses.english_definition: If you describe speech or writing as verbiage, you mean that it uses too many words and contains too little useful information.
senses.collocation_en: unnecessary verbiage; cut through the verbiage
senses.collocation_zh: 不必要的冗词赘语；透过繁冗措辞抓住要点
senses.sentence_en: Cut out the unnecessary verbiage and state your main point clearly.
senses.sentence_zh: 删去不必要的冗词赘语，把你的主要观点说清楚。

senses.meaning_zh: 措辞；用语，尤见于美式英语的中性用法
senses.meaning_en: The wording of something, especially in neutral American usage.
senses.english_definition: The verbiage of a document or statement is the particular wording used in it.
senses.collocation_en: the exact verbiage; change the verbiage
senses.collocation_zh: 确切措辞；修改措辞
senses.sentence_en: Please check the exact verbiage before we print the brochure.
senses.sentence_zh: 印刷宣传册之前，请核对确切措辞。

etymology_story.zh: verbiage 于18世纪从法语借入，与表示“絮叨、喋喋不休”的法语动词 verbier 有关。英语首先沿用“冗长话语”的贬义，后来又出现较中性的“措辞、用语”义，尤其见于美式英语。
etymology_story.en: Verbiage entered English from French in the eighteenth century and is associated with the French verb verbier, meaning to chatter. English adopted its disapproving sense of excessive language and later also developed the more neutral sense of wording, especially in American usage.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 verbiage 视为整体借词，通常不可数；其法语构词背景是 verbier 的词干 + -age，不宜用英语 verb（动词）直接拼解词义。英语没有常用的直接派生词；verbose（冗长的）和 verbosity（冗长；啰嗦）可作为语义关联词一起学习，但不是由 verbiage 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, verbiage is a whole-word borrowing and is normally uncountable. Its French formation involves the stem of verbier plus -age; its meaning should not be assembled directly from the English noun verb. It has no common direct derivatives; verbose and verbosity are useful semantic associates, but neither is derived directly from verbiage.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: wordiness（措辞冗长）突出用了过多的词；verbosity（冗长啰嗦）突出说写时过于铺陈的特点；wording（措辞）是中性词，对应 verbiage 的中性义。verbiage 的贬义用法还常暗示内容空泛。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Wordiness emphasizes using more words than necessary; verbosity emphasizes an excessively lengthy manner of speaking or writing; wording is neutral and matches the neutral sense of verbiage. In its disapproving sense, verbiage also often suggests a lack of substance.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 用“絮叨”串起核心义：话堆得太多，意思被埋住；中性用法则只指这些话的措辞。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor it in chattering: a pile of words can bury the message; in neutral usage, the word simply refers to how that message is worded.

senses.english_definition: A xylophone is a musical instrument with a row or rows of wooden bars that you strike with small mallets to produce different notes.

etymology_story.zh: xylophone 是19世纪形成的乐器名称，由希腊语来源的 xylo-（木头）和 -phone（声音）组成。名称直接描述木条受敲击后发声的特点，并不意味着这种乐器本身直到19世纪才出现。
etymology_story.en: Xylophone was formed as an instrument name in the nineteenth century from Greek-derived xylo-, meaning wood, and -phone, meaning sound. The name describes wooden bars producing sound when struck; it does not imply that the instrument itself originated in that century.

morphology_enriched.zh: xylo-（木）+ -phone（发声体；声音）→ xylophone（木琴）；复数为 xylophones。词族包括 xylophonist（木琴演奏者，xylophon- + -ist）和较少见的 xylophonic（木琴的；具有木琴音色的，xylophon- + -ic）；派生时去掉词尾不发音的 e。
morphology_enriched.en: Xylo-, meaning wood, + -phone, referring to sound or a sound-producing instrument, forms xylophone; its plural is xylophones. The family includes xylophonist, a xylophone player, formed from xylophon- + -ist, and the less common xylophonic, meaning relating to or resembling a xylophone, formed from xylophon- + -ic. The final silent e is dropped in these derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 以下是相关乐器名称，并非严格同义词：marimba（马林巴琴）也使用木条，通常音域更低、音色更浑厚；glockenspiel（钟琴）使用金属音条，音色清亮；vibraphone（颤音琴）使用金属音条，并可借助共鸣管中的转动装置产生颤动效果。xylophone 的典型音色较明亮、干脆。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: These are related instruments rather than exact synonyms: a marimba also has wooden bars but generally extends lower and sounds fuller; a glockenspiel has metal bars and a bright, bell-like tone; a vibraphone has metal bars and can produce a pulsing effect through rotating mechanisms in its resonators. A xylophone typically has a bright, crisp tone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: xylo-＝木，-phone＝声：敲木出声，就是木琴。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Xylo- means wood and -phone means sound: strike wood to make music.

etymology_story.zh: 19世纪，英语从德语 jodeln 借入此词，尤与阿尔卑斯地区的歌唱传统有关。德语词本身具有拟声性质，模仿这种唱法中反复出现的呼喊音节。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed the word in the nineteenth century from German jodeln, especially associated with Alpine singing traditions. The German word is imitative, echoing the repeated calling syllables used in this style.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 yodel 是不可再作常用词根、词缀拆分的词基，名词与动词同形。屈折形式：yodels、yodeled／yodelled、yodeling／yodelling；派生形式：yodel + -er → yodeler／yodeller（约德尔歌手），yodeling／yodelling 也可作名词，表示这种唱法。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, yodel is a base without a productive internal root-and-affix division; the noun and verb have the same form. Inflections are yodels, yodeled/yodelled, and yodeling/yodelling; derivatives include yodel + -er → yodeler/yodeller, a performer, and the activity noun yodeling/yodelling.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sing（唱歌）是上位词，不限定发声方法；warble（婉转地唱）突出音调流动、颤动；trill（颤音唱奏）通常突出相邻音高的快速交替。yodel 的关键则是胸声与假声之间明显的快速转换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sing is the general term and specifies no vocal technique; warble suggests flowing or quavering notes; trill usually emphasizes rapid alternation between adjacent pitches. Yodel specifically involves conspicuous, rapid changes between the normal vocal register and falsetto.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把山间“哟——哦”的高低声转换，连到 yodel 的拟声来源：真假声来回切换。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect an echoing mountain 'yo-oh' with the word's imitative origin: the voice keeps switching registers.

etymology_story.zh: bier 源自古英语 bǣr、bēr 一类表示搬运架的词，与 bear（搬运、承载）同源。它后来专指承放遗体或棺木的架子，现代拼写也受到法语 bière 的影响。
etymology_story.en: Bier descends from Old English bǣr or bēr, words for a carrying frame, and is related to bear, meaning 'carry.' Its meaning became specialized to a support for a body or coffin, and its modern spelling was influenced by French bière.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 bier 是独立词基，没有常用的前缀、后缀拆分；复数为 biers。它没有常用的派生词族；较少见的复合词 biercloth＝bier + cloth，指覆盖棺架或棺木的布。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, bier is an independent base with no productive prefix-and-suffix division; its plural is biers. It has no substantial everyday derivative family; the uncommon compound biercloth = bier + cloth means a covering for a bier or coffin.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: catafalque（灵柩台）通常是较高、较庄重的陈放平台；stretcher（担架）主要用于搬运伤病者，也可搬运遗体；coffin（棺材）是容纳遗体的箱体。bier 指承托或抬运遗体、棺木的架子本身。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A catafalque is usually an elevated, ceremonial platform; a stretcher primarily transports injured or ill people, though it can carry a body; a coffin is the container holding the body. A bier is the supporting or carrying frame itself.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: bier 与 bear（承载）同源：承载棺木的架子。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Bier belongs historically with bear, 'carry': picture the frame that bears the coffin.

etymology_story.zh: bilge 在16世纪作为 bulge（鼓起部分）的变体出现，用来指船体下部鼓起、弯曲的部位。词义随后从部位转指其中积存的污水，再引申为毫无价值的胡话。
etymology_story.en: Bilge appeared in the sixteenth century as a variant of bulge, referring to the rounded lower part of a ship's hull. It subsequently came to mean the dirty water collecting there and, figuratively, worthless talk.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 bilge 是独立词基，不能拆成有用的常见词根与词缀，名词与动词同形。屈折形式：bilges、bilged、bilging；派生词：bilgy（舱底污水般的；污浊的）；复合词：bilgewater／bilge water（舱底污水；胡话）、bilge pump（舱底泵）、bilge keel（舭龙骨）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, bilge is an independent base without a useful productive root-and-affix division; it functions as both noun and verb. Inflections are bilges, bilged, and bilging; the derivative bilgy means resembling bilge water or foul. Compounds include bilgewater/bilge water, bilge pump, and bilge keel.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: water in the bilges（舱底的水）是字面义的说明性近义表达；nonsense（胡说）语气较中性；drivel（蠢话、废话）强调愚蠢、无聊。比喻义 bilge 带明显的轻蔑，常把言论说得像舱底污水一样毫无价值。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Water in the bilges is a descriptive equivalent of the literal water sense; nonsense is a more neutral term for meaningless or untrue material; drivel stresses foolishness and tediousness. Figurative bilge is strongly dismissive, treating talk as worthless ship-bottom waste.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 船底鼓起处 → 积下的污水 → 一肚子废话。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Rounded ship-bottom → dirty water collected there → worthless talk.

etymology_story.zh: 19世纪初，英语以 borax（硼砂）的开头为基础，仿照 carbon（碳）的词尾造出 boron。名称体现了这种元素与含硼矿物硼砂之间的联系。
etymology_story.en: Boron was coined in English in the early nineteenth century from the beginning of borax, with an ending modeled on carbon. Its name reflects the element's connection with the mineral borax.

morphology_enriched.zh: boron 的历史命名公式是 bor(ax) + (carb)on，现代英语通常将它作为完整词基处理，-on 在这里不是可自由套用的普通后缀。主要化学词族包括 boric（硼的，如 boric acid 硼酸）、borate（硼酸盐）、boride（硼化物）、borane（硼烷）、boronic（硼酸类的，如 boronic acid 有机硼酸）、boronate（有机硼酸盐或酯）、borohydride（硼氢化物）；结合形式 boro- 见于 borosilicate（硼硅酸盐）。
morphology_enriched.en: The historical naming formula is bor(ax) + (carb)on; modern English normally treats boron as a whole base, and -on here is not an ordinary freely productive suffix. Principal chemical relatives include boric, as in boric acid; borate; boride; borane; boronic, as in boronic acid; boronate; and borohydride. The combining form boro- occurs in borosilicate.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: boron 没有严格的普通近义词；B 是其化学符号。相关词 borax（硼砂）是一种含硼化合物，boric acid（硼酸）是另一种含硼物质，均不能与元素名称 boron 互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Boron has no true everyday synonym; B is its chemical symbol. Related terms include borax, a boron-containing compound, and boric acid, another boron-containing substance; neither is interchangeable with the element name boron.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: borax 提供开头，carbon 提供结尾：boron 是“硼砂家族里的元素硼”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Borax supplies the beginning and carbon supplies the ending: boron is the element associated with borax.

etymology_story.zh: catchword 由 catch 与 word 合成，16世纪已有印刷用法，指页底提示下一页开头的接页词。后来词义扩展到帮助检索的显著词语，以及吸引注意、被反复使用的口号或流行语。
etymology_story.en: Catchword combines catch and word and was already used in sixteenth-century printing for a word at the foot of a page anticipating the next page's opening. Its meanings later extended to prominent reference words and to attention-catching, repeatedly used slogans or fashionable expressions.

morphology_enriched.zh: catch（抓住、引起注意）+ word（词）→ catchword，是名词复合词；复数为 catchwords。没有常用的直接后缀派生词；相关但独立的复合词包括 catchphrase（流行说法、标志性用语）和 catchline（醒目的宣传语或标题）。
morphology_enriched.en: Catch + word → catchword is a compound noun; its plural is catchwords. It has no common direct suffix derivatives; related but independently formed compounds include catchphrase, a familiar or characteristic expression, and catchline, an attention-catching promotional line or heading.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: slogan（口号）强调有意宣传某个组织、产品或主张；buzzword（时髦术语）强调某一领域里流行、常被滥用的说法；catchphrase（流行说法）常与特定人物、节目或反复出现的表达有关。catchword 更侧重浓缩某种理念、广泛流传的词或短语。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A slogan deliberately promotes an organization, product, or cause; a buzzword is fashionable within a field and may be overused; a catchphrase is often associated with a particular person, programme, or recurring expression. Catchword especially suggests a widely repeated word or phrase encapsulating an idea.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: catch + word：能“抓住”注意或帮助“抓到”位置的词——口号、检索词、接页词。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Catch + word: a word that catches attention or helps you catch the right place—a slogan, guide word, or page-linking word.

etymology_story.zh: 英语 chondrite 借自德语 Chondrit，其名称由源于希腊语 khondros（颗粒）的成分和矿物、岩石名称后缀构成。名称指向这类陨石中具有代表性的小球粒。
etymology_story.en: English chondrite was borrowed from German Chondrit, formed from an element derived from Greek khondros, meaning 'grain,' and a mineral or rock suffix. The name refers to the characteristic small, rounded grains found in these meteorites.

morphology_enriched.zh: 科学构词分析：chondr-（颗粒）+ -ite（矿物或岩石名称后缀）→ chondrite；复数 chondrites。主要词族：chondritic（球粒陨石的）、achondrite（无球粒陨石）、achondritic（无球粒陨石的）；chondrule（球粒）是共享词源成分的相关词，并非由 chondrite 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Scientific morphological analysis: chondr- ('grain') + -ite (a mineral or rock suffix) → chondrite; plural chondrites. The principal family includes chondritic, achondrite, and achondritic; chondrule shares the historical root but is not directly derived from chondrite.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 无严格同义词。stony meteorite（石陨石）是更宽泛的类别，也包括无球粒陨石；meteorite（陨石）范围更广，还包括铁陨石和石铁陨石。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact synonym. Stony meteorite is a broader category that also includes achondrites; meteorite is broader still and includes iron and stony-iron meteorites.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: chondr- 抓住“颗粒”：陨石切面上的小球粒，就是名称的线索。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect chondr- with 'grain': the little rounded grains inside the meteorite explain its name.

etymology_story.zh: consumptive 可追溯至拉丁语 consumere（用尽）的词干 consumpt-，经法语和拉丁语相关形式进入中古英语。肺结核过去称为 consumption，因为患者仿佛被疾病逐渐“耗尽”，由此产生了与肺结核有关的形容词义和患者名词义。
etymology_story.en: Consumptive ultimately comes from consumpt-, the stem of Latin consumere, meaning 'use up,' through related French and Latin forms into Middle English. Tuberculosis was formerly called consumption because it seemed to waste the body away, giving rise to the adjective and noun referring to the disease.

morphology_enriched.zh: consumpt-（与 consume“消耗”对应的拉丁来源词干）+ -ive（形容词后缀）→ consumptive；名词义由形容词转类而来，复数为 consumptives。主要词族：consume（消耗）、consumption（消耗；消费；旧称肺结核）、consumer（消费者）、consumable（可消耗的；消耗品）、consumerism（消费主义）、consumerist（消费主义的；消费主义者）；直接派生形式包括 consumptively（消耗性地）和 consumptiveness（消耗性），后二者较少见。
morphology_enriched.en: Consumpt- (the Latin-derived stem corresponding to consume) + -ive (an adjective suffix) → consumptive; the noun is formed by conversion from the adjective, with plural consumptives. The principal family includes consume, consumption, consumer, consumable, consumerism, and consumerist; direct derivatives include the less frequent consumptively and consumptiveness.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: resource-consuming（耗用资源的）是资源义的直白表达；depletive（使资源减少的）更强调存量下降；tubercular（结核病的；患结核病的）对应疾病义，不能替换资源义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Resource-consuming expresses the resource sense directly; depletive emphasizes a reduction in available reserves; tubercular corresponds to the disease sense and cannot replace consumptive in discussions of resource use.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 核心是“逐渐耗掉”：资源被耗用，身体被疾病消耗。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think 'used up over time': resources are consumed, and disease wastes the body away.

senses.meaning_zh: 腊肠犬：身体长、腿短的犬种
senses.meaning_en: A dog of a breed with a long body and short legs.
senses.english_definition: A dachshund is a small dog with a long body, short legs, and long ears.
senses.collocation_en: a miniature dachshund; a dachshund puppy
senses.collocation_zh: 迷你腊肠犬；腊肠犬幼犬
senses.sentence_en: Their miniature dachshund likes to sleep under a blanket.
senses.sentence_zh: 他们家的迷你腊肠犬喜欢钻在毯子下面睡觉。

etymology_story.zh: dachshund 借自德语 Dachshund，由 Dachs（獾）和 Hund（狗）组成，字面意思是“獾狗”。这种犬原本用于追猎獾，其短腿长身有助于进入洞穴。
etymology_story.en: Dachshund was borrowed from German Dachshund, combining Dachs, meaning 'badger,' and Hund, meaning 'dog.' The breed was developed to hunt badgers, with its short legs and long body helping it enter burrows.

morphology_enriched.zh: 英语中作为完整借词使用，不宜拆成英语词根和后缀；德语内部结构为 Dachs（獾）+ Hund（狗）。英语复数为 dachshunds；无常用的独立派生词族，miniature dachshund（迷你腊肠犬）、long-haired dachshund（长毛腊肠犬）等属于修饰性短语。
morphology_enriched.en: In English, dachshund functions as a whole borrowed word rather than an English root-plus-affix formation; its German structure is Dachs ('badger') + Hund ('dog'). The English plural is dachshunds; there is no established common derivational family, and expressions such as miniature dachshund and long-haired dachshund are descriptive phrases.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sausage dog（腊肠狗）是英国英语中常见的非正式称呼；wiener dog（热狗犬；腊肠犬）常见于美国口语；doxie（腊肠犬）是更亲昵的昵称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sausage dog is a familiar informal British term; wiener dog is common in informal American English; doxie is a more affectionate nickname.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 名字记用途：Dachs“獾”+ Hund“狗”＝能钻洞追獾的短腿长身狗。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the original job: 'badger' + 'dog' names a long, short-legged dog bred to follow badgers into burrows.

etymology.text: forum 来自拉丁语 forum，原指公共集会的广场；fora 保留了拉丁语复数形式，后来用于多个讨论场所。

usage_note: fora 和 forums 都是 forum 的复数；fora 较正式，作主语时搭配复数谓语。

senses.meaning_en: Public squares in ancient Roman towns; the classical plural of forum.
senses.english_definition: In descriptions of ancient Rome, fora are public squares where people gathered for trade, public business, and social activities.
senses.collocation_en: Roman fora; the imperial fora
senses.collocation_zh: 古罗马公共广场；帝国广场群

etymology_story.zh: fora 保留了拉丁语 forum 的中性复数形式；forum 原指公共广场或市场，也是处理公共事务的地方。英语后来将 forum 的含义扩展为讨论场所，因此 fora 也可表示多个论坛或议事场合。
etymology_story.en: Fora preserves the Latin neuter plural of forum, originally a public square or marketplace where public business was also conducted. English later extended forum to a setting for discussion, so fora also came to denote multiple discussion venues.

morphology_enriched.zh: 这是屈折变化而非派生构词：forum 的拉丁式复数将词尾 -um 替换为 -a，形成 fora。现代英语也使用规则复数 forums，且通常更常见；fora 本身不是单数，也不再加 -s，无独立的常用派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: This is inflection rather than derivation: the Latin-style plural replaces the ending -um in forum with -a to produce fora. Modern English also uses the regular plural forums, which is generally more frequent; fora is not singular, does not take an additional -s, and has no separate common derivational family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: forums（论坛）与讨论义的 fora 基本同义，适用范围更广，也更常见于网络语境；discussion venues（讨论场所）强调提供交流的平台；assemblies（集会）强调聚集的人群或会议，并非所有语境下都可替换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Forums is effectively equivalent to fora in the discussion sense and is more usual in everyday and online contexts; discussion venues emphasizes the settings provided for exchange; assemblies emphasizes gatherings or organized bodies and is not interchangeable in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: forum 一处，fora 多处：拉丁式 -um 变 -a，多个广场也就成了多个讨论场合。
mnemonic_anchor.en: One forum, several fora: Latin -um becomes -a, and public gathering places become settings for discussion.

etymology.text: 英语鱼名来自葡萄牙语 garupa。把它和礁石旁游动的大嘴海鱼联系起来，比按 group 来拆更容易记准。

usage_note: grouper 可以指活鱼，也可以指作为食材的鱼肉；不是“分组的人”。

senses.meaning_zh: 石斑鱼：一类身体粗壮、嘴大、多生活于温暖海域的海鱼；亦指其鱼肉

etymology_story.zh: 英语鱼名 grouper 借自葡萄牙语 garoupa，借入后词形逐渐英语化。它与英语 group（群；分组）没有词源关系，不能按“群体中的成员”来解释。
etymology_story.en: The fish name grouper was borrowed from Portuguese garoupa, with its form becoming anglicized. It is unrelated to English group and does not historically mean a member of a group.

morphology_enriched.zh: 鱼名 grouper 在现代英语中是不可再作有效词缀分析的借词，不是 group + -er。可数复数通常为 groupers，也可用 grouper 表示多条鱼；表示鱼肉时通常不可数，无常用的独立派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: As a fish name, grouper is a borrowed base word in modern English, not group + -er. Its count plural is usually groupers, though grouper can also be used for multiple fish; the food sense is normally uncountable, and there is no established common derivational family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 无覆盖全部石斑鱼的严格通用同义词。rock cod（岩鳕）在部分地区用于某些石斑鱼，但也指其他鱼；sea bass（海鲈）是范围交叠且用法不一的俗称；hind（某些小型石斑鱼）只指石斑鱼中的部分种类。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no universally interchangeable synonym for all groupers. Rock cod is a regional name for some groupers but also names other fish; sea bass is a variable common name with overlapping usage; hind names only certain, generally smaller, kinds of grouper.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 整词绑定“大嘴、粗身、礁边海鱼”的画面；词尾像 -er，也不要误拆成 group 的派生词。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Attach the whole word to a large-mouthed, heavy-bodied reef fish; its apparent -er ending does not make it a derivative of group.

etymology_story.zh: hieroglyph 由较早的 hieroglyphic 或 hieroglyphics 逆构而来；后者经法语和后期拉丁语追溯到希腊语 hieroglyphikos，意为“神圣雕刻的”，由 hieros（神圣的）和 glyphein（雕刻）构成。这个名称原指与宗教铭刻有关的古埃及文字，后来也用于其他象形字符，并引申为难懂的字迹。
etymology_story.en: Hieroglyph was back-formed from the earlier hieroglyphic or hieroglyphics, ultimately through French and Late Latin from Greek hieroglyphikos, meaning 'of sacred carving,' from hieros, 'sacred,' and glyphein, 'to carve.' Originally associated with Egyptian religious inscriptions, the word broadened to other pictorial characters and, figuratively, unreadable writing.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可分析为 hiero-（神圣的）＋ glyph（雕刻或书写的符号），但该名词在历史上属于逆构词。词族包括 hieroglyphic（象形文字的；象形字符）、hieroglyphical（象形文字的，较少用）、hieroglyphically（以象形文字方式）和 hieroglyphics（象形文字，尤指古埃及圣书体）；相关基础词有 glyph（字形；符号）和 glyphic（雕刻的；符号的）。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern form can be analyzed as hiero- ('sacred') + glyph ('a carved or written sign'), although the noun historically arose by back-formation. Its family includes hieroglyphic, hieroglyphical (less common), hieroglyphically, and hieroglyphics; related base words include glyph and glyphic.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pictograph（图画符号）侧重以图像表现对象；ideogram（表意符号）侧重表示概念；glyph（字形；符号）泛指书写或刻写的符号。hieroglyph 特别关联古埃及文字，而且既可表音，也可表词或表意。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pictograph emphasizes a picture representing something; ideogram emphasizes a sign representing a concept; glyph is a broader term for a written or carved sign. Hieroglyph is especially associated with ancient Egyptian writing and may represent a sound, a word, or an idea.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: hiero- 神圣＋glyph 刻写符号：神庙石壁上的字符，就是 hieroglyph。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Sacred + carved sign: picture a character carved into a temple wall.

etymology_story.zh: 该词形成于20世纪初，由 homo-（同性的；最终源自希腊语 homos，意为“相同”）与 erotic（情欲的）组合而成。erotic 最终源自希腊语 eros（爱欲）；该词常用于讨论艺术、文学或人际关系中表达或暗示的同性情欲。
etymology_story.en: The word arose in the early twentieth century from homo-, referring here to the same sex and ultimately from Greek homos, 'same,' plus erotic. Erotic ultimately derives from Greek eros, 'sexual love or desire'; homoerotic is often used to discuss expressed or suggested same-sex desire in art, literature, and relationships.

morphology_enriched.zh: homo-（同性的）＋ erotic（情欲的）→ homoerotic。直接词族包括 homoerotically（以表现同性情欲的方式）、homoeroticism（同性情欲；其表现）和较少见的 homoerotism（同性情欲）；erotic 的相关词族包括 erotically（色情地；情欲地）、eroticism（情欲；色情表现）、erotica（情色作品）和 eroticize（使带有情欲色彩）。
morphology_enriched.en: Homo- ('same-sex') + erotic → homoerotic. Direct family members include homoerotically, homoeroticism, and the less common homoerotism; the related erotic family includes erotically, eroticism, erotica, and eroticize.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: same-sex erotic（同性情欲的）是透明直白的释义；homosexual（同性恋的）可涉及性取向、身份或行为，范围更广；erotic（情欲的）不限定吸引对象的性别。homoerotic 尤其适合描述作品中的欲望、意象或暗示，并不必然说明作者或人物的性取向。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Same-sex erotic is a transparent paraphrase; homosexual can refer more broadly to orientation, identity, or behavior; erotic does not specify the sex of those involved. Homoerotic is particularly useful for desire, imagery, or suggestion in a work and does not necessarily establish its creator's or characters' sexual orientation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: homo- 相同＋erotic 情欲：情欲指向同性。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Homo- means 'same': erotic attraction directed toward the same sex.

etymology_story.zh: intracranial 是19世纪形成的医学构词，由拉丁语来源的 intra-（在……内部）与 cranial（颅的）组成。cranial 的基础词 cranium 经拉丁语来自希腊语 kranion（头骨），因此全词表示“头骨以内的”。
etymology_story.en: Intracranial was formed in nineteenth-century medical vocabulary from Latin-derived intra-, 'within,' and cranial. The base cranium came through Latin from Greek kranion, 'skull,' giving the compound its meaning 'within the skull.'

morphology_enriched.zh: intra-（内部）＋ cranial（颅的）→ intracranial；cranial 可分析为 crani-（颅）＋ -al（……的），对应名词 cranium（颅；复数 crania 或 craniums）。直接派生词为 intracranially（在颅内）；相关词有 cranially（向颅侧；在颅部）和表示相反空间位置的 extracranial（颅外的）、extracranially（在颅外）。
morphology_enriched.en: Intra- ('within') + cranial → intracranial; cranial can be analyzed as crani- ('skull') + -al, corresponding to the noun cranium (plural crania or craniums). The direct derivative is intracranially; related forms include cranially and the spatial opposites extracranial and extracranially.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: endocranial（颅内的）意义接近，但常侧重颅骨内面或颅腔；intracerebral（脑内的）限于脑组织内部；cerebral（脑的；大脑的）表示与脑或大脑有关，不直接表达“位于颅内”。intracranial 的范围包括颅内的脑、血管及其他结构。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Endocranial is close in meaning but often concerns the skull's inner surface or cavity; intracerebral is restricted to the interior of brain tissue; cerebral means relating to the brain or cerebrum rather than specifically being inside the skull. Intracranial covers the brain, vessels, and other structures within the skull.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Intra- means 'within' and crani- means 'skull': inside the skull.

etymology_story.zh: limbic 源于法语解剖学词 limbique，最终来自拉丁语 limbus（边缘；边界）。19世纪对“边缘叶”的命名依据其围绕脑内结构形成边缘的形态，后来该形容词被用于“边缘系统”等术语。
etymology_story.en: Limbic comes from French anatomical limbique, ultimately from Latin limbus, 'border' or 'edge.' The nineteenth-century name 'limbic lobe' referred to a border-like arrangement around inner brain structures, and the adjective later entered terms such as 'limbic system.'

morphology_enriched.zh: limb-（边缘，来自 limbus）＋ -ic（有关的）→ limbic；这里的 limb- 与表示“肢体”的英语 limb 来源不同。相关词族包括 limbus（边缘；缘）、limbal（缘的，常用于眼部解剖）、paralimbic（旁边缘的）和 corticolimbic（皮层与边缘系统的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Limb- ('border,' from limbus) + -ic ('relating to') → limbic; this base is etymologically distinct from English limb meaning an arm or leg. Related forms include limbus, limbal (often used in eye anatomy), paralimbic, and corticolimbic.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: limbic-system-related（与边缘系统有关的）是直接释义；paralimbic（旁边缘的）指邻近或过渡性的区域；corticolimbic（皮层与边缘系统的）强调皮层和边缘结构之间的联系。后两者是相关术语，不能直接替换 limbic。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Limbic-system-related is a direct paraphrase; paralimbic describes neighboring or transitional regions; corticolimbic emphasizes relationships between cortical and limbic structures. The latter two are related terms rather than interchangeable synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: limbus 意为“边缘”：记住脑内环绕成边缘的区域，不要联想到四肢。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Limbus means 'border': picture a border around inner brain structures, rather than an arm or leg.

senses.meaning_zh: 微观结构，尤指材料在显微尺度上的内部组织
senses.meaning_en: Small-scale internal structure, especially the microscopic organization of a material

etymology_story.zh: microstructure 是19世纪由 micro-（微小的，源自希腊语 mikros）与 structure（结构，最终源自拉丁语 structura）组成的词。它用于描述细微尺度的组织，尤其是显微镜下的材料组织，后来也用于市场交易机制和词典词条内部组织等领域。
etymology_story.en: Microstructure was formed in the nineteenth century from micro-, 'small,' ultimately from Greek mikros, and structure, ultimately from Latin structura. It describes organization at a fine scale, especially microscopic material organization, and also developed specialized uses for trading mechanisms and the organization of dictionary entries.

morphology_enriched.zh: micro-（微小尺度的）＋ structure（结构）→ microstructure。词族包括 microstructural（微观结构的）、microstructurally（从微观结构上）、microstructured（具有微观结构的）和 microstructuring（微结构加工；形成微结构）；相关对照词有 macrostructure（宏观结构）、macrostructural（宏观结构的）和 nanostructure（纳米结构）。
morphology_enriched.en: Micro- ('small-scale') + structure → microstructure. Family members include microstructural, microstructurally, microstructured, and microstructuring; related contrasting forms include macrostructure, macrostructural, and nanostructure.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: microscopic structure（显微结构）强调可在显微尺度观察的组织；fine structure（精细结构）强调更细层次的构造；internal structure（内部结构）范围更广，不限定尺度。这些词在材料语境中意义接近，但在金融和词典学中，microstructure 具有约定的专门含义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Microscopic structure emphasizes organization observable at a microscopic scale; fine structure emphasizes detailed organization; internal structure is broader and does not specify scale. These expressions overlap in materials contexts, while microstructure has established technical meanings in finance and lexicography.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: micro- 微小＋structure 结构：放大细看，观察内部如何排列。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Micro- + structure: zoom in to see how the small internal parts are arranged.

etymology_story.zh: midden 经中古英语 midding 传入，源于斯堪的纳维亚语言中表示“粪堆”的词，其历史构成与“粪便”和“堆”有关。它后来被考古学采用，指古人丢弃的贝壳、骨头及其他生活废物形成的堆积。
etymology_story.en: Midden came through Middle English midding from a Scandinavian word for a dung heap, historically combining elements meaning dung and heap. Archaeologists later adopted it for accumulations of shells, bones, and other refuse left by past communities.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 midden 视为不可再作常用词素切分的名词：midden + 复数词尾 -s → middens。常用复合形式有 shell midden（贝丘）、kitchen midden（古代厨房废弃物堆积）和 dung midden（粪堆）；没有常用的动词、副词或独立形容词派生形式，midden-like 只是可临时构成的描述性形式。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, midden is a noun without a useful productive internal breakdown: midden + plural -s → middens. Common compounds include shell midden, kitchen midden, and dung midden; there are no common derived verbs, adverbs, or independent adjectives, and midden-like is an occasional descriptive formation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: refuse heap（废物堆）泛指堆积的废弃物；rubbish dump（垃圾场）强调倾倒垃圾的地点；dung heap（粪堆）明确限定内容为粪便。midden 在考古语境中尤其强调可反映过去生活的废弃物堆积。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Refuse heap is a general term for accumulated waste; rubbish dump emphasizes the place where waste is deposited; dung heap specifically contains excrement. In archaeology, midden particularly denotes accumulated refuse that provides evidence of past life.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“粪堆”到“古人的垃圾堆”：废物留下来，就成了生活史的线索。

etymology_story.zh: multimillion 是英语用 multi-（多、多个）与 million（百万）构成的复合形容词；multi- 源于拉丁语 multus，million 则经法语来自意大利语 milione。它把“多个百万”的数量概念用于描述金额、价值或规模。
etymology_story.en: Multimillion was formed in English from multi-, meaning many and ultimately from Latin multus, and million, which came through French from Italian milione. It applies the idea of several millions to amounts, values, and scale.

morphology_enriched.zh: multi-（多个）+ million（百万）→ multimillion（数百万的），主要置于名词前。相关形式有 million（百万）、millions（数百万）、millionth（第一百万；百万分之一）、millionaire（百万富翁）、multimillionaire（拥有数百万资产的人）和 multimillionaires（其复数）；常见复合形容词有 multimillion-dollar（数百万美元的）和 multimillion-pound（数百万英镑的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Multi- meaning many + million → multimillion, an adjective used chiefly before nouns. Related forms include million, millions, millionth, millionaire, multimillionaire, and multimillionaires; common compound adjectives include multimillion-dollar and multimillion-pound.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: several-million（数百万的，通常用于复合修饰语）最接近其数量含义；million-dollar（百万美元的）不一定表示多个百万；multibillion（数十亿的）表示十亿单位的多个倍数，规模远大于 multimillion。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Several-million, usually used within a compound modifier, is the closest numerical equivalent; million-dollar does not necessarily indicate several million dollars; multibillion describes several billions and therefore a much larger scale.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: multi- 是“多个”：多个 million，就是数百万。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Multi- means many: several millions make a multimillion amount.

etymology_story.zh: overactive 由英语前缀 over-（过度）加 active（活跃的）构成。active 经法语源于拉丁语 activus，最终与 agere（做、行动）有关，因此全词表示行动或运作超过正常程度。
etymology_story.en: Overactive was formed in English by adding over-, meaning excessively, to active. Active came through French from Latin activus, ultimately related to agere, meaning to do or act, so the whole word describes activity beyond a normal level.

morphology_enriched.zh: over-（过度）+ active（活跃的）→ overactive；overactive + -ity → overactivity（活动过度，拼写时去掉末尾 e），另有较少见的 overactively（过于活跃地）。核心词族包括 act（行动）、action（行动）、active（活跃的）、actively（积极地；活跃地）、activity（活动）、activate（激活）、activation（激活）、inactive（不活跃的）、inactivity（不活跃）和 underactive（活动不足的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Over- meaning excessively + active → overactive; overactive + -ity → overactivity, with the final e dropped, and overactively is a less common adverb. The core family includes act, action, active, actively, activity, activate, activation, inactive, inactivity, and underactive.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hyperactive（异常活跃的）常强调明显过多的活动，尤其用于行为描述；overstimulated（受到过度刺激的）强调刺激过多这一原因；restless（坐立不安的）强调难以安静或放松。overactive 的适用范围更广，可描述想象力、腺体或其他系统。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hyperactive often emphasizes unusually excessive activity, especially in behavior; overstimulated identifies excessive stimulation as the cause; restless describes difficulty staying still or relaxing. Overactive has a broader range and can describe the imagination, glands, or other systems.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: active 是“活跃”，over- 把程度推过头：活跃过头就是 overactive。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Active means working or moving; over- pushes it too far: overactive means active to excess.

etymology_story.zh: sauropod 来自科学分类名称 Sauropoda，由希腊语 sauros（蜥蜴）和 pous 的词干 pod-（足）构成，字面意思是“蜥蜴足”。这个名称最初着眼于足部骨骼特征，后来成为这一类通常长颈、巨型食草恐龙的通称。
etymology_story.en: Sauropod comes from the scientific group name Sauropoda, formed from Greek sauros, meaning lizard, and pod-, the stem of pous, meaning foot. The name originally referred to features of the feet and became the general term for this group of typically long-necked, gigantic plant-eating dinosaurs.

morphology_enriched.zh: 科学构词形式 sauro-（蜥蜴）+ -pod（足；有某种足的动物）→ sauropod；普通复数为 sauropods（多只蜥脚类恐龙），分类群名称为 Sauropoda（蜥脚类）。相关形式有 sauropodan（蜥脚类的；蜥脚类成员）和较少见的 sauropodous（蜥脚类的）；sauropodomorph（蜥脚形类成员）指更广分类群的成员，并非 sauropod 的完全同义词。
morphology_enriched.en: The scientific combining forms sauro- meaning lizard + -pod meaning foot or an animal with a particular kind of foot form sauropod. Its ordinary plural is sauropods, and the taxonomic name is Sauropoda; related forms include sauropodan and the less common adjective sauropodous. Sauropodomorph denotes a member of a broader group and is not an exact synonym.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sauropod dinosaur（蜥脚类恐龙）是明确的同义展开形式；long-necked dinosaur（长颈恐龙）是便于理解的非正式描述，但不能精确界定分类；titanosaur（泰坦巨龙类恐龙）只指蜥脚类中的一个分支，不能替换所有 sauropod。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sauropod dinosaur is an explicit equivalent; long-necked dinosaur is an accessible informal description but does not precisely define the group; titanosaur names only one subgroup of sauropods and cannot replace sauropod in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: sauro- 是“蜥蜴”，-pod 是“足”：用“蜥蜴足”锁定蜥脚类，再联想长颈和巨大的身躯。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Sauro- means lizard and -pod means foot: use lizard-foot to recall the group, then picture its long neck and huge body.

etymology_story.zh: sherbet 经土耳其语和波斯语传入英语，最终源于阿拉伯语中表示“一饮、饮料”的词，与“喝”这一动词有关。它最初指甜味饮料，后来在不同英语地区分别发展出果味冰冻甜品和起泡糖粉等含义。
etymology_story.en: Sherbet entered English through Turkish and Persian, ultimately from an Arabic word meaning a drink and related to the verb meaning to drink. It originally named a sweet beverage, then developed regional meanings for a frozen fruit dessert and a fizzy confectionery powder.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 sherbet 是借入的单纯词，不能可靠地拆为常用英语词根和词缀；表示物质时通常不可数，sherbets 可表示不同品种或多份冰糕、饮料。相关拼写有 sherbert（变体拼写，通常对应额外的 r 音）和 sharbat（主要指传统甜饮的相关借词）；常见复合形式有 orange sherbet（橙味冰糕）和 sherbet powder（汽水糖粉），没有常用的动词或副词派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, sherbet is a borrowed simple word with no useful breakdown into productive English roots and affixes. It is usually uncountable as a substance, while sherbets can refer to varieties or servings. Related forms include sherbert, a variant spelling usually associated with an extra r sound, and sharbat, a related borrowing chiefly naming the traditional sweet drink; common compounds include orange sherbet and sherbet powder, and there are no common derived verbs or adverbs.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sorbet（雪葩；果汁冰沙甜品）通常不含乳制品，而美式 sherbet 通常含少量乳制品；ice cream（冰淇淋）一般更突出奶或奶油的质地与风味；sharbat（传统甜饮）接近其饮料义，不能替代冰糕义或英国糖粉义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sorbet is normally dairy-free, whereas American sherbet usually contains some dairy; ice cream generally emphasizes a richer milk or cream texture and flavor; sharbat closely matches the traditional drink sense but does not replace the frozen-dessert or British powder senses.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“甜饮料”出发：冻起来是美式冰糕，做成起泡粉是英国糖果。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with a sweet drink: freeze it for American sherbet, or think of fizzy powder for the British confection.

etymology_story.zh: simian 源自拉丁语 simia，意为“猴或猿”，经表示所属关系的形容词形式进入英语。它既用于描述猴猿及其特征，也用作这类动物的正式名称。
etymology_story.en: Simian comes from Latin simia, meaning “monkey” or “ape,” through an adjectival formation expressing a relationship. In English, it describes these animals and their characteristics and also serves as a formal noun for them.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代词根分析：simi-（猴、猿；黏着词根）+ -an（与……有关的）→ simian；同形词兼作形容词和名词，名词复数为 simians。相关同源术语有 simiiform（猴形类的）；simian-like（似猴猿的）是透明的描述性复合形式，并非独立的常用派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern root analysis: simi- (“monkey, ape,” a bound root) + -an (“relating to”) → simian. The same form functions as both adjective and noun; the noun plural is simians. The related technical term simiiform shares the root; simian-like is a transparent descriptive compound rather than a separate common derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: monkeylike（似猴的）专指像猴；apelike（似猿的）专指像猿；anthropoid（类人猿的；类人猿）强调类人特征，在分类学中的范围依体系而异。simian 的范围可同时涵盖猴与猿，语体较正式。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Monkeylike specifically means resembling a monkey; apelike means resembling an ape; anthropoid emphasizes humanlike primates, with its technical scope depending on the classification used. Simian can cover both monkeys and apes and has a more formal register.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住 simi-＝猴猿：形容词表示“猴猿的”，名词直接表示“猴猿”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor simi- to monkeys and apes: the adjective describes them, and the noun names them.

etymology_story.zh: ungulate 源自后期拉丁语 ungulatus，意为“有蹄的”，其基础词 ungula 表示“蹄”，又与表示“指甲、爪”的 unguis 有关。英语将“有蹄”这一身体特征用于形容动物，并进一步用它来命名这类哺乳动物。
etymology_story.en: Ungulate comes from Late Latin ungulatus, meaning “hoofed,” based on ungula, “hoof,” which is related to unguis, “nail” or “claw.” English uses this physical feature both to describe animals and to name hoofed mammals.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代词根分析：ungul-（蹄；黏着词根）+ -ate（具有……的）→ ungulate；同形兼作形容词和名词，名词复数为 ungulates。同源词包括 ungual（指甲、爪或蹄的）和 unguligrade（蹄行的，即以蹄端支撑行走的）；开头的 un- 不是否定前缀。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern root analysis: ungul- (“hoof,” a bound root) + -ate (“having”) → ungulate. It functions as both adjective and noun; the noun plural is ungulates. Related words include ungual (“relating to a nail, claw, or hoof”) and unguligrade (“walking on the tips of hoof-covered digits”). The initial un- is not a negative prefix.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hoofed mammal（有蹄哺乳动物）是最直接的释义性近义表达；hoofed animal（有蹄动物）更通俗。ruminant（反刍动物）仅指会反刍的动物，不能与 ungulate 互换，例如马是有蹄类动物，却不是反刍动物。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hoofed mammal is the closest explanatory equivalent; hoofed animal is a more everyday expression. Ruminant names an animal that chews cud and is not interchangeable with ungulate: a horse is an ungulate but not a ruminant.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: ungul-＝蹄，-ate＝具有：有蹄的动物，就是 ungulate。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Ungul- means hoof and -ate means having: an ungulate is an animal with hooves.

etymology_story.zh: urethane 借自19世纪法语化学名称 uréthane，该名称由 urée（尿素）和 éther（醚）的词形组合而成。它最初用于特定化合物，后来也用于相关氨基甲酸酯，并在材料行业中成为 polyurethane（聚氨酯）的简称。
etymology_story.en: Urethane was borrowed from the nineteenth-century French chemical name uréthane, formed from elements of urée, “urea,” and éther, “ether.” Originally a name for a particular compound, it also came to designate related carbamates and, in the materials industry, polyurethane.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中宜将 urethane 作为完整化学词基，不按普通英语词缀硬拆。主要词族与构词形式包括 urethane、复数 urethanes（不同氨基甲酸酯或相关产品）、poly-（多、聚合）+ urethane → polyurethane（聚氨酯），以及 polyurethanes（不同聚氨酯）；urethanization（氨基甲酸酯化）是专业派生词，urethane-based（以聚氨酯为基础的）是复合形容词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, urethane is best treated as a complete chemical base rather than forced into ordinary English affixes. Principal family members and formations include urethane, plural urethanes for different carbamates or products, poly- (“many, polymeric”) + urethane → polyurethane, and plural polyurethanes. Urethanization is a specialized derivative meaning the formation of urethane groups; urethane-based is a compound adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: ethyl carbamate（氨基甲酸乙酯）是特定化合物义的准确同义名称；carbamate（氨基甲酸酯，亦可指相应盐类）范围更广；polyurethane（聚氨酯）对应材料行业中的 urethane，但不能替换化学语境中的氨基甲酸乙酯。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Ethyl carbamate is the exact alternative name for the specific compound. Carbamate is broader and can also refer to corresponding salts. Polyurethane matches the commercial material sense of urethane but cannot replace ethyl carbamate in chemical descriptions.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 先记化学名 urethane，再加 poly-＝多个连接单元，联想到聚氨酯；注意小分子化合物与聚合材料的区别。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Learn urethane as a chemical name, then connect poly- with many linked units to recall polyurethane; keep the small compound and the polymer distinct.

etymology_story.zh: vermouth 经法语借入英语，最终来自德语 Wermut，意为“苦艾”，指传统上用于调味的植物。名称由一种代表性香草转而指经过草本调香的加强葡萄酒。
etymology_story.en: Vermouth entered English through French and ultimately comes from German Wermut, meaning “wormwood,” a plant traditionally used to flavor it. The name of a characteristic botanical became the name of the aromatized fortified wine.

morphology_enriched.zh: vermouth 是不可按现代英语词根和词缀继续拆分的借词，尤其不能拆成 verm + mouth。通常作不可数名词；vermouths 可表示不同种类或多份味美思；vermouth-based（以味美思为基础的）和 vermouth-flavored（味美思风味的）是描述性复合形式，没有常用的独立派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Vermouth is a borrowed base with no productive internal division into modern English roots and affixes; it is not verm + mouth. It is usually uncountable, while vermouths can refer to varieties or servings. Vermouth-based and vermouth-flavored are descriptive compounds; there is no common independent family of derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: aromatized wine（加香葡萄酒）是较宽泛的类别名称；fortified wine（加强葡萄酒）强调加入酒精，并不一定经过草本调香；aperitif（餐前酒）强调饮用场合。三者都是相关上位表达，不是 vermouth 的完全同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Aromatized wine names a broader category of flavored wines; fortified wine emphasizes added alcohol and need not involve botanical flavoring; aperitif describes a drink's role before a meal. These are related broader terms, not exact synonyms for vermouth.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Wermut means wormwood: picture botanicals flavoring wine to remember vermouth.

etymology_story.zh: wombat 借自澳大利亚悉尼一带的达鲁格语，是欧洲移民借用当地动物名称的例子。这个词进入英语后继续指这种矮壮、善于挖洞的澳大利亚有袋动物。
etymology_story.en: Wombat was borrowed from Dharug, an Aboriginal language of the Sydney region of Australia, as European settlers adopted a local animal name. In English, it retained its reference to this stocky, burrowing Australian marsupial.

morphology_enriched.zh: wombat 是完整借词，不能按 womb（子宫）+ bat（蝙蝠）分析；名词复数为 wombats。wombat-like（像袋熊的）是描述性复合形式；wombat 没有常用的独立动词、形容词或副词派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Wombat is a complete borrowed word, not a combination of womb and bat; its plural is wombats. Wombat-like is a descriptive compound. There are no common independent verb, adjective, or adverb derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: burrowing marsupial（穴居有袋动物）突出挖洞习性，但范围比 wombat 更广；Australian marsupial（澳大利亚有袋动物）更宽泛，也包括袋鼠和考拉。koala（考拉）是相关但不同的动物，主要栖息于树上，不能作 wombat 的同义词；wombat 没有常用的准确替代名称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Burrowing marsupial highlights its digging habits but has a broader scope; Australian marsupial is broader still and also includes kangaroos and koalas. Koala names a related but different, mainly tree-dwelling animal and is not a synonym. Wombat has no common exact alternative name.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 整词配画面：矮壮身躯、腹部育儿袋、地下长洞，就是袋熊。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Attach the whole word to one image: a stocky Australian animal with a pouch and a long underground burrow.

etymology.text: 从古英语短语 on bedde（在床上）缩合而来，中古英语已有 abed。把两个词挤成一个，就像人缩进了被窝。

usage_note: 较旧式或文学化；日常更常说 in bed。abed 表位置和状态，不保证已经睡着。

senses.meaning_en: In bed; literary or old-fashioned.

senses.meaning_zh: 在床上的；卧床的（用于表语，文学或旧式用语）
senses.meaning_en: In bed, used predicatively; literary or old-fashioned.
senses.english_definition: Someone who is abed is in bed, usually resting or sleeping.
senses.collocation_en: still abed; already abed
senses.collocation_zh: 仍在床上；已经上床

etymology_story.zh: abed 源自古英语 on bedde，意为“在床上”；其中 bedde 是 bed 的旧时屈折形式。短语逐渐合写，弱化后的 on 成为 a-，这种结构也见于其他表示位置或状态的旧词。
etymology_story.en: Abed developed from Old English on bedde, meaning 'in bed'; bedde was an inflected form of bed. The phrase became a single word, with the weakened on surviving as a-, a formation also found in other older expressions of position or state.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可分析为 a-（历史上表示“在……中／上”）+ bed（床），但这种 a- 构词方式如今通常不再自由产出新词。abed 本身没有常用派生词；基础词 bed 的常用词族包括 beds（床的复数）、bedded（安置于床上；铺设的）、bedding（寝具）、bedroom（卧室）、bedtime（就寝时间）和 bedridden（长期卧床的）。CEFR-C2 为编辑性难度估级，并非官方词表认定。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern word can be analyzed as a- (historically 'in' or 'on') + bed, although this use of a- is generally no longer productive. Abed has no common derivatives of its own; the base bed has the common family members beds, bedded, bedding, bedroom, bedtime, and bedridden. CEFR-C2 is an editorial difficulty estimate, not an official word-list assignment.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: in bed（在床上）是日常中性表达；bedridden（长期卧床的）强调因疾病或身体状况无法起床；asleep（睡着的）强调睡眠状态。abed 带文学或旧式色彩，本身并不表示生病或已经睡着。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: In bed is the neutral everyday equivalent; bedridden implies being unable to leave bed because of illness or physical limitations; asleep describes actual sleep. Abed is literary or old-fashioned and does not itself imply illness or sleep.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: a- 表位置，bed 是床：人还“在床上”，就是 abed。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of a- as a location marker: a person located in bed is abed.

senses.meaning_zh: 顽固守旧、持强硬民族主义立场的人（英国英语，常大写为 Blimp）
senses.meaning_en: A pompously conservative nationalist, especially in British usage and often capitalized.

etymology_story.zh: blimp 在第一次世界大战期间见于英国飞艇用语，其确切词源尚不确定。表示守旧人物的义项则来自漫画家戴维·洛于1934年创作的 Colonel Blimp，这一人物以自负、守旧和强硬的民族主义言论著称。
etymology_story.en: Blimp appeared in British airship terminology during the First World War, but its exact origin is uncertain. The reactionary-person sense comes from Colonel Blimp, the cartoon character created by David Low in 1934, known for pompous, conservative, and aggressively nationalist opinions.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 blimp 是不可进一步可靠拆分的词基；常用或透明的相关形式有 blimps（复数）、blimplike／blimp-like（像飞艇的）和 blimpish（布林普式的；自负守旧的）。较少见的派生词有 blimpishness（自负守旧的作风）和 Blimpism／blimpism（布林普式的守旧民族主义）。CEFR-C2 为编辑性难度估级，并非官方词表认定。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, blimp is a base with no reliable smaller morphological division. Common or transparent related forms include blimps, blimplike or blimp-like, and blimpish, meaning pompously reactionary. Less frequent derivatives include blimpishness and Blimpism or blimpism. CEFR-C2 is an editorial difficulty estimate, not an official word-list assignment.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: airship（飞艇）是上位词，包含软式和其他结构类型；dirigible（可操纵飞艇）强调能够控制飞行方向，并不专指软式结构；reactionary（反动保守者；极端守旧者）对应人物义，但不必带有 Blimp 所暗含的自负和民族主义色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Airship is the broader category and includes nonrigid and other structural types; dirigible emphasizes steerability rather than nonrigid construction; reactionary matches the political sense but need not suggest the pomposity and nationalism associated with a Blimp.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 blimp 连到“鼓鼓的飞艇”这一形象；形容人时，可能是在讥讽体形，也可能是在讥讽膨胀的自负。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor blimp to a swollen airship; figurative uses can mock either a person's size or an inflated sense of importance.

etymology_story.zh: 纺织义的 card 经法语梳理纤维的词进入英语，最终与拉丁语 carduus“蓟”有关，因为蓟状刺头曾用于处理纤维。证件、包装及体育等义项则属于另一词源的 card“卡片”，经法语追溯至拉丁语 charta“纸”；carded 是这些动词义的 -ed 形式。
etymology_story.en: The textile verb card entered English through French words for processing fibers and ultimately relates to Latin carduus, 'thistle,' reflecting the use of prickly plant heads in textile work. The identification, packaging, and sporting senses belong to the separate card meaning 'a piece of card,' derived through French from Latin charta, 'paper'; carded is the -ed form of these verbs.

morphology_enriched.zh: card + -ed → carded：既可构成过去式或过去分词，也可形成表示加工或包装状态的形容词。相关词族包括 card（梳理；查验证件；出牌处罚等）、cards（第三人称单数或名词复数）、carding（梳理；查验证件等）、carder（梳理工；梳理机）和 carding machine（梳理机）；card、cardboard（纸板）、cardholder（持卡人；卡套）属于卡片词源一支。CEFR-C2 为编辑性难度估级，并非官方词表认定。
morphology_enriched.en: Card + -ed forms carded, a past tense or past participle that can also function as an adjective describing a processed or packaged state. Related forms include card, cards, carding, carder, and carding machine; card, cardboard, and cardholder belong to the paper-card branch. CEFR-C2 is an editorial difficulty estimate, not an official word-list assignment.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: combed（精梳的）用于纺织时通常意味着进一步去除短纤维并使纤维更加平行；checked（查验过的）含义较宽，不能单独说明查验的是年龄证件；booked（被记名警告的）在足球中通常指吃黄牌，而 carded 可涉及黄牌或红牌。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Combed generally indicates further textile processing that removes short fibers and makes the remaining fibers more parallel; checked is broader and does not specifically identify an age check; booked usually means cautioned with a yellow card in football, whereas carded can refer to either a yellow or a red card.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 分清两条线：梳理工具处理纤维；卡片用来查身份、记成绩、排赛事或作处罚。-ed 表示动作已经发生或形成的状态。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Keep two branches separate: a carding tool processes fibers; a card checks identity, records scores, lists contests, or signals penalties. The ending -ed marks a completed action or resulting state.

meaning: 脉轮（瑜伽传统中的能量中心）

etymology.text: 来自梵语 cakra，原意是“轮、圆”。瑜伽传统借用轮的意象来称身体中的精神能量中心。

etymology_story.zh: chakra 借自梵语 cakra，原义是“轮、圆盘”。在某些宗教与瑜伽传统中，轮的形象被用于描述微妙身体中的能量中心，英语保留了这一专门含义。
etymology_story.en: Chakra was borrowed from Sanskrit cakra, meaning 'wheel' or 'disc.' Certain religious and yogic traditions applied the wheel image to energy centers in the subtle body, and English adopted this specialized meaning.

morphology_enriched.zh: chakra 在现代英语中是整体借入的词基，不宜拆成英语词根和词缀。相关形式有 chakras（复数）、chakric（脉轮的，较少见，chakra 去掉末尾 a 后加 -ic），以及 root chakra（海底轮）、heart chakra（心轮）和 chakra system（脉轮体系）等组合。CEFR-C2 为编辑性难度估级，并非官方词表认定。
morphology_enriched.en: Chakra is a borrowed base in modern English and should not be divided into English roots and affixes. Related forms include the plural chakras and the less common adjective chakric, formed by replacing final -a with -ic, along with combinations such as root chakra, heart chakra, and chakra system. CEFR-C2 is an editorial difficulty estimate, not an official word-list assignment.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: energy center（能量中心）是解释性近义表达，但范围比 chakra 更宽；psychic center（灵性能量中心）突出传统所说的微妙或灵性层面；plexus（神经丛）是解剖学术语，即使某些论述将两者对应，也不能视为 chakra 的严格同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Energy center is an explanatory near-equivalent but has a wider range; psychic center emphasizes the subtle or spiritual aspect described in these traditions; plexus is an anatomical term and is not an exact synonym, even when a particular account associates a chakra with a nerve plexus.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 本义是“轮”：把传统中的脉轮想成一个能量转轮。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with the original meaning 'wheel': picture a chakra as an energy wheel within the traditional model.

etymology.text: 18世纪英语以希腊语来源的 chrono-（时间）和 -meter（测量器）组成；航海时，准确的时间曾是确定位置的重要帮手。

usage_note: chronometer 强调计时精度；stopwatch 强调测量一段经过的时间。

senses.meaning_zh: 精密计时器；精密时钟或钟表，尤指航海计时器
senses.meaning_en: A highly accurate timepiece, especially one used in navigation.
senses.english_definition: A chronometer is a clock or watch designed to keep time very accurately, especially for navigation or other tasks requiring precise timekeeping.
senses.collocation_en: marine chronometer; precision chronometer
senses.collocation_zh: 航海精密计时器；精密时计

senses.sentence_zh: 领航员使用航海精密计时器辅助确定船只的经度。

etymology_story.zh: chronometer 由希腊语来源的 chrono-“时间”和 -meter“测量仪器”构成，字面意思是“测量时间的仪器”。这个词尤其与精密航海钟联系起来，因为海上准确计时曾是确定经度的关键。
etymology_story.en: Chronometer combines the Greek-derived elements chrono-, 'time,' and -meter, 'measuring instrument,' literally naming an instrument for measuring time. It became especially associated with precision marine clocks because accurate timekeeping at sea was crucial to determining longitude.

morphology_enriched.zh: chrono-（时间）+ -meter（测量仪器）→ chronometer。直接相关形式包括 chronometers（复数）、chronometry（精密计时；计时学）、chronometric（计时的）、chronometrical（计时的，较少见）和 chronometrically（以精密计时方式）；共享 chrono- 的相关构词有 chronology（年代顺序；年代学）和 chronograph（计时码表；记时仪），但它们不是 chronometer 的直接派生词。CEFR-C2 为编辑性难度估级，并非官方词表认定。
morphology_enriched.en: Chrono- ('time') + -meter ('measuring instrument') forms chronometer. Its direct family includes chronometers, chronometry, chronometric, the less common chronometrical, and chronometrically; chronology and chronograph share the combining form chrono- but are not direct derivatives of chronometer. CEFR-C2 is an editorial difficulty estimate, not an official word-list assignment.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: timepiece（时计；钟表）是泛称，不强调精度；clock（时钟）通常指非佩戴式钟；chronograph（计时码表；记时仪）强调测量或记录时间间隔的功能。chronometer 则突出走时准确，不能与 chronograph 简单互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Timepiece is a general term that does not imply exceptional accuracy; clock usually refers to a timepiece that is not worn; chronograph emphasizes measuring or recording elapsed intervals. Chronometer emphasizes accurate timekeeping and is not interchangeable with chronograph.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: chrono- 是时间，-meter 是测量仪器：专门把时间量准的精密时计。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Chrono- means time and -meter means measuring instrument: a chronometer measures time with particular accuracy.

etymology.text: 皮肤“鸡眼”义的 corn 来自古法语 corne（角），追溯到拉丁语 cornu（角）；硬化的皮肤让人联想到角质，并非来自玉米义的古英语 corn。

usage_note: 这里是脚上局部增厚的硬皮；玉米通常说不可数的 corn，不用 corns 表示日常食材。

etymology_story.zh: 鸡眼义的 corn 来自古法语 corn／corne，最终源于拉丁语 cornu（角），以角状的硬组织命名，与谷物义的 corn 同形而不同源。盐腌义的动词则来自表示小颗粒的 corn，原指用盐粒腌肉。
etymology_story.en: Corn meaning a hard skin growth came through Old French corn or corne from Latin cornu, meaning 'horn'; it is historically distinct from corn meaning grain. The curing verb comes from corn meaning a small grain or particle, referring to the grains of salt used to preserve meat.

morphology_enriched.zh: 鸡眼义：corn（鸡眼）＋-s（名词复数）→ corns；常见组合有 corn removal（去除鸡眼）、corn remover（鸡眼去除剂）。盐腌义：corn（盐腌）＋-s（第三人称单数）→ corns；动词变化为 corn、corns、corned、corning，常见组合为 corned beef（咸牛肉）。这些词形分属两个不同来源的词。
morphology_enriched.en: Skin-growth sense: corn + plural -s → corns; common combinations include corn removal and corn remover. Curing sense: corn + third-person singular -s → corns; the verb forms are corn, corns, corned, and corning, with corned beef as a familiar combination. These forms belong to two historically separate words.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: calluses（胼胝、老茧）通常面积较大，未必疼痛；hard skin（硬皮）是更宽泛的描述，corns 特指通常有硬芯的局部鸡眼。盐腌义近于 cures（腌制保存），但 cures 还可包括烟熏等方法。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Calluses are generally broader areas of thickened skin and may be painless; hard skin is a broader descriptive term, whereas corns are localized growths often containing a hard core. In the culinary sense, cures is close in meaning but also covers methods such as smoking.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 鸡眼像小角一样硬；盐腌则联想一粒粒盐。两条来源，分别记忆。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A skin corn is hard like a tiny horn; corning meat uses grains of salt. Keep the two origins separate.

etymology_story.en: Corsage comes from French corsage, originally referring to the upper body or the bodice of a garment, ultimately related to Latin corpus, meaning 'body.' Its floral meaning developed from bouquet de corsage, a bouquet worn at the bodice, and later extended to arrangements worn on the wrist.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常作为整体借词分析：corsage；复数为 corsages。它没有常用的派生词族；wrist corsage（腕花）和 corsage pin（胸花别针）是复合表达，corsage-like（像胸花的）是可临时构成的描述性形式。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, corsage is normally treated as an unanalyzed loanword; its plural is corsages. It has no established common family of derivatives; wrist corsage and corsage pin are compounds, while corsage-like is a possible descriptive formation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: boutonniere（男式纽扣眼花、领花）通常是一朵花或很小的花饰，佩在翻领处；posy（小花束）强调花束小巧，不一定佩戴；bouquet（花束）范围更广，常指手持花束。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A boutonniere is usually a single flower or very small arrangement worn on a lapel; a posy is a small bunch of flowers that need not be worn; a bouquet is a broader term and often refers to flowers carried in the hand.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“衣服胸身”想到“胸前花饰”，再延伸到腕花。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture flowers attached to a bodice: the garment location gave the flower arrangement its name.

etymology.text: 英语来自法语 découpler（解开连接），由表示解除的 dé- 与 coupler（连接）组成。可想象把连着的两个部件解开。

usage_note: 常用 decouple A from B；强调解除两者的联动，不一定是把东西切成碎片。

senses.meaning_en: make things independent of each other or stop them changing together
senses.english_definition: If one activity or process is decoupled from another, it no longer depends on it or changes in the same way.

senses.collocation_zh: 使经济增长与排放脱钩；使薪酬与绩效脱钩

etymology_story.zh: 由表示解除的 de- 与 couple（连接）构成；couple 经法语追溯至拉丁语 copula（连接物、纽带）。从解除实体连接的意思，发展出消除经济、系统或过程之间依赖关系的抽象用法。
etymology_story.en: Decouple combines reversative de- with couple, whose history runs through French to Latin copula, meaning a bond or connection. The idea of undoing a physical connection extended to removing dependencies between economies, systems, or processes.

morphology_enriched.zh: de-（解除、逆转）＋couple（连接）→ decouple。词形及常见派生有 decouples、decoupled、decoupling；decoupling 也可作名词表示“脱钩、解耦”，decoupled 可作形容词表示“已解耦的”。相关基础词族有 couple、coupled、coupling、recouple、recoupling。
morphology_enriched.en: de- 'undo or reverse' + couple 'connect' → decouple. Inflected and common derived forms include decouples, decoupled, and decoupling; decoupling also functions as a noun, and decoupled can function as an adjective. Related base-family forms include couple, coupled, coupling, recouple, and recoupling.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: disconnect（断开）强调切断连接；uncouple（解开连接）常用于机械连接；disentangle（解开纠缠、理清）强调解除复杂纠缠。decouple 尤其强调使原本关联的部分能够独立运作。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Disconnect emphasizes breaking a connection; uncouple often concerns a mechanical joining; disentangle emphasizes freeing things from complicated involvement. Decouple particularly suggests allowing previously linked parts to operate independently.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: couple 是“连成一对”，de- 把连接解除：从部件分离到关系脱钩。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Couple joins things together; de- undoes that joining, physically or functionally.

forms: 英式 decriminalise；美式 decriminalize；decriminalises / decriminalised / decriminalising。
family: decriminalisation（美式 decriminalization）非刑罪化

morphology.text: de-（取消） + criminal（刑事犯罪的） + -ise（使成为） → decriminalise（取消某行为的刑事犯罪地位）。

etymology.text: 英语 decriminalize 由名词 decriminalization 逆构而来：去掉名词词尾，形成动词；decriminalise 是其英式拼写。可联想为撤下某种行为的“刑事犯罪”标签。

usage_note: decriminalise 只说取消刑事犯罪地位，不保证完全合法或不受处罚；legalise 更强调使合法。

senses.meaning_zh: 使非刑罪化；取消某行为的刑事犯罪地位
senses.meaning_en: remove criminal status or criminal penalties from an activity
senses.english_definition: If a government decriminalises an activity, it changes the law so that the activity is no longer treated as a criminal offence.
senses.collocation_en: decriminalise drug possession; decriminalise homosexuality
senses.collocation_zh: 使持有毒品非刑罪化；使同性性行为非刑罪化

senses.sentence_zh: 这项提案将使持有少量该毒品的行为不再构成刑事犯罪。

etymology_story.zh: 这是现代法律与政策词汇，所属词族以 criminal（犯罪的）为基础，而 criminal 最终源于拉丁语 crimen（指控、罪行）。前缀 de- 表示取消原有的刑事犯罪地位；decriminalise 是 decriminalize 的英式拼写变体。
etymology_story.en: This modern legal and policy term belongs to the family of criminal, ultimately from Latin crimen, meaning an accusation or crime. The prefix de- expresses removal of criminal status; decriminalise is a British spelling variant of decriminalize.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词关系为 de-（取消）＋criminalise（将……定为刑事犯罪）；criminalise 又可分析为 criminal＋-ise。词族包括 decriminalises、decriminalised、decriminalising、decriminalisation；对应的 -ize 拼写形式为 decriminalize、decriminalizes、decriminalized、decriminalizing、decriminalization，相关词有 crime、criminal、criminality、criminalise、criminalisation。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern structure is de- 'reverse or remove' + criminalise 'make criminal'; criminalise itself contains criminal + -ise. The family includes decriminalises, decriminalised, decriminalising, and decriminalisation. Corresponding -ize forms are decriminalize, decriminalizes, decriminalized, decriminalizing, and decriminalization; related words include crime, criminal, criminality, criminalise, and criminalisation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: legalise（使合法化）通常表示法律明确允许某行为；depenalise（取消处罚）强调撤销处罚；liberalise（放宽限制）范围更广。decriminalise 只说明取消刑事犯罪地位，相关行为仍可能受到行政处罚或其他规制。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Legalise generally means making an activity lawful; depenalise emphasizes removing penalties; liberalise more broadly means relaxing restrictions. Decriminalise specifically removes criminal status, while civil penalties or other regulation may remain.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: de- 撤下 criminal 标签：不再按刑事犯罪处理。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of de- removing the criminal label from an activity.

forms: enervates；过去式、过去分词 enervated；现在分词 enervating。
family: enervation 衰弱；enervating 使人疲乏的

morphology.text: e-（向外、除去） + nerv-（力量，原指筋腱） + -ate（动词后缀） → enervate（使失去力量）。

etymology.text: 来自拉丁语 enervare，字面是去掉筋腱、削弱力量，由 ex- 与 nervus（筋腱）组成。记成“把力气抽走”。

usage_note: enervate 表示削弱精力，和 energise（使充满活力）的方向相反；语体较正式。
