senses.meaning_zh: 使衰弱；使失去精力或活力
senses.meaning_en: weaken someone or drain their energy
senses.english_definition: If something enervates you, it makes you feel weak and lacking in energy.
senses.collocation_en: enervating heat; feel enervated
senses.collocation_zh: 令人困乏的炎热；感到有气无力
senses.sentence_en: The oppressive heat enervated the players before the match had even begun.
senses.sentence_zh: 比赛还没开始，闷热的天气就已经让队员们感到浑身乏力。

etymology_story.zh: 源于拉丁语 enervare（削弱、使失去力量），由 e-／ex-（向外、除去）与 nervus（筋腱；力量）构成。它以抽去支撑力量的筋腱为意象，后来泛指削弱身体、精神或行动能力。
etymology_story.en: Enervate comes from Latin enervare, meaning to weaken, formed from e- or ex- 'out or away' and nervus 'sinew or strength.' The image of removing the sinews that supply strength developed into the broader sense of draining physical or mental energy.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是整体借入的动词；学习时可按历史成分分析为 e-（除去）＋nerv-（筋腱、力量）＋-ate（动词形式）。常见词族有 enervates、enervated（被削弱的、乏力的）、enervating（令人乏力的）、enervation（衰弱、精力耗损）；nerve 和 nervous 是历史相关词，并非由 enervate 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, this is a borrowed verb; for learning purposes its historical elements are e- 'away' + nerv- 'sinew or strength' + the verbal ending -ate. Common family forms include enervates, enervated, enervating, and enervation. Nerve and nervous are historically related words rather than derivatives of enervate.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: weaken（削弱）适用范围最广；debilitate（使虚弱）通常强调明显或持续的身体、功能损害；exhaust（使精疲力竭）强调精力被大量消耗。enervate 较正式，常强调精力、活力或意志逐渐被消磨。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Weaken is the broadest term; debilitate usually suggests substantial or lasting impairment of strength or functioning; exhaust emphasizes using up someone's energy. Enervate is more formal and often suggests a draining of vitality or resolve.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: e- 抽走 nerv- 所代表的筋力：越抽越乏力。别把它记成 energise（使充满活力）。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Imagine e- taking the strength out of the sinews: energy drains away. Keep it distinct from energise.

etymology.text: 中古英语写作 holihoc，通常解释为 holi（神圣的）加 hokke（葵类植物，来自古英语 hocc）。可把它记成花茎高高、花朵一层层开的花。

usage_note: hollyhock 指蜀葵，不能按开头的 holly 认作冬青；通常可见高花茎上排列着大花。

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常把 hollyhock 作为固定植物名称整体识记，不宜按 holly（冬青）＋hock 作字面分析。常用形式为单数 hollyhock、复数 hollyhocks；没有常用的派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, hollyhock is normally learned as a fixed plant name rather than interpreted literally as holly + hock. Its usual forms are singular hollyhock and plural hollyhocks; it has no common family of derived words.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有完全对应的常用近义词。mallow（葵类植物）范围更广；rose mallow（玫瑰葵等木槿属植物）和 hibiscus（木槿属植物）指相关但不同的植物，不能直接替换 hollyhock。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no common exact synonym. Mallow is a broader plant name, while rose mallow and hibiscus refer to related but different plants and are not interchangeable with hollyhock.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 旧词 hock 指葵：想象一根高花茎上层层开花的蜀葵；holy 只帮助记词源。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Old hock means mallow: picture a tall mallow with flowers stacked up its stem; holy is a historical memory cue.

etymology_story.zh: hothead 是由 hot（热的）和 head（头）组成的英语复合词，近代英语早期已用于形容容易激动或鲁莽的人。它把愤怒和冲动比作头脑发热，与 hot-headed 的表达相呼应。
etymology_story.en: Hothead is an English compound of hot and head, used since the early modern period for an excitable or rash person. It pictures anger and impulsiveness as heat in the head, matching the related expression hot-headed.

morphology_enriched.zh: hot（热的）＋head（头）→ hothead（容易头脑发热的人），复数 hotheads。相关词族：hotheaded／hot-headed（易冲动的）、hotheadedly／hot-headedly（冲动地）、hotheadedness／hot-headedness（急躁；冲动）。
morphology_enriched.en: Hot + head → hothead, literally a person with a metaphorically hot head; the plural is hotheads. Related forms include hotheaded/hot-headed, hotheadedly/hot-headedly, and hotheadedness/hot-headedness.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 同义或近义表达有 hotspur、rash person 和 quick-tempered person：hotspur 较文雅或旧式，强调性急好斗；rash person 强调不考虑后果；quick-tempered person 强调容易发怒，而 hothead 常兼有易怒和冲动两层意思。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Related expressions include hotspur, rash person, and quick-tempered person. Hotspur is literary or old-fashioned and suggests impetuous aggression; rash person stresses poor consideration of consequences; quick-tempered person stresses anger, while hothead commonly combines anger with impulsive action.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: hot＋head＝脑袋一热，就冲动行事的人。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hot + head: a heated head acts before it thinks.

etymology_story.zh: huckleberry 通常被认为是 hurtleberry 的变体，后者是与 whortleberry 相关的旧浆果名称。这个词在北美英语中用于若干结类似浆果的本土灌木及其果实，并不只对应一个物种。
etymology_story.en: Huckleberry is generally regarded as an alteration of hurtleberry, an older berry name related to whortleberry. In North American English, it came to name several native shrubs with similar berries, as well as their fruit, rather than a single species.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可识别为 huckle-（不能独立使用的植物名称成分）＋berry（浆果），但 huckle- 不是具有明确现代词义的自由词根。复数为 huckleberries；常见组合有 huckleberry bush（美洲越橘灌木）和 huckleberry jam（美洲越橘果酱），没有常用的派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern speakers can recognize huckle- + berry, but huckle- is a bound plant-name element rather than an independent root with a clear current meaning. The plural is huckleberries; common combinations include huckleberry bush and huckleberry jam, and there is no common family of derived words.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: blueberry（蓝莓）、bilberry（欧洲越橘）和 whortleberry（越橘的传统名称）是相关词，并非普遍可互换的同义词。huckleberry 是北美地区对多种浆果及灌木的俗称，blueberry 和 bilberry 通常指其他特定类群，具体名称也受地域影响。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Blueberry, bilberry, and whortleberry are related terms rather than universally interchangeable synonyms. Huckleberry is a North American common name covering several berries and shrubs; blueberry and bilberry usually identify other particular groups, and local naming practices vary.

etymology_story.en: The British chemist Smithson Tennant discovered iridium in 1803 and named it from Greek iris, meaning rainbow. The name refers to the varied colours of its salts rather than the silvery-white appearance of the metal itself.

morphology_enriched.zh: 科技词汇构词为 irid-（虹；在此指铱）＋-ium（常见元素名称后缀）→ iridium。相关词有 iridic（铱的；传统命名中指较高氧化态的）、iridous（亚铱的；传统命名中指较低氧化态的）和 iridate（铱酸盐）；这些派生形式多用于专业化学语境。
morphology_enriched.en: The scientific formation is irid- (rainbow, here associated with iridium) + -ium, a common element-name suffix. Related technical forms include iridic, traditionally associated with a higher oxidation state; iridous, associated with a lower oxidation state; and iridate, an iridium-containing oxyanion or its salt.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 铱没有真正的元素名称近义词。platinum（铂）、osmium（锇）和 rhodium（铑）都是相关的铂族金属，但分别是不同元素，不能替换 iridium；Ir 是铱的化学符号。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Iridium has no true synonym naming another element. Platinum, osmium, and rhodium are related platinum-group metals, but each is a different element and cannot replace iridium; Ir is its chemical symbol.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Irid- means rainbow: colourful iridium salts explain the metal's rainbow-based name.

etymology_story.zh: isometric 由希腊语来源的 iso-（相等）和表示测量的 metr- 构成，基本概念是“度量相等”。这一概念分别发展出几何中的保持距离、制图中的各轴比例相同，以及肌肉发力时长度基本不变等专业含义。
etymology_story.en: Isometric combines Greek-derived iso-, meaning equal, with metr-, referring to measurement, giving the basic idea of equal measure. This developed into specialized meanings involving preserved distances in geometry, equal axial scales in drawing, and approximately unchanged muscle length during exertion.

morphology_enriched.zh: iso-（相等）＋metr-（测量）＋-ic（……的）→ isometric。相关词族包括 isometry（等距变换；等距关系）、isometrically（以等距或等长方式）、isometrics（等长训练）和较少见的形容词变体 isometrical；名词 isometric 由形容词转用而来。
morphology_enriched.en: Iso- (equal) + metr- (measure) + -ic (relating to) → isometric. Its word family includes isometry, isometrically, isometrics, and the less common adjective variant isometrical; the noun isometric is formed by conversion from the adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: distance-preserving（保持距离的）可解释几何义；equal-measure（等度量的）概括构词含义；static（静态的）常用于描述等长训练。三者都只能在相应语境中接近 isometric，尤其 static 本身并不严格表示肌肉长度不变。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Distance-preserving explains the geometric sense; equal-measure captures the underlying formation; static often describes isometric exercise. These expressions overlap with particular senses rather than replacing the word everywhere, and static alone does not precisely specify unchanged muscle length.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: iso＝相等，metr＝度量：几何保距离，制图同轴比，肌肉发力长度稳。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Iso means equal and metr means measure: preserve distances, use equal axial scales, or keep muscle length steady.

etymology_story.zh: kilter 是较早形式 kelter 的变体，表示良好状态或正常运转，其更早来源尚不确定。现代英语主要在 out of kilter 中保留这个词，并将其用于机械、计划以及各种协调关系。
etymology_story.en: Kilter is a variant of the earlier kelter, meaning good condition or working order; its ultimate origin is uncertain. It survives chiefly in out of kilter, applied to machinery, plans, and other things whose parts should work together.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，kilter 是不可进一步分析的单纯词，没有常用的前后缀派生词。相关形式包括拼写变体 kelter、短语 out of kilter（失调）和 in kilter（正常），以及置于名词前的复合形容词 out-of-kilter，如 an out-of-kilter system（失调的系统）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, kilter is a simple word with no productive internal breakdown or common affixed derivatives. Related forms include the spelling variant kelter, the phrases out of kilter and in kilter, and the attributive compound adjective out-of-kilter, as in an out-of-kilter system.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: balance（平衡）强调各部分力量或数量的均衡；alignment（一致、对齐）强调位置或目标相互吻合；working order（正常运转状态）强调功能正常。kilter 主要出现在固定表达中，常概括这些方面的协调状态。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Balance emphasizes equilibrium between forces or amounts; alignment emphasizes matching positions or goals; working order emphasizes proper functioning. Kilter occurs mainly in fixed expressions and can refer broadly to any of these forms of coordination.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 kilter 记成“运转合拍的状态”：out of kilter，就是出了正常节奏。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of kilter as everything running in step: out of kilter means something has fallen out of step.

senses.meaning_zh: （牛等）哞哞叫；为 low 的过去式和过去分词

etymology_story.zh: 表示牛叫的 low 来自古英语 hlōwan，在其他日耳曼语言中也有同源词，通常被认为具有拟声性质。lowed 是这个古老动词按现代规则添加过去时词尾形成的屈折形式。
etymology_story.en: The cattle-call verb low comes from Old English hlōwan and has relatives in other Germanic languages; it is generally regarded as imitative in origin. Lowed is the regular modern past-tense and past-participle form of this old verb.

morphology_enriched.zh: low（哞叫）+ -ed（过去式、过去分词词尾）→ lowed；这里的 -ed 读 /d/，不另成音节。动词变化为 low、lows、lowed、lowing；同形名词 low 表示“一声哞叫”，lowing 也可作名词表示“哞叫声”。表示“低的”的形容词 low 不属于这里的词义系统。
morphology_enriched.en: Low, meaning to moo, + the past-tense and past-participle ending -ed → lowed; the ending is pronounced /d/ without an additional syllable. The verb forms are low, lows, lowed, and lowing; the noun low means a single cattle call, and lowing can name the sound collectively. The adjective low, meaning not high, belongs to a separate sense group.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: moo（哞叫）是最日常、直接的说法；bellow（吼叫）强调声音响亮而有力，也可用于人或其他动物；low（哞叫）较具文学色彩，常让人联想到低沉、绵长的牛叫声。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Moo is the ordinary everyday term; bellow emphasizes a loud, powerful call and can describe people or other animals; low is more literary and often suggests a deep, prolonged cattle call.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 想象牛拖长声音叫“low——”，再加表示过去的 -ed：lowed，就是“哞叫了”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Imagine a cow drawing out a long low sound, then add the past ending -ed: lowed means it made that call.

etymology.text: 中古英语由 moon 与 shine 组成，最初指月光；18世纪后也指走私或非法酿制的酒，联系到夜色掩护下的活动。

usage_note: 本卡教私酿烈酒义；moonshine 也可指月光或空话，要靠酒罐、蒸馏器等语境判断。

etymology_story.zh: moonshine 在中古英语中由 moon 和 shine 组成，最初指月光，后来也比喻虚幻、没有实质的东西。其“非法烈酒”义在十八世纪末已有记录，通常与借夜色掩护进行秘密活动的联想相联系；动词由这个酒类名词转化而来。
etymology_story.en: Moonshine was formed from moon and shine in Middle English, first meaning moonlight and later also something insubstantial or fanciful. Its illicit-liquor sense is recorded from the late eighteenth century and is commonly associated with clandestine activity under cover of darkness; the verb developed from this noun.

morphology_enriched.zh: moon（月亮）+ shine（光、照耀）→ moonshine，是复合词；表示酿制私酒的动词由名词零派生而来。词族包括 moonshiner（私酒酿造者或贩卖者）、moonshining（酿制私酒；也作动词现在分词）、moonshined（动词过去式及过去分词）和 moonshines（动词第三人称单数）。
morphology_enriched.en: Moon + shine → moonshine, a compound; the illicit-distilling verb is formed by conversion from the noun. Its family includes moonshiner, a maker or seller of illicit spirits; moonshining, the activity or present participle; moonshined, the past tense and past participle; and moonshines, the third-person singular verb form.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hooch（烈酒、私酒）是俚语，不一定强调非法酿制；moonlight（月光）是月光义最普通的对应词，moonshine 更具文学色彩；nonsense（胡言）直接表示没有道理的话，而 moonshine 的空话义常带有虚幻、不切实际的意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hooch is slang for strong liquor and does not necessarily imply illegal production; moonlight is the ordinary term for the literal light, while moonshine is more literary; nonsense directly means foolish or meaningless talk, whereas figurative moonshine often suggests fanciful unreality.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 月亮发光是 moonshine；借月色偷偷酿酒，联想到私酒；像月光一样抓不住，又联想到空话。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Moonshine lights the night: picture secret distilling after dark for the liquor sense, and something impossible to grasp for the nonsense sense.

etymology_story.zh: 英语 panzer 借自德语 Panzer，意为“装甲”或“坦克”。德语词经中古高地德语 panzier 追溯至古法语 panciere，原指保护腹部的铠甲，后来从人体护甲扩展到装甲车辆。
etymology_story.en: English panzer was borrowed from German Panzer, meaning armor or a tank. Through Middle High German panzier, it goes back to Old French panciere, armor protecting the belly, with the meaning later extending from bodily armor to armored vehicles.

morphology_enriched.zh: panzer 在现代英语中是整体借入的单纯词，不能拆成有意义的英语前缀和词根。名词复数为 panzers；同形形容词主要用于 panzer division（装甲师）、panzer corps（装甲军）等组合。没有常用的英语前后缀派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Panzer is a borrowed simple word in modern English and has no meaningful English prefix-and-root breakdown. Its noun plural is panzers; the same-form adjective occurs chiefly in combinations such as panzer division and panzer corps. It has no common English affixed derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: tank（坦克）是不限国家和时代的通称；armored vehicle（装甲车辆）范围更广，也包括并非坦克的车辆；armored（装甲的）用于一般装甲部队或装备，而 panzer 通常带有德国军事、尤其二战的历史背景。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Tank is the general term regardless of country or period; armored vehicle is broader and includes vehicles that are not tanks; armored describes such equipment or forces generally, while panzer usually carries a German military association, especially with the Second World War.

senses.english_definition: A person's physiognomy is the appearance of their face, especially the features that seem to express their character.
senses.collocation_en: human physiognomy; a distinctive physiognomy
senses.collocation_zh: 人的面容；独特的面部特征
senses.sentence_en: The portrait captures his distinctive physiognomy in remarkable detail.
senses.sentence_zh: 这幅肖像以惊人的细节刻画了他独特的面部特征。

senses.meaning_zh: 相面术；根据外貌推断性格的传统方法，现不被视为可靠科学
senses.meaning_en: The traditional practice of inferring character from appearance, not regarded as reliable science
senses.english_definition: Physiognomy is the traditional practice of trying to judge someone's character from their facial features.
senses.collocation_en: the study of physiognomy; the practice of physiognomy
senses.collocation_zh: 对相面术的研究；相面术的运用
senses.sentence_en: The exhibition explores the influence of physiognomy on nineteenth-century portraiture.
senses.sentence_zh: 这次展览探讨了相面术对十九世纪肖像画的影响。

senses.meaning_zh: （地方、景观等的）外观；总体面貌，正式或专业用语
senses.meaning_en: The characteristic outward appearance of a place or landscape, in formal or technical use
senses.english_definition: The physiognomy of a place or landscape is its distinctive outward appearance.
senses.collocation_en: the physiognomy of the landscape; urban physiognomy
senses.collocation_zh: 景观的外在面貌；城市面貌
senses.sentence_en: New towers have transformed the physiognomy of the city.
senses.sentence_zh: 新建的高楼改变了这座城市的面貌。

etymology_story.zh: physiognomy 经法语和拉丁语传入英语，最终来自希腊语 physiognōmonia，涉及根据自然外貌判断性格的观念。它早期指相面术，后来也指被观察的面容，并进一步扩展到地方或景观的外在面貌。
etymology_story.en: Physiognomy entered English through French and Latin from Greek physiognōmonia, associated with judging character from natural appearance. It referred to the practice of such judgment, then also to facial appearance itself, and eventually to the outward character of places and landscapes.

morphology_enriched.zh: 这是整体借入的学术词，可用希腊语来源的构词成分 physio-（自然、本性）和 -gnomy（判断、辨识）辅助理解；不能把 gnom- 与“地精”gnome 联系起来。常见词族包括 physiognomic、physiognomical（面容的；相面术的）、physiognomically（从面容或相面术角度）和 physiognomist（相面者；面相研究者）；名词复数为 physiognomies。
morphology_enriched.en: This is a learned borrowing that can be understood through the Greek-derived elements physio-, meaning nature, and -gnomy, associated with judgment or interpretation; gnom- here is unrelated to the creature called a gnome. Its established family includes physiognomic and physiognomical, the adverb physiognomically, and physiognomist, a practitioner or student of physiognomy; the noun plural is physiognomies.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: countenance（面容、神色）偏重脸上呈现的表情；facial features（五官、面部特征）客观指鼻子、眼睛等结构；appearance（外貌）范围最广，可包括衣着和体态。physiognomy 较正式，常强调有辨识度或被认为体现性格的面部整体特征。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Countenance often emphasizes the expression a face presents; facial features objectively identifies structures such as the nose and eyes; appearance is broader and may include clothing and posture. Physiognomy is formal and often emphasizes distinctive facial characteristics or their supposed connection with character.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: physio- 是“自然本性”，-gnomy 关联“判断”：从脸判断本性，便串起“相面术”和“面容”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect physio- with nature and -gnomy with judgment: judging nature from a face links the practice of physiognomy to the face itself.

senses.meaning_en: A cooking banana, or the plant that produces it.
senses.english_definition: A plantain is a large banana that is usually cooked before it is eaten, or the plant on which it grows.
senses.collocation_en: fried plantains; ripe plantains
senses.collocation_zh: 炸大蕉；成熟的大蕉

senses.meaning_zh: 车前草；车前属植物
senses.meaning_en: A small plant of the genus Plantago, often with low-growing leaves and slender flower spikes.
senses.english_definition: A plantain is a small wild plant that often grows in grass or beside paths and has leaves near the ground and small flowers on upright spikes.
senses.collocation_en: broadleaf plantain; ribwort plantain
senses.collocation_zh: 大车前；长叶车前

etymology_story.zh: 表示大蕉的 plantain 来自西班牙语 plátano，后者可追溯至表示“悬铃木”的拉丁语 platanus。表示车前草的同形词则经法语来自拉丁语 plantago，与 planta“脚掌”有关，通常认为得名于其叶片形状。
etymology_story.en: Plantain meaning a cooking banana comes from Spanish plátano, ultimately from Latin platanus, meaning a plane tree. The separate word for the herb came through French from Latin plantago, related to planta, meaning the sole of the foot, probably in reference to its leaf shape.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，两个义项的 plantain 都作为完整词干处理，不能拆成 plant 加英语后缀。复数为 plantains；plantain-like＝plantain＋-like，意为“像大蕉的”或“像车前草的”，具体取决于语境；常见复合词有 plantain chips“大蕉片”和 plantain lily“玉簪”，后者是另一类植物，并非大蕉或车前草。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, plantain is a whole stem in both meanings, not plant plus an English suffix. Its plural is plantains; plantain-like combines plantain with -like and means resembling either plant, depending on context. Compounds include plantain chips and plantain lily; the latter names a different plant, a hosta.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cooking banana“烹调用蕉”是大蕉义的近义表达，强调用途；broadleaf plantain“大车前”和 ribwort plantain“长叶车前”是车前类植物的具体种类，不能与泛称 plantain 在所有语境中互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cooking banana is a close equivalent of the fruit sense and emphasizes culinary use. Broadleaf plantain and ribwort plantain name particular kinds of the herb, so neither is interchangeable with the broader term in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 同形两词分开记：厨房里是大蕉，路边低叶抽穗的是车前草。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Keep the two words separate: a plantain in the kitchen is a cooking banana; a low-leaved plantain beside a path is an herb.

morphology.text: prompt（迅速的）+ -ly → promptly（迅速地）；pronto 是独立借词，与 prompt 有同源联系，作为独立词素记忆，不拆出英语后缀。

etymology.text: 英语从西班牙语借入 pronto，西班牙语形式来自拉丁语 promptus，意思与“准备就绪、迅速”有关。想象催人立刻动身。

usage_note: 口语，常见于带催促语气的指令；正式通知用 immediately 更稳妥。

senses.meaning_zh: 马上；赶快（非正式用语）
senses.meaning_en: Immediately or very quickly, in informal speech.
senses.english_definition: If someone tells you to do something pronto, they want you to do it immediately.
senses.collocation_en: get here pronto; do it pronto
senses.collocation_zh: 马上到这里来；马上做这件事

senses.sentence_zh: 我们得赶快把那处漏水修好。

etymology_story.zh: 英语 pronto 借自西班牙语 pronto“迅速地；很快”，最终来自拉丁语 promptus“准备就绪的”。它与英语 prompt 同源，但不是由 prompt 加英语后缀构成的。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed pronto from Spanish pronto, meaning quickly or soon, ultimately from Latin promptus, meaning ready. It shares an origin with prompt but was not formed from prompt by adding an English suffix.

morphology_enriched.zh: pronto 是不变形的借入副词，在现代英语中不再拆分，没有常用的直接派生词。prompt“迅速的”、promptly“迅速地”、promptness“迅速；及时”和 promptitude“敏捷；及时”是同源相关词，并非 pronto 的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Pronto is an uninflected borrowed adverb with no productive internal breakdown or common direct derivatives in English. Prompt, promptly, promptness, and promptitude are related through their shared historical origin, rather than derived from pronto.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: immediately“立即”语体中性，直接强调没有延迟；promptly“及时地；迅速地”强调响应迅速或按时完成；pronto 更口语化，常带催促、命令或诙谐语气。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Immediately neutrally emphasizes the absence of delay; promptly emphasizes a quick response or timely action. Pronto is more conversational and often sounds urgent, commanding, or playful.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 与 prompt 的“准备就绪”相连：准备好了，就马上行动。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect it with prompt and readiness: once you are ready, act right away.

senses.meaning_zh: 讨好而虚情假意的；谄媚得令人反感的
senses.meaning_en: Unpleasantly flattering or friendly in an insincere way.
senses.english_definition: Someone who is smarmy is very polite or flattering in a way that seems insincere and makes you dislike or distrust them.

senses.collocation_zh: 油嘴滑舌的推销员；虚情假意的讨好笑容

etymology_story.zh: smarmy 由 smarm 加形容词后缀 -y 构成；smarm 的更早来源尚不明确。smarm 曾有“把头发抹平、抹顺”等意思，后来也表示以过分热情或奉承来讨好人。
etymology_story.en: Smarmy was formed from smarm with the adjective suffix -y; the earlier origin of smarm is uncertain. Smarm has been used for smoothing down hair and later for ingratiating behavior involving excessive friendliness or flattery.

morphology_enriched.zh: smarm“奉承；讨好行为”＋-y“具有……特征的”→smarmy。常用词形和派生词包括 smarmier“更谄媚的”、smarmiest“最谄媚的”、smarmily“谄媚地”和 smarminess“虚情假意的讨好”；动词 smarm 的变化形式为 smarms、smarmed、smarming。
morphology_enriched.en: Smarm, meaning flattery or ingratiating behavior, plus adjectival -y forms smarmy. Its regular family includes the comparative smarmier, superlative smarmiest, adverb smarmily, and noun smarminess; the verb smarm has the forms smarms, smarmed, and smarming.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: unctuous“假意殷勤的”强调油滑、过分热情的言谈举止；obsequious“卑躬屈膝的”强调对权势者的顺从；ingratiating“刻意讨好的”强调争取好感，而 smarmy 尤其突出这种讨好既虚假又令人反感。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Unctuous emphasizes oily, excessive warmth in speech or behavior; obsequious emphasizes submissiveness toward someone powerful; ingratiating emphasizes trying to win approval. Smarmy particularly stresses how false and unpleasant the friendliness feels.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“抹顺头发”联想到“用甜话抹平关系”：过分顺滑的奉承，就是 smarmy。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Move from smoothing hair to smoothing relationships with flattery: friendliness that feels too slick is smarmy.

senses.meaning_zh: 苏克雷（厄瓜多尔原货币单位）
senses.meaning_en: The former monetary unit of Ecuador.
senses.english_definition: The sucre was the unit of money used in Ecuador before the country adopted the US dollar.
senses.collocation_en: the Ecuadorian sucre; a thousand sucres
senses.collocation_zh: 厄瓜多尔苏克雷；一千苏克雷
senses.sentence_en: The old banknote has a face value of a thousand sucres.
senses.sentence_zh: 这张旧钞票的面值是一千苏克雷。

etymology_story.zh: 英语直接借用了西班牙语货币名称 sucre，该名称纪念南美独立运动领袖安东尼奥·何塞·德·苏克雷。它因此是由人名转为普通名词的货币名称。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed the Spanish currency name sucre, which honors the South American independence leader Antonio José de Sucre. The monetary term is therefore a common noun derived from a person's name.

morphology_enriched.zh: sucre 在现代英语中是不可进一步分析的名词词干，复数为 sucres，没有常用的直接派生词。sucre-denominated＝sucre＋denominated，意为“以苏克雷计价的”，属于复合修饰语，不能把 -denominated 当作派生后缀。
morphology_enriched.en: Sucre is an unanalyzed noun stem in modern English; its plural is sucres, and it has no common direct derivatives. Sucre-denominated combines sucre with denominated to mean expressed in sucres; it is a compound modifier, not a formation with a derivational suffix -denominated.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Ecuadorian sucre“厄瓜多尔苏克雷”是明确所指的同义表达；Ecuador's former currency“厄瓜多尔的旧货币”是描述性改述；monetary unit“货币单位”只是上位概念。该词没有两三个可自由替换的普通单词近义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Ecuadorian sucre is an explicit equivalent; Ecuador's former currency is a descriptive paraphrase; monetary unit is a broader category. There are not two or three ordinary single-word synonyms that can freely replace this specific currency name.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 Sucre 人名印在旧钞票上：纪念苏克雷的货币，就叫 sucre。

etymology_story.zh: trapezius 来自新拉丁语的解剖学名称，与表示“梯形”的 trapezium 有关，最终可追溯至希腊语中表示“小桌子”的词。左右两侧斜方肌合起来的轮廓近似梯形，因此得名。
etymology_story.en: Trapezius comes from an anatomical term in New Latin related to trapezium, meaning a trapezoid, ultimately from a Greek word meaning a small table. The name refers to the roughly trapezoidal outline formed by the muscles on the two sides together.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语把 trapezius 作为完整的借入解剖学名词，不宜机械拆成英语词根加 -us；拉丁式复数为 trapezii，也可见英语规则复数 trapeziuses。相关形式包括口语简称 trap，通常用复数 traps；trapezial 是相关形容词，但也可指腕部的大多角骨，须结合语境判断；trapezium、trapezoid 和 trapezoidal 是同源相关词，并非直接从 trapezius 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats trapezius as a complete borrowed anatomical noun rather than a productive English root plus -us; its Latin plural is trapezii, and the regular English plural trapeziuses also occurs. Related forms include the informal shortening trap, usually plural traps, and the adjective trapezial, which can also refer to the trapezium bone in the wrist. Trapezium, trapezoid, and trapezoidal are historically related words, not direct derivatives of trapezius.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: trapezius muscle“斜方肌”是完整、明确的同义名称；trap“斜方肌”是健身语境中的口语简称，常用复数 traps；upper trapezius“斜方肌上部”只指该肌肉的一部分，不能代替整个斜方肌。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Trapezius muscle is the full, explicit equivalent; trap is an informal fitness term, commonly used in the plural traps. Upper trapezius identifies only the upper portion of the muscle and is not a synonym for the whole muscle.

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 vapidus，意为“味道淡薄的、走了味的”，早期英语常用来形容失去滋味的酒。后来由味觉上的寡淡引申为谈话、人物或作品缺少生气与内容。[来源：韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/vapid)
etymology_story.en: Vapid comes from Latin vapidus, meaning flat-tasting, and was formerly often applied to liquor that had lost its flavor. This physical blandness developed into a description of conversation, people, or writing lacking vitality or substance. [Source: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/vapid)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 vapid 是不可再作有效拆分的形容词词基。主要派生词：vapid + -ly → vapidly（乏味空洞地）；vapid + -ness → vapidness（乏味；空洞）；vapid + -ity → vapidity（乏味；空洞）；比较形式为 more vapid、most vapid。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, vapid is an adjective base without a useful productive internal division. Main derivatives: vapid + -ly → vapidly, meaning in a dull or empty manner; vapid + -ness → vapidness, meaning dullness or emptiness; vapid + -ity → vapidity, with the same core meaning. Comparative forms are more vapid and most vapid.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: insipid（平淡无味的）突出缺乏吸引力或滋味；inane（愚蠢空洞的）突出没有意义或缺乏理性；banal（陈腐平庸的）突出毫无新意。vapid 尤其强调缺乏生气、思想或实质内容。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Insipid emphasizes a lack of flavor or appeal; inane emphasizes foolishness or meaninglessness; banal emphasizes stale familiarity and lack of originality. Vapid particularly suggests an absence of vitality, thought, or substance.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 酒走了味，话没了料：从“寡淡”记到“空洞乏味”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Wine loses its flavor; talk loses its substance: flat taste becomes flat conversation.

etymology_story.zh: 该词由 barn“谷仓”与 storm“猛攻、席卷”组成，19世纪末首先用于乡间巡演，与巡回剧团使用谷仓等简陋场地演出有关。后来扩展到巡回竞选、体育表演和早期航空表演。[来源：韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/barnstorm)
etymology_story.en: Formed from barn and storm, the word first referred to rural theatrical touring in the late nineteenth century, associated with performances in barns and similar makeshift venues. Its use later expanded to political campaigning, exhibition sports, and early flying displays. [Source: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/barnstorm)

morphology_enriched.zh: barn（谷仓）+ storm（猛攻；席卷）→ barnstorm（复合动词）。屈折形式：barnstorms、barnstormed、barnstorming；barnstorm + -er → barnstormer（巡回演说者、演员或特技飞行员）；barnstorming 也用作名词，表示巡回活动，并可作形容词，表示巡回进行的或气势热烈的。
morphology_enriched.en: Barn, meaning a farm building, + storm, meaning attack or sweep through, → barnstorm, a compound verb. Inflections: barnstorms, barnstormed, barnstorming. Barnstorm + -er → barnstormer, a touring speaker, performer, or stunt pilot. Barnstorming also functions as a noun for the activity and as an adjective meaning touring or impressively energetic.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: tour（巡回）只说明到多地活动，适用范围最广；campaign（开展竞选或运动）突出争取支持，不一定涉及旅行；stump（巡回竞选演说，主要用于美式英语）突出政治演说。barnstorm 强调短时间内辗转多地、声势活跃。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Tour broadly means visiting several places; campaign emphasizes seeking support and need not involve travel; stump, chiefly American, specifically emphasizes political speechmaking. Barnstorm suggests an energetic succession of visits, often within a short period.

etymology_story.en: The name derives from Cepheus, the constellation containing Delta Cephei, the prototype for this class of stars. Cepheid entered English around the beginning of the twentieth century and commonly retains its initial capital in astronomy. [Source: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/Cepheid)

morphology_enriched.zh: 命名结构为 Cephe-（源自 Cepheus／Cephei 的专名词干）+ -id（表示所属或相关类型的后缀）→ Cepheid。复数为 Cepheids；常见组合有 Cepheid variable（造父变星）、classical Cepheid（经典造父变星）、Type II Cepheid（Ⅱ型造父变星）。无常用副词或动词派生形式；部分词典独立列出其形容词用法。[来源：柯林斯词典](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/cepheid)
morphology_enriched.en: The naming structure is Cephe-, a proper-name stem from Cepheus/Cephei, + -id, a suffix indicating affiliation or type, → Cepheid. The plural is Cepheids. Established combinations include Cepheid variable, classical Cepheid, and Type II Cepheid. There are no common adverbial or verbal derivatives; some dictionaries separately recognize adjectival use. [Source: Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/cepheid)

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Cepheid variable（造父变星）是完整的同义名称；pulsating variable（脉动变星）是上位概念，还包括其他脉动恒星；variable star（变星）范围更广，也包括因食等其他原因发生亮度变化的恒星，不能与 cepheid 完全互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cepheid variable is the equivalent full name. Pulsating variable is a broader category containing other kinds of pulsating stars. Variable star is broader still and includes stars whose observed brightness changes for other reasons, such as eclipses; it is not an interchangeable synonym.

etymology_story.zh: 借自法语 chemise，经古法语可追溯到晚期拉丁语 camisia，指贴身穿的衬衣。英语后来用它指女式连身内衣，并延伸为外形相似的宽松直筒裙。[来源：韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/chemise)
etymology_story.en: Chemise was borrowed from French and ultimately goes back through Old French to Late Latin camisia, a shirt worn next to the skin. English came to use it for a woman's one-piece undergarment and later for a similarly loose, straight-hanging dress. [Source: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/chemise)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 chemise 是整体借入的名词词基，复数为 chemises。相关词 chemisette（女式胸前装饰衬片、短衬衣）同样借自法语，其结构为 chemise + 法语指小后缀 -ette，不能简单当作英语中现造的派生词；常见复合形式为 chemise dress（直筒连衣裙）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, chemise is a borrowed noun base; its plural is chemises. The related word chemisette, meaning a decorative bodice insert or short underbodice, was also borrowed from French, where it combines chemise with the diminutive suffix -ette. It is therefore not simply a newly formed English derivative. A common compound is chemise dress.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: slip（衬裙）主要穿在裙装下面，通常更贴身；shift（直筒裙；旧时的贴身衬衣）与 chemise 在宽松直筒裙义上接近；camisole（女式吊带背心）通常只覆盖上身，而 chemise 通常延伸到臀部以下。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A slip is worn under a dress or skirt and is usually more closely fitted. A shift is close to chemise in the loose, straight-dress sense and historically also meant an undergarment. A camisole normally covers only the upper body, whereas a chemise generally extends below the hips.

senses.meaning_en: An opioid drug used to relieve pain and suppress coughing.
senses.english_definition: Codeine is a drug obtained from opium or made from morphine that is used in some medicines to reduce pain or coughing.

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自法语 codéine，该名称由希腊语 kōdeia“罂粟果荚”与化学命名后缀 -ine 构成。法国化学家皮埃尔·让·罗比凯于1832年提出这一名称，以体现该物质与鸦片的来源联系。[来源：韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/codeine)
etymology_story.en: English borrowed French codéine, formed from Greek kōdeia, meaning a poppy seed capsule, and the chemical suffix -ine. The French chemist Pierre Jean Robiquet introduced the name in 1832, reflecting the substance's connection with opium. [Source: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/codeine)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 codeine 通常作为整体化学名称使用；历史命名结构为 code-（来自希腊语“罂粟果荚”，并非英语 code“代码”）+ -ine（化学物质后缀）。该词通常不可数；常见组合为 codeine-containing（含可待因的）、codeine-based（以可待因为基础的）和 codeine phosphate（磷酸可待因），没有常用的普通英语动词或副词派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English normally treats codeine as a complete chemical name. Its historical naming structure is code-, from the Greek word for a poppy capsule, + -ine, a chemical suffix; the base is unrelated to English code. Codeine is normally uncountable. Common combinations include codeine-containing, codeine-based, and codeine phosphate. There are no common general-English verb or adverb derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: methylmorphine（甲基吗啡，更精确为 O-甲基吗啡）是可待因的化学同义名称；opioid（阿片类药物）是包含可待因等药物的上位类别；analgesic（镇痛药）按用途分类，范围更广。后两者都不是可待因这一具体物质的同义名称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Methylmorphine, more precisely O-methylmorphine, is a chemical synonym for codeine. Opioid names the broader drug class containing codeine. Analgesic names a still broader functional category of pain-relieving drugs. The latter two are related category terms, not names for the same specific substance.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 罂粟果荚 kōdeia + 化学后缀 -ine → 可待因：用来源串起药名。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Poppy capsule kōdeia + chemical ending -ine → codeine: remember the drug through its botanical source.

etymology_story.zh: 该词见于19世纪的美国英语，通常被解释为 curly（卷曲的）与 cue（辫子，queue 的变体）的组合。词义从像卷曲辫子一样的形状发展为装饰性花线，后来也用作动词。
etymology_story.en: Recorded in nineteenth-century American English, curlicue is usually explained as a combination of curly and cue, a variant of queue meaning a pigtail. The image of a curling tail developed into the meaning of an ornamental flourish, with a verb use developing later.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可分析为 curly + cue → curlicue，其中 curly 在复合词中写作 curli-；也可将全词作为一个词基掌握。词族及屈折形式：curlicues（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、curlicued（动词过去式、过去分词；也可表示有卷曲花饰的）、curlicuing（现在分词）；另有拼写变体 curlycue。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern word can be analyzed as curly + cue → curlicue, with curly appearing as curli- in the compound; it can also be learned as a single base. Family and inflected forms include curlicues, curlicued, and curlicuing; curlicued can also describe something bearing ornamental curls. Curlycue is a spelling variant.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: flourish（装饰性花笔）强调潇洒或夸张的装饰笔画；scroll（涡卷形装饰）强调卷轴状图案；curl（卷曲形状）范围最广，不一定具有装饰作用。curlicue 尤指小巧、盘绕的装饰线条。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Flourish emphasizes a showy decorative stroke; scroll suggests a rolled or spiral ornamental pattern; curl is broader and need not be decorative. Curlicue specifically suggests a small, looping ornamental line.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 curly 的卷曲和 cue 的小辫子连起来：卷起的小辫子，就是花体卷线。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a curly little pigtail: its looping outline becomes an ornamental curlicue.

etymology_story.zh: divot 来自苏格兰语，早期有 duvat、divat 等拼写，最初指用作屋顶覆盖材料等的一块草皮，更早的来源尚不确定。后来它成为高尔夫常用语，既可指削起的草皮，也可指留下的坑。

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 divot 是不可再作可靠拆分的词基，不宜硬拆成词根和词缀。相关形式：divots（复数）；divoted（带有草皮坑或小凹坑的，较少见）；divot repair tool（草皮坑修补工具，复合词组）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, divot is an unanalyzable base rather than a transparent root-and-affix formation. Related forms include divots, the less common adjective divoted, and compounds such as divot repair tool.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: turf（草皮）通常泛指地表的草及其根土；sod（草皮块）强调连草带土的一块，常用于铺草坪；dent（凹痕）指表面受压或受击形成的凹陷。divot 特别联系到被削起的草皮及其留下的坑。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Turf generally denotes the grassy surface and its rooted soil; sod often means a cut piece used for laying lawns; dent means a depression caused by pressure or impact. Divot particularly evokes displaced turf or the resulting hole.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住同一击的两个结果：飞起的一块草皮，以及地上留下的小坑，都可以叫 divot。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture one golf swing producing two things: a flying piece of turf and the little hole it leaves. Both can be a divot.

senses.sentence_zh: 他把山地拨弦琴横放在膝上，开始扫弦。

etymology_story.zh: dulcimer 的中古英语形式经法语可追溯至古意大利语 dolcimelo，其名称结合了拉丁语 dulcis（甜美的）和希腊语 melos（曲调、歌曲）的成分。原本表示甜美琴声的名称，后来也用于形制不同的阿巴拉契亚拨弦琴。
etymology_story.en: The Middle English forms of dulcimer can be traced through French to Old Italian dolcimelo, combining elements from Latin dulcis, meaning sweet, and Greek melos, meaning song or melody. The name suggesting sweet music was later also applied to the structurally different Appalachian instrument.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 dulcimer 通常作为完整词基使用，不能把词尾 -er 当作表示人的后缀。词族：dulcimers（复数）、dulcimerist（扬琴或阿巴拉契亚拨弦琴演奏者）、dulcimerists（演奏者复数）；常见复合词组有 hammered dulcimer 和 mountain dulcimer。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, dulcimer functions as a whole base; its final -er is not the suffix meaning a person who performs an action. Its family includes dulcimers, dulcimerist, and dulcimerists, with established compounds such as hammered dulcimer and mountain dulcimer.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: zither（齐特琴）是相关乐器类别名称，范围比 dulcimer 广；hammered dulcimer（击弦扬琴）明确指用小槌演奏的类型；mountain dulcimer（山地拨弦琴）明确指阿巴拉契亚有品拨弦类型。后两者用于消除 dulcimer 在具体乐器类型上的歧义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Zither names a broader related instrument category; hammered dulcimer specifies the type played with small hammers; mountain dulcimer specifies the fretted Appalachian type. The latter two terms remove ambiguity about which instrument dulcimer refers to.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住词源中的“甜美＋曲调”：dulcimer，就是奏出甜美旋律的弦乐器。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect its historical elements, sweet and melody: a dulcimer makes sweet music on strings.

pronunciation.note: 英式读音；重音见 ˈ 标记。

etymology.text: 经中古法语 engorgier 借入英语，古法语形式由 en- 与 gorge“喉咙”组成，从吞入、塞满的画面联想到胀满。

usage_note: 偏专业或正式。常见 be engorged with blood；本课讲组织或血管充血胀大，另有狼吞虎咽之义。

senses.meaning_en: to fill or swell with blood or another fluid

senses.collocation_en: engorged with blood; engorged veins
senses.collocation_zh: 充血胀大的；充血扩张的静脉

senses.meaning_en: to eat greedily or fill oneself with food
senses.english_definition: If an animal or person engorges itself, it eats a large amount until its body or stomach is very full.
senses.collocation_en: engorge itself with food; engorge themselves on a meal

etymology_story.zh: engorge 经法语 engorger 及其早期形式进入英语，由 en-（进入、使进入）和 gorge（喉咙）构成。早期的吞入、塞满之义后来扩展为组织或器官因血液等液体充盈而胀大。
etymology_story.en: Engorge entered English through French engorger and its earlier forms, built from en-, meaning in or into, and gorge, meaning throat. Early meanings involving swallowing and filling developed into the sense of bodily tissue swelling as it fills with blood or another fluid.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可分析为 en-（使进入某状态）+ gorge（吞食、塞满）→ engorge。词族：engorges、engorged、engorging、engorgement（充盈、充血肿胀）；engorged 也常作形容词。相关基础词有 gorge（大量吞食）和 gorged（吃得胀满的）。
morphology_enriched.en: A useful modern analysis is en- + gorge → engorge, meaning to cause or undergo filling. Its family includes engorges, engorged, engorging, and engorgement; engorged also commonly functions as an adjective. Related base-word forms include gorge and gorged.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: gorge（狼吞虎咽、大量进食）主要强调吃得多；swell（肿胀、膨胀）只说明体积增大，不限定原因；distend（使胀大）强调内部压力把组织撑开。engorge 更具体地强调因充满血液、液体或食物而胀满。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Gorge chiefly emphasizes eating a large amount; swell describes an increase in size without specifying the cause; distend emphasizes stretching outward under internal pressure. Engorge specifically links fullness or swelling to an accumulation of blood, fluid, or food.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: gorge 是“喉咙、吞食”：不断往里填，直到胀满，就是 engorge。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with gorge, throat or greedy eating: keep filling something until it swells, and you engorge it.

usage_note: 本课是书或章节开头的引语；另可指碑刻铭文。注意与短小机智语 epigram 区分。

etymology_story.zh: epigraph 最终源于希腊语 epigraphē（题写、铭文），来自动词 epigraphein，由 epi-（在……上）和 graphein（书写）组成。它从物体上题写的文字，发展出书籍或篇章开头引语的文学用法。
etymology_story.en: Epigraph ultimately comes from Greek epigraphē, meaning inscription, from epigraphein, formed with epi-, meaning upon, and graphein, meaning to write. From writing placed on an object, it developed the literary sense of a quotation placed at the beginning of a text.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词分析：epi-（在……上）+ -graph（书写、文字）→ epigraph。词族：epigraphs（复数）、epigraphic／epigraphical（铭文的、碑铭学的）、epigraphically（从铭文角度）、epigraphy（碑铭学；铭文研究）、epigrapher／epigraphist（碑铭学家）。这一派生词族主要围绕铭文研究展开。
morphology_enriched.en: The formation is epi-, upon, + -graph, writing → epigraph. Its family includes epigraphs, epigraphic, epigraphical, epigraphically, epigraphy, epigrapher, and epigraphist. These derivatives chiefly concern inscriptions and their scholarly study.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: quotation（引语）泛指引用的话，不限定位置或用途；motto（格言、座右铭）表达信念或指导原则，可以用作题辞；inscription（铭文、题字）强调写刻在物体上的文字。epigraph 特指篇首引语，也可指物体上的铭文。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Quotation is any cited wording, regardless of position or purpose; motto expresses a guiding belief and may serve as an epigraph; inscription emphasizes words written or carved on an object. Epigraph specifically denotes an opening quotation or, in its inscription sense, text placed on an object.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: epi- 表示“在上”，-graph 表示“写”：写在正文上方的是题辞，写在石头上的是铭文。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Epi- means upon and -graph means writing: words above the main text form an epigraph, while words on stone form an inscription.

meaning: 减轻（过错等的严重性）；为……开脱

morphology.text: ex-（加强）+ tenu-（薄、细）+ -ate（动词后缀）→ extenuate（使严重性减轻）。

etymology.text: 借自拉丁语 extenuare 的过去分词形式 extenuatus，其中 tenuis 是“薄的”。把严重性“说薄一点”来记其开脱之义。

usage_note: 正式用语，常涉及 blame、guilt 或 an offence；extenuating circumstances 是“可减轻责任的情节”。

senses.meaning_zh: 减轻过错的严重性；使行为显得较可原谅
senses.meaning_en: to make wrongdoing seem less serious or more excusable
senses.english_definition: If something extenuates a person's wrongdoing, it makes that wrongdoing seem less serious or the person less deserving of blame.
senses.collocation_en: extenuating circumstances; extenuate an offence
senses.collocation_zh: 可减轻过错的情节；减轻罪行的严重性

senses.sentence_zh: 他艰难的童年或许能解释他的行为，却不能减轻其残忍行为的严重性。

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 extenuare，意为“使变薄、削弱”，由 ex- 与 tenuis（薄的）构成。由削薄实体或削弱力量，引申为减轻过错的严重性。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin extenuare, meaning 'to make thin or weaken,' formed from ex- and tenuis, 'thin.' Physical thinning or weakening developed into the figurative idea of making wrongdoing seem less serious.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是整体借入的动词，并非由能自由组合的词素新造；可按历史词根分析为 ex-（此处起强化作用）+ tenu-（薄）+ -ate（动词结尾）。词族：extenuates（第三人称单数）、extenuated（过去式及过去分词）、extenuating（现在分词及形容词，表示可减轻过错的）、extenuation（减轻；开脱）、extenuatory（开脱性的，较少见）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, this is a borrowed verb rather than a freely productive formation; its historical elements are ex- with intensive force, tenu- 'thin,' and the verb ending -ate. Family: extenuates, extenuated, extenuating as a participle and adjective meaning 'providing grounds for reduced blame,' extenuation 'mitigation or excuse,' and the less common adjective extenuatory.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: mitigate（减轻）可指实际减轻危害或处罚；excuse（为……开脱）强调提供理由以免除责备；palliate（掩饰或缓和）常指使问题显得较轻，却未解决根本问题。extenuate 尤其强调降低对过错的严重性判断。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Mitigate can mean actually reducing harm or punishment; excuse emphasizes providing grounds for withholding blame; palliate often means making a problem seem less serious without addressing its cause. Extenuate specifically concerns judging wrongdoing as less serious or more forgivable.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: tenu-＝薄：把过错的“严重程度削薄”，就是减轻其可责性。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Tenu- means 'thin': thinning the seriousness of a wrong makes it less blameworthy.

usage_note: 正式，语气强。可用于清除入侵物种或根除弊病；另有外科切除义，本课不涉及操作说明。

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 exstirpare（连根拔除），相关过去分词为 exstirpatus，由 ex-（向外）和 stirps（树桩、根株）构成。“拔去根株”的具体动作后来引申为彻底消除，也用于局部物种灭绝和外科切除。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin exstirpare, 'to root out,' with the related past participle exstirpatus, combining ex- 'out' and stirps 'stump or rootstock.' Literal uprooting broadened into complete elimination, including local loss of species and surgical removal.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是整体借入词；历史构成为 ex-（向外）+ stirp-（根株）+ -ate（动词结尾）。拉丁语 exst- 在英语拼写中简化为 ext-，不能据此把词根误写为 tirp-。词族：extirpates、extirpated、extirpating；extirpation（根除；局部灭绝；完全切除）、extirpator（根除者）、extirpative 和 extirpatory（根除性的，较少见）。
morphology_enriched.en: This is a borrowed word in modern English; its historical structure is ex- 'out' + stirp- 'rootstock' + the verb ending -ate. Latin exst- was simplified to ext- in English spelling; tirp- is not the underlying root. Family: extirpates, extirpated, extirpating, extirpation 'eradication, local extinction, or complete surgical removal,' extirpator 'one who roots something out,' and the less common adjectives extirpative and extirpatory.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: eradicate（根除）最接近，适用范围更广；exterminate（灭绝；消灭）强调杀死生物；uproot（连根拔起）保留较鲜明的拔根画面，也可指迫使人离开家园。extirpate 语体正式，突出彻底清除；生态学中不必意味着全球灭绝。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Eradicate is the closest general synonym; exterminate emphasizes killing living things; uproot retains a vivid root-removal image and can also describe displacing people. Extirpate is formal and stresses complete removal; in ecology, it need not imply worldwide extinction.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: ex-＝向外，stirp-＝根株：连根拔出去，才算彻底清除。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Ex- means 'out' and stirp- means 'rootstock': pull out the roots to remove something completely.

etymology_story.zh: 来自古英语 forswerian，经中古英语 forsweren 演变而来，由 for- 与 swerian（发誓）构成。早期含有发假誓、违背誓言等意思，后来发展出通过郑重誓言放弃某事的含义。
etymology_story.en: The word descends from Old English forswerian through Middle English forsweren, combining for- with swerian, 'to swear.' Early meanings included swearing falsely or breaking an oath, alongside the developing sense of renouncing something by a solemn declaration.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可分析为 for-（古老前缀，此处与放弃、拒绝相关）+ swear（发誓）；不是 fore-（在前）。不规则变化：forswears、forswore（过去式）、forsworn（过去分词）、forswearing（现在分词）；较少见的 forswearer 指发誓弃绝者或发假誓者。相关词族：swear、swore、sworn、swearing、swearer（发誓者）。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern form can be analyzed as the inherited prefix for-, associated here with rejection or renunciation, plus swear; it does not contain fore- 'before.' Irregular forms: forswears, forswore, forsworn, and forswearing; the uncommon noun forswearer can denote someone who renounces something or swears falsely. Related family: swear, swore, sworn, swearing, and swearer.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: renounce（正式宣布放弃）强调公开拒绝某种权利、信念或行为；abjure（郑重弃绝）尤用于信仰或立场，语体更庄重；abstain from（戒绝；避免）强调实际不参与。forswear 突出以郑重承诺表达放弃的决心。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Renounce emphasizes formally rejecting a right, belief, or practice; abjure is especially solemn and often concerns beliefs or allegiances; abstain from emphasizes refraining in practice. Forswear highlights a serious commitment to give something up.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: swear＝发誓；forswear＝用誓言把某事从生活中划掉。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Swear an oath that crosses something out of your life: forswear it.

etymology_story.en: The word comes from the New Latin genus name Forsythia, coined in honor of the Scottish horticulturist William Forsyth. The genus name became an English common noun for shrubs belonging to that genus.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构成为 Forsyth（人名）+ -ia（用于属名等名称的拉丁化词尾），属于人名衍生词，不应强拆为有普通词义的词根。常用形式：forsythia（单数或统称）、forsythias（复数）；Forsythia 为首字母大写的科学属名，forsythia 为普通名词。
morphology_enriched.en: The formation is Forsyth, a personal name, + -ia, a Latinizing ending used in genus names and other names. It is an eponym rather than a combination of ordinary meaning-bearing roots. Common forms are forsythia and the plural forsythias; capitalized Forsythia is the scientific genus name, while lowercase forsythia is the common noun.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Golden bells is a common name for some forsythias; yellow bells can refer to forsythia regionally but also names unrelated plants; shrub is a broader category rather than a true synonym. Forsythia is the specific plant name, so these alternatives are not universally interchangeable.

etymology_story.en: The word developed from Middle English forms such as gredire, related to gredil, a cooking implement, with later spelling influenced by iron. The parallel bars of a cooking gridiron supplied the image for a marked football field and regular street layouts.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代拼写可重分析为 grid（格栅）+ iron（铁），适合助记，但不是准确的历史造词顺序：grid 本身是从 gridiron 缩略而来的。形式与组合：gridirons（复数）、gridiron football（美式或加拿大式橄榄球）、gridiron pattern（格栅状图案）；gridiron 在这些组合中通常是名词作定语。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern spelling can be reanalyzed as grid + iron for learning purposes, but this reverses the historical relationship: grid itself was shortened from gridiron. Forms and combinations include the plural gridirons, gridiron football, and gridiron pattern; in these combinations, gridiron normally functions as a noun modifier.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Grill is more usual for the cooking sense and can also denote the whole cooking appliance; football field directly names a sports ground, with the sport depending on regional context; grid broadly denotes a regular network of crossing lines. Gridiron connects these meanings through the image of a barred cooking frame.

etymology.text: 20世纪形成的新拉丁语科学术语，由 homeo- 与 stasis 组成。可想成外界变化时，身体仍努力把内部条件维持在合适范围。

usage_note: 生物学术语，常与 maintain 搭配；“稳态”是持续调节的结果，不表示身体内部完全不变。

senses.meaning_zh: 内环境稳态；通过自我调节维持的相对稳定状态
senses.meaning_en: The maintenance of relatively stable internal conditions through self-regulation.
senses.english_definition: Homeostasis is the process by which a living organism keeps its internal conditions within suitable limits despite changes inside or outside it.

senses.collocation_zh: 维持内环境稳态；葡萄糖稳态

etymology_story.zh: 美国生理学家沃尔特·坎农于20世纪20年代创造了这一术语，用来发展关于机体内部环境相对恒定的理论。它结合源自希腊语的 homeo-（相似）与 stasis（站立、状态），强调通过调节保持相对稳定。
etymology_story.en: The American physiologist Walter Cannon coined the term in the 1920s to develop the idea of a relatively constant internal environment. It combines Greek-derived homeo-, meaning 'similar,' with stasis, meaning 'standing' or 'state,' emphasizing relative stability maintained through regulation.

morphology_enriched.zh: 科学构词：homeo-（相似、相近）+ -stasis（维持某种状态）→ homeostasis（稳态）。主要词族：homeostatic（稳态的）、homeostatically（以稳态调节的方式）；名词复数为 homeostases。形容词采用 homeostat- 词干，不是直接在完整名词后加 -ic。
morphology_enriched.en: Scientific formation: homeo- ('similar') + -stasis ('maintenance of a state') → homeostasis. Principal family members are homeostatic ('relating to homeostasis') and homeostatically ('through homeostatic regulation'); the noun plural is homeostases. The adjective uses the stem homeostat-, rather than simply adding -ic to the full noun.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: equilibrium（平衡）侧重相互作用的力量或过程达到平衡；balance（均衡）是更宽泛的日常用词；stability（稳定性）强调抵抗变化的性质。homeostasis 特指依靠调节使内部条件保持在适宜范围，并不表示完全不变。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Equilibrium emphasizes balanced forces or processes; balance is a broader everyday term; stability emphasizes resistance to change. Homeostasis specifically involves regulation that keeps internal conditions within suitable limits, rather than complete absence of change.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: homeo-＝相近，stasis＝状态：外界在变，内部状态仍保持相近。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Homeo- means 'similar' and stasis means 'state': the surroundings change, but internal conditions stay similar.

senses.meaning_zh: 杂乱的混合物；缺乏条理的大杂烩
senses.meaning_en: A confused mixture of different things that do not fit together well.

etymology_story.zh: 这个词的早期形式可追溯到晚期中古英语，通常被解释为与 mash（混合物、捣成糊状）有关的变音重叠构词。德语 Mischmasch 等语言形式与它相似，但不能据此直接认定英语词借自意第绪语。
etymology_story.en: Early forms go back to late Middle English, and the word is generally explained as a vowel-changing reduplication associated with mash. Similar forms occur in German Mischmasch and elsewhere, but their resemblance does not establish a direct borrowing from Yiddish.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词可分析为 mish-（变音重叠成分）+ mash（混合物）→ mishmash；mish- 不是表示“错误”的前缀 mis-。常用复数为 mishmashes；没有常用的独立派生词族。mash、mashed、mashing 可辅助理解相关的混合意象，但不是由 mishmash 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern analysis: mish- (a vowel-changing reduplicative element) + mash ('a mixture') → mishmash; mish- is not the prefix mis- meaning 'wrongly.' The regular plural is mishmashes, and there is no common independent family of derivatives. Mash, mashed, and mashing help explain the associated mixing imagery but are not derivatives of mishmash.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hodgepodge（杂乱混合物）与 mishmash 最接近；jumble（杂乱的一堆）更突出无序堆放；medley（混合组合）通常较中性，也可指经过安排的歌曲串烧。mishmash 常带有“搭配不协调、缺乏统一性”的批评意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hodgepodge is very close in meaning; jumble emphasizes disorder; medley is usually more neutral and can describe a deliberately arranged musical selection. Mishmash often criticizes a mixture for lacking coherence or a unified style.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: mish—mash，声音也东拼西凑：东西混在一起，整体乱成一团。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Mish—mash: even the changing vowels suggest bits mixed together without a coherent pattern.

senses.meaning_zh: 夹竹桃；一种常绿、有毒、开粉红色或白色等花的灌木
senses.meaning_en: An evergreen poisonous shrub with narrow leaves and clusters of pink, white, or other colored flowers.

etymology_story.zh: 英语经中世纪拉丁语 oleander 借入此词；其更早的名称形式通常被追溯到拉丁语 lorandrum，并与希腊语 rhododendron 联系起来。词形可能受到拉丁语 olea（橄榄树）的影响，但夹竹桃并不是橄榄树。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed the word through medieval Latin oleander; earlier forms are usually traced through Latin lorandrum and connected with Greek rhododendron. Its form may have been influenced by Latin olea, meaning 'olive tree,' although the plants are distinct.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 oleander 是不可再作常规词缀拆分的植物名称，末尾 -er 不是施事后缀。复数为 oleanders；相关技术词 oleandrin（夹竹桃苷）由 oleandr-（夹竹桃词干）+ -in（化合物名称后缀）构成。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, oleander is a plant name without a productive internal affix structure; its final -er is not an agent suffix. The plural is oleanders. The related technical term oleandrin, a cardiac glycoside found in the plant, consists of oleandr- (the plant-name stem) + -in (a chemical naming suffix).

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: rose laurel（夹竹桃的传统别名）和 rosebay（夹竹桃的传统别名）都可指 oleander，但这些俗名在不同地区也可能指其他植物。Nerium oleander（夹竹桃的学名）指称最精确；日常英语通常使用 oleander。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Rose laurel and rosebay are traditional alternative names for oleander, but these common names can refer to other plants in different regions. Nerium oleander is the precise scientific name; oleander is the usual everyday English term.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 整词连画面：细长常绿叶，成簇粉白花——oleander，夹竹桃。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Attach the whole word to one image: narrow evergreen leaves and clusters of pink or white flowers—oleander.

etymology_story.zh: outrigger 于18世纪见于英语，由表示“向外”的 out 与表示装配、索具配置的 rig 所属词族构成。它以向外伸出的船用装置为核心意象，后来也用于起重机等设备的外伸支撑结构。
etymology_story.en: Outrigger is recorded in eighteenth-century English and combines out with the word family of rig, referring to fitting or equipping a structure. Its central image of projecting nautical equipment later extended to outward supports on cranes and other machinery.

morphology_enriched.zh: out（向外）+ rigger（装配者或装配装置）→ outrigger；rigger 内部为 rig + -er，添加后缀时 g 双写。常用形式为 outriggers（复数）；相关词族包括 rig（装配；索具）、rigging（索具；装配工作）、rigger（装配工；索具工），常见复合词为 outrigger canoe（舷外浮架独木舟）。
morphology_enriched.en: Out ('outward') + rigger ('a person or device associated with rigging') → outrigger. Within rigger, rig takes -er and doubles its final g. The regular plural is outriggers; related family members include rig, rigging, and rigger. A common compound is outrigger canoe.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: stabilizer（稳定装置）是更宽泛的功能名称；float（浮体）只指提供浮力的部件；sponson（舷侧浮舱或突出支撑体）通常指船体侧面的突出结构。outrigger 的关键是从主体向外伸出的支撑布局，可包括支架和浮体。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Stabilizer is a broader functional term; float names only the buoyant component; sponson usually denotes a projecting structure along a hull's side. Outrigger specifically emphasizes support extending outward from the main body and may include both a frame and a float.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: out＝向外，rig＝装配：向外架出一条“支撑臂”，让主体更稳。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Out + rig: rig a supporting arm outward to give the main structure greater stability.

meaning: 刮去旧字后重写的古抄本；重写本

usage_note: 常指旧字未完全消失的重写手稿；也可比喻保留历史层次的地方，本课讲实际抄本。

senses.meaning_zh: 重写本；擦去或刮去原有文字后重新书写、仍可辨认旧字痕迹的古抄本

etymology_story.zh: 此词经拉丁语 palimpsestus 源自希腊语 palimpsēstos，意为“再次刮过的”，由 palin（再次）和表示“刮擦”的动词构成。它原指刮去旧字后重复使用的书写材料，后来比喻新旧痕迹层层共存的事物。
etymology_story.en: The word came through Latin palimpsestus from Greek palimpsēstos, meaning 'scraped again,' formed from palin ('again') and a verb meaning 'to scrape.' It originally described reused writing material and later came to represent things in which newer layers coexist with traces of older ones.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常将 palimpsest 视为整体借入的词干，不宜把它拆成能自由组合的英语词缀。主要词族：palimpsests（复数）、palimpsestic（重写本的；具有层累痕迹的）、palimpsestuous（具有新旧层次交织特征的，文学或学术用语）；其中两个形容词分别由 palimpsest + -ic 和 palimpsest + -uous 构成。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English generally treats palimpsest as a borrowed stem rather than a combination of freely productive English elements. Principal family members are palimpsests (plural), palimpsestic ('relating to a palimpsest or layered traces'), and palimpsestuous ('characterized by interwoven earlier and later layers,' chiefly literary or academic). The adjectives use palimpsest + -ic and palimpsest + -uous respectively.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: rewritten manuscript（重写抄本）是字面义的近义解释，但不一定保留旧字；layering（层层叠加）侧重形成过程；patchwork（拼凑体）侧重不同部分的并置。palimpsest 的独特之处在于：新层覆盖旧层，而旧层仍留下可辨认的痕迹。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Rewritten manuscript approximates the literal sense but does not necessarily imply surviving earlier writing; layering emphasizes the process of accumulation; patchwork emphasizes juxtaposed pieces. Palimpsest distinctively suggests newer layers covering older ones whose traces remain detectable.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 再次刮写，却刮不尽过去：新字在上，旧痕在下。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Scrape and write again, but the past remains: new writing above, old traces below.

senses.meaning_zh: 充足；丰盛；大量（正式或文学用语）
senses.meaning_en: Abundance; a plentiful supply of something, especially in formal or literary language.
senses.english_definition: If there is a plenitude of something, there is a large amount of it, usually more than enough.
senses.collocation_en: a plenitude of resources; a plenitude of opportunities
senses.collocation_zh: 丰富的资源；大量的机会
senses.sentence_en: The region offers a plenitude of fresh ingredients throughout the year.
senses.sentence_zh: 这个地区一年四季都有丰富的新鲜食材。

senses.meaning_zh: 充盈；完整；充分发展的状态（文学用语）
senses.meaning_en: Fullness, completeness, or the state of being fully developed, especially in literary language.
senses.english_definition: The plenitude of something is its full or complete state, with nothing lacking.
senses.collocation_en: the plenitude of life; spiritual plenitude
senses.collocation_zh: 生命的充盈；精神上的充实
senses.sentence_en: Her poems celebrate the plenitude of life, from ordinary pleasures to profound love.
senses.sentence_zh: 她的诗歌赞颂生命的充盈，从日常的乐趣到深沉的爱。

etymology_story.zh: 该词在15世纪初进入英语，来自古法语 plenitude 及拉丁语 plenitudo，后者源于 plenus，意为“满的”。早期的“完整、充盈”与后来的“丰盛、充足”都保留了“满而不缺”的核心意象。[词源资料](https://www.etymonline.com/word/plenitude)
etymology_story.en: The word entered English in the early fifteenth century through Old French plenitude and Latin plenitudo, from plenus, meaning “full.” Its senses of completeness and abundance share the underlying idea of fullness with nothing lacking. [Etymology source](https://www.etymonline.com/word/plenitude)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是整体借入的名词，可辅助分析为 plen-（满）+ -itude（状态），但不是由独立英语词 plen 临时派生而成。相关同源词族包括 plenary（全体出席的；完全的）、plenum（全体会议；充气室）、plenty（大量）、plentiful（丰富的）、plentifully（丰富地）、plentifulness（丰富）、plenteous（丰盛的，文学用语）、plenteously（丰盛地）、plenteousness（丰盛），以及 replenish（补充）、replenishment（补充）、replenisher（补充者或补充物）；这些并非全部直接由 plenitude 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, this is a borrowed noun that can be analyzed for learning purposes as plen- “full” + -itude “state”; it is not productively formed from an independent English word plen. Its related historical family includes plenary, plenum, plenty, plentiful, plentifully, plentifulness, literary plenteous, plenteously, plenteousness, and replenish, replenishment, and replenisher; these are not all direct derivatives of plenitude.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: abundance（丰富、大量）最通用，强调数量充裕；profusion（大量、纷繁）突出事物涌现或分布繁多；fullness（充盈、完整）侧重状态完整，与 plenitude 的第二义更接近。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Abundance is the most general term for a plentiful quantity; profusion suggests lavish quantities or a rich scattering of things; fullness emphasizes completeness and is closest to the second sense of plenitude.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: plen- 表示“满”：容器装满是“丰盛”，生命充满是“充盈”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think “full”: a full container suggests abundance, and a full life suggests completeness.

meaning: 同时有多个配偶的；多配偶制的

pronunciation.note: 英式读音；重音见 ˈ 标记。

forms: 形容词，无复数或时态变化。
family: polygamy 多配偶制；polygamously 以多配偶方式

morphology.text: poly-（多）+ gam-（婚配）+ -ous（形容词后缀）→ polygamous（多配偶的）。

etymology.text: 由中世纪拉丁语及希腊语的同源形式借入，希腊语 polygamos 含“多次婚配”的构词成分；现代英语重点指同时有多个配偶。

usage_note: 可用于人类婚姻制度和动物配偶关系；不是先后多次结婚。

senses.meaning_zh: 同时有多个配偶的；实行多配偶制的

senses.meaning_zh: （动物）多配偶交配的

senses.english_definition: A polygamous animal mates with more than one partner during a breeding period.
senses.collocation_en: a polygamous species; a polygamous mating system
senses.collocation_zh: 实行多配偶交配的物种；多配偶交配制度

senses.sentence_zh: 在这种实行多配偶交配的物种中，一只雄性可能在一个繁殖季与多只雌性交配。

etymology_story.zh: 该词见于17世纪初，可能由 polygamy 加形容词后缀形成，也可能直接联系后期希腊语 polygamos，意为“多次结婚的”，其中 polys 表示“多”，gamos 表示“婚姻”。现代婚姻语境强调同时有多个配偶，动物学用法则指与多个伴侣交配。[词源资料](https://www.etymonline.com/word/polygamous)
etymology_story.en: Recorded in the early seventeenth century, the adjective may have been formed from polygamy or borrowed from Late Greek polygamos, meaning “often married,” combining polys “many” and gamos “marriage.” Modern marital usage emphasizes simultaneous spouses, while zoological usage concerns multiple mating partners. [Etymology source](https://www.etymonline.com/word/polygamous)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词可分析为 poly-（多）+ -gamous（具有某种婚配方式的），进一步可识别 gam-（婚配）与形容词成分 -ous。核心词族：polygamy（多配偶制）、polygamist（有多个配偶的人）、polygamous（多配偶的）、polygamously（以多配偶方式）；相关对照词包括 monogamy/monogamous（一夫一妻制／单配偶的）、polygyny/polygynous（一夫多妻制／一雄多雌的）及 polyandry/polyandrous（一妻多夫制／一雌多雄的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern analysis: poly- “many” + -gamous “having a particular marriage or mating arrangement,” with gam- “marriage or mating” and the adjectival element -ous. The core family is polygamy, polygamist, polygamous, and polygamously; related contrasts include monogamy/monogamous, polygyny/polygynous, and polyandry/polyandrous.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 多配偶语境中的相关词并非完全同义：polygynous（一夫多妻的／一雄多雌的）只指一个男性或雄性对应多个女性或雌性；polyandrous（一妻多夫的／一雌多雄的）方向相反；polyamorous（多重伴侣关系的）强调知情同意的多重恋爱关系，不必涉及婚姻。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: These related terms are not interchangeable: polygynous specifies one male with multiple female partners; polyandrous specifies one female with multiple male partners; polyamorous concerns consensual multiple romantic relationships and does not necessarily involve marriage.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: poly-＝多，gam-＝婚配：一个婚配关系网中有多个配偶。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Poly- means “many” and gam- means “marriage or mating”: connect the word with multiple spouses or mates.

meaning: 泼尼松（糖皮质激素类药物）
aliases: 泼尼松（糖皮质激素类药物）

pronunciation.note: 英式读音；重音见 ˈ 标记。

forms: 通常不可数的药物通用名。
family: prednisone-induced 泼尼松引起的；prednisolone 泼尼松龙（相关药物）

morphology.text: prednisone + -induced → prednisone-induced（由泼尼松引起的）；prednisone 是药物名，作为独立词素记忆。

etymology.text: 20世纪药物命名形成 prednisone，英语1955年已有记录；词名属于合成的药物名称。可把整个名称与药瓶标签一起记，不按普通单词硬拆。

usage_note: 药物通用名通常小写。prednisone 是泼尼松，prednisolone 是泼尼松龙，二者不能当成同一拼写。

senses.meaning_zh: 泼尼松；一种合成糖皮质激素药物
senses.meaning_en: A synthetic glucocorticoid medicine used to reduce inflammation and suppress immune activity.
senses.english_definition: Prednisone is a steroid medicine that doctors use to reduce inflammation and suppress the immune system.
senses.collocation_en: oral prednisone; a course of prednisone
senses.collocation_zh: 口服泼尼松；一个疗程的泼尼松
senses.sentence_en: Her doctor prescribed a short course of prednisone.
senses.sentence_zh: 医生给她开了一个短疗程的泼尼松。

etymology_story.zh: Prednisone 是20世纪形成的合成药物名称，英语中1955年已有记录；其名称可能结合了 pregnadiene 的部分成分与 cortisone 的词尾。它属于化学药物命名，不能按普通英语词把 pre- 解释为“在……之前”。[词源资料](https://www.etymonline.com/word/prednisone)
etymology_story.en: Prednisone is a twentieth-century coined drug name recorded in English in 1955, probably combining elements of pregnadiene with an ending taken from cortisone. It belongs to chemical nomenclature, so its opening letters should not be interpreted as the ordinary English prefix pre- meaning “before.” [Etymology source](https://www.etymonline.com/word/prednisone)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 prednisone 作为完整药名词干处理，没有常用的普通派生词族。常见复合表达包括 prednisone-induced（泼尼松引起的）、prednisone-treated（接受泼尼松治疗的）和 prednisone-containing（含泼尼松的）；prednisolone（泼尼松龙）是相关但不同的药物名称。此处采用的英式读音见[剑桥发音资料](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/pronunciation/english/prednisone)。
morphology_enriched.en: Treat prednisone as a complete drug-name base in modern English; it has no common general-purpose derivational family. Common compounds include prednisone-induced, prednisone-treated, and prednisone-containing; prednisolone names a related but distinct drug. The British pronunciation used here follows [Cambridge's pronunciation entry](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/pronunciation/english/prednisone).

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有可自由替换的常用严格同义词。corticosteroid（皮质类固醇）是较大的药物类别，glucocorticoid（糖皮质激素）是更具体的所属类别，steroid（类固醇）则范围更广且常用于日常简称；三者都不专指泼尼松。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no common exact synonym that can freely replace this drug name. Corticosteroid names a broader drug class, glucocorticoid identifies a more specific class to which it belongs, and steroid is a still broader term often used informally; none uniquely identifies prednisone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 整词对应药瓶标签：prednisone＝泼尼松＝糖皮质激素药。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use a whole-word label: prednisone → a medicine bottle → a glucocorticoid drug.

meaning: 一窝中最弱小的幼畜；发育矮小的动物

usage_note: 常见 the runt of the litter。用于人可能带侮辱意味，本课采用动物语境。

etymology_story.zh: Runt 的确切来源不明；16世纪已有指小型牛的记录，后来扩展为发育矮小的动物，也用于贬称矮小的人。“一窝中最小的幼崽”这一如今熟悉的用法在19世纪已有记录。[词源资料](https://www.etymonline.com/word/runt)
etymology_story.en: The precise origin of runt is uncertain; it was used for small cattle in the sixteenth century and later extended to undersized animals and, insultingly, small people. The now-familiar sense of the smallest young animal in a litter is recorded in the nineteenth century. [Etymology source](https://www.etymonline.com/word/runt)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代结构为单纯词 runt，不作词根加词缀拆分。词族包括复数 runts，runt + -y → runty（矮小瘦弱的），runty 去 y 加 -iness → runtiness（矮小瘦弱的状态），以及较少见的 runtish（像弱小幼畜的；矮小的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Runt is a simple modern base with no useful root-and-affix division. Its family includes the plural runts, runt + -y → runty, runty with -y replaced by -iness → runtiness, and the less common adjective runtish.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: weakling（弱者、软弱的人）强调力量或意志薄弱，不一定个子小；shrimp（小个子，非正式贬称）主要嘲笑身材矮小；undersized animal（发育偏小的动物）是较中性的描述，而 runt 常暗示在同窝或同类中尤其弱小。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Weakling emphasizes lack of physical strength or courage rather than size; shrimp is an informal insult focused on small stature; undersized animal is a more neutral description, whereas runt often singles out an especially small or weak member of a litter or group.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 想象一窝幼崽排成一排：最小、最弱的那只就是 runt。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a litter lined up together: the smallest, weakest youngster is the runt.

senses.english_definition: If you scrimp on something, you spend or provide less than is needed to make it adequate or satisfactory.
senses.collocation_en: scrimp on food; scrimp on materials
senses.collocation_zh: 在食物上过分节省；在材料上省钱省料
senses.sentence_en: The builders refused to scrimp on materials, even when costs rose.
senses.sentence_zh: 即使成本上涨，施工人员也不肯在材料上省钱省料。

etymology_story.zh: Scrimp 在17世纪先见于苏格兰语境，形容词表示“不足的”，随后出现“使不足”的动词用法，19世纪发展出“节省开支”的含义。它可能与北欧或其他日耳曼语言中表示“收缩、干瘪”的词有关，但具体来源尚不确定。[词源资料](https://www.etymonline.com/word/scrimp)
etymology_story.en: Scrimp first appeared in seventeenth-century Scots contexts as an adjective meaning “scant,” followed by a verb meaning to make insufficient; the sense of economizing developed in the nineteenth century. It may be related to Scandinavian or other Germanic words for shrinking or shriveling, although its precise origin remains uncertain. [Etymology source](https://www.etymonline.com/word/scrimp)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代常用结构为单纯动词 scrimp。屈折形式为 scrimps、scrimped、scrimping；派生词包括 scrimper（节省或吝啬的人）、scrimpy（不足的；吝啬的）、scrimpily（吝啬地；不足地）、scrimpiness（不足；吝啬）。历史及地域性的名词、形容词和副词用法不属于现代通用英语的常用词性。
morphology_enriched.en: In common modern usage, scrimp is a simple verb base. Its inflections are scrimps, scrimped, and scrimping; derivatives include scrimper, scrimpy, scrimpily, and scrimpiness. Historical and regional noun, adjective, and adverb uses are not common parts of speech in contemporary general English.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: economize（节约开支）较中性，强调控制花费；skimp（少给；草率节省）强调投入不足，容易损害质量；save（节省；储蓄）范围最广，不一定需要牺牲生活所需，而 scrimp 常带有拮据或克扣开支的意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Economize neutrally emphasizes reducing expenditure; skimp emphasizes providing too little, often at the expense of quality; save is broader and need not involve hardship, whereas scrimp often suggests financial constraint or pinching expenditure.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把开销“压缩到很小”：为攒钱而压缩就是节衣缩食，压缩过头就是少给、克扣。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture shrinking spending: doing so to build savings means economizing; shrinking it too far means providing too little.

etymology_story.zh: Scrumptious 出现于19世纪的英语口语，其确切来源尚不确定，常被解释为 sumptuous（豪华的；丰盛的）的诙谐变体。它主要用来热情地称赞食物，也可延伸表示事物令人十分喜爱。
etymology_story.en: Scrumptious appeared in nineteenth-century colloquial English; its precise origin is uncertain, but it is often explained as a playful alteration of sumptuous. It chiefly expresses enthusiastic approval of food, with an extended use for something especially delightful.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 scrumptious 作为整体词干，不拆出表示食物的 scrum。常用派生：scrumptious + -ly → scrumptiously（极其美味地）；scrumptious + -ness → scrumptiousness（极其美味的特质）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, treat scrumptious as a whole stem; scrum is not a food-related root here. The usual derivatives are scrumptious + -ly → scrumptiously and scrumptious + -ness → scrumptiousness.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Delicious（美味的）最通用；delectable（美味可口的）较正式，常带精致感；mouthwatering（令人垂涎的）强调食物使人产生食欲。Scrumptious 更口语化，赞叹语气更强。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Delicious is the general-purpose choice; delectable is more formal and often suggests refinement; mouthwatering emphasizes the appetite food arouses. Scrumptious is more conversational and enthusiastically approving.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 整词记忆：美味到让人脱口而出“太好吃了！”
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the whole word as the enthusiastic reaction: “That tastes amazing!”

etymology_story.zh: 英语从西班牙语借入 sombrero；西班牙语中的这个词泛指帽子，由 sombra（阴影；荫凉）加后缀 -ero 构成。进入英语后，它主要指与墨西哥联系紧密的宽檐高顶帽。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed sombrero from Spanish, where it is a general word for a hat, formed from sombra, meaning “shade” or “shadow,” and the suffix -ero. In English, its meaning narrowed chiefly to the wide-brimmed, high-crowned hat associated with Mexico.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 sombrero 是整体借词；普通复数为 sombreros。Sombrero-like（像墨西哥宽檐帽的）是可自由构成的组合形式，并非常用的独立派生词；西班牙语的 sombra + -ero 属于历史来源分析。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, sombrero is an unanalyzed loanword, with the regular plural sombreros. Sombrero-like is a freely formed combination rather than an established common derivative; Spanish sombra + -ero explains its historical formation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Wide-brimmed hat（宽檐帽）是范围更广的上位表达；Mexican hat（墨西哥帽）是较宽泛的描述性近义表达，具体样式不如 sombrero 明确。两者都不能在所有语境中精确替代 sombrero。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Wide-brimmed hat is a broader category; Mexican hat is a looser descriptive alternative that identifies the style less precisely. Neither expression is an exact substitute for sombrero in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Sombra 是“阴影”：宽大的帽檐给脸投下一圈阴影。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Sombra means “shade”: picture the wide brim shading your face.

morphology.text: uni-（一）+ polar（极的）→ unipolar（单极的）。

usage_note: 基本意思是“单极的”。本课句子采用国际关系中“一个主导力量”的用法；技术搭配 unipolar transistor 指单极晶体管。遇到不同领域需看具体语境。

etymology_story.zh: Unipolar 由表示“一”的 uni- 与 polar（极的）组成，最初用于描述单个极或单一极性的技术现象。后来，“只有一个极”的概念扩展到国际政治中的单一权力中心，以及精神医学中与双相障碍相区分的单相抑郁。
etymology_story.en: Unipolar combines uni-, meaning “one,” with polar and initially described technical phenomena involving a single pole or polarity. The idea later extended to one dominant center in international politics and to depression distinguished from bipolar disorder.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：uni-（一）+ polar（极的）→ unipolar；unipolar + -ity → unipolarity（单极性；单极格局）。相关词族有 pole（极）、polar（极的）、polarity（极性）；bipolar（双极的；双相的）和 multipolar（多极的）是共享 polar 的并列构词，并非由 unipolar 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: uni- “one” + polar → unipolar; unipolar + -ity → unipolarity. The related family includes pole, polar, and polarity; bipolar and multipolar are parallel formations sharing polar, rather than direct derivatives of unipolar.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Monopolar（单极的）在部分技术语境中接近，但须遵守各领域术语习惯；single-pole（单极的）常用于开关等具体器件；hegemonic（霸权的）强调支配地位，而 unipolar 在政治中强调体系只有一个主要权力中心。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Monopolar overlaps in some technical contexts, subject to each field's terminology; single-pole commonly describes specific components such as switches; hegemonic emphasizes dominance, whereas political unipolar emphasizes a system with one principal center of power.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Uni- 是“一”：一个极、一种极性，或一个主要权力中心。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Uni- means “one”: one pole, one polarity, or one principal center of power.

etymology_story.zh: Aflame 由表示状态或位置的 a- 与 flame（火焰）结合而成；这个 a- 在历史上与 on 有关。词义从实际处于燃烧状态，扩展到激情、愤怒或羞窘等仿佛火焰般强烈的状态。
etymology_story.en: Aflame combines the state- or position-marking prefix a-, historically related to on, with flame. Its literal meaning of being in flames extended to intense states such as passion, anger, or embarrassment.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：a-（处于……状态）+ flame（火焰）→ aflame。Aflame 本身没有常用的屈折变化或派生词；基础词 flame 的常见形式和相关词有 flames（火焰；燃烧）、flamed（燃烧了）、flaming（燃烧的）和 flamelike（像火焰的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: a- “in a state of” + flame → aflame. Aflame itself has no usual inflections or common derivatives; common forms and relatives of the base flame include flames, flamed, flaming, and flamelike.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Ablaze（熊熊燃烧的）常强调火势或光亮强烈；afire（着火的；激情满怀的）与 aflame 接近，也带文学色彩；burning（燃烧着的）最通用，且能自然置于名词前。Aflame 通常用于 be aflame、set aflame 等结构。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Ablaze often emphasizes strong flames or brightness; afire closely resembles aflame and also has a literary flavor; burning is more general and readily precedes a noun. Aflame typically occurs in constructions such as be aflame and set aflame.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: A- 表状态，flame 是火焰：实物着火，情绪也能像火一样燃烧。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A- marks a state and flame supplies the image: objects burn, and strong emotions burn figuratively.

etymology_story.zh: Auteur 借自法语，原意为“作者”，可经古法语追溯至拉丁语 auctor（创作者；发起者），与英语 author 同源。20世纪中叶的法国电影批评把导演视为电影的主要创作“作者”，英语由此采用了这一专门含义。
etymology_story.en: Auteur comes from the French word for “author,” ultimately from Latin auctor, meaning an originator or creator, and is cognate with English author. Mid-twentieth-century French film criticism treated the director as a film's principal creative author, giving English its specialized cinematic sense.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 auteur 是整体借词，复数为 auteurs。主要派生：auteur + -ism → auteurism（导演作者论）；auteur + -ist → auteurist（导演作者论支持者；导演作者论的）；auteuristic（具有作者型导演风格的）较少见。Author 是同源词，并非 auteur 的英语派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, auteur is an unanalyzed loanword, with the plural auteurs. Principal derivatives are auteur + -ism → auteurism and auteur + -ist → auteurist, used as a noun or adjective; auteuristic is less common. Author is a cognate, not an English derivative of auteur.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Director（导演）指执导职务，不必具有鲜明个人风格；filmmaker（电影创作者）范围更广，可包含导演、编剧或制片人；cinéaste（电影工作者；电影爱好者）带文化或专业色彩，也不必指创作风格鲜明的导演。Auteur 特别强调导演作为作品“作者”的个人印记。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Director names the directing role without implying a distinctive style; filmmaker is broader and may include a director, writer, or producer; cinéaste has a cultural or professional flavor and can also mean a film enthusiast. Auteur specifically emphasizes the director's personal imprint as the film's creative author.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 auteur 与同源的 author 相连：把电影拍出个人笔迹的“作者型导演”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect auteur with its cognate author: a director whose films carry a recognizable personal signature.

etymology_story.zh: bellman 在中古英语时期已出现，由 bell“铃”和 man“人”组成，早先指摇铃或敲铃的人，尤其是沿街报事者；后来也用于指酒店行李员。[来源：柯林斯词典](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/bellman)
etymology_story.en: Recorded in Middle English, bellman combines bell and man and originally referred to someone who rang a bell, especially a town crier; it later also became a term for a hotel luggage attendant. [Source: Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/bellman)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：bell（铃）+ man（从事某项工作的人）→ bellman（酒店行李员）。复数为 bellmen，读音仍为 /ˈbelmən/；没有常用的直接派生词。同一 bell 词素构成的相关职业名称有 bellboy（酒店行李员）、bellhop（酒店行李员）和 bellperson（不限定性别的酒店行李员），它们不是由 bellman 添加后缀形成的。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: bell + man, meaning a person performing a particular job, → bellman. The plural is bellmen, also pronounced /ˈbelmən/; there are no common direct derivatives. Related occupational compounds sharing bell include bellboy, bellhop, and the gender-neutral bellperson; these are parallel compounds rather than suffixed derivatives of bellman.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: bellhop（酒店行李员）与 bellman 在美式英语中基本同义；porter（搬运行李的服务员）范围更广，也用于车站等场所；concierge（酒店礼宾员）主要负责提供信息、安排预订及协调服务，不专指搬运行李的人。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Bellhop is essentially synonymous with bellman in American English; porter is broader and also covers luggage carriers at places such as railway stations; concierge denotes someone who chiefly provides information, makes arrangements, and coordinates guest services.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Bell + man: picture the hotel bell ringing and the luggage attendant coming to help.
