etymology_story.zh: epistolary 于17世纪进入英语，源自拉丁语 epistolaris“与书信有关的”，其基础词 epistola“书信”最终来自希腊语 epistolē。它既保留了“与书信有关”的广义，也用于描述由书信构成的叙事作品。[来源：柯林斯词典](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/us/dictionary/english/epistolary)
etymology_story.en: Epistolary entered English in the seventeenth century from Latin epistolaris, meaning relating to letters, based on epistola, ultimately from Greek epistolē. Alongside its general connection with correspondence, it describes narratives constructed from letters. [Source: Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/us/dictionary/english/epistolary)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代学习分析：epistol-（书信词干）+ -ary（表示“与……有关”的形容词后缀）→ epistolary；历史上该词是借入词。词族包括 epistle（正式或文学性的书信；《圣经》中的使徒书信）、epistolary（书信的；书信体的），以及较少见的 epistolarily（以书信方式）、epistolarity（书信体特征）和 epistolist（书信作者）。epistles 是 epistle 的复数。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern learning analysis: epistol-, the letter stem, + the relational adjective suffix -ary → epistolary; historically, the word was borrowed. Its family includes epistle, a formal or literary letter or a biblical letter; epistolary; and the less frequent epistolarily, meaning through letters, epistolarity, meaning the quality of using the letter form, and epistolist, a letter writer. Epistles is the plural of epistle.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: letter-based（以书信为基础的）是较通俗的释义表达；correspondence-based（基于通信往来的）强调交流方式；documentary（以文献材料构成或为依据的）范围更广，材料可以包括日记、报告和书信，因此不与 epistolary 完全同义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Letter-based is a plain-language equivalent; correspondence-based emphasizes the means of communication; documentary is broader, covering material such as diaries and reports as well as letters, so it is only a partial synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: epistol- 表示“书信”：一封封信既能维系友谊，也能串起小说。
mnemonic_anchor.en: The epistol- stem means letter: letters can sustain a friendship or build a novel.

etymology_story.zh: erythema 经医学拉丁语借自希腊语 erythēma“发红”，与 erythainein“使变红”和 erythros“红的”有关。它在医学中沿用这一颜色含义，专指皮肤发红的体征。[来源：Taber医学词典](https://www.tabers.com/tabersonline/view/Tabers-Dictionary/740539/0/erythema?q=blood)
etymology_story.en: Erythema was borrowed through medical Latin from Greek erythēma, meaning redness, related to erythainein, to redden, and erythros, red. Its medical use preserves this color meaning as a term for skin redness. [Source: Taber’s Medical Dictionary](https://www.tabers.com/tabersonline/view/Tabers-Dictionary/740539/0/erythema?q=blood)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中宜把 erythema 作为完整的医学名词记忆，而非自由组合的日常词。派生时常用 erythemat- 词干：erythemat- + -ous → erythematous（红斑性的），erythemat- + -ic → erythematic（红斑的）；另有 erythem- + -al → erythemal（与红斑有关或能引起红斑的）。相关形式包括 nonerythematous（无红斑的）；复数可为 erythemas 或 erythemata，但该词常作不可数名词使用。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, erythema is best learned as a whole medical noun rather than a freely assembled everyday word. Derivation commonly uses erythemat-: erythemat- + -ous → erythematous, and erythemat- + -ic → erythematic, both describing erythema; erythem- + -al → erythemal means relating to or producing erythema. Related forms include nonerythematous, without erythema. Plurals include erythemas and erythemata, although the noun is often uncountable.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: redness（发红）是最直接的通俗对应词，但适用范围不限于皮肤；flushing（潮红）通常强调短暂或突然发生的发红；rash（皮疹）可涉及丘疹、水疱等多种皮肤变化，不能与只描述发红的 erythema 等同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Redness is the closest everyday equivalent but is not limited to skin; flushing usually suggests a temporary or sudden episode of redness; rash covers a wider range of skin changes, including bumps or blisters, and is not an exact synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 erythema 与“红”相连：皮肤变红这一体征，就是记忆核心。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor erythema to red: the central image is skin showing redness.

senses.collocation_en: exegete a passage; exegete scripture

etymology_story.zh: exegete 源自希腊语 exēgētēs“解释者”，其基础动词 exēgeisthai 表示“引导说明、解释”，历史构词包含 ex-“向外”和 hēgeisthai“引导”。英语既用它指诠释者，也有把它转作及物动词、表示“诠释文本”的学术用法。[来源：美国传统词典](https://ahdictionary.com/word/search.html?q=exegete)
etymology_story.en: Exegete comes from Greek exēgētēs, an interpreter, based on exēgeisthai, to explain or interpret, historically combining ex-, out, with hēgeisthai, to lead. English uses it both for an interpreter and, through conversion, as a scholarly transitive verb meaning to interpret a text. [Source: The American Heritage Dictionary](https://ahdictionary.com/word/search.html?q=exegete)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 exegete 是借入的名词，也可零派生转为动词；不要把词尾 -e 当作能产的“人”后缀。词族使用 exeges- 和 exeget- 等相关词干：exegesis（文本诠释，复数 exegeses）、exegete（诠释者；诠释）、exegetist（诠释者）、exegetic／exegetical（诠释的）、exegetically（以诠释方式）、exegetics（诠释学或经文诠释研究）。动词变形为 exegetes、exegeted、exegeting，后两者去掉词尾不发音的 -e。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, exegete is a borrowed noun that also functions as a verb through zero derivation; final -e is not a productive suffix meaning person. The family uses related stems such as exeges- and exeget-: exegesis, plural exegeses, means textual interpretation; exegete and exegetist name interpreters; exegetic and exegetical are adjectives; exegetically is the adverb; and exegetics denotes the study or practice of interpretation. Verb forms are exegetes, exegeted, and exegeting, with silent final -e dropped before -ed and -ing.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 名词 interpreter（解释者）范围最广，也可指口译员；expositor（阐释者）强调清楚而系统地说明；commentator（评注者）强调发表评论或逐段评注。作动词时，interpret（解释）较宽泛，expound（详细阐述）强调展开说明，explicate（细致解析）最接近 exegete 对文本的深入分析。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: As nouns, interpreter is broad and can also mean an oral translator; expositor emphasizes clear, systematic explanation; commentator emphasizes commentary or annotation. As verbs, interpret is general, expound emphasizes detailed explanation, and explicate is especially close to exegete in suggesting close textual analysis.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 历史逻辑是“向外引导”：exegete 把文本里的含义引出来；既可指这个人，也可指这一动作。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think lead out: an exegete draws meaning out of a text, and to exegete is to perform that work.

etymology_story.zh: expat 是 expatriate 的非正式截短形式，20世纪中叶已有记录；expatriate 的词源涉及 ex-“向外”和拉丁语 patria“祖国”，早期有放逐含义，后来也指自愿在国外生活。截短形式沿用了这种现代侨居含义。[来源：柯林斯词典](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/expat)、[词源词典](https://www.etymonline.com/word/expatriate)
etymology_story.en: Expat is an informal clipping of expatriate recorded by the mid-twentieth century; expatriate ultimately involves ex-, out, and Latin patria, native country, and developed from meanings involving banishment to voluntary residence abroad. The shortened form carries this modern residence-abroad meaning. [Sources: Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/expat), [Online Etymology Dictionary](https://www.etymonline.com/word/expatriate)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：expatriate 截短 → expat，不宜再把 expat 拆成 ex- 加独立词 pat；复数为 expats。主要词族有 expatriate（n. 侨居者；adj. 侨居国外的；v. 移居国外或使离开祖国）、expatriation（移居国外；放逐；脱离本国国籍或效忠关系）、expatriated（已移居或被放逐的）和 expatriating（正在移居或使离境）。expatriation 可作 expatriate 去掉词尾 -e 后加 -ion 的学习分析；相关的对应词还有 repatriate（遣返；返回祖国）和 repatriation（遣返；归国）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: expatriate → expat by clipping; expat should not be split into ex- plus an independent word pat. Its plural is expats. The main family includes expatriate as a noun, adjective, and verb; expatriation, covering residence abroad, banishment, or withdrawal from nationality or allegiance; expatriated; and expatriating. For learning purposes, expatriation can be analyzed as expatriate minus final -e plus -ion. Related contrasting formations include repatriate, to return or send someone home, and repatriation, the corresponding process.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: expatriate（侨居者）是 expat 的完整、较正式形式；immigrant（移民）从迁入国角度描述迁入居住的人，常涉及长期定居；migrant（迁移者）范围更广，可包括国内迁移。expat 本身不表示特定签证身份，也不必然表示短期居住。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Expatriate is the full, more formal equivalent of expat; immigrant describes someone from the receiving country’s perspective and often suggests long-term settlement; migrant is broader and can include movement within a country. Expat does not itself specify a visa status or necessarily imply a short stay.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 顺着完整形式记：ex-“向外”+ patria“祖国”→ 在祖国之外生活的人；expat 是其短称。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Follow the full form: ex-, out, plus patria, homeland, suggests living outside one’s homeland; expat is the short label.

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 grātīs，是 grātiīs 的缩约形式；后者是 grātia“恩惠、感谢”的复数夺格形式，可表示“出于好意、不求报酬”。英语借入后保留了“不收费”的核心含义。
etymology_story.en: Gratis comes from Latin grātīs, a contraction of grātiīs, the ablative plural of grātia, meaning 'favor' or 'thanks,' used in the sense 'out of kindness, without reward.' English retained the central meaning 'without charge.'

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 gratis 视为不可再分的借词，不宜硬拆为英语词根和后缀；其形容词和副词形式相同，没有常用的直接派生词。gratitude（感激）、gratuity（小费、酬金）和 gratuitous（无正当理由的；无偿的）属于相关的拉丁语词源家族，并非由英语 gratis 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, gratis is an unanalyzed loanword rather than a productive combination of an English root and suffix; its adjective and adverb forms are identical, and it has no common direct derivatives. Gratitude, gratuity, and gratuitous belong to its wider Latin-derived family but are not formed directly from English gratis.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: free（免费的）最通用，也有“自由的”等其他含义；free of charge（免费地、免费的）明确强调不收费；complimentary（免费赠送的）通常指商家或主办方出于礼遇提供的物品或服务。gratis 含义明确，语气较正式。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Free is the broadest everyday equivalent but has other meanings; free of charge explicitly excludes payment; complimentary usually describes something supplied as a courtesy by a business or host. Gratis is unambiguous and somewhat formal.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“出于好意给予”到“不收钱”：gratis = 免费。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Given as a favor, with no payment expected: gratis means free.

etymology_story.zh: 由 hop“单脚跳”和 scotch 的旧义“划痕、刻线”组成，名称指在地上划出的格子间跳跃的玩法。后来转用为动词，形容像玩跳房子一样在地点或话题之间跳跃移动。
etymology_story.en: Hopscotch combines hop with scotch in its older sense 'a scratch or scored line,' referring to the marked spaces used in the game. Its later verbal use extends the game's jumping movement to travel between places or shifts between topics.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：hop（单脚跳）+ scotch（划线，旧义）→ hopscotch。这里的 scotch 不是“苏格兰的”；名词通常不可数，也可直接转作动词；动词屈折形式为 hopscotches、hopscotched、hopscotching。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: hop + scotch, using the older meaning 'a scored line,' gives hopscotch. Scotch here does not mean 'Scottish'; the usually uncountable noun also functions as a verb through conversion, with the forms hopscotches, hopscotched, and hopscotching.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 名词没有通用的精确同义词。动词近义表达中，hop 强调短距离跳跃或快速移动；skip 强调跳过中间环节；leapfrog 强调越过某人、某物或某个阶段。hopscotch 更突出接连辗转、路径不连续的移动。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: The noun has no widely used exact synonym. For the verb, hop suggests short jumps or quick moves, skip emphasizes omitting intervening steps, and leapfrog emphasizes passing over someone, something, or a stage. Hopscotch particularly suggests successive moves along a discontinuous route.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: hop“跳”＋scotch“划线”：沿着地面格子跳，也可比喻跳着换地点或话题。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hop over scored lines: first a playground game, then a way of jumping between places or topics.

senses.english_definition: If you kowtow to someone, you obey them or show them respect in a way that seems excessively submissive; literally, you kneel and touch the ground with your forehead.

senses.collocation_zh: 对权威卑躬屈膝；对某人的要求唯命是从
senses.sentence_en: She refused to kowtow to the demands of wealthy donors.
senses.sentence_zh: 她拒绝对富有捐赠者的要求唯命是从。

senses.meaning_zh: 叩头礼；卑躬屈膝的举动，使用频率低于动词
senses.meaning_en: a bow with the forehead touching the ground; an act of excessive submission, less frequent than the verb
senses.english_definition: A kowtow is an act of kneeling and touching the ground with your forehead to show respect, or, figuratively, an act of excessive submission.
senses.collocation_en: perform a kowtow; a kowtow to authority
senses.collocation_zh: 行叩头礼；向权威卑躬屈膝的举动
senses.sentence_en: The envoy was expected to perform a kowtow before the emperor.
senses.sentence_zh: 按照要求，使节应在皇帝面前行叩头礼。

etymology_story.zh: 借自汉语“叩头”，字面意为以头叩地，最初指跪下并以前额触地的礼节。英语后来将这种身体姿态引申为过度顺从或谄媚，现代比喻用法通常带有贬义。
etymology_story.en: Kowtow was borrowed from Chinese kòutóu, literally 'knock the head,' referring to kneeling and touching the ground with the forehead as a gesture of respect. English later extended the physical gesture to excessive obedience or deference, usually with a disapproving tone.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 kowtow 是整体借入的词干，不按英语词根和词缀拆分；其汉语来源可分析为“叩”＋“头”。名词和动词同形；动词形式为 kowtows、kowtowed、kowtowing，行为者名词为 kowtower；kowtowing 也可作名词，表示“卑躬屈膝的行为”。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, kowtow is a borrowed stem rather than a combination of English roots and affixes; its Chinese source consists of elements meaning 'knock' and 'head.' It functions as both noun and verb; related forms include kowtows, kowtowed, kowtowing, and the agent noun kowtower. Kowtowing can also name the behavior.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: grovel（卑躬屈膝）强调有失尊严地讨好或求饶；fawn（谄媚）强调过分热情地奉承；defer（听从、尊重）可表示合理而有礼的顺从，本身不含贬义。kowtow 强调向权势低头或过度屈从。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Grovel emphasizes humiliating attempts to please or obtain mercy; fawn emphasizes exaggerated affection or flattery; defer can describe reasonable, respectful acceptance of another person's judgment without disapproval. Kowtow stresses submission to power or excessive deference.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “叩头”的英语借词：身体上低头，进而比喻态度上过度屈从。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A head lowered to the ground becomes an image of excessive submission.

senses.phonetic: BrE 英式 /əʊˈdɒmɪtə/; AmE 美式 /oʊˈdɑːmətər/
senses.meaning_zh: 里程表；累计行驶距离计
senses.meaning_en: an instrument that records the distance a vehicle has traveled
senses.english_definition: An odometer is an instrument in a vehicle that shows the total distance the vehicle has traveled.
senses.collocation_en: an odometer reading; a digital odometer
senses.collocation_zh: 里程表读数；数字里程表
senses.sentence_en: The odometer showed that the car had traveled 80,000 kilometers.
senses.sentence_zh: 里程表显示，这辆车已经行驶了八万公里。

etymology_story.zh: 由源于希腊语的构词成分组成：hodos 意为“道路、旅程”，metron 意为“测量、尺度”。其名称体现了“测量走过的路程”这一功能，现代通常指车辆上的累计里程表。
etymology_story.en: Odometer is built from elements derived from Greek hodos, meaning 'road' or 'journey,' and metron, meaning 'measure.' Its name describes measuring distance traveled, and today it usually refers to a vehicle's cumulative distance recorder.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：odo-（道路、行程）+ -meter（测量仪器）→ odometer。相关词族包括 odometers（复数）、odometry（里程测量；机器人等设备的运动位置估算）和 odometric（里程测量的）；这些词共享 odo-，但使用不同的测量类构词成分。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: odo- ('road, travel') + -meter ('measuring instrument') gives odometer. Its family includes the plural odometers, odometry ('measurement of distance traveled,' also motion-based position estimation in robotics), and odometric ('relating to odometry'); these share odo- with different measurement-related formations.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: mileometer（里程表，英式英语）是接近的对应词；milometer 是其另一种拼写；trip meter（短程里程表）只记录某一段行程，通常可以归零，而 odometer 通常累计车辆的总行驶距离。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Mileometer is a close British English equivalent, with milometer as a spelling variant. A trip meter records a particular journey and can usually be reset, whereas an odometer normally records the vehicle's cumulative distance.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: odo-“路程”＋-meter“测量仪”：量的是走了多远。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Road or journey + measuring instrument: a recorder of how far you have traveled.

senses.phonetic: BrE 英式 /ˌɒrɪˈɡɑːmi/; AmE 美式 /ˌɔːrəˈɡɑːmi/
senses.meaning_zh: 折纸艺术；折纸
senses.meaning_en: the art of making shapes by folding paper
senses.english_definition: Origami is the art of folding paper into shapes such as animals, flowers, and decorative objects.
senses.collocation_en: origami paper; an origami crane
senses.collocation_zh: 折纸用纸；折纸鹤
senses.sentence_en: She taught the children how to make an origami crane.
senses.sentence_zh: 她教孩子们如何折纸鹤。

etymology_story.zh: 借自日语 origami（折り紙），由 ori“折叠”和 kami“纸”组成；复合时，kami 的起首辅音发生连浊，变为 gami。英语借用这一名称来指折纸艺术及其相关作品。
etymology_story.en: Origami was borrowed from Japanese origami, combining ori ('folding') and kami ('paper'); in the compound, kami becomes gami through the voicing process called rendaku. English adopted the term for the paper-folding art and its associated creations.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 origami 通常作为整体借词使用；ori + kami → origami 是其日语内部构词分析，不是英语词缀拆分。相关派生词有 origamist（折纸艺术家，词干 origam- + -ist）、origamists（复数）和较少见的 origamic（折纸的）；origami 通常为不可数名词，也可放在名词前作修饰语。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English generally treats origami as a whole loanword; ori + kami → origami describes its Japanese formation rather than English affixation. Derivatives include origamist ('a paper-folding artist,' origam- + -ist), the plural origamists, and the less common adjective origamic. Origami is usually uncountable and can also modify another noun.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: paper folding（折纸）是最接近的描述性表达，范围也可包括普通折叠操作；paper craft（纸艺）范围更广，可包含剪裁、粘贴等技法；kirigami（剪折纸）特指结合剪裁与折叠的纸艺。origami 的核心技法是折叠。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Paper folding is the closest descriptive equivalent, though it can include ordinary folding operations. Paper craft is broader and may involve cutting and gluing, while kirigami specifically combines cutting with folding. Origami centers on folding.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: ori“折”＋gami“纸”：把一张纸折出立体形状。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Ori means folding and gami means paper: one sheet becomes a shape.

senses.meaning_en: a restaurant or shop that makes and sells pizzas
senses.english_definition: A pizzeria is a restaurant or shop where pizzas are made and sold.

etymology_story.zh: 借自意大利语 pizzeria，由 pizza“披萨”和表示店铺或经营场所的 -eria 构成；英语沿用其“制作和出售披萨的场所”之义。[词源参考](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/pizzeria)
etymology_story.en: Borrowed from Italian pizzeria, formed from pizza and -eria, a suffix naming a shop or establishment; English retained the meaning of a place that makes and sells pizzas. [Etymology reference](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/pizzeria)

morphology_enriched.zh: 借词内部可分析为 pizz(a) + -eria → pizzeria，即 pizza 去掉末尾 a 后接意大利语店铺后缀；这不是英语中可自由套用的构词规则。常规复数为 pizzerias，亦见保留意大利语形式的 pizzerie；相关词有 pizza“披萨”、pizzaiolo“披萨师傅”，但它们不是从 pizzeria 派生的。[词形参考](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/pizzeria)
morphology_enriched.en: The borrowed word can be analyzed as pizz(a) + -eria → pizzeria: the final a of pizza is replaced by the Italian establishment suffix. This is not a freely productive English formation rule. The regular plural is pizzerias; Italian pizzerie also occurs. Related words include pizza and pizzaiolo, meaning a pizza maker, but neither is derived from pizzeria. [Word-form reference](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/pizzeria)

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pizza restaurant“披萨餐馆”是中性、明确的近义表达；pizza parlor“披萨店”常见于美式英语，通常带有休闲餐饮色彩；pizza shop“披萨店”更突出店铺性质，可侧重外卖。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pizza restaurant is a neutral, explicit equivalent; pizza parlor is especially associated with American English and casual dining; pizza shop emphasizes the business as a shop and may suggest a takeaway focus.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: pizza 是披萨，-eria 标记店铺：卖披萨的地方就是 pizzeria。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Pizza names the food; -eria names the establishment: a pizzeria is the place that sells it.

morphology.text: pneumococc-（肺炎球菌词干） + -al（……的） → pneumococcal（肺炎球菌的）。

etymology.text: 由新拉丁语菌名pneumococcus派生，菌名使用希腊语“肺”和“颗粒”的成分；-al把菌名变成相关的形容词。

usage_note: 医学用语，修饰 infection、vaccine 等；这里命名细菌类别，不泛指所有肺炎。

senses.meaning_zh: 肺炎球菌的；与肺炎球菌有关的；由肺炎球菌引起的
senses.meaning_en: relating to or caused by the pneumococcus bacterium
senses.english_definition: Something described as pneumococcal is related to the bacterium Streptococcus pneumoniae or is caused by it.
senses.collocation_en: pneumococcal infection; pneumococcal vaccine
senses.collocation_zh: 肺炎球菌感染；肺炎球菌疫苗
senses.sentence_en: The laboratory confirmed that the infection was pneumococcal.
senses.sentence_zh: 实验室确认，这次感染是由肺炎球菌引起的。

etymology_story.zh: 由新拉丁语菌名 pneumococcus 派生；菌名结合了源于希腊语的 pneumo-“肺”和 coccus“颗粒、球状细菌”，反映这种细菌与肺炎的联系。加上形容词后缀 -al 后，表示与该菌有关或由其引起的。[词源与词义参考](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/pneumococcus)
etymology_story.en: Derived from the New Latin bacterial name pneumococcus, combining Greek-derived elements meaning lung and grain or spherical bacterium, reflecting its association with pneumonia. The adjective suffix -al gives the meaning relating to or caused by that bacterium. [Etymology and definition reference](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/pneumococcus)

morphology_enriched.zh: pneumococc-（pneumococcus 的词干，去掉 -us）+ -al（……的）→ pneumococcal。核心词族包括 pneumococcus“肺炎球菌”、其不规则复数 pneumococci，以及 pneumococcal“肺炎球菌的”；形容词本身不变复数。pneumococcal vaccine 是名词短语，不是另一个派生词。[词形与读音参考](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/pneumococcal)
morphology_enriched.en: pneumococc-, the stem of pneumococcus after removal of -us, + -al, meaning relating to, → pneumococcal. The core family comprises pneumococcus, its irregular plural pneumococci, and the adjective pneumococcal, which has no plural inflection. Pneumococcal vaccine is a noun phrase rather than a separate derivative. [Word-form and pronunciation reference](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/pneumococcal)

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pneumococcus-related“与肺炎球菌有关的”是解释性近义表达；streptococcal“链球菌的”和 bacterial“细菌的”范围依次更广，不能准确替换 pneumococcal，因为它们不专指肺炎球菌。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pneumococcus-related is a close explanatory equivalent. Streptococcal and bacterial are progressively broader terms, not exact substitutes, because neither specifically identifies Streptococcus pneumoniae.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: pneumo- 联想到肺，cocc- 联想到球菌，-al 表示“……的”：肺炎球菌的。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think lung association + spherical bacterium + relating to: pneumococcal means relating to the pneumococcus.

etymology_story.zh: 这是现代化学名称，由 poly-“多、聚合”和 carbonate“碳酸酯”构成，名称指向聚合物链中的碳酸酯连接结构；英语中至少自1930年已有该词记录。[词源参考](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/polycarbonate)
etymology_story.en: This modern chemical name combines poly-, meaning many or polymeric, with carbonate, referring to carbonate linkages in the polymer chain. The word is recorded in English from at least 1930. [Etymology reference](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/polycarbonate)

morphology_enriched.zh: poly-（多、聚合）+ carbonate（碳酸酯）→ polycarbonate。表示材料时通常不可数，表示不同种类时可用复数 polycarbonates；PC 是常用缩写。相关基础词有 carbon“碳”、carbonate“碳酸盐；碳酸酯”、carbonic“碳酸的”，它们不是由 polycarbonate 派生的。polycarbonate sheet 中是名词作定语，不必另列形容词词性；词尾也可读 /nət/。[词性与读音参考](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/polycarbonate)
morphology_enriched.en: poly-, meaning many or polymeric, + carbonate → polycarbonate. It is usually uncountable as a material name, with polycarbonates used for different types; PC is a common abbreviation. Related base-family words include carbon, carbonate, and carbonic, but these are not derivatives of polycarbonate. In polycarbonate sheet, the noun modifies another noun rather than establishing a separate adjective entry. The ending can also be pronounced /nət/. [Part-of-speech and pronunciation reference](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/polycarbonate)

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: PC 是 polycarbonate 的常用技术缩写，在明确的材料语境中可等指；plastic“塑料”和 thermoplastic“热塑性塑料”都是上位词，后者范围较窄，但两者都不能唯一确定为聚碳酸酯。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: PC is a common technical abbreviation and can be equivalent in a clear materials context. Plastic and thermoplastic are broader category terms; thermoplastic is the narrower category, but neither uniquely identifies polycarbonate.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: poly- 表示聚合，carbonate 表示碳酸酯：用碳酸酯结构串起的聚合物。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Poly- signals a polymer; carbonate names its characteristic linkage: picture a chain containing carbonate connections.

etymology_story.zh: 得名于墨西哥尤卡坦半岛的港口 Sisal，相关纤维曾经由该港出口；英语中的 sisal 是 Sisal hemp 或 Sisal grass 的缩略形式，后来也用来指产纤维的植物。[词源与词义参考](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/sisal)
etymology_story.en: Named after Sisal, a port on Mexico’s Yucatán Peninsula through which the fibre was exported. English sisal is shortened from Sisal hemp or Sisal grass and also names the plant that produces the fibre. [Etymology and definition reference](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/sisal)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是不可再拆分的简单词，没有可可靠分析的英语词根与词缀。纤维义通常不可数，指单株或种类时可用复数 sisals；常见复合表达有 sisal fibre“剑麻纤维”、sisal rope“剑麻绳”、sisal-based“以剑麻为基础的”。没有常用的独立动词或副词派生形式；名词作定语不另立形容词词性。美式英语中另有 /ˈsɪsəl/ 的读法。[词性与读音参考](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/sisal)
morphology_enriched.en: Sisal is a simple word in modern English, with no reliable division into English roots and affixes. The fibre sense is usually uncountable; sisals can denote individual plants or types. Common compound expressions include sisal fibre, sisal rope, and sisal-based. There are no common independent verb or adverb derivatives, and attributive noun use does not require a separate adjective entry. American English also permits /ˈsɪsəl/. [Part-of-speech and pronunciation reference](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/sisal)

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sisal hemp“剑麻；剑麻纤维”是传统近义名称，但不表示它属于真正的大麻；agave fibre“龙舌兰属植物纤维”范围更广；natural fibre“天然纤维”范围更广，还包括棉、羊毛等。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sisal hemp is a traditional equivalent, although sisal is not true hemp. Agave fibre is broader because it includes fibres from other agaves; natural fibre is broader still and includes materials such as cotton and wool.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 港口名变材料名：从 Sisal 港出去的坚韧纤维，就叫 sisal。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A port became a material name: remember tough fibre shipped through Sisal.

etymology_story.zh: 19世纪上半叶已有记录，可能与苏格兰英语 smitch“一点、微量”有关，但具体起源并不完全确定。它后来成为可修饰实物数量和抽象程度的口语名词，如“一点盐”或“一丝希望”。[词源参考](https://www.etymonline.com/word/smidgen)
etymology_story.en: Recorded in the first half of the nineteenth century, smidgen probably relates to Scots smitch, meaning a tiny amount, although its precise origin remains uncertain. It became an informal noun applicable to both physical quantities and abstract amounts, such as salt or hope. [Etymology reference](https://www.etymonline.com/word/smidgen)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常作为整体词处理，不宜硬拆成具有明确生产力的词根与后缀。复数为 smidgens；变体拼写有 smidgin、smidgeon；smidge 是其缩略形式，没有常用的动词或形容词派生词。a smidgen 在 a smidgen better“好一点点”等表达中作程度状语，不因此把单词 smidgen 另列为常用副词。[词族参考](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/smidgen)
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English generally treats smidgen as a whole word rather than a productive combination of root and suffix. Its plural is smidgens; spelling variants include smidgin and smidgeon, and smidge is a shortened form. There are no common verb or adjective derivatives. The phrase a smidgen functions adverbially in expressions such as a smidgen better, without making smidgen itself a separate common adverb. [Word-family reference](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/smidgen)

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: smidge“一点点”与 smidgen 几乎同义，同属非正式用语；pinch“一撮”尤其常用于盐、香料等可用指尖捏取的东西；trace“微量；一丝”强调极微弱或仅可察觉的存在，语体更中性。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Smidge is an almost exact informal equivalent; pinch especially suggests an amount of salt, spice, or another substance held between the fingertips; trace emphasizes a barely perceptible presence and is more neutral in register.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture the tiny amount of salt left on a fingertip: a smidgen is only the smallest bit.

senses.meaning_zh: 同时发生；同步性

etymology_story.zh: 该词由 synchronic 加 -ity 构成，其希腊语词源包含 syn-（共同）和 khronos（时间）。它既可表示事件同时发生，也因荣格的心理学理论而获得“没有明显因果联系却似乎富有意义的巧合”这一专门含义。
etymology_story.en: The word was formed from synchronic and -ity, ultimately drawing on Greek syn-, meaning 'together,' and khronos, meaning 'time.' Alongside its sense of simultaneous occurrence, it acquired a specialized sense through Jung's psychological theory of apparently meaningful coincidences without an evident causal connection.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：synchronic（共时的）+ -ity（性质、状态）→ synchronicity。相关词族：synchronic（共时的）、synchronically（从共时角度）、synchrony（同步；共时状态）、synchronous（同步的）、synchronously（同步地）、synchronize / synchronise（使同步）、synchronization / synchronisation（同步化）、synchronizer / synchroniser（同步装置）；这些词共享词源，并非都直接由 synchronicity 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: synchronic + -ity, a suffix forming nouns of quality or state, → synchronicity. The related family includes synchronic, synchronically, synchrony, synchronous, synchronously, synchronize/synchronise, synchronization/synchronisation, and synchronizer/synchroniser; these share an origin rather than all deriving directly from synchronicity.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: simultaneity（同时性）只强调发生时间相同；synchronization（同步化）强调使过程协调一致的行为或结果；coincidence（巧合）强调事件偶然重合，而 synchronicity 在荣格语境中还包含当事人感受到的意义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Simultaneity emphasizes occurrence at the same time; synchronization emphasizes the process or result of coordinating timing; coincidence emphasizes chance concurrence, while synchronicity in Jungian usage also involves perceived meaning.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: syn-＝共同，chron-＝时间：事情落在同一时间；若这种巧合似乎有特殊意义，就是荣格式“共时性”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Syn- means 'together' and chron- means 'time': events share a time; when their coincidence seems personally meaningful, think of Jungian synchronicity.

senses.meaning_zh: 合子；受精卵，即两个配子融合形成的细胞
senses.meaning_en: A cell formed by the fusion of two gametes during fertilization.
senses.english_definition: A zygote is the cell formed when two reproductive cells, such as a sperm and an egg, join during fertilization.

senses.collocation_zh: 受精形成的合子；合子的形成

etymology_story.zh: zygote 取自希腊语 zygōtos，意为“套在同一轭下的、结合起来的”，与 zygon（轭）同源。生物学借用“结合”的形象，为两个配子融合形成的细胞命名。
etymology_story.en: Zygote comes from Greek zygōtos, meaning 'yoked' or 'joined together,' related to zygon, 'a yoke.' Biology adopted this image of joining to name the cell produced by the fusion of two gametes.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，zygote 通常作为完整词基使用：zygote 去末尾 -e，加 -ic → zygotic（合子的），再加 -ally → zygotically（以合子方式）。相关词族包括 homozygote（纯合子）、heterozygote（杂合子）、hemizygote（半合子）、homozygous（纯合的）、heterozygous（杂合的）、hemizygous（半合的）、zygosity（合子性）、monozygotic（单卵的）、dizygotic（双卵的）、prezygotic（合子形成前的）和 postzygotic（合子形成后的）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, zygote normally functions as a whole base: zygote minus final -e + -ic → zygotic, followed by -ally → zygotically. Related family members include homozygote, heterozygote, hemizygote, homozygous, heterozygous, hemizygous, zygosity, monozygotic, dizygotic, prezygotic, and postzygotic.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: fertilized egg（受精卵）是涉及卵细胞受精时最接近的通俗对应词；embryo（胚胎）通常指随后发育的阶段，不能在所有语境中替换 zygote；gamete（配子）是融合前的生殖细胞，并非合子。这些词中后两项用于辨别相邻概念，并非严格近义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Fertilized egg is the closest everyday equivalent when fertilization involves an egg cell. Embryo usually refers to a subsequent developmental stage, whereas a gamete is a reproductive cell before fusion; these last two are neighboring concepts rather than interchangeable synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 词源中的“轭”把两者连在一起：两个配子结合，形成一个合子。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A yoke joins two things: two gametes join to form one zygote.

usage_note: 常用于批评解释或观点忽略时代背景；不等于“从未发生过的”。

senses.sentence_zh: 这篇文章忽略了冲突的殖民历史根源，因而对冲突的叙述脱离了历史背景。

senses.meaning_zh: 与特定历史时期无关的；被视为超越历史变化的
senses.meaning_en: Unconnected with a particular historical period or regarded as independent of historical change.
senses.english_definition: Something described as ahistorical is considered to exist independently of particular historical periods or changes.
senses.collocation_en: an ahistorical view of human nature; ahistorical categories
senses.collocation_zh: 认为人性超越历史变化的观点；被视为不受历史变化影响的范畴
senses.sentence_en: The theory treats human desires as ahistorical and universal.
senses.sentence_zh: 这一理论把人的欲望视为不受历史变化影响且普遍存在的。

etymology_story.zh: ahistorical 是在 historical 前加源自希腊语的否定前缀 a-（无、不）形成的英语词。historical 最终源于希腊语 historia（探究、记述）；加上否定前缀后，该词表示缺少历史视角，或被认为独立于历史。
etymology_story.en: Ahistorical was formed in English by adding the Greek-derived negative prefix a-, 'without' or 'not,' to historical. Historical ultimately traces to Greek historia, 'inquiry' or 'narrative'; the prefixed form denotes an absence of historical perspective or supposed independence from history.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：a-（不、缺少）+ historical（历史的）→ ahistorical；historical 可进一步分析为 history（历史，词干形式 histori-）+ -ical（形容词后缀）。直接派生词为 ahistorically（脱离历史背景地）、ahistoricity（非历史性）和 ahistoricism（非历史主义）；基础词族包括 history（历史）、historian（历史学家）、historic（具有历史意义的）、historical（与历史有关的）、historically（从历史上看）和 historicity（历史真实性；历史性）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: a-, 'not' or 'without,' + historical → ahistorical; historical can be further analyzed as history, with the stem histori-, + -ical. Direct derivatives include ahistorically, ahistoricity, and ahistoricism. The base family includes history, historian, historic, historical, historically, and historicity.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: unhistorical（不符合历史事实或缺乏历史依据的）更容易涉及事实或史料问题；nonhistorical（非历史的）通常中性地表示不属于历史领域；decontextualized（脱离语境的）范围更广，而 ahistorical 特别指出忽略历史背景或历史变化。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Unhistorical can suggest a lack of historical support or inconsistency with historical fact; nonhistorical usually neutrally means outside the subject of history; decontextualized is broader, while ahistorical specifically concerns neglect of historical context or change.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: a-＝没有：分析时“拿掉历史”，就是 ahistorical。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A- means 'without': take history out of the explanation, and it becomes ahistorical.

etymology.text: 借自法语appliqué“附着上的”，来自动词appliquer；再往前是拉丁语applicare“贴上、连接”。联想把小布片贴缝到大布面。

usage_note: 本课是名词；也写作 appliqué，其中 é 是法语拼写符号。本课采用英式 /əˈpliːkeɪ/，主重音在第二音节 /pliː/。

senses.meaning_zh: 贴布绣；贴花装饰；缝贴在底布上的装饰布片
senses.meaning_en: Decoration made by attaching pieces of fabric to a larger fabric surface, or the technique used to make it.

senses.collocation_en: applique work; floral applique
senses.collocation_zh: 贴布绣工艺或作品；花卉贴布装饰

senses.meaning_zh: 用贴布绣装饰；把装饰布片缝贴到……上
senses.meaning_en: To decorate fabric by attaching smaller pieces of fabric to it.
senses.english_definition: If you applique a design onto fabric, you attach pieces of fabric to it to create that design.
senses.collocation_en: applique a design onto fabric; applique flowers onto a quilt
senses.collocation_zh: 把图案贴绣到底布上；把花朵布片贴绣到被子上
senses.sentence_en: She plans to applique bright stars onto the quilt.
senses.sentence_zh: 她打算把色彩鲜艳的星形布片贴绣到被子上。

etymology_story.zh: applique 是法语借词 appliqué 的不带重音符号写法；appliqué 是 appliquer（贴上、施加）的过去分词，最终源于拉丁语 applicare（附着、连接）。英语用它指把装饰布片附着到底布上的工艺、装饰物及相应动作。
etymology_story.en: Applique is the unaccented spelling of French-derived appliqué, the past participle of appliquer, 'to apply or attach,' ultimately from Latin applicare, 'to attach or join.' English uses it for the technique, the resulting decoration, and the act of attaching decorative fabric pieces.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，applique / appliqué 通常作为完整借入词基使用，并通过名词与动词之间的零派生兼作两种词性，不宜强拆为英语前后缀。常用形式：appliques / appliqués（复数或第三人称单数）、appliqued / appliquéd（过去式、过去分词）、appliqueing / appliquéing（现在分词、动名词）；进行式常保留词干末尾的 e，而不是机械地写成 appliquing。apply（应用、施加）、application（应用）和 applicable（适用的）是同源词，并非直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, applique/appliqué is normally treated as a whole borrowed base and functions as both noun and verb through conversion. Common forms include appliques/appliqués, appliqued/appliquéd, and appliqueing/appliquéing; the participle commonly retains the base's final e rather than mechanically becoming appliquing. Apply, application, and applicable are historical relatives, not direct derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: patchwork（拼布）主要把布块拼接成整体，而 applique 把布片附着在已有底布上；embroidery（刺绣）主要用线绣出图案；ornamentation（装饰）是更宽泛的上位词。这些词是相关工艺或概括性对应词，并非处处可以互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Patchwork mainly joins fabric pieces to form a larger whole, whereas applique attaches pieces to an existing background; embroidery mainly creates designs with thread; ornamentation is a broader term for decoration. These are related techniques or broader equivalents rather than fully interchangeable synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 与 apply 的“施加、贴上”同源：把小布片贴到底布上，就是 applique。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect it with its relative apply: apply a small fabric shape to a larger fabric background.

senses.meaning_zh: 诋毁；中伤之词；损害名誉的指责或暗示
senses.meaning_en: A damaging or disparaging accusation or suggestion about someone's character or reputation.
senses.english_definition: If someone casts aspersions on a person or their motives, they make critical accusations or suggestions that damage that person's reputation.
senses.collocation_en: cast aspersions on someone's character; cast aspersions on someone's motives
senses.collocation_zh: 诋毁某人的品格；恶意质疑某人的动机

senses.sentence_zh: 他否认自己试图诋毁她的职业操守。

etymology_story.zh: aspersion 来自拉丁语 aspersio（洒、喷洒），与 aspergere（洒在……上）有关，后者由表示“向、在……上”的成分与 spargere（散播、洒）构成。英语后来把“洒上污物”的意象引申为玷污名誉，形成现代常用的“诋毁、中伤”义。
etymology_story.en: Aspersion comes from Latin aspersio, 'a sprinkling,' related to aspergere, 'to sprinkle upon,' formed from an element meaning 'upon' and spargere, 'to scatter or sprinkle.' English extended the image of spattering something to the figurative staining of a person's reputation.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代词形关系：asperse（诋毁）去末尾 -e，加 -ion → aspersion（诋毁之词），但这只是便于理解的现代对应关系；历史上 asperse 是根据 aspersion 逆向构成的。词族包括 aspersions（复数，最常用）、asperse（诋毁）、asperses（第三人称单数）、aspersed（过去式、过去分词）、aspersing（现在分词）和 asperser（诋毁者，较少见）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern form relationship: asperse minus final -e + -ion → aspersion, although this is a useful present-day analysis rather than the historical direction: asperse was back-formed from aspersion. The family includes aspersions, the usual plural form, asperse, asperses, aspersed, aspersing, and the less common agent noun asperser.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: slur（诋毁之词）通常是简短而侮辱性的言语；calumny（恶意诽谤）明确强调虚假和恶意；insinuation（影射、暗示）强调间接表达。aspersion 着重损害品格或名誉，尤其常见于 cast aspersions on（诋毁、恶意质疑）这一结构。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A slur is typically a brief insulting remark; calumny explicitly emphasizes malicious falsehood; an insinuation works through indirect suggestion. Aspersion focuses on damage to character or reputation and occurs especially in the expression cast aspersions on.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 词源是“洒上去”：把污点泼向别人的名声，就是 cast aspersions。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with 'sprinkling upon': spatter someone's reputation with verbal stains, and you cast aspersions.

etymology_story.zh: bionic 与现代术语 bionics“仿生学”同源，其构词把表示“生命”的 bio- 与仿照 electronics“电子学”形成的词尾结合起来。它起初关联对生物系统的技术模仿，后来因人造身体部件及科幻作品而广泛用于身体功能增强，并引申为“超人般的”。
etymology_story.en: Bionic belongs to the modern terminology of bionics, combining bio-, meaning “life,” with an ending modeled on electronics. Its association with technological imitation of living systems expanded through artificial body parts and science fiction to bodily enhancement and, figuratively, superhuman ability.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词关系：bionics（仿生学）→ bionic（仿生的，形容词形式）；其内部融合了 bio- 与 electronics 的词形材料，不宜机械拆成两个完整单词。主要词族：bionics（仿生学）、bionic（仿生的）、bionically（以仿生方式）；bionics 作学科名时虽以 -s 结尾，通常按单数使用。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern relationship: bionics → bionic, its corresponding adjective; the formation blends bio- with material modeled on electronics rather than simply joining two complete words. Principal family: bionics, bionic, and bionically; as the name of a discipline, bionics normally takes singular agreement despite its final -s.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: prosthetic（假体的）强调替代缺失身体部位，不一定含电子技术；biomimetic（仿生的）强调模仿生物结构或过程；cybernetic（控制论的）强调控制、通信与反馈。bionic 在日常用法中尤其容易让人想到具有机电功能的身体部件。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Prosthetic emphasizes replacing a missing body part and does not necessarily imply electronics; biomimetic emphasizes copying biological structures or processes; cybernetic concerns control, communication, and feedback. In everyday use, bionic especially suggests body parts with electronic or mechanical capabilities.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: bio- 是“生命”：让技术学会生命的本领，也让身体获得技术的帮助。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Bio- means life: technology learns life's abilities and gives the body technological help.

etymology.text: 现代英语把希腊语来源的bio-“生命”与physical“物理的”组合，用来描述生命现象中的物理过程。

usage_note: 用于研究、性质或模型，强调生物与物理的结合；不只泛指生物学。

etymology_story.zh: biophysical 由表示“生命、生物”的希腊语来源成分 bio- 与 physical“物理的”组合而成，与 biophysics“生物物理学”相对应。该词既用于以物理学研究生命系统，也用于描述环境中生物和物理要素的共同作用。
etymology_story.en: Biophysical combines bio-, ultimately from Greek words for life, with physical, and corresponds to the discipline called biophysics. It is used both for the physical study of living systems and for the combined biological and physical features of environments.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词公式：bio-（生命、生物）+ physical（物理的）→ biophysical。主要词族：biophysics（生物物理学）、biophysicist（生物物理学家）、biophysical（生物物理的）、biophysically（从生物物理角度）；biophysics 作学科名时通常按单数使用。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: bio- (life, biological) + physical → biophysical. Principal family: biophysics, biophysicist, biophysical, and biophysically; biophysics normally takes singular agreement when it names the discipline.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: physical（物理的）范围更广，不限定生命系统；physiological（生理的）强调生物体及其器官如何运作；biochemical（生物化学的）强调生命活动中的化学物质与反应。biophysical 特别突出力、能量、电学性质等物理层面。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Physical is broader and need not concern living systems; physiological emphasizes how organisms and their organs function; biochemical emphasizes chemicals and reactions in living things. Biophysical specifically highlights physical aspects such as forces, energy, and electrical properties.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: bio- 加 physical：用物理眼光看生命，或把环境中的生物与物理条件一起看。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Bio- plus physical: view life through physics, or consider an environment's living and physical features together.

usage_note: 常用 get one's comeuppance，带“咎由自取”的评价，不是中性地说任何结果。

senses.sentence_zh: 当队友们拒绝再支持他时，这个恃强凌弱的家伙终于得到了应有的报应。

etymology_story.zh: comeuppance 于19世纪见于英语，由 come up 与名词后缀 -ance 构成。它可能关联“上前接受审判或评断”的 come up，但这一具体来源并不完全确定；现代含义固定为坏行为招来的应得惩罚。
etymology_story.en: Comeuppance appeared in English in the nineteenth century, formed from come up and the noun suffix -ance. It may refer to coming up for judgment, although that particular connection is uncertain; its established meaning is a deserved adverse consequence for bad behavior.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可识别结构：come up（短语动词）+ -ance（名词后缀）→ comeuppance，拼写中 p 双写；全词的“报应”义已词汇化，不能直接由 come up 的一般含义推算。没有常用的直接派生形容词或动词；通常用单数，复数 comeuppances 可用于分别谈论多次或多人的报应。
morphology_enriched.en: Recognizable structure: come up (phrasal verb) + -ance (noun suffix) → comeuppance, with doubled p. Its meaning is lexicalized and cannot be predicted directly from the ordinary meanings of come up; it has no common directly derived adjective or verb, and the normally singular noun can take the plural comeuppances for separate instances.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: punishment（惩罚）是中性通称，不一定表示罪有应得；retribution（报应、惩罚）较正式，常带道德清算或严厉惩罚意味；just deserts（应得的下场）同样强调应得。comeuppance 较口语化，常带说话人认为“大快人心”的态度。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Punishment is a neutral general term and does not necessarily imply that it is deserved; retribution is more formal and often suggests moral reckoning or severe punishment; just deserts likewise emphasizes what someone deserves. Comeuppance is more conversational and often conveys the speaker's satisfaction.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记忆画面：坏人被叫“上前”接受评判，终于自食其果；这是助记联想，具体历史联系尚不完全确定。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a wrongdoer coming up for judgment and facing the consequences; this is a memory image, while the precise historical connection remains uncertain.

etymology_story.zh: commissary 经法语等传入英语，源于中世纪拉丁语 commissarius“受托办事的人”，与拉丁语 committere“交付、委托”有关。它先指受任官员，也曾指负责军需的官员，随后由供应职责转指供应食品的商店或餐厅。
etymology_story.en: Commissary entered English through French and related learned usage from Medieval Latin commissarius, an entrusted official, ultimately related to Latin committere, “to entrust.” From an appointed official, including one responsible for military provisions, the word developed meanings for places supplying groceries or meals.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常把 commissary 视为整体借词，不宜把 commiss- 当作可自由使用的词根；历史上可辨认 commiss-（受托）与 -ary 的构词关系。屈折变化：commissaries（复数）；相关词族包括 commissariat（军需部门；军需供应系统），以及历史同源词 commission（委任；委员会）、commissioner（专员）、commissar（政治委员），它们并非都由 commissary 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, commissary is normally treated as a whole borrowed word rather than a productive combination with a freely usable root commiss-; historically, a commiss- stem and an -ary formation can be recognized. Its plural is commissaries; related vocabulary includes commissariat and the historically related commission, commissioner, and commissar, which are not all direct derivatives of commissary.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: canteen（食堂；小卖部）可对应供餐或售货场所；exchange（军人服务商店）在美军语境中通常更侧重百货等商品，而 commissary 主要供应食品杂货；delegate（代表）对应受托人员义，不表示商店或食堂。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Canteen can denote a place providing meals or small supplies; an exchange in US military usage generally emphasizes general merchandise, whereas a commissary primarily sells groceries; delegate overlaps with the appointed-person sense and does not mean a shop or cafeteria.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“受托供应”：受托办事的是官员，供应物资的是商店，供应饭菜的是食堂。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor it to entrusted provision: an entrusted person is an official, a place providing groceries is a store, and one providing meals is a cafeteria.

senses.collocation_en: a cutaneous reaction; cutaneous lesions
senses.collocation_zh: 皮肤反应；皮肤损害
senses.sentence_en: The doctor examined the cutaneous lesions on the patient's arms.
senses.sentence_zh: 医生检查了患者手臂上的皮肤损害。

etymology_story.zh: cutaneous 源于拉丁语 cutaneus“皮肤的”，其基础是 cutis“皮肤”。它进入英语后主要保留医学和解剖学用途，表示与皮肤有关，并不只限于皮肤最外表面。
etymology_story.en: Cutaneous comes from Latin cutaneus, “of the skin,” based on cutis, “skin.” In English it has retained a mainly medical and anatomical use for things relating to the skin, without being restricted to its outermost surface.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可分析为 cutane-（皮肤，黏着词干）+ -ous（形容词后缀）→ cutaneous。主要词族及相关构词：cutaneously（经皮肤地）、subcutaneous（皮下的）、subcutaneously（皮下地）、percutaneous（经皮的）、percutaneously（经皮地）、transcutaneous（穿皮的；经皮的）、transcutaneously（经皮地）、intracutaneous（皮内的）、intracutaneously（皮内地）、mucocutaneous（黏膜与皮肤的）；cutis 是同源的医学名词，意为“皮肤”。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern analysis: cutane- (a bound stem meaning skin) + -ous (adjective suffix) → cutaneous. Principal family and related formations include cutaneously, subcutaneous, subcutaneously, percutaneous, percutaneously, transcutaneous, transcutaneously, intracutaneous, intracutaneously, and mucocutaneous; cutis is a related medical noun meaning skin.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: dermal（皮肤的；真皮的）可泛指皮肤，但在解剖学中常特指真皮；epidermal（表皮的）严格指表皮；integumentary（体被系统的）范围更广，可包括皮肤及毛发、指甲等附属结构。cutaneous 通常是“与皮肤有关”的一般医学形容词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Dermal can refer broadly to skin but often specifically means the dermis in anatomy; epidermal refers specifically to the epidermis; integumentary is broader and may include skin and associated structures such as hair and nails. Cutaneous is the general medical adjective for relating to the skin.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: cutane- 锁定“皮肤”：cutaneous 是皮肤的，subcutaneous 是皮肤下面的。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Fix cutane- to skin: cutaneous concerns the skin, and subcutaneous lies beneath it.

etymology.text: 20世纪英语材料术语，由elastic的一部分、连接元音-o-和-mer组成；-mer最终关联希腊语meros“部分”。联想能拉伸后回弹的聚合物。

usage_note: 材料科学名词，常用于 seal、gasket 等部件材料描述；不是所有塑料都属于弹性体。

senses.sentence_zh: 这个密封件由一种在低温下仍能保持柔韧性的弹性体制成。

etymology_story.zh: elastomer 是20世纪形成的材料学术语，由 elastic（有弹性的）的词干部分与表示“部分、单元”的构词成分 -mer 组合而成。-mer 最终源于希腊语 meros（部分），整个词用于命名具有橡胶般弹性的聚合物。
etymology_story.en: Elastomer was formed in the twentieth century from the stem of elastic and the combining form -mer, meaning a part or unit. The latter ultimately comes from Greek meros, meaning 'part'; the resulting term names polymers with rubber-like elasticity.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：elast-（取自 elastic，表示弹性）+ -o-（连接元音）+ -mer（聚合物名称中的构词成分）→ elastomer。主要直接派生词：elastomeric（弹性体的）、elastomerically（以弹性体的方式）；复数：elastomers。相关词族：elastic（有弹性的）、elastically（有弹性地）、elasticity（弹性）、inelastic（缺乏弹性的）、inelasticity（缺乏弹性）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: elast- (from elastic) + linking -o- + -mer (a combining form used in polymer names) → elastomer. Principal direct derivatives are elastomeric and elastomerically; the plural is elastomers. Related words include elastic, elastically, elasticity, inelastic, and inelasticity.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: elastic polymer（弹性聚合物）是解释性近义表达；rubber（橡胶）与 elastomer 大量重叠，但在具体材料分类中用法可能不同；polymer（聚合物）是上位词，许多聚合物并不具有弹性体的回弹性能。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Elastic polymer is a close explanatory equivalent. Rubber overlaps extensively with elastomer, although usage can differ in particular material classifications. Polymer is a broader term: many polymers do not have elastomeric recovery.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: elastic 的“弹性”加上 polymer 的材料联想：拉得开，也弹得回。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect elastic with polymer: a material that stretches and springs back.

senses.english_definition: If something flummoxes you, it confuses you so much that you do not know what to think or do.

senses.collocation_zh: 完全摸不着头脑；被一个问题问住

etymology_story.zh: flummox 在19世纪早期已有记录，通常被认为与英国方言中的表达有关，但确切来源尚不清楚。它带有口语和诙谐色彩，表示把人弄得糊里糊涂、无从应对。
etymology_story.en: Flummox is recorded from the early nineteenth century and is generally associated with English dialect, although its exact origin is uncertain. It developed as an informal, often humorous word for leaving someone thoroughly confused.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：flummox 是不可再作可靠词根、词缀拆分的单纯词。词形：flummoxes、flummoxed、flummoxing；flummoxed 也常作形容词，意为“困惑不解的”，flummoxing 可作形容词，意为“令人困惑的”。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: flummox is a simple base with no reliable division into smaller roots and affixes. Its inflected forms are flummoxes, flummoxed, and flummoxing. Flummoxed also commonly functions as an adjective meaning bewildered, while flummoxing can function as an adjective meaning confusing.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: confuse（使困惑）最宽泛、最中性；baffle（使难以理解）突出问题难以破解；bewilder（使茫然）强调失去头绪的状态。flummox 更口语化，常带有被突然问住或难住的诙谐意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Confuse is the broadest and most neutral term. Baffle emphasizes difficulty in understanding or solving something. Bewilder emphasizes a loss of mental direction. Flummox is more informal and often humorously suggests being caught without an answer.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 整词记场景：难题一来，脑子卡住，完全不知如何应对。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the whole word through a scene: a difficult question arrives, and your mind gets stuck.

etymology_story.zh: hake 可追溯至中古英语鱼名，通常被认为与表示“钩”的日耳曼语词有关，可能指这种鱼下颌或头部的钩状外形，但具体来源并不完全确定。这个名称也自然延伸为这种鱼供食用的鱼肉。
etymology_story.en: Hake goes back to a Middle English fish name and is usually connected with Germanic words for a hook, possibly referring to the shape of the fish's jaw or head, though the precise origin is uncertain. The name also came to denote the fish's flesh as food.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：hake 是单纯词，不能拆成具有现代构词意义的词根和词缀。指鱼时复数通常仍为 hake，也可用 hakes；指鱼肉时为不可数名词。没有常用的直接派生词；hake fillet（狗鳕鱼片）等是名词组合。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: hake is a simple word without a productive root-and-affix breakdown. As a fish name, its plural is usually hake, though hakes also occurs; as food, it is uncountable. It has no common direct derivatives; expressions such as hake fillet are noun combinations.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hake 没有适用于所有语境的常用单词近义词。cod（鳕鱼）和 whiting（牙鳕）是可比较的食用鱼名称，并非同一种鱼；white fish（白肉鱼）是包含狗鳕在内的宽泛食材类别。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hake has no common single-word synonym that works in every context. Cod and whiting name comparable food fish, but they are not the same fish. White fish is a broader culinary category that includes hake.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 hake 与 hook（钩）的可能历史联系相连：钩状鱼嘴，白嫩鱼肉。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use the possible historical link with hook: picture a hooked-looking mouth and white flesh.

etymology_story.zh: 英语 Hausa 借自当地名称 Hausa，用于称呼豪萨人及其语言。随着英语对西非民族、语言和文化的描述增多，这个名称也用于表示相关属性。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed Hausa from the local name Hausa to identify the people and their language. It also came to be used adjectivally in descriptions of their culture and other associated features.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：Hausa 是借入的专名，不能按英语词根和词缀拆分，首字母须大写。民族成员名词的复数可用 Hausa 或 Hausas；常用组合有 Hausa-speaking（说豪萨语的）和 Hausa-language（使用豪萨语的），其中 speaking 和 language 是复合词成分。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: Hausa is a borrowed proper name, not a combination of English roots and affixes, and it takes an initial capital. The noun referring to a person has the plurals Hausa and Hausas. Common compounds include Hausa-speaking and Hausa-language; speaking and language are compound elements.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有可通用于全部词义的真正近义词。Hausa language（豪萨语）明确指语言；Hausa people（豪萨人）明确指民族；Chadic language（乍得语族语言）是语言分类的上位表达，不能替代 Hausa。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no true synonym covering all its meanings. Hausa language explicitly identifies the language, while Hausa people identifies the ethnic group. Chadic language is a broader linguistic classification and cannot replace Hausa.

etymology_story.zh: inboard 由 in（里面）和 board（船舷、船侧）组成，最初用于航海，表示在船舷以内或朝船体内部。后来也用于飞机和车辆，表示靠近中心线，并可作名词指舷内发动机或装有这种发动机的船。
etymology_story.en: Inboard combines in with board in its nautical sense of a ship's side, originally indicating a position or direction inside that side. It later extended to aircraft and vehicles for positions nearer the centre line, and became a noun for an internally mounted boat engine or a boat fitted with one.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：in（向内、在内）+ board（船舷）→ inboard，可作形容词、副词和名词。名词复数为 inboards；主要相关复合词有 inboard-outboard（舷内外机式的；舷内外机装置）。outboard（舷外的；舷外发动机）是对应的反义复合词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: in (inside or inward) + board (a vessel's side) → inboard, used as an adjective, adverb, and noun. The noun plural is inboards. A principal related compound is inboard-outboard, referring to a propulsion system with an engine inside the hull and a drive unit outside it. Outboard is the corresponding opposite compound.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: inner（内侧的）只表达相对位置；internal（内部的）强调处于物体内部；inward（向内）主要表达方向。inboard 更具体，通常以船舷或船舶、飞机、车辆的中心线为参照。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Inner describes relative position, internal emphasizes being within something, and inward mainly expresses direction. Inboard is more specific: its reference point is usually a vessel's side or the centre line of a vessel, aircraft, or vehicle.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: board 在这里是“船舷”：in + board，就是舷内或朝船中心。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Here board means a ship's side: in + board puts something inside that side or towards the centre.

usage_note: 解剖和医学用语，限定纵隔部位；不等于肺部的。

etymology_story.zh: 由医学拉丁语 mediastinum（纵隔）派生，其历史词源与拉丁语表示“位于中间”的 mediastinus 及 medius（中间的）有关。这个名称体现了纵隔位于两肺之间的位置。
etymology_story.en: The adjective derives from medical Latin mediastinum, historically connected with Latin mediastinus, meaning situated in the middle, and medius, meaning middle. The name reflects the mediastinum's position between the lungs.

morphology_enriched.zh: mediastin-（mediastinum 去掉拉丁语词尾 -um 后的词干，意为“纵隔”）+ -al（……的）→ mediastinal。核心词族：mediastinum（纵隔，复数 mediastina）、mediastinal（纵隔的）、mediastinitis（纵隔炎）；相关医学构词还有 mediastinoscopy（纵隔镜检查）和 mediastinotomy（纵隔切开术）。
morphology_enriched.en: mediastin- (the stem of mediastinum after removal of Latin -um) + -al (relating to) → mediastinal. The core family includes mediastinum (plural mediastina), mediastinal, and mediastinitis (inflammation of the mediastinum); related medical formations include mediastinoscopy and mediastinotomy.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: of the mediastinum（纵隔的）是准确释义性替换；thoracic（胸部的）和 intrathoracic（胸腔内的）只是相关词，范围均比 mediastinal 大，不能在要求解剖位置精确时直接替换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Of the mediastinum is an exact paraphrase. Thoracic means relating to the chest, while intrathoracic means within the chest; both cover a wider area and cannot replace mediastinal when anatomical precision matters.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“中间”：两肺之间的中央区域是纵隔，mediastinal 就是“纵隔的”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor it to middle: the mediastinum lies between the lungs, and mediastinal means relating to that central compartment.

etymology_story.zh: 英语经意第绪语 pastrame 借入该词，其来源是罗马尼亚语 pastramă，指经过调味和保存处理的肉。英语形式的词尾通常被认为受到 salami（萨拉米香肠）的影响。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed the word through Yiddish pastrame from Romanian pastramă, referring to seasoned, preserved meat. The English ending is generally thought to have been influenced by salami.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是不可再作有效词缀拆分的借词，通常作不可数名词；没有常用的派生词族。pastrami sandwich（熏肉三明治）是名词作前置修饰语，pastrami-style（帕斯特拉米风味的）是临时构成的复合修饰语，不代表独立的常用形容词词性。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, pastrami is an unanalyzed loanword, normally used as a mass noun, with no common derivational family. In pastrami sandwich it is a noun modifier; pastrami-style is a freely formed compound modifier rather than evidence of a separate common adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有完全对应的常用英语近义词。smoked beef（烟熏牛肉）范围更广，不一定采用帕斯特拉米的腌制和调味方法；corned beef（盐腌牛肉）是相关食品，通常不经烟熏，不能视为同一种肉制品。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact common synonym. Smoked beef is broader and does not specify pastrami's curing and seasoning; corned beef is a related cured beef product that is usually not smoked, so it is not interchangeable with pastrami.

etymology_story.zh: 由 penis（阴茎）加形容词后缀 -ile 构成，属于医学和解剖学用语。Penis 来自拉丁语 pēnis，该词早期有“尾巴”的意思，后来也用于指男性生殖器。
etymology_story.en: Penile was formed from penis with the adjective suffix -ile for medical and anatomical use. Penis comes from Latin pēnis, which had the earlier meaning tail and also came to denote the male organ.

morphology_enriched.zh: pen-（在此词中代表 penis 的结合词干）+ -ile（与……有关的）→ penile；不要把 pen- 理解为英语 pen（钢笔）。核心相关词：penis（阴茎；复数 penises 或 penes）、penile（阴茎的）；专业相关构词包括 penectomy（阴茎切除术）和 penoplasty（阴茎成形术）。
morphology_enriched.en: pen- (the combining stem representing penis in this formation) + -ile (relating to) → penile; this pen- is unrelated to pen, the writing instrument. Core related forms are penis (plural penises or penes) and penile; specialist formations include penectomy and penoplasty.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: phallic（阴茎的；阴茎形象的）可涉及阴茎，但更常见于形状、象征或文化语境；genital（生殖器的）涵盖更广，不能精确限定阴茎。Penile 是直接描述阴茎组织、功能和疾病的医学形容词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Phallic can refer to the penis but often emphasizes its shape, representation, or symbolism. Genital applies to the reproductive organs more broadly. Penile is the direct medical adjective for the penis and its tissues, functions, and disorders.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 penis 与 penile 成对记：器官名变成“该器官的”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Pair penis with penile: the name of the organ becomes the adjective meaning relating to that organ.

senses.collocation_en: a simple repast; a sumptuous repast
senses.collocation_zh: 一顿简单的饭；一顿丰盛的饭
senses.sentence_en: After the walk, they enjoyed a simple repast of bread, cheese, and fruit.
senses.sentence_zh: 散步后，他们享用了一顿由面包、奶酪和水果组成的简单餐食。

etymology_story.zh: 经古法语 repast 进入英语，最终来自拉丁语 repascere（再次喂养、进食）的相关形式，其中 re- 表示“再次”，pascere 表示“喂养”。现代英语保留了“一餐、餐食”的意思，但语体比普通的 meal 更正式或更具文学色彩。
etymology_story.en: Repast entered English through Old French repast and ultimately comes from forms related to Latin repascere, to feed again, combining re- with pascere, to feed. In modern English it retains the meaning meal but has a more formal or literary tone than meal.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常把 repast 作为整体词处理，不应分析成现代前缀 re- 加英语 past（过去的）。常用形式为名词 repast 和复数 repasts；虽有历史性的动词用法及相应屈折形式，但不属于现代常用词性，也没有常用的派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English normally treats repast as a whole lexical base, not as productive re- plus English past. Its current common forms are the noun repast and plural repasts; historical verb uses and their inflections exist but are not common modern parts of speech, and there is no common derivational family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: meal（一餐）最中性、最日常；feast（盛宴）强调食物丰盛或庆祝气氛；refreshment（茶点、饮食补给）通常强调少量食物或饮料。Repast 本身只表示一餐，并不必然丰盛。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Meal is the neutral everyday term; feast suggests abundance or celebration; refreshment usually suggests light food or drink. Repast names a meal in an elevated register without necessarily implying a large amount of food.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 历史逻辑是“再次进食”，现代落点是“一餐”；联想小说里的一顿饭。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Follow the historical idea of feeding again to its modern result: a meal, especially one described in literary language.

senses.meaning_en: inflammation of the lining of the nose
senses.english_definition: Rhinitis is a condition in which the lining of your nose becomes inflamed, often causing sneezing and a runny or blocked nose.
senses.collocation_en: allergic rhinitis; nonallergic rhinitis
senses.collocation_zh: 过敏性鼻炎；非过敏性鼻炎
senses.sentence_en: She experiences allergic rhinitis during the pollen season.
senses.sentence_zh: 她在花粉季会出现过敏性鼻炎。

etymology_story.zh: 这是由希腊语来源的 rhin-（鼻，来自 rhis 的词干 rhin-）和医学后缀 -itis（炎症）构成的医学名称。其构词意义直接对应“鼻部炎症”，现代用法特指鼻腔黏膜的炎症。
etymology_story.en: This medical term combines Greek-derived rhin-, the stem of rhis meaning nose, with -itis, the medical suffix for inflammation. Its literal construction means inflammation of the nose, and modern usage specifically concerns the nasal lining.

morphology_enriched.zh: rhin-（鼻）+ -itis（炎症）→ rhinitis；后缀以元音开头，因此这里不用连接元音 -o-。相关形式有 rhinitic（鼻炎的，专业用语）；同根医学构词包括 rhinology（鼻科学）、rhinologist（鼻科专家）、rhinoplasty（鼻成形术）和 rhinosinusitis（鼻及鼻窦炎），这些是同根相关词，并非都由 rhinitis 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: rhin- (nose) + -itis (inflammation) → rhinitis; the combining vowel -o- is absent before this vowel-initial suffix. Related forms include the specialist adjective rhinitic; shared-root medical formations include rhinology, rhinologist, rhinoplasty, and rhinosinusitis, which are not all direct derivatives of rhinitis.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: nasal inflammation（鼻部炎症）是通俗释义，解剖范围不如“鼻黏膜炎症”精确；coryza（鼻卡他）偏指伴有流鼻涕的鼻黏膜炎症，常见于感冒；hay fever（花粉症、枯草热）通常指花粉等引起的过敏性鼻炎，不涵盖所有 rhinitis。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Nasal inflammation is a plain-language paraphrase but is less anatomically precise than inflammation of the nasal lining. Coryza emphasizes nasal inflammation with discharge, often in a cold; hay fever usually refers to allergic rhinitis associated with pollen or other airborne allergens, rather than every form of rhinitis.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: rhin- 是“鼻”，-itis 是“炎”：鼻 + 炎 = 鼻炎。
mnemonic_anchor.en: rhin- means nose and -itis means inflammation: nose plus inflammation gives rhinitis.

etymology_story.zh: seine 经中古英语和古英语 segne，追溯至拉丁语 sagena 和希腊语 sagēnē，原义为一种大型渔网。英语后来也把这个名词用作动词，表示用这种网捕鱼；seines 因而既可表示复数，也可表示动词第三人称单数。
etymology_story.en: Seine passed through Middle English and Old English segne from Latin sagena, ultimately from Greek sagēnē, a large fishing net. English also developed a verb from the noun, so seines can be either a plural noun or a third-person singular verb.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：seine（围网；用围网捕鱼）+ -s → seines（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）；seine 在现代英语中是不可进一步拆解的词基。核心词族：seine；seines；seined（过去式、过去分词）；seining（现在分词，也指围网捕捞）；seiner（去掉词尾不发音的 e 后加 -er，指围网渔民或围网渔船）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: seine (a fishing net; to fish with one) + -s → seines, either a plural noun or a third-person singular verb. Seine is an unanalyzable base in modern English. The core family comprises seine, seines, seined, seining (also the activity of seine fishing), and seiner (a seine fisher or fishing boat, formed by dropping silent -e before -er).

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: fishing nets（渔网）是上位词，不限定结构或用法；drag nets（拉网）强调拖拉收网，与某些 seine 用法重合；trawls（拖网）通常由船在水中拖曳，而 seines 主要通过围住鱼群并收拢来捕鱼。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Fishing nets is the broader term and does not specify construction or technique; drag nets emphasizes hauling and overlaps with some uses of seines; trawls are generally towed through the water, whereas seines principally enclose fish before being drawn together.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住一张长网“围住再收拢”：seine 是这种网，也表示这样捕鱼；加 -s 可指多张网，也可指某人这样捕鱼。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a long net enclosing fish and then closing in: seine names both the net and the action; -s marks either several nets or what one fisher does.

etymology_story.zh: stenographer 属于 stenography（速记）词族，其希腊语来源成分 stenos 意为“狭窄的”，graphein 意为“书写”。“紧缩的书写”指用简略符号记录语言，stenographer 则指从事这种记录工作的人。
etymology_story.en: Stenographer belongs to the family of stenography, whose Greek elements are stenos, meaning narrow, and graphein, meaning to write. The idea of compressed writing developed into recording speech with abbreviated signs, and stenographer names the person who does this.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：steno-（速记；历史上指紧缩）+ -grapher（从事某种书写或记录的人）→ stenographer。核心词族：stenography（速记术）、stenograph（速记机；用速记记录）、stenographer（速记员）、stenographers（复数）、stenographic／stenographical（速记的）、stenographically（以速记方式）；相关技术词有 stenotype（机器速记；速记机）和 stenotypist（机器速记员）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: steno- (shorthand, historically compression) + -grapher (a person who writes or records) → stenographer. The core family includes stenography, stenograph (a shorthand machine or the verb meaning to record in shorthand), stenographer, stenographers, stenographic or stenographical, and stenographically. Related technical formations include stenotype and stenotypist.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: shorthand writer（速记员）强调用速记系统记录讲话；court reporter（法庭记录员）强调制作正式庭审记录的职业职责，可能使用速记机或其他记录技术；transcriptionist（转写员）通常根据已有录音制作文字稿，不一定现场速记。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A shorthand writer specifically records speech in shorthand; a court reporter produces the official record of legal proceedings and may use stenographic or other recording methods; a transcriptionist typically turns an existing recording into text and need not record speech live.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: steno- 把话“压缩”，-grapher 把话“写下”：把长讲话快速压缩成记录的人。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Steno- compresses the speech; -grapher writes it down: a person who turns long speech into compact, rapid records.

usage_note: 常见 in synchrony，强调节奏或事件在时间上配合；不表示事件之间必有因果关系。

senses.meaning_zh: 同步；同时发生；多个过程在时间或节律上的协调一致

senses.english_definition: Synchrony is a state in which events happen at the same time or processes follow matching patterns of timing.

senses.meaning_en: The state or study of a language at a particular period.
senses.english_definition: In linguistics, synchrony is the consideration of a language as a system at a particular time.

etymology_story.zh: synchrony 的词源基础是希腊语 synkhronos，意为“同时的”，由 syn-（共同）和 khronos（时间）构成。它表示共同的时间关系，在语言学中又用于指某一时期的语言状态，与研究时间演变的 diachrony 相对应。
etymology_story.en: Synchrony ultimately rests on Greek synkhronos, meaning simultaneous, formed from syn- (together) and khronos (time). It expresses shared timing and also has a linguistic use for a language's state at a particular period, paired with diachrony, which concerns change through time.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：synchron-（同时、同步）+ -y（名词后缀，表示状态）→ synchrony；词源层面可识别 syn-（共同）和 chron-（时间）。核心词族：synchronous（同步的）、synchronously（同步地）、synchronize／synchronise（使同步）、synchronization／synchronisation（同步；同步化）、synchronizer／synchroniser（同步器）、synchronism（同步；同时性）、synchronic（共时的）、synchronically（共时地）；对应反义词族包括 asynchrony（异步）、asynchronous（异步的）和 asynchronously（异步地）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: synchron- (simultaneous or synchronized) + -y (a noun suffix denoting a state) → synchrony; historically, syn- means together and chron- means time. The core family includes synchronous, synchronously, synchronize or synchronise, synchronization or synchronisation, synchronizer or synchroniser, synchronism, synchronic, and synchronically. The contrasting family includes asynchrony, asynchronous, and asynchronously.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: simultaneity（同时性）侧重事件在同一时间发生；synchronization（同步化；同步）常强调使过程时间一致的操作，也可指形成的状态；coordination（协调）范围更广，只要求配合有效，不一定严格同时。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Simultaneity emphasizes events occurring at the same time; synchronization often emphasizes the act of aligning processes, though it can also name the resulting state; coordination is broader and requires effective cooperation without necessarily requiring exact timing.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: syn-＝一起，chron-＝时间：让多个过程“走在同一个时间里”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Syn- means together and chron- means time: several processes running on shared timing.

usage_note: 本课指三方参与；不把它与只有两方的 bilateral 混用。

etymology_story.zh: trilateral 由表示“三”的 tri- 和 lateral 构成，后者源自拉丁语 latus 的词干 later-，意为“边、侧面”。“三条边”的空间含义后来也用于政治和外交中的“三个参与方”。
etymology_story.en: Trilateral combines tri-, meaning three, with lateral, which comes from Latin later-, the stem of latus, meaning side. The spatial idea of three sides also developed into the political and diplomatic meaning of three participating parties.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：tri-（三）+ lateral（侧面的；一方的）→ trilateral。核心词族：trilaterally（以三方方式）、trilateralism（三边主义；三方合作原则）、trilateralist（三边主义者；三边主义的）、trilaterality（三边性；三方性，较少用）；同一构词系列包括 unilateral（单方面的）、bilateral（双边的）、quadrilateral（四边的；四边形）和 multilateral（多边的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: tri- (three) + lateral (relating to a side or party) → trilateral. The core family includes trilaterally, trilateralism, trilateralist, and the less common trilaterality. Parallel formations include unilateral, bilateral, quadrilateral, and multilateral.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: three-party（三方的）最明确地指出有三个参与方；three-way（三方的；三向的）更日常，可用于竞争、交流或安排；triangular（三角形的；三角关系的）在几何义上接近，但描述政治或人际关系时常强调三方之间的关系结构。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Three-party explicitly identifies three participants; three-way is more everyday and suits contests, communication, or arrangements; triangular is close in the geometric sense but often emphasizes the pattern of relationships when applied to politics or people.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: tri-＝三，lateral＝边：图形有三条边，谈判有三个参与方。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Tri- means three and lateral means side: three sides in a shape, or three parties at the negotiating table.

etymology.text: 英语俚语在wack后加-o形成，wack与wacky“古怪的”相连；词尾-o增加了随意、戏谑的语气。

usage_note: 口语贬称，直接称呼别人可能冒犯；本课用于识别引语里的评价，不作医学诊断。

etymology_story.zh: wacko 是与 wacky（古怪的）有关的现代英语俚语，也拼作 whacko；其具体形成过程并不完全确定。词尾 -o 带有口语和戏谑色彩，这个词既可指被认为古怪的人，也可形容其行为或想法。
etymology_story.en: Wacko is modern English slang related to wacky, meaning eccentric or strange, and is also spelled whacko; its precise formation is not entirely certain. The ending -o gives it a colloquial, sometimes mocking flavor, and the word can label a person or describe behavior and ideas.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词可作教学性分析：wack-（与 wacky“古怪的”相关的词干）+ 口语词尾 -o → wacko；这不等于已确定其全部历史构词过程。核心形式：wacko（名词、形容词）、wackos（名词复数）、whacko（异体拼写）；相关词族：wacky（古怪的）、wackier（更古怪的）、wackiest（最古怪的）、wackily（古怪地）、wackiness（古怪；滑稽）。
morphology_enriched.en: A useful modern teaching analysis is wack- (the stem associated with wacky) + colloquial -o → wacko; this does not establish its complete historical formation. Core forms are wacko (noun and adjective), wackos (plural noun), and the spelling variant whacko. Related forms include wacky, wackier, wackiest, wackily, and wackiness.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: eccentric（古怪的人；古怪的）通常较温和，甚至带欣赏意味；nutcase（疯子；怪人）是较强烈的口语贬称，与名词 wacko 接近；crazy（疯狂的；荒唐的）适用范围更广，也可表示兴奋或热衷，而 wacko 更突出离奇或不理性。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Eccentric, as a noun or adjective, is usually milder and can even be approving; nutcase is a strongly derogatory informal noun close to wacko; crazy has a wider range, including excitement or enthusiasm, while wacko more specifically suggests oddness or irrationality.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从 wacky“古怪的”联想：wacko 可指“古怪的人”，也可形容“古怪得离谱”；语气常不客气。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link it to wacky: a wacko is someone judged very strange, and a wacko idea is judged wildly odd; the tone is often unkind.

etymology.text: 中古英语借入中古荷兰语或中古低地德语的木材名称，最初指优质橡木，后来指用这种木料做的室内墙板。

usage_note: 指室内墙面的木质板饰，常在下半部；不是屋顶瓦片。

etymology_story.zh: 中古英语从中古荷兰语或中古低地德语中借入了与 wagenschot 有关的木材名称，早期指适合制作墙板的优质橡木。词义后来从木材本身转向用它制成的护壁板，并进一步产生了“安装护壁板”的动词用法。
etymology_story.en: Middle English borrowed a timber term related to Middle Dutch or Middle Low German wagenschot, originally referring to fine oak suitable for paneling. Its meaning shifted from the timber to the wall panels made from it, and it subsequently became a verb meaning to install such panels.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中把 wainscot 作为不可再按常用词缀拆分的词基；名词可零派生为动词。常用词形和派生词：wainscots；wainscoted／wainscotted；wainscoting／wainscotting，其中后两种 -ing 形式也作名词，表示护壁板或护壁板装修。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, wainscot is a base without a productive root-and-affix breakdown; the noun also becomes a verb through zero derivation. Common forms and derivatives are wainscots, wainscoted/wainscotted, and wainscoting/wainscotting; the -ing forms also function as nouns for the paneling or its installation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: wainscoting 通常与名词 wainscot 同义，在现代装修语境中更常见；paneling 泛指墙面等处的镶板，不限于墙壁下部；dado 指墙壁下段的装饰区域，可以采用木板，也可以采用其他材料。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Wainscoting is usually equivalent to the noun wainscot and is more usual in modern decorating contexts; paneling is broader and need not be confined to the lower wall; a dado is the decorated lower section of a wall and need not be wooden.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住一条演变链：优质橡木 → 墙上的木护板 → 给墙装护板。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the progression: fine oak → wooden wall panels → fitting a wall with panels.

morphology.text: 历史构词：alizari（茜草根，去末尾 i） + -ine（物质名后缀） → 法语 alizarine，英语借入后写作 alizarin。这是借词的历史形成方式；现代英语把 alizarin 作为整词记忆。

etymology.text: 英语借自法语alizarine，由alizari“茜草根”形成；名字把这种红色染料与茜草联系起来。

usage_note: 化学和染色用语，指一种化合物或染料；不是所有红颜料的统称。

senses.meaning_zh: 茜素；原从茜草根中提取、现也可人工合成的红色染料
senses.meaning_en: A red dye originally obtained from madder roots and also produced synthetically.
senses.english_definition: Alizarin is a red dye that was originally obtained from madder roots and can also be made synthetically.
senses.collocation_en: synthetic alizarin; alizarin dye

etymology_story.zh: 英语 alizarin 借自法语 alizarine，后者根据表示商品茜草根的 alizari 构成。这个名称保留了染料与茜草的历史联系，即使后来生产的茜素来自人工合成。
etymology_story.en: English alizarin was borrowed from French alizarine, formed from alizari, a name for madder roots traded for dyeing. The name preserves the dye's historical connection with madder even when the substance is produced synthetically.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常把 alizarin 作为完整的化学物质名称识记，不宜强拆成常用英语词根和词缀。alizarine 是异体拼写；相关术语有 alizarin dye（茜素染料）和 alizarin red S（茜素红 S，一种相关的染色试剂），后者指相关衍生化合物，并非原词的普通词形变化。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English generally treats alizarin as a complete chemical name rather than a productive combination of familiar English roots and affixes. Alizarine is a spelling variant; related terms include alizarin dye and alizarin red S, the latter naming a related derivative used as a stain rather than an ordinary inflected form.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: alizarine 是同一物质的异体拼写；synthetic alizarin 特指人工合成的茜素，化学物质本身相同；madder dye 指茜草来源的染料，通常含有多种色素，不能与纯茜素完全互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Alizarine is an alternative spelling for the same substance; synthetic alizarin specifies how that substance is produced; madder dye refers to dye obtained from madder and generally contains several pigments, so it is not an exact synonym for pure alizarin.

etymology_story.zh: boxwood 由植物名 box 与 wood“木材”复合而成；这里的 box 经古英语追溯至拉丁语 buxus“黄杨”。这个复合词既指黄杨木，也用于指提供这种木材的植物，后一用法在美式英语中尤其常见。
etymology_story.en: Boxwood combines the plant name box with wood; this sense of box goes back through Old English to Latin buxus, meaning the box tree. The compound denotes both the timber and the plant that produces it, with the plant sense especially common in American English.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：box（黄杨植物）＋ wood（木材）→ boxwood。木材义通常不可数，植物义可以可数，复数为 boxwoods；相关复合词有 box tree／boxtree（黄杨树）、boxwood hedge（黄杨绿篱）和 boxwood carving（黄杨木雕），没有常用的后缀派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: box, the plant, + wood → boxwood. The timber sense is normally uncountable, while the plant sense can be countable, with the plural boxwoods; related compounds include box tree/boxtree, boxwood hedge, and boxwood carving, with no common family of suffixal derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: box 在植物义上通常可与 boxwood 对应，尤其常见于英式英语；common box 专指普通黄杨这一物种，范围比 boxwood 窄；hardwood 是木材类别的上位词，不能单独表示黄杨木。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Box commonly corresponds to the plant sense of boxwood, especially in British English; common box names a particular species and is therefore narrower; hardwood is a broader timber category and does not specifically identify boxwood.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 这里 box 是“黄杨”：box ＋ wood，就是黄杨的木材，也可指黄杨植株。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Read box as the plant name: box + wood gives its timber, and the compound also names the plant.

senses.meaning_zh: 司法礼让；不同国家或司法管辖区之间对彼此法律和司法行为的适当尊重
senses.meaning_en: Respect shown by one jurisdiction toward another's laws and judicial acts.

senses.collocation_zh: 国际礼让；司法礼让

etymology_story.zh: comity 源自拉丁语 comitas“亲切、礼貌”，其基础是形容词 comis“友善的、和蔼的”。英语保留了友好礼让的基本含义，并将其用于国家和司法管辖区之间相互尊重的关系。
etymology_story.en: Comity comes from Latin comitas, meaning friendliness or courtesy, based on comis, meaning friendly or affable. English retained the general idea of courteous relations and extended it to mutual respect between states and jurisdictions.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常把 comity 作为整体词基；词尾形式与表示性质的 -ity 相似，但不存在可以自由使用的现代英语词基 com。它主要用作不可数名词，没有常用的动词、形容词或副词派生词族；comity-based（基于礼让的）是短语式复合修饰语。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English normally treats comity as a whole lexical base; although its ending resembles the quality suffix -ity, there is no freely usable modern English base com. It is mainly an uncountable noun and has no common family of derived verbs, adjectives, or adverbs; comity-based is a phrasal compound modifier.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: courtesy 强调礼貌行为或体贴；civility 强调交往中基本的文明与克制；amity 强调友好和睦的关系。comity 尤其突出群体、机构或国家之间的相互礼让，法律义不能简单用这些词替换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Courtesy emphasizes polite or considerate conduct; civility emphasizes basic politeness and restraint; amity emphasizes friendly relations. Comity particularly suggests reciprocal respect between groups, institutions, or states, and its legal sense is not freely interchangeable with these words.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“友善有礼”想到“彼此礼让”：关系越跨机构、跨国界，越容易遇到 comity。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Move from friendliness to reciprocal courtesy: comity is mutual respect across groups, institutions, or borders.

senses.meaning_zh: 使氢化；通过化学反应向物质中加入氢
senses.meaning_en: To add hydrogen to a substance through a chemical reaction.
senses.english_definition: If you hydrogenate a substance, you cause it to react with hydrogen so that hydrogen becomes part of its chemical structure.

etymology_story.zh: hydrogenate 是十九世纪由 hydrogen“氢”加动词后缀 -ate 构成的英语词，表示使物质与氢发生反应。hydrogen 本身源于表示“水”和“产生”的希腊语成分，反映了氢与氧结合生成水这一性质。
etymology_story.en: Hydrogenate was formed in nineteenth-century English from hydrogen and the verb-forming suffix -ate to describe causing a substance to react with hydrogen. Hydrogen itself uses Greek elements meaning water and producing, reflecting the formation of water when hydrogen combines with oxygen.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：hydrogen（氢）＋ -ate（形成动词，表示使发生相应变化）→ hydrogenate。常用词形为 hydrogenates、hydrogenated、hydrogenating；核心派生词有 hydrogenation（氢化）和 hydrogenator（加氢设备）；相关词族包括 dehydrogenate（使脱氢）、dehydrogenation（脱氢）及 unhydrogenated／non-hydrogenated（未经氢化的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: hydrogen + the verb-forming suffix -ate → hydrogenate. Common inflections are hydrogenates, hydrogenated, and hydrogenating; core derivatives include hydrogenation and hydrogenator, a device for hydrogenation; related family members include dehydrogenate, dehydrogenation, and unhydrogenated/non-hydrogenated.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hydrogenize 是较少见的近义动词，也表示使氢化；reduce 在化学中表示还原，范围更广，不一定涉及加入氢；harden 在油脂加工中可描述氢化带来的硬化效果，但并非所有硬化都是氢化，也并非所有氢化都会使物质变硬。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hydrogenize is a less common equivalent meaning to treat with hydrogen; reduce is broader in chemistry and does not necessarily involve adding hydrogen; harden can describe the effect of hydrogenating fats, but the two processes are not generally equivalent.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: hydrogen 是氢，-ate 把它变成动作：把氢加进分子结构。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hydrogen names the element; -ate makes it an action: add hydrogen to a molecular structure.
