fields.label: 句中目标词表示（专业辅助人员／独立执业的专业人员）
fields.wrong_reason: 这里的语境是：学校里，辅助人员在教师指导下支持教学。 因此 paraprofessional 表示“专业辅助人员”，不是“独立执业的专业人员”。

senses.meaning_zh: 专业辅助人员；受过培训的专业助理
senses.meaning_en: A trained worker who assists a qualified professional.
senses.english_definition: A paraprofessional is someone who has training to help a professional, such as a teacher, but does not have all the qualifications required for that profession.
senses.collocation_en: classroom paraprofessional; educational paraprofessional
senses.collocation_zh: 课堂教学辅助人员；教育辅助人员
senses.sentence_en: A classroom paraprofessional helps students who need extra support during lessons.
senses.sentence_zh: 课堂教学辅助人员帮助那些在上课时需要额外支持的学生。

senses.meaning_zh: 专业辅助性的；专业辅助人员的
senses.meaning_en: Relating to trained support work within a profession.
senses.english_definition: Paraprofessional work involves helping qualified professionals with tasks that require some specialist training.
senses.collocation_en: paraprofessional staff; paraprofessional training
senses.collocation_zh: 专业辅助人员；专业辅助人员培训
senses.sentence_en: The school provides paraprofessional training before the start of each academic year.
senses.sentence_zh: 学校在每个学年开始前为专业辅助人员提供培训。

etymology_story.zh: 该词在20世纪由 para-（在旁、辅助）与 professional（专业的；专业人员）组合而成，用于描述协助专业人员工作的岗位。它既可表示这类辅助工作的性质，也可直接指从事这类工作的人员。
etymology_story.en: The word was formed in the twentieth century from para-, meaning alongside or auxiliary, and professional, to describe roles supporting professional work. It functions both as an adjective describing such work and as a noun naming the worker.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：para-（辅助、在旁）+ professional（专业的；专业人员）；professional 本身可分析为 profession（职业、专业）+ -al（形容词后缀）。相关词族：paraprofessionals（复数）、paraprofessionalism（专业辅助工作的实践或职业特征）；基础词族包括 profession、professional、professionally（专业地）、professionalism（专业精神）、professionalize/professionalise（使专业化）、professionalization/professionalisation（专业化）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: para- (auxiliary or alongside) + professional; professional can itself be analyzed as profession + the adjective-forming suffix -al. Related forms include paraprofessionals and paraprofessionalism, referring to paraprofessional practice or occupational characteristics; the base family includes profession, professional, professionally, professionalism, professionalize/professionalise, and professionalization/professionalisation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: assistant（助理）范围最广，不一定受过专业培训；aide（辅助人员）强调提供实际帮助，常见于教育和照护领域；technician（技术员）强调专门技术操作，未必处于辅助专业人员的岗位。paraprofessional 尤其强调经过一定培训、协助专业人员工作的职业角色。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Assistant is the broadest term and does not necessarily imply specialist training; aide emphasizes practical support, especially in education and care; technician emphasizes technical skills and does not necessarily describe a supporting role. Paraprofessional specifically highlights a trained occupational role assisting a professional.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: para-＝在旁：站在专业人员身旁、提供专业辅助的人。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Para- means alongside: picture a trained helper working alongside a professional.

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；重音记号标在重读音节前。

forms: 复数 zeolites。
family: zeolites：复数；zeolitic：沸石的。

morphology.text: zeo-（沸腾） + -lite（石） → zeolite（沸石）。

etymology.text: 由希腊语 zein（沸腾）和 lithos（石头）组成的矿物名进入英语；加热时释放水分的现象使人想到沸腾的石头。

usage_note: 指一类具有孔隙结构的矿物及其合成材料；不要因中文有沸字就理解为熔化的石头。

senses.meaning_en: A natural or synthetic microporous crystalline aluminosilicate used for adsorption, ion exchange, or catalysis.
senses.english_definition: A zeolite is a mineral or a similar manufactured material with tiny spaces in its crystal structure that can hold water, trap molecules, or exchange ions.

etymology_story.zh: 瑞典矿物学家阿克塞尔·弗雷德里克·克龙斯泰特于1756年创造了这一矿物名称，采用希腊语 zein（沸腾）和 lithos（石头）。某些沸石受热时释放所含的水，呈现类似沸腾的现象，因此得名“沸腾的石头”。
etymology_story.en: The Swedish mineralogist Axel Fredrik Cronstedt coined the mineral name in 1756 from Greek zein, meaning to boil, and lithos, meaning stone. The name refers to the boiling-like behavior of certain zeolites as they release water when heated.

morphology_enriched.zh: 科学构词成分：zeo-（沸腾）+ -lite（石、矿物）；现代普通英语中通常把 zeolite 作为完整的矿物名称使用。词族包括 zeolites（复数）、zeolitic（沸石的）、zeolitize/zeolitise（使沸石化）、zeolitization/zeolitisation（沸石化）；常见复合表达有 zeolite catalyst（沸石催化剂）。
morphology_enriched.en: Scientific combining forms: zeo- (boiling) + -lite (stone or mineral); in ordinary modern English, zeolite is generally treated as a complete mineral name. Its family includes zeolites, zeolitic, zeolitize/zeolitise, and zeolitization/zeolitisation; a common compound expression is zeolite catalyst.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 该技术名词没有通用的严格同义词。molecular sieve（分子筛）强调按分子大小筛分的功能，部分分子筛是沸石；aluminosilicate（铝硅酸盐）是更宽泛的化学类别；ion exchanger（离子交换剂）强调交换离子的功能，也包括许多非沸石材料。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: This technical term has no general exact synonym. Molecular sieve emphasizes separation by molecular size, and some molecular sieves are zeolites; aluminosilicate names a broader chemical category; ion exchanger emphasizes ion-exchange function and also includes many non-zeolite materials.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “沸腾的石头”：受热放水，内部微孔像小房间。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A boiling stone: heating releases water from tiny rooms inside its crystal structure.

usage_note: 生物化学用语，指参与电子传递的一类含血红素蛋白；不是植物的叶绿素。

senses.meaning_zh: 细胞色素：参与电子传递或其他氧化还原反应的一类含血红素蛋白质

etymology_story.zh: 生物化学家戴维·凯林于1925年提出 cytochrome 这一名称，结合了希腊语来源的 cyto-（细胞）和 chroma（颜色）。名称突出了这些细胞内含血红素蛋白质的颜色及其特征性吸收光谱。
etymology_story.en: The biochemist David Keilin introduced the name cytochrome in 1925, combining Greek-derived cyto-, meaning cell, with chroma, meaning color. The name highlights the color and characteristic absorption spectra of these cellular haem proteins.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代科学构词：cyto-（细胞）+ -chrome（与颜色有关的成分）。相关形式包括 cytochromes（复数）、apocytochrome（脱辅基细胞色素，即尚未结合血红素的蛋白质部分）、holocytochrome（全细胞色素，即已结合血红素的完整形式）；cytochrome c（细胞色素c）和 cytochrome oxidase（细胞色素氧化酶）是命名或复合表达，并非后缀派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern scientific structure: cyto- (cell) + -chrome (a color-related element). Related forms include cytochromes, apocytochrome, the protein component without its haem group, and holocytochrome, the complete haem-containing form; cytochrome c and cytochrome oxidase are naming or compound expressions rather than suffix-derived words.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 该词没有适用于所有语境的严格同义词。haem protein/heme protein（血红素蛋白）是上位概念，也包括血红蛋白等；electron carrier（电子载体）强调电子传递功能，也包括非蛋白质分子；respiratory pigment（呼吸色素）是较宽泛的功能性称呼，不能与 cytochrome 普遍互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact synonym that works in every context. Haem protein/heme protein is a broader category that also includes proteins such as haemoglobin; electron carrier emphasizes electron transfer and includes non-protein molecules; respiratory pigment is a broader functional description and is not generally interchangeable with cytochrome.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: cyto- 细胞 + -chrome 颜色：细胞里的有色蛋白，帮助传电子、做反应。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Cell + color: a colored cellular protein that helps move electrons or drive reactions.

morphology.text: en-（使进入某状态） + amour（爱） → enamour；enamour + -ed → enamoured（倾心的）。

etymology.text: 来自古法语 enamourer（使爱上），其中 amour 表示爱；英语 enamour 的 -ed 形式又常用作形容词。

etymology_story.zh: enamour 在中古英语时期借自古法语 enamourer，意为“使爱上”，其中 amour 最终源自拉丁语 amor（爱）。其过去分词 enamoured 逐渐成为常用形容词，含义也从爱慕某人扩展到热衷某种事物或想法。
etymology_story.en: Enamour entered Middle English from Old French enamourer, meaning to make someone fall in love, with amour ultimately coming from Latin amor, love. Its past participle enamoured became an established adjective, extending from romantic attraction to enthusiasm for things or ideas.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代直接构词：enamour（使倾心）+ -ed（过去式、过去分词或形容词词尾）；词源层面可理解为 en-（使进入某状态）+ amour（爱）。英式词形包括 enamour、enamours、enamouring、enamoured；美式对应形式为 enamor、enamors、enamoring、enamored。enamoured 常用作形容词，也可以是动词 enamour 的过去式或过去分词；amour（恋情）和 amorous（多情的；表达爱意的）属于同源相关词。
morphology_enriched.en: Immediate modern structure: enamour + -ed, marking the past tense, past participle, or an adjective; historically, the structure reflects en- (put into a state) + amour (love). British forms include enamour, enamours, enamouring, and enamoured; American equivalents are enamor, enamors, enamoring, and enamored. Enamoured commonly functions as an adjective and can also be an inflected form of enamour; amour and amorous are related words sharing the same historical root.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: infatuated（迷恋的）常暗示感情强烈但缺乏理性或难以持久；smitten（一下子爱上的；深受吸引的）更强调突然产生的强烈吸引；enchanted（陶醉的；着迷的）强调因魅力或美感而欣喜，不一定涉及爱情。enamoured 可表达爱慕，也可较正式地表达对事物的热衷。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Infatuated often suggests intense but unreasoning or short-lived attraction; smitten emphasizes being suddenly and strongly attracted; enchanted emphasizes delighted fascination and need not imply romance. Enamoured can express romantic attraction or, somewhat formally, strong enthusiasm for something.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: amour＝爱；enamoured＝进入“爱上了”的状态，也可爱上一个想法。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Amour means love: enamoured means being in a state of loving someone—or loving an idea.

senses.meaning_en: An edible flatfish, especially the European species with orange spots, or its flesh.
senses.english_definition: A plaice is a flat sea fish, typically with orange spots on its upper side, that people eat; plaice also means its flesh as food.

etymology_story.zh: plaice 经古法语 plaiz、plaise 等形式进入中古英语，源自晚期拉丁语 platessa，原本就是一种比目鱼的名称。英语保留了这种鱼的名称，并进一步用它表示作为食物的鱼肉。
etymology_story.en: Plaice entered Middle English through Old French forms such as plaiz and plaise, from Late Latin platessa, a name for a flatfish. English retained the fish name and also used it for the flesh eaten as food.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是不可再作有效词缀拆分的单纯词，没有常用的前后缀派生词。指鱼时可数，复数通常仍为 plaice；指鱼肉时不可数。plaice fillet（欧鲽鱼片）等属于名词复合表达，不是派生词；plaice 在这类表达中仍是作前置修饰语的名词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, plaice is a simple word with no productive internal affix breakdown and no common affix-derived family. It is countable for the fish, with the plural usually unchanged as plaice, and uncountable for its flesh. Expressions such as plaice fillet are noun compounds, not derivatives; plaice remains a noun when used as a modifier.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有可在所有语境中替换 plaice 的严格同义词。flatfish（比目鱼、鲽形鱼）是更宽泛的类别；flounder（鲽、比目鱼）在不同地区可指多种相关鱼类，范围与 plaice 不完全重合；sole（鳎、鳎鱼）通常指另一类食用比目鱼，不能在物种名称或菜单中随意替换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact synonym that replaces plaice in every context. Flatfish is the broader category; flounder names various related flatfish in different regions and does not have exactly the same scope; sole usually refers to other edible flatfish and is not freely interchangeable in species names or on menus.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 想象一条像盘子般扁平、背面带橙色斑点的欧鲽；plaice 与 place 同音，但词源不同。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a plate-flat fish with orange spots; plaice sounds like place, though the words have different origins.

senses.meaning_zh: 铊：符号为 Tl 的柔软、有毒金属元素
senses.meaning_en: a soft, poisonous metallic element with the symbol Tl
senses.english_definition: Thallium is a soft, poisonous metal that is a chemical element and has the symbol Tl.
senses.collocation_en: thallium compounds; thallium poisoning
senses.collocation_zh: 铊化合物；铊中毒
senses.sentence_en: The laboratory tested the sample for traces of thallium.
senses.sentence_zh: 实验室检测了样品中是否含有微量铊。

etymology_story.zh: 英国化学家威廉·克鲁克斯于1861年发现铊，并根据其鲜绿色光谱线，以希腊语 thallos（嫩枝、绿芽）为词源命名。名称中的“绿芽”描述的是发现时的光谱特征，而非金属本身的颜色。
etymology_story.en: The British chemist William Crookes discovered thallium in 1861 and named it after Greek thallos, meaning a young shoot or green twig, because of its bright green spectral line. The reference to green describes the identifying spectrum rather than the colour of the metal itself.

morphology_enriched.zh: 科学构词：thall-（源自希腊语，意为嫩枝、绿芽）+ -ium（元素名称后缀）。相关专业词有 thallous（亚铊的，通常指铊为 +1 价）和 thallic（高铊的，通常指铊为 +3 价）；常见组合有 thallium compound（铊化合物）和 thallium salt（铊盐）。
morphology_enriched.en: Scientific formation: thall- (from Greek, meaning a young shoot or green twig) + -ium (an element-name suffix). Related technical adjectives are thallous, usually referring to thallium in the +1 oxidation state, and thallic, usually referring to the +3 state; common combinations include thallium compound and thallium salt.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有严格的词汇近义词。Tl 是其化学符号，与 thallium 指同一种元素；metal（金属）和 chemical element（化学元素）只是上位词，不能在需要指明铊的语境中替换它。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact lexical synonym. Tl is the chemical symbol for the same element; metal and chemical element are broader category terms and cannot replace thallium when its specific identity matters.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “绿芽”般的光谱线 → 名为 thallium 的金属铊。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A spectral line as green as a young shoot gave thallium its name.

usage_note: 通常指未经烘烤的燕麦、果干和坚果混合早餐，可配牛奶或酸奶；与通常经过烘烤的 granola 有别。

senses.meaning_zh: 什锦早餐麦片，通常由燕麦片、坚果和果干混合而成
senses.meaning_en: a breakfast mixture usually containing rolled oats, nuts, and dried fruit
senses.english_definition: Muesli is a mixture of oats, nuts, and usually dried fruit that you eat for breakfast, often with milk or yoghurt.
senses.collocation_en: a bowl of muesli; muesli with yoghurt

senses.sentence_zh: 她早餐吃了一碗拌酸奶的什锦麦片。

etymology_story.zh: Muesli 借自瑞士德语 Müesli，是表示糊状食物的 Mues 的指小形式，字面意思近于“小份糊食”。瑞士医生马克西米利安·比尔歇-本纳在20世纪初推广了一种含浸泡燕麦和新鲜水果的食品，后来这个名称扩展到各种什锦早餐麦片。
etymology_story.en: Muesli comes from Swiss German Müesli, a diminutive of Mues, meaning a mash or soft preparation of food. The Swiss physician Maximilian Bircher-Benner popularized a preparation containing soaked oats and fresh fruit in the early twentieth century, and the name later broadened to cover various mixed breakfast cereals.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 muesli 是整体借入的单纯词，通常作不可数名词，不宜拆成英语词根和后缀。源语结构为 Mues（糊状食物）+ -li（指小后缀）；常见复合词有 muesli bar（什锦麦片棒）、muesli mix（什锦麦片混合物）和 Bircher muesli（比尔歇式浸泡麦片），没有常用的英语派生动词或形容词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, muesli is an unanalysed loanword, usually an uncountable noun, rather than an English root-plus-suffix formation. Its source-language structure is Mues (a mash) + -li (a diminutive suffix); common compounds include muesli bar, muesli mix, and Bircher muesli, with no established everyday derived verb or adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Breakfast cereal（早餐谷物食品）是上位词；granola（格兰诺拉麦片）通常经过烘烤，常加甜味料和油；porridge（粥、燕麦粥）通常加液体煮成。Muesli 通常以未烘烤的混合麦片为基础，可直接拌食或先浸泡。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Breakfast cereal is the broader category; granola is usually baked and often contains added sweetener and oil; porridge is usually cooked with liquid. Muesli typically starts as an untoasted cereal mixture and may be eaten after mixing or soaking.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 瑞士的“小份糊食” → 一碗拌牛奶或酸奶的什锦麦片。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of a Swiss little mash becoming a bowl of mixed cereal with milk or yoghurt.

forms: 本课指礼仪，通常用单数；另有圣像牌义，可数复数为 paxes。
family: Pax Romana：罗马治下的和平；此短语中的 Pax 大写。

morphology.text: pax + brede（古英语来源的板） → paxbrede（供亲吻的圣像牌）；pax 作为独立词素记忆。

etymology.text: 从中世纪拉丁语 pax 借入，拉丁语原义是和平；英语用于教会中的平安之吻及相关礼仪。

usage_note: 这里是教会礼仪用语。历史政治短语 Pax Romana 中的 Pax 大写，本课不考那一义。

senses.meaning_zh: 平安礼；基督教礼仪中表达平安与团契的亲吻或其他动作
senses.meaning_en: a ritual kiss or other exchange expressing peace and fellowship in Christian worship
senses.english_definition: The pax is a kiss or another ceremonial exchange through which worshippers express peace and fellowship during a Christian service.
senses.collocation_en: the exchange of the pax; the pax at Mass

senses.meaning_en: a sacred tablet formerly kissed by worshippers during the exchange of peace

senses.pos: n. 名词（正式用语，常写作 Pax）
senses.meaning_zh: 由强国或主导力量维持的和平时期或和平秩序
senses.meaning_en: a period or order of peace maintained by a dominant power
senses.english_definition: A pax is a period of relative peace maintained over a wide area by a powerful state or other dominant authority.
senses.collocation_en: Pax Romana; Pax Britannica
senses.collocation_zh: 罗马治下的和平；英国治下的和平
senses.sentence_en: Historians use Pax Romana to describe a period of relative peace within the Roman Empire.
senses.sentence_zh: 历史学家用“罗马治下的和平”来描述罗马帝国内部一段相对和平的时期。

senses.pos: interj. 感叹词（英国传统儿童用语）
senses.meaning_zh: 停！休战！用于游戏或打闹中请求暂停
senses.meaning_en: a call for a truce or a pause in a game or fight
senses.english_definition: Children traditionally shout 'Pax!' when they want others to stop fighting or pause a game.
senses.collocation_en: shout 'Pax!'; cry 'Pax!'
senses.collocation_zh: 喊“停！”；叫“休战！”

senses.sentence_zh: 游戏中的打闹变得太激烈时，他喊道：“停！”

senses.pos: n. 名词（旅游、航空及酒店业缩略用法）
senses.meaning_zh: 乘客；宾客；人数，通常用于数字之后
senses.meaning_en: passengers, guests, or people, especially in numerical counts
senses.english_definition: In travel and hospitality, pax is an abbreviation used after a number to show how many passengers, guests, or people are involved.
senses.collocation_en: a booking for 20 pax; maximum capacity: 50 pax
senses.collocation_zh: 20人的预订；最大容纳人数：50人
senses.sentence_en: The booking form listed the group size as 12 pax.
senses.sentence_zh: 预订表上注明该团体共有12人。

etymology_story.zh: 表示和平、平安礼及请求休战的 pax 源自拉丁语 pax（和平）；教会用法后来也指礼仪中供亲吻的圣像牌，政治历史用法则见于 Pax Romana 等表达。旅游和酒店业中表示乘客或人数的 pax 属于现代行业缩略用法，应与上述拉丁语词义分开理解。
etymology_story.en: Pax in its peace, liturgical, and truce-call senses comes from Latin pax, meaning peace; the church term also came to denote a tablet kissed during worship, while political and historical uses appear in expressions such as Pax Romana. The travel and hospitality use for passengers or people is a modern industry abbreviation and should be distinguished from those Latin-derived senses.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，拉丁语借词 pax 不再细分为英语词根和词缀。相关词有 paxbrede 和 paxboard（均指平安牌）；Pax Romana（罗马治下的和平）是拉丁语短语，旅游业 pax 是通常不变形的行业缩略形式；peace（和平）、pacific（和平的）和 pacify（使平静）属于历史相关词，而非由英语 pax 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: The Latin loanword pax has no productive English root-and-affix breakdown. Related formations include paxbrede and paxboard, both denoting the ceremonial tablet; Pax Romana is a Latin phrase, and travel-industry pax is generally an invariant abbreviation; peace, pacific, and pacify are historically related words rather than direct English derivatives of pax.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Peace（和平）含义最广；truce（休战、暂停争斗）通常是暂时性的，更接近感叹词 Pax! 的功能；kiss of peace（平安之吻）对应宗教礼仪义，但不一定指平安牌。表示人数时，可按场景改用 passengers（乘客）或 guests（宾客）。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Peace is the broadest term; truce usually means a temporary halt to conflict and best matches the function of 'Pax!'; kiss of peace corresponds to the religious ceremony but does not necessarily denote the ceremonial tablet. For numerical counts, passengers or guests can replace pax according to context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 拉丁语 pax＝和平：礼拜中传递和平，打闹中请求休战；行程表上的数字加 pax 则表示人数。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Latin pax means peace: share it in worship or call for it during a fight; a number followed by pax on a booking means people.

etymology.text: 来自中世纪拉丁语 in quarto，意为处在四分之一的形式；quartus 是第四，联系整张纸两折后形成四叶。

usage_note: 传统书籍开本术语：整张印刷纸折两次成四叶、八页；不能只凭一本书的厘米尺寸断定开本。

comprehension_check.question: 句中 quarto 表示什么？请选择符合语境的意思。
comprehension_check.wrong_reason: 这里的语境是：在特藏阅览室观察古书的制作形式。 因此 quarto 表示“四开本”，不是“对开本”。

fields.wrong_reason: 这里的语境是：在特藏阅览室观察古书的制作形式。 因此 quarto 表示“四开本”，不是“对开本”。

senses.meaning_zh: 四开本：每张全纸折叠两次、形成四叶八页的书或这种开本
senses.meaning_en: a book or format made by folding each full sheet twice to produce four leaves and eight pages
senses.english_definition: A quarto is a book made from sheets of paper that have each been folded twice to form four leaves, or eight pages.
senses.collocation_en: the first quarto; a Shakespeare quarto
senses.collocation_zh: 首版四开本；莎士比亚作品的四开本
senses.sentence_en: The library owns a rare quarto of the play.
senses.sentence_zh: 这家图书馆藏有该剧的一部珍贵四开本。

senses.meaning_zh: 四开的；采用四开本形式的
senses.meaning_en: having the format produced by folding each full sheet into four leaves
senses.english_definition: A quarto book or edition has pages made by folding each full sheet of paper into four leaves.
senses.collocation_en: a quarto edition; quarto format
senses.collocation_zh: 四开版；四开形式
senses.sentence_en: The play was first published in quarto format.
senses.sentence_zh: 这部戏剧最初以四开本形式出版。

etymology_story.zh: Quarto 来自拉丁语 in quarto，意为“以四分之一的形式”，其中 quarto 是 quartus（第四）的变格形式。印刷术语把它用于整张纸折叠两次后形成四叶的开本；书页的实际尺寸仍取决于原纸大小。
etymology_story.en: Quarto comes from Latin in quarto, meaning in a fourth or quarter form, with quarto being an inflected form of quartus, fourth. Printers applied it to the format produced by folding a full sheet twice into four leaves; the actual page dimensions still depend on the original sheet.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 quarto 是整体借词，不宜把 -o 当成能自由构词的英语后缀。复数为 quartos（多部四开本）；常见组合有 quarto-sized（四开大小的）、quarto edition（四开版）和 quarto format（四开形式），书目缩写为 4to；quarter（四分之一）和 quart（夸脱）与其词源相关，但并非由 quarto 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, quarto is an unanalysed loanword, and its final -o is not a productive English suffix. Its plural is quartos; common formations include quarto-sized, quarto edition, and quarto format, and its bibliographical abbreviation is 4to; quarter and quart are etymologically related but are not derivatives of quarto.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有严格近义词；4to 是 quarto 的书目缩写。相邻术语 folio（对开本）通常每张纸折一次，形成两叶；octavo（八开本）通常每张纸折三次，形成八叶；quarto 则是四叶，不能仅凭书的外部尺寸判定。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact lexical synonym; 4to is the bibliographical abbreviation for quarto. The neighbouring term folio normally means two leaves per sheet after one fold, while octavo normally means eight leaves after three folds; quarto means four leaves, and external dimensions alone do not establish the format.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: quart- 联想“四”：整纸两折，四叶八页。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect quart- with four: two folds make four leaves and eight pages.

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；重音记号标在重读音节前。

forms: 复数 oncogenes。
family: oncogenes：复数；oncogenic：致癌的。

morphology.text: onco-（肿瘤） + gene（基因） → oncogene（癌基因）。

etymology.text: 20世纪英语把源自希腊语 onkos（肿块）的 onco- 与 gene 组合，用来命名能促进肿瘤形成的基因。

usage_note: 生物学术语，指能促进细胞癌变的基因；不等于所有与癌症研究有关的基因。

teaching.sentence: The experiment measured the expression of one oncogene in the cells.

fields.wrong_reason: 这里的语境是：阅读实验报告，区分促进和抑制肿瘤的基因。 因此 oncogene 表示“癌基因”，不是“抑癌基因”。

senses.meaning_zh: 癌基因：激活或异常表达时能促进癌症发生发展的基因
senses.meaning_en: a gene that can promote cancer when activated or abnormally expressed
senses.english_definition: An oncogene is a gene that can help cause cancer by making cells grow or divide in an uncontrolled way.
senses.collocation_en: oncogene activation; an activated oncogene
senses.collocation_zh: 癌基因激活；被激活的癌基因
senses.sentence_en: The mutation converted a normal growth-regulating gene into an oncogene.
senses.sentence_zh: 这一突变使一个正常调控生长的基因变成了癌基因。

etymology_story.zh: Oncogene 是20世纪形成的科学合成词，由源自希腊语 onkos（肿块、肿瘤）的 onco- 与 gene（基因）组成。这个术语在致瘤病毒研究中得到发展，后来也用于细胞中经异常激活而促进癌症形成的基因。
etymology_story.en: Oncogene is a twentieth-century scientific compound combining onco-, from Greek onkos, meaning a mass or tumour, with gene. The term developed in research on tumour-causing viruses and was later also applied to cellular genes whose abnormal activation promotes cancer.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：onco-（肿瘤）+ gene（基因）→ oncogene（癌基因），复数为 oncogenes。常见词族及相关构词有 oncogenic（致癌的）、oncogenicity（致癌性）、oncogenically（以致癌方式）、oncogenesis（肿瘤发生）、oncogenetic（与肿瘤发生有关的）和 proto-oncogene（原癌基因，即正常情况下参与细胞调控、发生特定异常后可成为癌基因的基因）；其中 oncogenesis 应分析为 onco- + -genesis（发生、形成）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: onco- (tumour) + gene → oncogene, with the plural oncogenes. Common family members and related formations include oncogenic, oncogenicity, oncogenically, oncogenesis, oncogenetic, and proto-oncogene, a normally regulated cellular gene that can become an oncogene through particular abnormalities; oncogenesis is separately analysed as onco- + -genesis, meaning formation or development.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Cancer-promoting gene（促癌基因）是较通俗的释义；cancer gene（癌症相关基因）范围更广，也可包括抑癌基因；proto-oncogene（原癌基因）是尚未发生致癌性激活的正常基因，不能与 oncogene 完全互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cancer-promoting gene is a plain-language paraphrase; cancer gene is broader and can also include tumour-suppressor genes; proto-oncogene denotes the normal precursor before cancer-promoting activation and is not interchangeable with oncogene.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: onco-＝肿瘤，gene＝基因：细胞生长的“油门”异常开启，就可能成为癌基因。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Onco- means tumour and gene means gene: a growth accelerator stuck on can become an oncogene.

pronunciation.note: 本课采用英式骂语常用读音 /twæt/；其他用法也可见 /twɒt/。

forms: 名词复数 twats；本课只学骂人用法。
family: twats：复数；twattish：愚蠢讨厌的，粗俗。

morphology.text: twat + -ish → twattish（愚蠢讨厌的）；twat 作为独立词素记忆，派生时双写 t。

etymology.text: 英语在17世纪已用它粗俗地指女性外阴，20世纪又出现骂人笨蛋的用法；从禁忌身体词到侮辱语的变化，提醒你它很冒犯。

usage_note: 粗俗且有冒犯性，尤其不适合正式场合；英式骂语义常读 /twæt/，另有粗俗身体部位义。

translation: 他用一句粗俗的骂语，称那个粗心的司机是蠢货。

call someone a twat 骂某人是蠢货
feel like a twat 觉得自己蠢透了
hint: The sentence explicitly describes the word as a rude insult.
context_hint: The sentence explicitly describes the word as a rude insult.

teaching.contrast: twat 在这里是粗俗侮辱语；fool 也可批评人傻，但粗俗程度不同。
teaching.sentence: After missing the obvious sign, he said he felt like a twat.
teaching.translation: 漏看了那么显眼的标志后，他说自己感觉蠢透了。

comprehension_check.sentence: He called the careless driver a twat, using a rude insult.

fields.wrong_reason: 这里的语境是：辨认对话中的冒犯表达，理解而不模仿这种骂法。 因此 twat 表示“笨蛋（粗俗骂语）”，不是“聪明人（赞语）”。

senses.meaning_zh: 笨蛋；讨厌鬼（粗俗、冒犯性的骂语，尤用于英国英语）
senses.meaning_en: A stupid or unpleasant person; a vulgar insult, especially in British English.
senses.english_definition: If someone calls a person a twat, they are saying in a very rude way that the person is stupid or unpleasant.
senses.collocation_en: a complete twat; a stupid twat
senses.collocation_zh: 十足的混蛋；蠢货
senses.sentence_en: I felt like a complete twat when I realized I had been arguing with the wrong person.
senses.sentence_zh: 发现自己一直找错人争论时，我觉得自己简直是个大蠢货。

senses.meaning_zh: 女性外阴（粗俗用语）
senses.meaning_en: The vulva or female genitals; a vulgar term.
senses.english_definition: A woman's twat is her external genital area, referred to in very rude language.
senses.collocation_en: a woman's twat; her twat
senses.collocation_zh: 女性的外阴（粗俗说法）；她的外阴（粗俗说法）
senses.sentence_en: In its anatomical sense, 'twat' is a vulgar word for the vulva.
senses.sentence_zh: 在指身体部位时，twat 是表示女性外阴的粗俗词。

senses.meaning_zh: 猛打；重击（英国粗俗俚语）
senses.meaning_en: To hit someone or something hard; vulgar British slang.
senses.english_definition: If someone twats a person or thing, they hit them hard.
senses.collocation_en: twat someone on the head; twat someone in the face
senses.collocation_zh: 猛击某人的头部；猛打某人的脸
senses.sentence_en: He threatened to twat me if I touched his bike.
senses.sentence_zh: 他威胁说，如果我碰他的自行车，就狠狠揍我。

etymology_story.zh: 该词至少在17世纪已见于英语，起初粗俗地指女性生殖部位，但更早的词源不明。后来发展出辱骂人的名词义，以及英国俚语中“猛打”的动词义。
etymology_story.en: The word is recorded in English from at least the seventeenth century as a vulgar term for female genitals, but its earlier origin is unknown. It later developed an insulting personal sense and a British slang verb meaning to hit hard.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中为不可再拆分的词基 twat；名词转作动词，无须添加词缀。屈折形式：twats（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、twatted（过去式和过去分词）、twatting（现在分词）；派生词包括 twattish、twatty（均指愚蠢讨厌的，粗俗），后接这些元音起首的后缀时双写 t。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, twat is an unanalyzable base; the verb is formed from the noun by conversion without an affix. Inflections are twats, twatted, and twatting; derivatives include twattish and twatty, both vulgar adjectives meaning stupid or unpleasant, with the final t doubled before these vowel-initial suffixes.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: idiot（笨蛋）侧重愚蠢，通常没有 twat 那么粗俗；cunt（女性生殖器；极粗俗骂语）与其身体义及辱骂义重叠，通常冒犯性更强；whack（猛打）接近其动词义，但本身不属于禁忌粗口。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Idiot emphasizes stupidity and is generally less vulgar; cunt overlaps with both the anatomical and insulting senses and is usually more offensive; whack resembles the verb sense but is not itself a taboo word.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把它记成一个粗俗词的三个用法：身体部位、骂人、猛打；这是意义联结，不是词源解释。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link one vulgar word to three uses: a body part, an insult, and a hard hit; this is a memory aid, not an etymology.

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；重音记号标在重读音节前。

forms: 感叹词，没有复数、时态变化。
family: crikey Moses：加强惊讶语气的固定感叹语。

morphology.text: crikey + Moses → crikey Moses（加强惊讶的固定感叹语）；crikey 作为独立词素记忆。

etymology.text: 19世纪英语中出现的委婉惊叹语，通常认为是对 Christ 的改写，用变音的方式表达惊讶。

usage_note: 主要用于英国和澳大利亚非正式口语；常带感叹号。句首写 Crikey，句中引用原词可用 crikey。

teaching.sentence: He whispered, 'Crikey, the tickets cost twice as much now.'
teaching.translation: 他低声说：天哪，现在票价涨了一倍。

comprehension_check.sentence: She said, 'Crikey, that suitcase is heavy!'

senses.meaning_zh: 天哪；哎呀（表示惊讶或震惊，尤用于英国和澳大利亚英语）
senses.meaning_en: An informal exclamation of surprise or shock, especially in British and Australian English.
senses.english_definition: People say 'Crikey!' when they are surprised or shocked.
senses.collocation_en: Oh, crikey!; Crikey Moses!
senses.collocation_zh: 哎呀，天哪！；我的老天爷！
senses.sentence_en: Crikey, I didn't realize it was so late!
senses.sentence_zh: 天哪，我没想到已经这么晚了！

etymology_story.zh: 该词出现于19世纪，通常被解释为感叹用语 Christ 的委婉变体。通过改变宗教称呼的读音，说话者仍可表达惊讶，同时减轻直接使用该称呼的冒犯性。
etymology_story.en: The word appeared in the nineteenth century and is generally explained as a softened alteration of the exclamation Christ. Changing the religious name allowed speakers to express surprise with less offense.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 crikey 作为完整感叹词记忆，不能按 cri- + -key 分析，也没有常用的屈折或派生词族。Crikey Moses 是加强语气的固定表达，并非由添加派生词缀构成。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats crikey as a complete interjection, not as cri- plus -key, and it has no established common inflectional or derivational family. Crikey Moses is an emphatic fixed expression rather than an affix-derived word.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: gosh（天哪）是较温和的惊叹语；wow（哇）常带赞叹或兴奋；blimey（天哪）也表示惊讶，具有鲜明的英国口语色彩。Crikey 尤其让人联想到英国或澳大利亚英语。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Gosh is a mild exclamation; wow often suggests admiration or excitement; blimey expresses surprise with a distinctly British flavor. Crikey is particularly associated with British and Australian English.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Christ 的委婉惊叹变体：突然吃惊时的一声“天哪”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A softened Christ exclamation: the 'Good heavens!' that comes out when something surprises you.

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；重音记号标在重读音节前。

forms: 复数 halons 表示不同的哈龙化合物。
family: halons：复数；halogen：卤素。

morphology.text: halo-（卤素） + -on（化学名称词尾） → halon（哈龙）；把它作为卤代烃类灭火剂记忆。

etymology.text: 现代英语化学命名用希腊语来源的 halo-（卤素）加词尾 -on 构成，用来称呼一类含卤素的灭火化合物。

usage_note: 常见于灭火系统或环境历史资料；它是一类化合物的名称，不是所有灭火剂的统称。

fields.wrong_reason: 这里的语境是：阅读旧式消防设备的成分标签。 因此 halon 表示“哈龙（卤代烃灭火剂）”，不是“水基灭火剂”。

senses.meaning_zh: 哈龙；卤代烃灭火剂，尤指含溴的灭火化合物
senses.meaning_en: A halogenated hydrocarbon used as a fire-extinguishing agent, especially one containing bromine.
senses.english_definition: A halon is one of a group of chemicals that contain halogens and are used to put out fires.
senses.collocation_en: halon fire extinguisher; halon suppression system
senses.collocation_zh: 哈龙灭火器；哈龙灭火系统
senses.sentence_en: The aircraft's fire extinguisher contains halon.
senses.sentence_zh: 这架飞机的灭火器内装有哈龙灭火剂。

etymology_story.zh: Halon 是20世纪形成的化学名称，与 halogen（卤素）一词有关，用于命名一类卤代烃。它因这类化合物的灭火用途而成为消防领域的专门术语。
etymology_story.en: Halon is a twentieth-century chemical name associated with halogen and used for a class of halogenated hydrocarbons. It became a specialist firefighting term through these compounds' use as extinguishing agents.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代使用中通常将 halon 作为完整化学词基；可借 halo-（与卤素有关）帮助理解，但不宜把 -on 当作意义明确、可自由套用的英语后缀。复数为 halons（多种哈龙）；常见组合有 halon-free（不含哈龙的）和 halon-based（以哈龙为基础的）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern use, halon normally functions as a complete chemical base; halo- can help connect it with halogens, but -on should not be treated as a freely productive English suffix with a precise meaning. The plural is halons, and common formations include halon-free and halon-based.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: fire-extinguishing agent（灭火剂）是功能上的上位词；halogenated hydrocarbon（卤代烃）是范围更广的化学类别；brominated fire suppressant（含溴灭火剂）强调含溴及抑火作用。这些都不是在所有语境中可替换 halon 的严格同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Fire-extinguishing agent is a broader functional term; halogenated hydrocarbon names a broader chemical class; brominated fire suppressant emphasizes bromine content and fire suppression. None is an exact substitute for halon in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 由 halogen（卤素）联想到 halon：用于灭火的卤代烃。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect halon with halogen: a halogen-containing hydrocarbon used to extinguish fires.

pronunciation.note: 英语中借用法语词的英式近似读音；法语原音为 /ɔm/。

forms: 法语复数 hommes；英语中常保留在法语短语内。
family: hommes：法语复数；bonhomme：和善的人。

morphology.text: bon（好） + homme（人、男子） → bonhomme（和善的人，法语借词）；homme 作为独立借词词素记忆。

etymology.text: 法语 homme 源自拉丁语 homo（人）；英语主要在保留的法语短语里使用这个词，如 pour homme。

usage_note: 这是英语中沿用的法语词，多见于香水、服装标签或法语短语；日常英语说男人通常用 man，不单独替换为 homme。

pour homme 男士用（香水标签）
homme de lettres 文人（人物介绍）

context_hint: The label uses a French word for the male customer.

teaching.contrast: homme 在法语短语中表示男子；femme 表示女子，日常英语分别用 man 和 woman。
teaching.sentence: The shop assistant explained that pour homme means for men.

senses.pos: n. 名词（主要见于保留法语形式的短语或商品名称）
senses.meaning_zh: 男子；男人（法语词，英语中主要用于法语短语和商品名称）
senses.meaning_en: A man; a French word appearing chiefly in retained French expressions and product names in English.
senses.english_definition: Homme is the French word for a man, used in English mainly as part of French expressions or product names.
senses.collocation_en: pour homme; homme d'affaires
senses.collocation_zh: 男士用；商人
senses.sentence_en: The words 'pour homme' on the bottle indicate that the fragrance is marketed to men.
senses.sentence_zh: 瓶身上的 pour homme 表示这款香水面向男性销售。

etymology_story.zh: 法语 homme 经古法语承自拉丁语 homo，其宾格形式为 hominem，原指人或人类个体。现代法语中它也表示成年男子，英语主要在借入的法语表达中保留这一形式。
etymology_story.en: French homme developed through Old French from Latin homo, with the accusative form hominem, meaning a human being or person. In modern French it also means an adult male, and English chiefly preserves it within borrowed French expressions.

morphology_enriched.zh: 在英语词条中应把 homme 作为完整法语借词处理，没有常用的英语派生词族。法语复数为 hommes，通常与单数同音；pour homme（男士用）和 homme d'affaires（商人）是短语，bonhomme 中的 bon 意为“好的”，但这些都不是英语后缀派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: For an English lexical entry, homme is a complete French borrowing with no common English derivational family. Its French plural is hommes, normally pronounced like the singular; pour homme and homme d'affaires are phrases, while bon in bonhomme means good, and none of these is an English suffix-derived form.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: man（男子）是英语中的普通对应词；gentleman（先生；绅士）更礼貌或带社会评价；male（男性）突出性别分类，可用于人与动物。Homme 主要保留法语或商品命名色彩，不是普通英语中 man 的通用替代词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Man is the ordinary English equivalent; gentleman adds politeness or a social judgment; male emphasizes sex classification and can refer to humans or animals. Homme retains a French or branding association and is not a general replacement for man in ordinary English.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 看到香水上的 pour homme，就读作“男士用”：homme 对应“男人”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Read pour homme on a fragrance as 'for men': homme supplies the meaning 'man'.

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；重音记号标在重读音节前。

forms: 复数 paters。
family: paters：复数；paternal：父亲的、父系的。

morphology.text: patern-（父亲的同源词干） + -al → paternal（父亲的）；pater 作为独立借词词素记忆。

etymology.text: 直接借自拉丁语 pater（父亲）；英语中曾被英国学生或戏谑说话者用来称呼父亲。

usage_note: 旧式、带戏谑色彩的英国用语，日常称呼父亲通常用 dad 或 father；不要当作当代中性称谓。

teaching.sentence: In his letter, the schoolboy asks his pater to send a little money.

comprehension_check.sentence: In the old novel, the boy calls his father pater.

comprehension_check.wrong_reason: 这里的语境是：阅读旧小说，理解学生对家长的戏谑称呼。 因此 pater 表示“父亲（旧式戏谑称呼）”，不是“母亲”。

fields.label: 句中目标词表示（父亲（旧式戏谑称呼）／母亲）
fields.wrong_reason: 这里的语境是：阅读旧小说，理解学生对家长的戏谑称呼。 因此 pater 表示“父亲（旧式戏谑称呼）”，不是“母亲”。

senses.meaning_zh: 父亲；老爸（旧式英国用语，常带戏谑口吻）
senses.meaning_en: A father; an old-fashioned, often humorous British term.
senses.english_definition: Someone's pater is their father, referred to in an old-fashioned and often humorous way.
senses.collocation_en: my pater; the old pater
senses.collocation_zh: 我父亲；老爸
senses.sentence_en: My pater would never have approved of such extravagance.
senses.sentence_zh: 我家老爷子绝不会赞成这样铺张浪费。

etymology_story.zh: 该词直接借自拉丁语 pater，意为“父亲”。英语曾将它用作带有古典教育色彩的父亲称呼，尤其见于旧式英国学生用语，后来常带戏谑意味。
etymology_story.en: The word was borrowed directly from Latin pater, meaning father. English adopted it as a classically flavored term for one's father, particularly in old-fashioned British school usage, and it often carries a humorous tone.

morphology_enriched.zh: 英语 pater 是完整借词，复数为 paters。相关词族采用拉丁语来源的 patern- 词干：paternal（父亲的）→ paternally（以父亲的方式）、paternalism（家长式作风）→ paternalist（家长主义者）、paternalistic（家长式的）→ paternalistically（以家长式方式）；另有 paternity（父亲身份；父子关系）。这些词并非都由英语 pater 直接添加后缀而成。
morphology_enriched.en: English pater is a complete borrowing, with the plural paters. Its related family uses the Latin-derived stem patern-: paternal → paternally; paternalism → paternalist and paternalistic → paternalistically; and paternity. These words were not all formed by directly adding suffixes to English pater.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: father（父亲）是中性标准用词；dad（爸爸）亲切自然；papa（爸爸）多带家庭亲昵色彩。Pater 则显得旧式、带古典教育背景，且常用于戏谑。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Father is neutral and standard; dad is familiar and affectionate; papa is an intimate family term. Pater sounds old-fashioned, classically educated, and often humorous.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 pater 与 paternal、paternity 连起来：共同的意义核心都是“父亲”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link pater with paternal and paternity: the shared meaning at the center is 'father'.

aliases: 结肠部分或全部切除术

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；重音记号标在重读音节前。

family: colectomies：复数；colon：结肠。

morphology.text: col-（结肠） + -ectomy（手术切除） → colectomy（结肠切除术）。

etymology.text: 19世纪英语医学用语，把源自希腊语 kolon（结肠）的词干和 -ectomy（切除）组合，名称直接指出切除的器官。

usage_note: 指切除部分或全部结肠的手术；具体范围由 partial、total 等修饰语说明，不等于所有肠道手术。

sentence: The report describes a colectomy in which part of the colon was removed.
translation: 报告描述了一次切除了部分结肠的手术。
scenario: 阅读病历中的手术名称，识别涉及的器官。
cloze: The report describes a _____ in which part of the colon was removed.
collocation:
a partial colectomy 部分结肠切除术
recover after a colectomy 结肠切除术后恢复
hint: Identify the organ named in the surgical report.
context_hint: Identify the organ named in the surgical report.

teaching.contrast: colectomy 切除结肠；appendectomy 切除阑尾，名称指向不同部位。
teaching.sentence: The student learned that a total colectomy removes the whole colon.
teaching.translation: 学生了解到，全结肠切除术切除的是整个结肠。

comprehension_check.sentence: The report describes a colectomy in which part of the colon was removed.
comprehension_check.question: 句中 colectomy 表示什么？请选择符合语境的意思。
comprehension_check.wrong_reason: 这里的语境是：阅读病历中的手术名称，识别涉及的器官。 因此 colectomy 表示“结肠切除术”，不是“阑尾切除术”。

fields.label: 句中目标词表示（结肠切除术／阑尾切除术）
fields.wrong_reason: 这里的语境是：阅读病历中的手术名称，识别涉及的器官。 因此 colectomy 表示“结肠切除术”，不是“阑尾切除术”。

senses.meaning_zh: 结肠切除术；切除部分或全部结肠的手术
senses.meaning_en: Surgical removal of part or all of the colon.
senses.english_definition: A colectomy is an operation in which a surgeon removes part or all of a person's colon.
senses.collocation_en: partial colectomy; total colectomy
senses.collocation_zh: 部分结肠切除术；全结肠切除术
senses.sentence_en: She underwent a partial colectomy to remove the affected section of her colon.
senses.sentence_zh: 她接受了部分结肠切除术，以切除结肠中受累的肠段。

etymology_story.zh: 该词形成于19世纪的医学英语，由表示结肠的构词成分与表示手术切除的 -ectomy 组合而成。前者源自希腊语 kōlon（结肠），后者最终源自希腊语表示“切除”的词。
etymology_story.en: The word arose in nineteenth-century medical English by combining an element meaning 'colon' with -ectomy, meaning surgical removal. The first element comes from Greek kōlon, 'colon', while the second ultimately comes from a Greek word meaning 'excision'.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代医学构词：col-（结肠，取自 colon 的组合词干）+ -ectomy（手术切除）→ colectomy。复数为 colectomies；相关复合词包括 hemicolectomy（半结肠切除术）、subtotal colectomy（次全结肠切除术）和 proctocolectomy（直肠结肠切除术）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern medical formation: col- (the combining stem referring to the colon) + -ectomy (surgical removal) → colectomy. The plural is colectomies; related compounds include hemicolectomy, subtotal colectomy, and proctocolectomy.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: colon resection（结肠切除术）与 colectomy 意义接近，但在具体语境中常指切除一段结肠；bowel resection（肠切除术）范围更广，也可涉及小肠；hemicolectomy（半结肠切除术）是切除结肠一侧的特定术式。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Colon resection is a close equivalent, often referring in context to removal of a segment of the colon; bowel resection is broader and can involve the small intestine; hemicolectomy is a specific operation removing one side of the colon.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: col- 指结肠，-ectomy 指切除：名称直接说明“切除结肠”。CEFR-C2 为专业词汇学习难度估计，并非已核实的官方词级。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Col- identifies the colon; -ectomy identifies removal: the name directly describes the operation. CEFR-C2 is an estimated learning level for this specialist term, not a verified official word rating.

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；重音记号标在重读音节前。

forms: 形容词，无常用比较级变化。
family: excite：使兴奋；excitation：兴奋、激发。

morphology.text: excit-（兴奋，excite 的词干） + -atory（表示作用的形容词词尾） → excitatory（兴奋性的）。

etymology.text: 来自英语 excite 的拉丁语来源词干，配上形容词词尾 -atory；excite 可追溯到拉丁语 excitare（唤起、激发）。

usage_note: 常用于神经科学，描述促进兴奋的信号、作用或连接；不是说某人感到情绪激动。

sources.label: 词源词典 · excitatory
sources.scope: 历史路径；中文讲解和教学句为本批原创

sentence: An excitatory signal makes the neuron more likely to fire.
translation: 兴奋性信号使神经元更有可能放电。
scenario: 比较促进神经活动和抑制神经活动的信号。
cloze: An _____ signal makes the neuron more likely to fire.
collocation:
an excitatory signal 兴奋性信号
an excitatory drug 起兴奋作用的药物
hint: The signal increases the chance that the neuron will fire.
context_hint: The signal increases the chance that the neuron will fire.

teaching.contrast: excitatory 描述引起兴奋的作用；inhibitory 描述抑制作用，方向相反。
teaching.sentence: The diagram marks the excitatory connection with a plus sign.
teaching.translation: 示意图用加号标出兴奋性连接。

comprehension_check.sentence: An excitatory signal makes the neuron more likely to fire.
comprehension_check.question: 句中 excitatory 表示什么？请选择符合语境的意思。
comprehension_check.wrong_reason: 这里的语境是：比较促进神经活动和抑制神经活动的信号。 因此 excitatory 表示“兴奋性的”，不是“抑制性的”。

fields.label: 句中目标词表示（兴奋性的／抑制性的）
fields.wrong_reason: 这里的语境是：比较促进神经活动和抑制神经活动的信号。 因此 excitatory 表示“兴奋性的”，不是“抑制性的”。

senses.meaning_zh: 兴奋性的；促进神经元放电或增强生理活动的
senses.meaning_en: Causing excitation or increasing physiological activity, especially in nerve cells.
senses.english_definition: An excitatory signal or substance increases the activity of a cell or makes a nerve cell more likely to produce an electrical impulse.
senses.collocation_en: excitatory neurotransmitter; excitatory synapse
senses.collocation_zh: 兴奋性神经递质；兴奋性突触
senses.sentence_en: Glutamate is the main excitatory neurotransmitter in the mammalian brain.
senses.sentence_zh: 谷氨酸是哺乳动物脑内主要的兴奋性神经递质。

etymology_story.zh: 该词由 excite 所属词族加上形容词后缀构成；excite 最终源自拉丁语 excitare，意为“唤起、激发”。excitatory 在生理学中形成了“引起兴奋或增强活动”的专门含义。
etymology_story.en: The word belongs to the excite family and uses an adjective-forming suffix; excite ultimately comes from Latin excitare, meaning 'to rouse or stir up'. In physiology, excitatory developed the specialized meaning of producing excitation or increasing activity.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：excit-（excite 去掉词尾 e 的词干）+ -atory（表示相关作用的形容词后缀）→ excitatory。核心词族包括 excite（使兴奋）、excitation（兴奋；激发）、excited（兴奋的；被激发的）、exciting（令人兴奋的）、excitement（兴奋）、excitable（易兴奋的）、excitability（兴奋性）、excitably（易激动地）、excitatory（兴奋性的）、excitative（激发性的，较少用）和 non-excitatory（非兴奋性的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: excit- (excite without its final e) + -atory (an adjective suffix indicating a related action or effect) → excitatory. The core family includes excite, excitation, excited, exciting, excitement, excitable, excitability, excitably, excitatory, the less common excitative, and non-excitatory.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: stimulatory（刺激性的）同样表示促进活动，但适用范围更广；activating（激活性的）强调使某个过程或机制开始运作；stimulating（有刺激作用的；令人振奋的）也常描述心理体验。excitatory 尤其强调生理兴奋效应，与 inhibitory（抑制性的）相对。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Stimulatory also means promoting activity but has a broader range; activating emphasizes switching a process or mechanism into operation; stimulating can also describe an engaging mental experience. Excitatory particularly identifies a physiological excitation effect and contrasts with inhibitory.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: excite 的“激发”落实到细胞：excitatory 使细胞更容易活跃或放电。CEFR-C2 为专业词汇学习难度估计，并非已核实的官方词级。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Apply the 'rousing' idea of excite to a cell: excitatory input makes it more active or more likely to fire. CEFR-C2 is an estimated learning level for this specialist term, not a verified official word rating.

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；重音记号标在重读音节前。

forms: 形容词用法通常无词尾变化；另有名词奢华义，本课不考。
family: deluxe：豪华的；luxury：奢华。

morphology.text: de（具有） + luxe（奢华） → deluxe（豪华的）；luxe 作为独立借词词素记忆。

etymology.text: 由法语 luxe（奢华）借入英语，法语又来自拉丁语 luxus（奢侈、富丽）；英语后来也把 luxe 用作豪华的形容词。

usage_note: 常见于时尚、酒店和广告文案，用在名词前，如 luxe fabrics；本课只学形容词。

senses.meaning_zh: 豪华的；奢华精美的
senses.meaning_en: Luxurious, elegant, and expensive in appearance or quality.
senses.english_definition: Something that is luxe looks or feels luxurious and expensive.
senses.collocation_en: luxe fabrics; a luxe look
senses.collocation_zh: 奢华面料；奢华的外观
senses.sentence_en: Velvet cushions give the room a luxe look.
senses.sentence_zh: 天鹅绒靠垫让房间显得奢华精致。

senses.meaning_zh: 奢华；豪华格调，常用于时尚或设计语境
senses.meaning_en: Luxury or a luxurious style, especially in fashion and design.
senses.english_definition: Luxe is the quality or style of being luxurious, especially in clothes, furnishings, or design.
senses.collocation_en: understated luxe; a touch of luxe
senses.collocation_zh: 低调的奢华；一抹奢华气息
senses.sentence_en: Brass handles add a touch of luxe to the kitchen.
senses.sentence_zh: 黄铜把手为厨房增添了一抹奢华气息。

etymology_story.zh: 英语从法语 luxe 借入该词，原义为“奢华”，最终源自拉丁语 luxus（奢侈、富丽）。英语后来也将其用作形容词，尤其常见于时尚、室内设计及商业宣传。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed luxe from French, where it means 'luxury'; it ultimately comes from Latin luxus, meaning 'luxury or extravagance'. English subsequently also used it as an adjective, especially in fashion, interior design, and advertising.

morphology_enriched.zh: luxe 是整体借入的自由词，在现代英语中不拆分为词根和词缀。相关形式包括 de luxe、deluxe（豪华的）和 super-luxe（极其豪华的）；法语 de luxe 的字面结构是“具有奢华性质的／奢华的”，其中 de 不是英语派生前缀。luxury、luxurious、luxuriously 和 luxuriousness 是具有共同历史来源的相关词，并非直接给 luxe 加后缀构成。
morphology_enriched.en: Luxe is a borrowed free-standing word and has no productive internal root-and-affix division in modern English. Related forms include de luxe, deluxe, and super-luxe; French de luxe literally means 'of luxury', and de is not an English derivational prefix here. Luxury, luxurious, luxuriously, and luxuriousness share its historical source but are not formed by directly adding suffixes to luxe.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: luxurious（豪华舒适的）侧重高品质带来的舒适和享受；opulent（富丽堂皇的）突出显而易见的财富与华美；lavish（铺张丰盛的）强调投入或供给之丰厚。名词 luxe 接近 luxury（奢华），但更带时尚与设计宣传色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Luxurious emphasizes comfort and pleasure provided by high quality; opulent highlights conspicuous wealth and richness; lavish emphasizes generous or extravagant provision. As a noun, luxe is close to luxury but has a stronger association with fashion and design language.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把熟悉的 deluxe 与 luxe 联系起来：luxe 就是“奢华”，也可直接修饰奢华的事物。CEFR-C1 为学习难度估计，并非已核实的官方词级。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect luxe with the familiar deluxe: luxe names luxury and can also describe something luxurious. CEFR-C1 is an estimated learning level, not a verified official word rating.

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；重音记号标在重读音节前。

forms: 复数 peroxidases。
family: peroxidases：复数；peroxide：过氧化物。

morphology.text: per-（过，化学词首） + oxidase（氧化酶） → peroxidase（过氧化物酶）。

etymology.text: 现代科学英语由 per- 加 oxidase（氧化酶）构成；-ase 是酶名称后缀，整个名字把这类酶与过氧化物反应联系起来。

usage_note: 生物化学术语，指利用过氧化物催化氧化反应的一类酶；不要把酶本身当成过氧化物。

sources.scope: 历史路径；中文讲解和教学句为本批原创

sentence: The enzyme peroxidase uses a peroxide to help oxidise another compound.
translation: 过氧化物酶利用过氧化物，帮助氧化另一种化合物。
scenario: 学习酶名，区分催化剂与反应中的化合物。
cloze: The enzyme _____ uses a peroxide to help oxidise another compound.
collocation:
peroxidase in plant tissue 植物组织中的过氧化物酶
a peroxidase-labelled antibody 过氧化物酶标记的抗体
hint: The word names an enzyme, while peroxide names a chemical compound.
context_hint: The word names an enzyme, while peroxide names a chemical compound.

teaching.contrast: peroxidase 是酶，peroxide 是过氧化物；词尾 -ase 是识别酶名的重要线索。
teaching.sentence: The laboratory used peroxidase as a label in the assay.
teaching.translation: 实验室在检测中用过氧化物酶作标记物。

comprehension_check.sentence: The enzyme peroxidase uses a peroxide to help oxidise another compound.
comprehension_check.question: 句中 peroxidase 表示什么？请选择符合语境的意思。
comprehension_check.wrong_reason: 这里的语境是：学习酶名，区分催化剂与反应中的化合物。 因此 peroxidase 表示“过氧化物酶”，不是“淀粉酶”。

fields.label: 句中目标词表示（过氧化物酶／淀粉酶）
fields.wrong_reason: 这里的语境是：学习酶名，区分催化剂与反应中的化合物。 因此 peroxidase 表示“过氧化物酶”，不是“淀粉酶”。

senses.meaning_zh: 过氧化物酶；利用过氧化物氧化其他物质的一类酶
senses.meaning_en: An enzyme that uses a peroxide to oxidize another substance.
senses.english_definition: A peroxidase is an enzyme that uses hydrogen peroxide or another peroxide to oxidize a substance while reducing the peroxide.
senses.collocation_en: horseradish peroxidase; peroxidase activity
senses.collocation_zh: 辣根过氧化物酶；过氧化物酶活性
senses.sentence_en: The researchers measured peroxidase activity in the leaf samples.
senses.sentence_zh: 研究人员测定了叶片样本中的过氧化物酶活性。

etymology_story.zh: 该词由 peroxide（过氧化物）与酶名称后缀 -ase 构成，用来命名与过氧化物参与的氧化反应有关的酶。其命名重点是反应底物 peroxide，而不是简单地给 oxidase（氧化酶）加上 per-。
etymology_story.en: The word was formed from peroxide and the enzyme-naming suffix -ase to name enzymes involved in oxidation reactions using peroxides. Its naming basis is the substrate peroxide, rather than simply oxidase with per- added to it.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代科学构词：peroxid-（peroxide 去掉词尾 e）+ -ase（酶）→ peroxidase；复数为 peroxidases。相关形式包括 peroxidatic（具有过氧化物酶作用的）、peroxidase-like（类过氧化物酶的）、myeloperoxidase（髓过氧化物酶）和 lactoperoxidase（乳过氧化物酶）。peroxide（过氧化物）、peroxidation（过氧化）和 peroxidize（使过氧化）属于相关基础词族，并非全部直接派生自 peroxidase。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern scientific formation: peroxid- (peroxide without its final e) + -ase (enzyme) → peroxidase; the plural is peroxidases. Related forms include peroxidatic, peroxidase-like, myeloperoxidase, and lactoperoxidase. Peroxide, peroxidation, and peroxidize belong to the associated base-word family rather than all being direct derivatives of peroxidase.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有适用于所有语境的常见严格同义词。peroxide-reducing enzyme（还原过氧化物的酶）是描述性近义表达，但范围可能更广；oxidoreductase（氧化还原酶）是其上位类别；catalase（过氧化氢酶）是相关但不同的酶，主要催化过氧化氢分解为水和氧气。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no common exact synonym covering every context. Peroxide-reducing enzyme is a descriptive near-equivalent but may be broader; oxidoreductase names the wider enzyme class; catalase is a related but distinct enzyme that primarily breaks hydrogen peroxide down into water and oxygen.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: peroxide 是过氧化物，-ase 是酶：peroxidase 用过氧化物来氧化其他底物。CEFR-C2 为专业词汇学习难度估计，并非已核实的官方词级。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Peroxide supplies the reaction partner, and -ase identifies an enzyme: peroxidase uses peroxide to oxidize another substrate. CEFR-C2 is an estimated learning level for this specialist term, not a verified official word rating.

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；重音记号标在重读音节前。

forms: 形容词，无常用词尾变化。
family: covalence：共价；covalently：以共价方式。

morphology.text: co-（共同） + valent（价的） → covalent（共价的）。

etymology.text: 20世纪由 covalence 发展而来，co- 表示共同，valence 表示化合价；后者经德语化学用语追溯到拉丁语表示力量的词。

usage_note: 化学用语，常与 bond 连用，强调原子之间共享电子对；不是泛指所有化学连接。

sources.label: 词源词典 · covalent
sources.scope: 历史路径；中文讲解和教学句为本批原创

sentence: A covalent bond joins the atoms through a shared pair of electrons.
translation: 共价键通过一对共享电子把原子连接起来。
scenario: 比较化学键的形成方式。
cloze: A _____ bond joins the atoms through a shared pair of electrons.
collocation:
a covalent bond 共价键
a covalent compound 共价化合物
hint: Focus on the pair of electrons shared between atoms.
context_hint: Focus on the pair of electrons shared between atoms.

teaching.contrast: covalent 以共享电子对为特征；ionic 指离子之间的作用，不能互换。
teaching.sentence: The lesson compares a covalent compound with an ionic compound.
teaching.translation: 这节课比较一种共价化合物和一种离子化合物。

comprehension_check.sentence: A covalent bond joins the atoms through a shared pair of electrons.
comprehension_check.question: 句中 covalent 表示什么？请选择符合语境的意思。
comprehension_check.wrong_reason: 这里的语境是：比较化学键的形成方式。 因此 covalent 表示“共价的”，不是“离子性的”。

fields.label: 句中目标词表示（共价的／离子性的）
fields.wrong_reason: 这里的语境是：比较化学键的形成方式。 因此 covalent 表示“共价的”，不是“离子性的”。

senses.meaning_zh: 共价的；涉及原子间共享电子对的
senses.meaning_en: Involving the sharing of electron pairs between atoms.
senses.english_definition: A covalent bond is a chemical bond in which atoms share one or more pairs of electrons.
senses.collocation_en: covalent bond; covalent bonding
senses.collocation_zh: 共价键；共价成键
senses.sentence_en: The two hydrogen atoms are joined by a covalent bond.
senses.sentence_zh: 这两个氢原子通过一个共价键相连。

etymology_story.zh: covalent 出现在20世纪初共价成键理论发展的背景下，与 covalence（共价；共价数）属于同一组术语。co- 表示“共同”，valence 表示“化合价”，后者最终关联拉丁语 valere（有力量、有能力），借此表达原子共同参与成键的能力。
etymology_story.en: Covalent arose in the early twentieth-century development of theories of shared-electron bonding and belongs to the same terminology as covalence. Co- means 'together', while valence refers to combining capacity and ultimately relates to Latin valere, 'to be strong or capable'.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词可分析为 co-（共同）+ valent（具有某种化合价或成键能力的）→ covalent。核心词族包括 covalence、covalency（共价性；共价数，依语境而定）、covalently（以共价方式）、noncovalent／non-covalent（非共价的）和 noncovalently／non-covalently（以非共价方式）；valence、valency、monovalent 和 polyvalent 属于更广的价态词族。
morphology_enriched.en: A modern analysis is co- (together) + valent (having a particular valence or combining capacity) → covalent. The core family includes covalence, covalency, covalently, noncovalent/non-covalent, and noncovalently/non-covalently; valence, valency, monovalent, and polyvalent belong to the wider valence family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有完全可互换的常见单词同义词。electron-sharing（共享电子的）是解释性近义表达；nonionic（非离子的）仅排除离子性质，不一定特指共价；molecular（分子的）描述分子结构或层级，不能替代 covalent。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no common single-word synonym that is fully interchangeable. Electron-sharing is an explanatory near-equivalent; nonionic only excludes ionic character and does not necessarily specify covalent bonding; molecular describes molecules or molecular structure and cannot replace covalent.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: co- 表示“共同”：原子共享电子对来成键，就是 covalent。CEFR-C2 为专业词汇学习难度估计，并非已核实的官方词级。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Co- means 'together': atoms share electron pairs to form a covalent bond. CEFR-C2 is an estimated learning level for this specialist term, not a verified official word rating.

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；重音记号标在重读音节前。

forms: 通常不可数；区分不同类型时可见 neoplasias。
family: neoplasm：肿瘤、新生物；neoplastic：肿瘤的。

morphology.text: neo-（新） + -plasia（形成、增生） → neoplasia（肿瘤形成）。

etymology.text: 19世纪医学英语以希腊语来源的 neo-（新）和 -plasia（形成）构成，用于组织异常新生、形成肿瘤的过程。

usage_note: 指肿瘤形成或肿瘤性生长过程；不单凭这个词判断良性还是恶性。

sentence: The report uses neoplasia to describe abnormal growth that forms a tumour.
translation: 报告用 neoplasia 描述形成肿瘤的异常生长。
scenario: 阅读病理术语时，区分生长过程与形成的肿块。
cloze: The report uses _____ to describe abnormal growth that forms a tumour.
collocation:
epithelial neoplasia 上皮肿瘤形成
evidence of neoplasia 肿瘤形成的证据
hint: The growth in the report is abnormal and forms a tumour.
context_hint: The growth in the report is abnormal and forms a tumour.

teaching.contrast: neoplasia 偏重异常增生的过程或状态，neoplasm 指形成的新生物或肿瘤。
teaching.sentence: The textbook distinguishes neoplasia from normal tissue repair.
teaching.translation: 课本把肿瘤形成与正常组织修复区分开来。

comprehension_check.sentence: The report uses neoplasia to describe abnormal growth that forms a tumour.
comprehension_check.question: 句中 neoplasia 表示什么？请选择符合语境的意思。
comprehension_check.wrong_reason: 这里的语境是：阅读病理术语时，区分生长过程与形成的肿块。 因此 neoplasia 表示“肿瘤形成”，不是“正常组织修复”。

fields.label: 句中目标词表示（肿瘤形成／正常组织修复）
fields.wrong_reason: 这里的语境是：阅读病理术语时，区分生长过程与形成的肿块。 因此 neoplasia 表示“肿瘤形成”，不是“正常组织修复”。

senses.meaning_zh: 肿瘤形成；组织异常增生，可为良性或恶性
senses.meaning_en: Abnormal tissue growth resulting in a benign or malignant neoplasm.
senses.english_definition: Neoplasia is the abnormal growth of cells that produces a benign or malignant tumour.
senses.chinese_definition: 肿瘤形成是指细胞异常增生并形成良性或恶性肿瘤的过程。
senses.collocation_en: malignant neoplasia; cervical intraepithelial neoplasia
senses.collocation_zh: 恶性肿瘤形成；宫颈上皮内瘤变
senses.sentence_en: The tissue sample was examined for evidence of neoplasia.
senses.sentence_zh: 研究人员检查了该组织样本，以寻找肿瘤形成的证据。

etymology_story.zh: 该词是由希腊语来源的 neo-（新）和 -plasia（形成）构成的近代医学术语，字面意思是“新生形成”。其医学含义逐渐专指组织的异常新生，而非正常生长或修复。
etymology_story.en: A modern medical formation, neoplasia combines Greek-derived neo-, meaning 'new', with -plasia, meaning 'formation'. Its medical meaning concerns abnormal new tissue growth rather than ordinary growth or repair.

morphology_enriched.zh: 医学构词：neo-（新）＋-plasia（形成、发育）→ neoplasia（肿瘤形成）。同族词包括 neoplasm（肿瘤；异常新生组织）、neoplastic（肿瘤性的）和较少见的 neoplastically（以肿瘤性方式）。
morphology_enriched.en: Medical formation: neo- ('new') + -plasia ('formation or development') → neoplasia. The family includes neoplasm, an abnormal tissue growth; neoplastic, relating to neoplasia; and the less common adverb neoplastically.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: neoplastic growth（肿瘤性生长）最接近本词；tumorigenesis（肿瘤发生）更强调肿瘤启动和发展的过程；hyperplasia（增生）指细胞数量增加，本身不等于肿瘤形成。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Neoplastic growth is the closest equivalent; tumorigenesis emphasizes the initiation and development of tumours; hyperplasia means an increase in cell number and does not by itself imply neoplasia.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: neo-＝新，-plasia＝形成：组织异常“另起炉灶”，形成肿瘤。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Neo- means 'new' and -plasia means 'formation': abnormal tissue starts a new growth of its own.

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；重音记号标在重读音节前。

forms: 复数 emoluments，实际使用中常见复数。
family: emoluments：复数；emolumentary：有利可图的，较少见。

morphology.text: emolument + -ary → emolumentary（有利可图的）；emolument 作为独立词素记忆。

etymology.text: 中古英语经古法语 émolument 借自拉丁语 emolumentum（收益、利益）；后来集中用于任职或工作带来的报酬。

usage_note: 正式用语，常用复数 emoluments，指任职所得的薪水、费用或其他报酬；不是自己付出去的办公支出。

sentence: The fee was an emolument paid to her for holding the office.
translation: 这笔费用是因她担任该职务而支付的报酬。
scenario: 查看职位待遇文件，辨认任职所得的款项。
cloze: The fee was an _____ paid to her for holding the office.
collocation:
receive an emolument 领取职务报酬
official emolument disclosures 职务报酬披露
hint: The money is paid to the office holder rather than paid out by her.
context_hint: The money is paid to the office holder rather than paid out by her.

teaching.contrast: emolument 是任职带来的收入；expense 是支出，资金流向相反。
teaching.sentence: The document states that no emolument is attached to the honorary post.
teaching.translation: 文件说明，这个荣誉职位不附带任何报酬。

comprehension_check.sentence: The fee was an emolument paid to her for holding the office.
comprehension_check.question: 句中 emolument 表示什么？请选择符合语境的意思。
comprehension_check.wrong_reason: 这里的语境是：查看职位待遇文件，辨认任职所得的款项。 因此 emolument 表示“职务报酬”，不是“自费支出”。

fields.wrong_reason: 这里的语境是：查看职位待遇文件，辨认任职所得的款项。 因此 emolument 表示“职务报酬”，不是“自费支出”。

senses.meaning_zh: 职务报酬；任职所得的薪酬或其他收益，常用复数
senses.meaning_en: Pay or other financial benefits received from employment or an official position, usually plural.
senses.english_definition: An emolument is money or another financial benefit that someone receives because of their job or official position.
senses.chinese_definition: 职务报酬是一个人因工作或担任某项职务而获得的金钱或其他经济利益。
senses.collocation_en: salary and emoluments; emoluments of office
senses.collocation_zh: 薪金及其他报酬；任职所得的报酬
senses.sentence_en: The report lists the directors' salaries and other emoluments.
senses.sentence_zh: 该报告列出了董事的薪金及其他报酬。

etymology_story.zh: 该词经法语进入中古英语，源自拉丁语 emolumentum，意为“收益、利益”。英语中的用法后来主要集中于工作或职务带来的报酬；其更深层词源存在争议，不宜把“磨坊收入”的说法当作定论。
etymology_story.en: The word entered Middle English through French from Latin emolumentum, meaning 'gain' or 'advantage'. English usage narrowed mainly to benefits received from employment or office; its deeper derivation is disputed, so the familiar connection with milling income should not be treated as certain.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 emolument 作为整体词干，不宜硬拆为具有现行意义的前后缀。词族：emolument（职务报酬）→ emoluments（复数，最常见形式）；emolument＋-ary → emolumentary（报酬的；带来收益的，罕见）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, emolument is best treated as a whole stem rather than divided into productive prefixes and suffixes. Its family includes emoluments, the usual plural form, and emolument + -ary → emolumentary, a rare adjective meaning 'relating to remuneration' or 'yielding profit'.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: remuneration（报酬）是较正式的工作报酬总称；salary（薪金）强调定期支付的固定工资；perquisite（额外待遇）强调基本工资之外的职务福利。emolument 语体正式，尤其常用于职务收益。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Remuneration is a formal general term for payment for work; salary is regular fixed pay; a perquisite is an additional benefit attached to a position. Emolument is formal and particularly associated with the financial benefits of holding office.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把“职位带来的进账”整体记作 emoluments：薪金加上任职所得的其他收益。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor emoluments to 'what the position pays': salary plus other financial benefits of holding the post.

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；重音记号标在重读音节前。

forms: 通常不可数；需用复数时为 lyses，读音与单数不同。
family: lyse：使细胞裂解；lytic：引起溶解的。

morphology.text: hemo-（血） + lysis（溶解） → hemolysis（溶血）；lysis 作为独立词素记忆。

etymology.text: 经拉丁语来自希腊语 lysis（松开、解开）；医学英语先用来表示病势逐渐减退，后来也指细胞被破坏、溶解。

usage_note: 本课学细胞被破坏、内容物释放的意思，不考病势减退义；不要与细胞分裂混淆。

sources.label: 词源词典 · lysis
sources.scope: 历史路径；中文讲解和教学句为本批原创

sentence: Cell lysis released the contents of the cells into the solution.
translation: 细胞溶解释放了细胞内容物，使其进入溶液。
scenario: 实验观察细胞破裂后内容物进入液体的过程。
cloze: Cell _____ released the contents of the cells into the solution.
collocation:
lysis buffer for DNA extraction 用于 DNA 提取的裂解缓冲液
viral lysis of bacteria 病毒引起的细菌溶解
hint: The contents leave the cells after the cell structures break down.
context_hint: The contents leave the cells after the cell structures break down.

teaching.contrast: lysis 指细胞结构破坏、内容物释放；cell division 是细胞分裂形成新细胞。
teaching.sentence: The experiment measured bacterial lysis by tracking the release of cell contents.
teaching.translation: 实验通过追踪细胞内容物的释放来测量细菌溶解。

comprehension_check.sentence: Cell lysis released the contents of the cells into the solution.
comprehension_check.question: 句中 lysis 表示什么？请选择符合语境的意思。
comprehension_check.wrong_reason: 这里的语境是：实验观察细胞破裂后内容物进入液体的过程。 因此 lysis 表示“细胞溶解”，不是“细胞分裂”。

fields.label: 句中目标词表示（细胞溶解／细胞分裂）
fields.wrong_reason: 这里的语境是：实验观察细胞破裂后内容物进入液体的过程。 因此 lysis 表示“细胞溶解”，不是“细胞分裂”。

senses.meaning_zh: 细胞裂解；细胞膜或细胞壁受破坏而导致的细胞解体
senses.meaning_en: The disintegration of a cell following damage to its membrane or wall.
senses.english_definition: Lysis is the breaking apart of a cell when its outer covering is damaged or destroyed.
senses.chinese_definition: 细胞裂解是指细胞的外层结构受损或遭到破坏后，细胞发生解体的过程。
senses.collocation_en: cell lysis; lysis buffer
senses.collocation_zh: 细胞裂解；裂解缓冲液
senses.sentence_en: Cell lysis released the proteins into the solution.
senses.sentence_zh: 细胞裂解使蛋白质释放到溶液中。

senses.meaning_zh: 消溶；组织、凝块等生物物质的分解或溶解
senses.meaning_en: The breakdown or dissolution of biological material such as tissue or a clot.
senses.english_definition: Lysis is the process in which biological material, such as a blood clot, is broken down or dissolved.
senses.chinese_definition: 消溶是指血凝块等生物物质被分解或溶解的过程。
senses.collocation_en: clot lysis; fibrin lysis
senses.collocation_zh: 血凝块溶解；纤维蛋白溶解
senses.sentence_en: The experiment measured the rate of clot lysis.
senses.sentence_zh: 该实验测定了血凝块溶解的速率。

etymology_story.zh: 该词经医学拉丁语来自希腊语 lysis，意为“松开、解除”，与 lyein（解开）有关。医学上曾用它表示发热等症状逐渐消退，后来也用来表示细胞和其他生物物质的解体或溶解。
etymology_story.en: The word came through medical Latin from Greek lysis, meaning 'loosening' or 'release', related to lyein, 'to loosen'. It was used medically for the gradual subsiding of conditions such as fever and later also for the disintegration or dissolution of cells and other biological material.

morphology_enriched.zh: lysis 是借入的完整名词，也以 -lysis 形式充当医学和科学复合词的构词成分，表示“分解、裂解、溶解”；复数为 lyses。核心词族：lyse（使裂解）、lysed（已裂解的；过去式及过去分词）、lysing（正在裂解；现在分词）、lytic（裂解的）、lysate（裂解产物）、lysin（溶素）；相关构词有 cytolysis（细胞溶解）、hemolysis／haemolysis（溶血）、autolysis（自溶）和 hydrolysis（水解）。
morphology_enriched.en: Lysis is a borrowed noun and also appears as the scientific combining form -lysis, meaning 'breakdown, disintegration, or dissolution'; its plural is lyses. The core family includes lyse, lysed, lysing, lytic, lysate, and lysin. Related formations include cytolysis, hemolysis or haemolysis, autolysis, and hydrolysis.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: disintegration（解体）强调结构散开；dissolution（溶解）强调物质逐渐消失于液体或被溶解；rupture（破裂）强调外层结构突然破开。lysis 在生物医学中指具体的裂解或消溶过程，破裂可以是其中一步。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Disintegration emphasizes loss of structural integrity; dissolution emphasizes material being dissolved; rupture emphasizes a covering breaking open. In biomedicine, lysis names the breakdown or dissolution process, of which rupture may be one stage.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“解开”：细胞结构被解开，内容物便释放出来。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think 'loosen apart': the cell's structure comes apart and its contents are released.

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；重音记号标在重读音节前。

forms: 复数 mummers。
family: mummery：装腔作势、哑剧表演；mumming：化装表演。

morphology.text: mumm（戴面具表演） + -er（人） → mummer（化装表演者、哑剧演员）；词干接后缀时不再增加 m。

etymology.text: 中古英语中已有这个词，通常认为与古法语 momeur（化装表演者）及英语表示低语、沉默的旧词有关；可联系戴面具、靠动作演戏的画面。

usage_note: 带历史或文学色彩，也可指传统节庆化装戏的表演者；本课取用手势、表情而不用台词的哑剧演员义。

sources.label: 词源词典 · mummer
sources.scope: 历史路径；中文讲解和教学句为本批原创

sentence: The mummer told the story through gestures without speaking.
translation: 这位哑剧演员不说话，只用手势讲述故事。
scenario: 观看无台词表演，理解演员如何传达情节。
cloze: The _____ told the story through gestures without speaking.
collocation:
a mummer in a street performance 街头表演中的哑剧演员
hire a mummer for a festival 为节庆聘请哑剧演员
hint: The performer communicates through gestures and remains silent.
context_hint: The performer communicates through gestures and remains silent.

teaching.contrast: mummer 在本课靠动作表演；opera singer 用歌声表演，表达方式不同。
teaching.sentence: The audience laughed as the mummer mimed opening an enormous door.
teaching.translation: 哑剧演员用动作模仿打开一扇巨门，观众笑了起来。

comprehension_check.sentence: The mummer told the story through gestures without speaking.
comprehension_check.question: 句中 mummer 表示什么？请选择符合语境的意思。
comprehension_check.wrong_reason: 这里的语境是：观看无台词表演，理解演员如何传达情节。 因此 mummer 表示“哑剧演员”，不是“歌剧演员”。

fields.label: 句中目标词表示（哑剧演员／歌剧演员）
fields.wrong_reason: 这里的语境是：观看无台词表演，理解演员如何传达情节。 因此 mummer 表示“哑剧演员”，不是“歌剧演员”。

senses.meaning_zh: 传统民俗剧的化装表演者，常戴面具并在节庆期间演出
senses.meaning_en: A costumed performer in a traditional seasonal folk play or procession.
senses.english_definition: A mummer is someone who wears a costume, often with a mask, and performs in a traditional folk play or seasonal celebration.
senses.chinese_definition: 民俗化装表演者是指穿着戏服、常戴面具，在传统民俗剧或节庆活动中演出的人。
senses.collocation_en: a troupe of mummers; mummers' play
senses.collocation_zh: 一队民俗化装表演者；民俗化装剧
senses.sentence_en: A troupe of mummers performed a traditional play in the village square.
senses.sentence_zh: 一队化装表演者在村庄广场上演出了一部传统民俗剧。

etymology_story.zh: 该词在中古英语中已经出现，通常认为与法语 momeur（化装表演者）及 momer（化装表演、模仿）有关。它逐渐与节庆期间的化装巡演和民俗戏剧联系起来，这类表演可以包含台词。
etymology_story.en: The word is recorded in Middle English and is generally linked with French momeur, 'a masquerader', and momer, 'to masquerade or mime'. It became associated with seasonal costumed performances and folk plays, which can include spoken dialogue.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代词族可按 mum（化装表演，罕见动词）＋-er（从事者）理解；mum 接元音开头的后缀时双写 m，形成 mummer、mummed 和 mumming。相关词有 mumming（民俗化装表演）和 mummery（化装表演；贬义的繁文缛节或装模作样）。
morphology_enriched.en: Within the modern word family, mummer can be understood as mum, a rare verb meaning 'to perform in disguise', + -er, an agent suffix. The final m is doubled before vowel-initial suffixes, giving mummer, mummed, and mumming. Related words include mumming, traditional costumed performance, and mummery, masquerading or, disparagingly, empty ceremony or pretence.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: folk performer（民俗表演者）范围更广；masquerader（化装者）强调乔装或戴面具，不一定演戏；mime（哑剧演员）强调通过动作而非语言表演。mummer 的核心是传统化装演出，并不必然保持沉默。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Folk performer is broader; masquerader emphasizes wearing a disguise or mask without necessarily acting; mime emphasizes performance through movement rather than speech. A mummer belongs to a tradition of costumed performance and need not be silent.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住节日里“戴面具、穿戏服、演民俗剧”的人。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a festival performer in a mask and costume acting in a folk play.

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；重音记号标在重读音节前。

forms: 复数 anastomoses。
family: anastomotic：吻合的；anastomoses：复数。

morphology.text: ana-（重新） + stom-（口） + -osis（过程、状态） → anastomosis（吻合）；联系给管道接通开口的画面。

etymology.text: 经医学拉丁语来自希腊语 anastomosis（开口、通口），与 stoma（口）有关；后来用于血管等管状结构之间的连通。

usage_note: 可指天然连接，也可指手术建立的连接；本课重点是管状结构接通，不是切断。

sources.label: 词源词典 · anastomosis
sources.scope: 历史路径；中文讲解和教学句为本批原创

sentence: The diagram shows an anastomosis connecting two blood vessels.
translation: 图中显示一个连接两条血管的吻合。
scenario: 在解剖图上看两条管状结构之间的连通位置。
cloze: The diagram shows an _____ connecting two blood vessels.
collocation:
a vascular anastomosis 血管吻合
an intestinal anastomosis 肠吻合
hint: Two vessels are connected to allow continuity between them.
context_hint: Two vessels are connected to allow continuity between them.

teaching.contrast: anastomosis 指接通形成的连接；division 在外科语境中可指切断，方向不同。
teaching.sentence: The surgeon checked the intestinal anastomosis for leaks.
teaching.translation: 外科医生检查肠吻合口是否渗漏。

comprehension_check.sentence: The diagram shows an anastomosis connecting two blood vessels.
comprehension_check.question: 句中 anastomosis 表示什么？请选择符合语境的意思。
comprehension_check.wrong_reason: 这里的语境是：在解剖图上看两条管状结构之间的连通位置。 因此 anastomosis 表示“吻合（管状结构的连接）”，不是“管状结构的切断”。

fields.label: 句中目标词表示（吻合（管状结构的连接）／管状结构的切断）
fields.wrong_reason: 这里的语境是：在解剖图上看两条管状结构之间的连通位置。 因此 anastomosis 表示“吻合（管状结构的连接）”，不是“管状结构的切断”。

senses.meaning_zh: 吻合；血管、肠管等管状结构之间的天然或人工连通
senses.meaning_en: A natural or surgically created connection between tubular structures.
senses.english_definition: An anastomosis is a connection between two tubes in the body, such as blood vessels or sections of intestine.
senses.chinese_definition: 吻合是指体内两条管状结构之间的连接，例如血管之间或两段肠管之间的连通。
senses.collocation_en: vascular anastomosis; intestinal anastomosis
senses.collocation_zh: 血管吻合；肠吻合
senses.sentence_en: The diagram shows an anastomosis between two arteries.
senses.sentence_zh: 该图显示了两条动脉之间的一处吻合。

senses.meaning_zh: 吻合术；通过手术连接两段管状结构的操作
senses.meaning_en: The surgical joining of two tubular structures.
senses.english_definition: An anastomosis is an operation in which a surgeon joins two tubular structures so that material can pass between them.
senses.chinese_definition: 吻合术是外科医生将两段管状结构连接起来，使其中的物质能够相互通行的手术。
senses.collocation_en: perform an anastomosis; end-to-end anastomosis
senses.collocation_zh: 施行吻合术；端端吻合术
senses.sentence_en: The surgeon performed an end-to-end anastomosis after removing the damaged section of bowel.
senses.sentence_zh: 外科医生切除受损肠段后，进行了端端吻合术。

etymology_story.zh: 该词经医学拉丁语来自希腊语 anastomōsis，意为“开口、使相通”，与 stoma（口、开口）有关。其医学含义由“开通连接”发展为血管等管状结构之间的连通，以及建立这种连通的手术。
etymology_story.en: The word came through medical Latin from Greek anastomōsis, meaning 'opening' or 'providing communication', related to stoma, 'mouth' or 'opening'. Its medical meaning developed into a connection between tubular structures and the operation used to create that connection.

morphology_enriched.zh: 这是借入的医学词，历史构词可分析为 ana-（在此与打开有关）＋stom-（口、开口）＋-osis（过程或状态），不宜将 ana- 机械地理解为“重新”。词族：anastomosis（吻合，单数）、anastomoses（复数）、anastomose（使吻合；相互连通）、anastomosed（过去式及过去分词）、anastomosing（现在分词；相互连通的）、anastomotic（吻合的）、anastomotically（通过吻合；以吻合方式）。
morphology_enriched.en: This borrowed medical term can historically be analysed as ana-, associated here with opening, + stom-, 'mouth or opening', + -osis, 'process or condition'; ana- should not mechanically be read as 'again'. The family includes anastomosis, plural anastomoses; anastomose; anastomosed; anastomosing; anastomotic; and anastomotically.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: connection（连接）最宽泛；junction（交接处）强调结构相接的位置；communication（交通、连通）在解剖学中强调结构之间存在通路。anastomosis 更具体地指管状结构之间的吻合或建立吻合的操作。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Connection is the broadest term; junction emphasizes the point where structures meet; communication, in anatomy, emphasizes the existence of a passage. Anastomosis more specifically denotes a connection between tubular structures or the procedure that creates it.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: stom-＝口：给两段管道接通开口，使它们相互连通。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Stom- means 'mouth': connect the openings of two tubes so that their contents can pass through.

meaning: 花生四烯酸的（用于 arachidonic acid）

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；重音记号标在重读音节前。

forms: 形容词，无复数、时态变化；通常用于 arachidonic acid。
family: arachidic：花生酸的；Arachis：花生属名。

morphology.text: arachid-（取自 arachidic 的词干） + -onic（化学形容词词尾） → arachidonic；常与 acid 连用。

senses.meaning_zh: 花生四烯酸的；与花生四烯酸有关的
senses.meaning_en: Of or relating to arachidonic acid.
senses.english_definition: Arachidonic is used to describe a particular fatty acid found in cell membranes, or substances and processes involving that acid.
senses.collocation_en: arachidonic acid; arachidonic acid metabolism
senses.collocation_zh: 花生四烯酸；花生四烯酸代谢
senses.sentence_en: The researchers studied arachidonic acid metabolism in human cells.

etymology_story.zh: arachidonic 于20世纪初由 arachidic 改造而来，其名称最终与花生属的新拉丁语名称 Arachis 有关。名称体现了化学命名上的联系，但 arachidonic acid（花生四烯酸）与 arachidic acid（花生酸）是不同的脂肪酸。
etymology_story.en: Arachidonic was formed in the early twentieth century by modifying arachidic, a name ultimately connected with Arachis, the New Latin genus name for peanuts. The names reflect a chemical naming relationship, but arachidonic acid and arachidic acid are different fatty acids.

morphology_enriched.zh: 命名构词可表示为 arachid(ic) + -onic → arachidonic；这是专门化学名称的改造，不能把 -onic 当作可自由套用的普通英语后缀。核心词族与相关术语：arachidonic acid（花生四烯酸）、arachidonate（花生四烯酸根、盐或酯）；arachidic acid（花生酸）是相关但不同的化合物名称。arachidonic 本身为形容词，整个 arachidonic acid 短语为名词性术语。
morphology_enriched.en: The naming formation can be represented as arachid(ic) + -onic → arachidonic; this is a specialized chemical modification, rather than an ordinary productive English suffix pattern. The core family and related terms include arachidonic acid and arachidonate, meaning its anion, a salt, or an ester; arachidic acid names a related but different compound. Arachidonic itself is an adjective, while arachidonic acid is a noun phrase.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有通用的单词近义词。相关术语中，arachidonate 指花生四烯酸根、盐或酯，不能任意替换 arachidonic acid；omega-6 fatty acid（ω-6脂肪酸）与 polyunsaturated fatty acid（多不饱和脂肪酸）都是更大的类别，不能单独确定这种酸。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no general single-word synonym. Among related terms, arachidonate denotes the anion, a salt, or an ester and cannot freely replace arachidonic acid; omega-6 fatty acid and polyunsaturated fatty acid are broader categories that do not identify this particular acid.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 arachidonic acid 整体绑定“花生四烯酸”；词名联系花生属，“四烯”提示四个碳碳双键。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Learn arachidonic acid as one unit: its name connects with the peanut genus, and the acid has four carbon–carbon double bonds.

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；重音记号标在重读音节前。

forms: 形容词，无常用比较级词尾变化。

morphology.text: atroph-（萎缩，atrophy 的词干） + -ic（形容词后缀） → atrophic（萎缩的）。

etymology.text: 由 atrophy 加形容词后缀构成；atrophy 经法语、晚期拉丁语来自希腊语 atrophia，原意与缺乏营养而消瘦有关。

usage_note: 医学或生物学用语，描述组织、器官萎缩的状态；词本身不说明萎缩的具体原因。

fields.label: 句中目标词表示（萎缩的／肥大的）
fields.wrong_reason: 这里的语境是：阅读影像或组织报告，辨认体积减小的描述。 因此 atrophic 表示“萎缩的”，不是“肥大的”。

senses.meaning_zh: 萎缩的；与组织或器官萎缩有关的
senses.meaning_en: Affected by or relating to the wasting or thinning of tissue or an organ.
senses.english_definition: If tissue or an organ is atrophic, it has become smaller or thinner because its cells have decreased in size or number.
senses.collocation_en: atrophic changes; atrophic gastritis
senses.collocation_zh: 萎缩性改变；萎缩性胃炎
senses.sentence_en: The examination revealed atrophic changes in the stomach lining.
senses.sentence_zh: 检查发现胃黏膜出现了萎缩性改变。

etymology_story.zh: atrophic 是19世纪初由 atrophy 加形容词后缀形成的。atrophy 经法语和晚期拉丁语追溯至希腊语 atrophia，其构词含义与“缺乏营养”有关，后来用于表示组织或器官因多种原因发生的萎缩。
etymology_story.en: Atrophic was formed in the early nineteenth century from atrophy with an adjective suffix. Atrophy came through French and Late Latin from Greek atrophia, whose formation relates to lack of nourishment; its meaning broadened to tissue or organ wasting from various causes.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：atroph-（atrophy 的词干）+ -ic（形容词后缀）→ atrophic。历史构词中的 a- 表示“无、缺乏”，troph- 与“营养、滋养”有关；核心词族：atrophy（名词：萎缩；动词：萎缩）、atrophies（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、atrophied（已萎缩的；过去式及过去分词）、atrophying（正在萎缩；现在分词）、atrophic（萎缩的）、atrophically（以萎缩方式；较少见）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: atroph-, the stem of atrophy, + the adjective suffix -ic → atrophic. Historically, a- means without and troph- relates to nourishment; the core family comprises atrophy as a noun and verb, atrophies as a plural or third-person singular form, atrophied, atrophying, atrophic, and the less common adverb atrophically.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: atrophied（已萎缩的）强调已经发生的萎缩结果；wasted（瘦损的、萎缩的）更直观地描述组织或身体明显消瘦；degenerative（退行性的）涵盖更广泛的结构或功能退化，不一定伴随萎缩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Atrophied emphasizes the result of wasting that has already occurred; wasted describes visible loss of tissue or bodily bulk more directly; degenerative covers a broader decline in structure or function and does not necessarily imply shrinkage.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: a-（缺乏）+ troph-（滋养）→ 联想组织失去滋养后萎缩；这是词源记忆线索，并非全部病因。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A- suggests absence and troph- suggests nourishment: picture tissue wasting without nourishment, while remembering that modern atrophy has several causes.

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；重音记号标在重读音节前。

morphology.text: cud + chewing → cud-chewing（反刍的）；cud 作为独立词素记忆。

etymology.text: 来自古英语 cudu，也有 cwudu 的旧形式；原来就指反刍物，并与可咀嚼的树脂、胶状物有关，记住食物回到嘴里再嚼的画面。

senses.meaning_zh: 反刍食物；反刍动物返回口中再次咀嚼的食团
senses.meaning_en: Partly digested food brought back into the mouth by a ruminant for further chewing.
senses.english_definition: Cud is food that an animal such as a cow brings back from its stomach into its mouth and chews again.
senses.collocation_en: chew the cud; a bolus of cud
senses.collocation_zh: 反刍；一团反刍食物
senses.sentence_en: The cows lay in the shade, chewing the cud.
senses.sentence_zh: 牛群卧在阴凉处，反刍着食物。

etymology_story.zh: cud 来自古英语 cudu，较早也作 cwudu，当时既可指反刍食物，也可指树胶或树脂。其日耳曼语亲属词也有“树脂、胶”等含义，而现代英语的核心意义集中于反刍食物。
etymology_story.en: Cud comes from Old English cudu, earlier also cwudu, which could denote both regurgitated food and gum or resin. Its Germanic relatives likewise include words for resin or glue, while the central modern English meaning concerns food chewed again by ruminants.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 cud 是不可再分析的独立词素，通常作不可数名词。常见复合形式：cud-chewing（形容词：反刍的；名词性用法：反刍活动）、cud-chewer（反刍动物）；chew the cud 是动词短语，既可指反刍，也可比喻反复思考或从容闲谈，但 cud 本身并未因此变成动词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, cud is an unanalyzable free morpheme and is normally an uncountable noun. Common compounds include cud-chewing, used adjectivally or for the activity, and cud-chewer, an animal that chews cud; chew the cud is a verb phrase that can also mean reflecting at length or chatting leisurely, without making cud itself a verb.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: regurgitated food（反流回口中的食物）是较宽泛的描述，不限于反刍动物；rumen contents（瘤胃内容物）包括仍在瘤胃内的物质，不等于已返回口中的反刍食团；digesta（消化道内容物）泛指正在消化的物质。三者均不能在所有语境中替换 cud。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Regurgitated food is a broader description that is not restricted to ruminants; rumen contents includes material still inside the rumen, rather than specifically the food returned to the mouth; digesta refers generally to material undergoing digestion. None is interchangeable with cud in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住牛的动作：吞下 → 返回口中 → 再嚼；反复“咀嚼”也能联想到反复思考。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a cow swallowing, bringing food back up, and chewing again; repeated chewing also suggests turning a thought over.

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；ˈ 标在重读音节前。

forms: dehumanises；dehumanised；dehumanising。美式拼写 dehumanize。
